records.text: Graphite studies itself first: its purpose, windows, commands, settings and evidence. It explains selected program data and uses registered capabilities through the shared Kernel. Custom reference libraries augment independently replaceable model weights. Durable awareness, quarantine admission into a clean V1 project, context checkpoints, The current expanded campaign covers passes 13 through 37 and the approved window campaign. Object Glass binds selected identities, sources, evidence, gaps and read actions. Retain evidence-backed ARC-1 enhancement leads discovered by software tests for separate review. Capability prerequisites are inspected separately from permission and qualification. Study, recovery and external reasoning still require their declared host and real-provider qualification.

records.text:
# ARC Ledger maintenance

Evolve the existing PySide6 interface and shared Engineering Kernel. Preserve explicit saves, source bindings, private profiles, scoped candidate edits, execution grants, independent source acceptance, recovery and rollback. Never broaden permissions for a presentation change.

The project has fourteen devices, seven workspace areas and a maximum of five pinned workspaces. Keep menus, keyboard shortcuts and accessible names available when shortcut icons have no captions.

R10 authority is F133-B / D213ECV / ECP5-12F / ECP5-45F. No eMMC or microSD path. J12/J13 are controllers; J14 is game media. Fabrication, routing release and physical programming remain HOLD. Host/RTL evidence is not board qualification.

Policy, SDK contracts/runtime, hardware manifests/sources/tools/budgets, tool pins and tests are protected. Disclose changes and obtain independent acceptance; never weaken a test to make a candidate pass. Preserve upstream provenance and licences.

Use focused checks for changed behavior, an actual UI walkthrough, fresh-package verification and privacy checks. Preserve canonical source until separately reviewed acceptance. Reusable behavior should live in the portable SDK rather than only in a GUI.

## Reproduce

Run `python3 tools/check_release.py`, then `python3 -m workbench.launch --check`. Build a native starter on a host with a C compiler and Icarus Verilog. Physical and live-provider qualification remain separate.

Retain ARC-1 architecture improvements revealed by Ledger tests as source-bound private investigation findings with evidence, conditions, uncertainty and follow-up. Preserve existing evidence and original sources. Candidate improvements still require their own scoped source change and acceptance; do not silently promote a reference snapshot or physical qualification.

# Graphite 0.4.3 · The desk does, doubts, and looks ahead

Graphite is a quiet workspace for ideas, research, documents and engineering work, with its AI beside the work. It runs on
one minimal Debian computer (a phone is optional access) and keeps everything on that computer unless you turn a service
on. Graphite is the public name of the workspace; its assistant's face is Stacy, and she speaks staC; before November 6, 2026 the program was called Ledger &
Slate, and folders, scripts, settings keys and internal names keep those earlier names for compatibility.

- **Start here** · [ThinkPad first install](docs/THINKPAD_FIRST_INSTALL.md) covers USB setup, the model-free first launch and the observed hardware.
- **Look ahead** · with a sheet or a calculation selected in the Field, ask "what if B4 were 100?": the cell is set without changing anything, the wires are followed, and the Field marks everything that would move with what it would say (**Esc** clears).
- **The brief** · press **B** in the Field: the whole desk written up as one page, from the records and by no model; **G** keeps it as a page that knows when the desk has moved on.
- **Right-click** · on a sheet in the Field the menu cascades: What if › a number › a value to try; Doubt it › what Stacy finds, each row opening its evidence; Trace it › every step back and on; What can be done › the steps; Your words ›.
- **Your own words** · `word waits = field.read | pick waiting | select kind,title,state`, then `waits`, `waits | count`, `words`, `forget waits`: a staC line kept under a word of yours.
- **Doubt** · press **X** on a sheet in the Field: Stacy cross-examines it for what a plausible result may hide (an edited input, mixed conditions, one source, a check that cannot fail, a number recorded nowhere) and **D** offers the step that removes the doubt.
- **staC reads the desk** · `field.read | pick waiting | select kind,title,state`; `this` is the sheet selected in the Field; **T** traces a thing to its source; ask "what if B3 were 320?" about a calculation and nothing is changed.
- **Doing** · press **D** on a sheet in the Field for the steps the records offer (a read runs; a change waits for **G**, your go); **C** checks the desk and offers to settle what needs no decision of yours.
- **The shelf** · press **P** in the Field: every program and room in six fixed columns; Enter opens one.
- **The Field** · press **F9** (or Arrange → Field, or type `field` in the writing strip): the work in this workspace as sheets with the wires that say what feeds what. Arrow keys follow the wires, Enter opens the real page, Esc comes back. Stacy's rail shows the staC line for the selected sheet: **S** puts it in the writing strip, **Shift+Enter** runs it. **N** shows this computer's network the same way; **W** returns to the work. It is the first slice of the objects and instruments desktop (master specification, sections 70 to 72), new in 0.3. Right-click a sheet (or press the Menu key) for what can be done with it. Guide → What's New has the rest.
- **Visual baseline** · [Visual Pass 1 reference review](docs/BOSS_VISUAL_PASS_01_REVISION.md) compares the five owner references with the revised worksheet, PDF evidence review and research journal.
- **Halfway release** · [P08–P10](docs/BOSS_HALFWAY_P10.md) covers resident model handling, project collections and reviewed PDF tables that become sheets and reports.
- **Evidence preparation** · [Intelligent data arrangement P07](docs/INTELLIGENT_DATA_P07.md) covers source preparation, exact calculations and follow-up passages.
- **Resource scheduling** · [Traffic cop P06](docs/TRAFFIC_COP_P06.md) covers shared-memory admission, foreground turns and readable waiting reasons.
- **Hardware route:** read [ThinkPad / Vulkan P05](docs/THINKPAD_VULKAN_P05.md): the bundled Vulkan worker, hardware profile, launch defaults, actual backend readback and CPU fallback.
- **Current desk:** read [BOSS M1](docs/BOSS_M1.md): the new native interface, path, contextual commands and constructed chains.
- **Earlier guide:** read [the daily guide](docs/DAILY_GUIDE.md) (the desk, the cat and its programs list, the System menu, the
  writing line and its four modes, Log with its Events and Network streams, the right-click menu, documents, assignments, the
  Finder, Ingress and Egress, the local model, the game behind the mark).
- **Working on it:** read [RECORD_OF_DIRECTIONS.md](RECORD_OF_DIRECTIONS.md) first: the owner's directions, where the
  knowledge is, where things stand and how to continue.

The supplied Graphite 0.1 baseline has historical mechanical and offscreen evidence from the build container, and live trials of the small Qwen models
where the docs say so. The owner's ThinkPad, its display and inputs, and the owner's model file have not been tried yet;
nothing here claims they are accepted.

The BOSS upgrade implements P01–P10 of the twenty-pass campaign. Try **References → Read technical PDF → Review table** to make a sheet from a reviewed source. Open **Project Desk → Ask Stacy → Prepare evidence** to see matching project passages and exact results before a model turn. Live model and owner-host Vulkan qualification remain pending. P11 covers full native programs.

## Install

From the release volumes (`Graphite_0.4.3_part_NN.zip`, `RELEASE_PARTS.json` and `INSTALL_LS.py` in one folder, for
example a USB stick), as your ordinary Debian user:

```
python3 INSTALL_LS.py --usb . --target "$HOME/Applications/Graphite-0.4.3" --minimal-session --vulkan --plan
python3 INSTALL_LS.py --usb . --target "$HOME/Applications/Graphite-0.4.3" --minimal-session --vulkan --yes
```

`INSTALL_LS.py` is the Graphite installer (its file name is kept: scripts, tests and earlier notes call it). It verifies
every volume, restores the program into a new folder, installs the Debian prerequisites (with `--yes`, through sudo) and
the pinned Python dependencies, checks the runtime imports, the payload and the seed, and ends with one line that says
what actually happened. `--extract-only` verifies and restores without installing anything; `--offline` uses a prepared
cache only; `--public-manifest URL --manifest-sha256 HASH` installs from a published release. Every option and refusal is
explained in [docs/MINIMAL_DEBIAN_INSTALL_01.md](docs/MINIMAL_DEBIAN_INSTALL_01.md).

From an already extracted program folder:

```
bash INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh --quick            # asks before sudo; add --vulkan for Radeon dependencies, --minimal-session for the dedicated session, or other tool options as needed
bash INSTALL_LEDGER.sh --quick            # the runtime only, on a system that already has the prerequisites
```

Keep your previous program folder and every workspace; install a new release into a new folder. A local model is
optional: the daily guide says which small GGUF file to fetch and how to register it in the Brain room. No model file is
included.

## Start

```
bash START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh   # from a Debian text login: the dedicated fullscreen session; prints "Graphite ended with status N" when you leave
bash START_OFFICE.sh           # from an existing desktop: the ordinary window on the Office workspace (~/Concern/Office)
```

Leave through the System menu (the pale Graphite symbol at the upper right) → Return to Debian, or Exit Graphite on an
existing desktop. The same menu's Log out, Restart and Shut down first save or set aside your work as leaving does, ask you
to confirm, and then ask the system's own logind (never sudo); without a login session they say they are unavailable. On Windows, `START_OFFICE.cmd` starts the same program after Python
and `requirements-qt.txt` are installed.

## Operator tools

```
bash LEDGER.sh doctor                 # inspects the installation; creates no workspace, starts nothing
bash LEDGER.sh doctor --self-test     # a disposable capture, restart, backup and restore round trip
bash LEDGER.sh doctor --qt-check      # the real window and capture widget, offscreen
bash LEDGER.sh baseline --out my-baseline.json
bash LEDGER.sh inventory
```

## Complete backups

Close Graphite before taking a backup. This includes ordinary workspace files and working copies; restore always writes
NEW folders and leaves existing work untouched:

```
bash LEDGER.sh backup create --root ~/Concern/Office --out ~/Graphite-backups/office
bash LEDGER.sh backup verify ~/Graphite-backups/office
bash LEDGER.sh backup restore ~/Graphite-backups/office --to ~/Concern/Office-restored
bash LEDGER.sh open --root ~/Concern/Office-restored --profile ~/Concern/Office-restored-profile
```

External originals and external model weights are not included; model files inside the workspace are left out unless
`--include-models` is given. Complete snapshots and no-replace publication target Linux. docs/STAGE1.md explains backup and
restore in full.

## Checks

```
python3 tools/check_release.py               # payload, seed and syntax; the live program against docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json; the privacy scan
python3 tools/check_release.py --self-test   # adds the focused tests_integrated modules, one module per child process
python3 tools/check_release.py --ui          # adds the offscreen Qt checks of the UI gate
python3 -m workbench.slate_checks --runtime
python3 -m workbench.continuing_checks --workers
python3 -m workbench.deployment_checks --ui
```

`tools/check_release.py` is the one entry for the release check (it runs `tools/check_hatch.py`). The registry record
`docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json` holds every operation's scope and argument-schema digest, the job tools, every setting
definition's digest and the adapters; `tools/record_registry.py` writes it from the live tree, and any difference is listed
in words. It submits no job, starts no model or worker, makes no provider request and invokes no native tool. A passing
check is integrity, not readiness or acceptance. Tests run one module at a time:
`python3 -B -m unittest tests_integrated.test_graphite` (tests_integrated has no `__init__.py`; do not use discover).

## Paired exchange, signed releases and deployment

Arrange → Exchange & deployment holds recipient-bound request and result pills, pinned mutual TLS 1.3, replay protection,
explicit signed offline release verification and recovery, reviewable launch files and optional read-only phone progress.
A received pill stays in quarantine until explicitly accepted; returned edits become a frozen working-copy proposal, and
originals still need separate owner publication. Nothing starts merely by opening the panel. Read docs/STAGE6.md before
pairing or updating. No publisher private key or default trust root is included.

## Packaging

```
python3 tools/package_graphite.py --dry-run                                     # what would be shipped; writes nothing
python3 tools/package_graphite.py OUT
python3 tools/package_release_parts.py OUT/Graphite_0.4.3_full.zip PARTS "Graphite 0.4.3"
```

Graphite's own code and documents are free software under the GNU General Public License, version 2 only (COPYING).
Stacy's artwork, the other project art, the names and the game copy are kept back (RIGHTS.md). Licences of bundled fonts,
runtimes and dependencies are in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md; the pinned dependencies are the requirements-*.txt files.

records.text:
# Graphite · record of directions

Read this first. It says where Graphite is going, what holds, where it stands, and what comes next. It is the whole
record: one page, kept current, with no history of what was tried and dropped. The owner keeps backups of everything
earlier; the previous record is in the 0.2a13 release.

## Where this is going

On 12 November 2026, once the source was free: "let's develop where it can go." It "is basically going to be my ultimate
desktop from which I can launch every program from a basic screen and do basic things, or launch the program into its full
window. But when I am inside of the graphite workbench, I am inside of a nice dark orange and green fantasy computer land
that is tremendously effective, efficient, smart, and knows what I'm doing because I'm doing it."

In the owner's words (master specification, `docs/briefs/Graphite_Master_Specification_v5_BOSS.pdf`):

- "The destination is a usable computer: I can work directly, delegate an edit or sustained investigation, and return
  to inspectable progress."
- "the Hello computer experience: address the machine with an intention and work at the level of the problem."
- "Completed assignments should leave the machine more capable."

And on 12 November 2026: "My wish is like Lains computer from the awesome anime." Read that as a feeling to build, not a
picture to copy: a machine you sit down to at night that is already awake, where the work hangs in layers in the dark,
the wires between things are visible, and you speak to it in one line. Everything drawn is original.

One ThinkPad on minimal Debian runs it. The model is local. Nothing leaves the computer unless the owner turns a
service on. Finished means installed and seen working on that ThinkPad, judged by real completed work.

## What holds

- **Authority.** "I pre approve all your expert opinions, recommendations, and choices." "My goal with you is to build,
  complete, and finish the project." 12 November: "Do everything auto and surprise me." Decide, say what you decided,
  keep moving. Ask only when the answer changes the result or reaches outside the computer.
- **Two people to steer by** (12 November: the source is "whatever Linus" Torvalds "would do"; "Also think what would
  Woz do ... kindness to humanity"). Linus: the source is open under the GPL version 2 only, the work is done in public, and
  what counts is whether it runs. Woz: the fewest parts that do the job; a machine one person can understand whole; the
  schematics come in the box; it is ready the moment it is switched on; it is generous, a little playful, and kind to
  the person at the keyboard (plain words, no blame, nothing taken from them, useful on a modest machine).
- **Simple, for a power user** (12 November: "let's concentrate on simple power user"). Keyboard first. One line to
  speak in. Few words on the screen and none that explain themselves twice. One rule instead of a setting where a rule
  will do. No hand-holding, no second way to do a thing unless the second way is the keyboard.
- **Checking.** Light. Batch related edits, then one launch-and-use check. Dig deeper only for a real failure or a
  worry about the owner's data. No new test suites, no test-count campaigns.
- **Honesty.** Say plainly what is not done. Nothing counts as accepted on the ThinkPad until it is tried there.
  A picture is not a run.
- **Records.** This page, and a slim tree. Keep what teaches how the program works or why. When unsure, keep.
- **The owner stays in control.** One dispatcher for all work (the Kernel). One kill switch for every job, model and
  capture (Stop all jobs, Ctrl+Shift+F12). Session and power actions only on the owner's confirmation, never sudo.
- **Build for the smallest model.** Put the intelligence in the records and exact computation, so a better model is a
  free upgrade.
- **Use mature programs.** Open the real spreadsheet, the real editor; hand files over and take them back. Do not
  rewrite what exists. Keep every capability when the look changes.
- **Two names, one for each thing** (12 November: "to simplify things, Stacy should be the face of the assistant as
  communicated through the language of Stacy. S-T-A-C."). Graphite is the workspace. Stacy is the assistant: one
  assistant, and hers is its face. staC, said "Stacy", is how she speaks: what she reads, she shows as a staC line the
  owner can run. Her portrait is still, in its own places. Folders, settings keys and scripts keep their older names
  (Ledger, Slate, Hatch, LS, arc1) on purpose; do not rename them.

## The desk

- **The look.** Near-black ground, cream reading text, amber for what is selected and what waits for the owner, small
  green marks for live readings and what is current. Monospaced lettering, thin rules, original ink-and-halftone art.
  Surfaces are still. Art sits in its own places (Illustrated, ASCII or Clean) and never enters documents.
- **The frame.** The path of the current work across the top with Work, Programs and System; Files, Machine and
  Settings on the left; Talk, Activity and Context on the right; one writing strip along the bottom (Assistant,
  Terminal, Log) with CPU, GPU, RAM and TXT beside it. The work is in the middle.
- **The Field** (new, 12 November; specification sections 70 to 72; F9, Arrange → Field, or type `field`). An
  overview where the real objects of the work hang as sheets in the dark with the wires that say what feeds what:
  material, tables, calculations, findings, open questions. The selected sheet is brightest and what touches it stays
  near. Arrow keys follow the wires; Enter opens the real editor; coming back keeps the place. N shows this computer's
  network the same way (interfaces, programs, the places they reach), and Enter there opens the Log's Network stream.
  Right-click or the Menu key on a sheet opens the desk's own menu for it: open, what feeds it, what it feeds, its
  staC line, ask Graphite about it.
- **Stacy is staC, and she is more than a picture** (12 November: "She is more then wallpaper", "StaC is the secret code.
  Let's use the hell out of it!!!"). Every object in the Field carries the staC line that reads it. Her rail at the right
  of the Field shows that line for the selected sheet; S puts it in the writing strip and Shift+Enter runs it, with the
  answer in the working area. Wherever Graphite shows a thing, it should be able to say that thing in staC, and Stacy is
  where it is said. In Talk she is the assistant: asked about a sheet (its menu, or a question typed while it is
  selected) she answers with the staC line that reads it and what the records say, model or no model
  (`workbench/shell2.py`, SlateFace.answer_in_stac). A model, when there is one, adds her own words to that; it does not
  replace it.
  This is the desktop model to grow: every kind of work should be findable there, and the same action should be
  reachable from the sheet, the right-click menu, the keyboard, a typed staC line and the assistant. The code is
  `workbench/field_model.py` (no Qt), `field_qt.py` (drawing), `field_source.py` (reads through the Kernel) and
  `field_page.py` (the way in and out).
- **The desk does** (12 November: "I want a do, not a chatbot"; "Build more then I can imagine"). The program, not a
  model, knows what there is to do: for a sheet it asks the records how the thing stands and offers the steps that fit
  (`workbench/field_do.py`), each an exact line. A read runs at once. A change is put in Talk with its line and waits for
  one go. C checks the desk; one go settles what needs no decision of the owner's; then the desk checks itself, and that
  check is what "done" means. Keys in the Field: D, a digit to choose, G for the go (a digit never approves), C, and F
  on the shelf for a program's full window. Whether a step runs by itself is the Kernel's scope for it, read from the
  Kernel. Every step is an operation the program already had;
  add steps there, not a second engine. A model's place is to put reads into words and, later, to pick among steps the
  program offers; it does not plan.
- **Catch the trap first** (13 November: the owner's whole-build specification, 35 situations each with a "difficult
  variation", and "build what you think is the neatest ... upon the spirit of the idea"). Before Stacy makes more, she
  catches more: X doubts a sheet with exact questions (`workbench/field_doubt.py`), worst first, each row a read; a doubt
  comes with the step that removes it; the desk check doubts everything. No model takes part, and a model is not asked to
  rephrase a doubt. The specification is the map and the acceptance test (it counts on the ThinkPad, on the owner's own
  material); it is reached one trap and one situation at a time, by adding a question here and its steps in
  `field_do.py`, never by trusting a model more.
- **Look ahead, write it up, the owner's own words** (13 November: "Build a few ideas surprise me"). Four additions in the
  same spirit, none with a model. A what-if on a sheet is followed along the wires (`workbench/field_ripple.py`,
  `field.ripple`): calculations worked again exactly, words that carry a number that would move, and each check run by
  its own program on the sheet as it would be; the Field marks what would move. More traps as exact questions
  (a subtotal counted twice, the same digits under another unit, a check on a replaced page); quantities are compared in
  base units. B writes the desk up as one page from the records (`workbench/field_brief.py`); the go keeps what was
  shown, and the page knows when the desk has moved on. The owner keeps staC reads under words of their own
  (`workbench/stac_words.py`); a word is written out before it runs. And a rule of working that proved itself: a second
  set of readers went through the code while it was being written and found real faults in 0.4.1 and 0.4.2; have a
  reader that did not write the code read it before it is called done.
- **staC reads the desk** (12 November: "Can we make staC and Stacy more powerful in creative ways"). The Field is a staC
  source: `field.read` (objects, wires, what waits), `field.trace {id}` (where a thing comes from, what rests on it),
  `field.whatif {id, set}` (a calculation worked with other values, changing nothing). `this` at the start of a line is
  the selected sheet. Stacy's trace (T) and her "what if" are those reads, shown as lines like everything she reads.
  When a new power is wanted for Stacy, make it a read staC can run first, then give it a key and words.
- **The shelf** (12 November; P in the Field). Every program and room as a sheet, in six columns set by hand that do not
  move (Work, Think, Make, Build, Move, Set up; `field_source.SHELF`). Enter opens the room, which is the basic screen;
  a native program's full window is started from its room. This is the launcher the owner asked for, first slice.
- **With a model, she reads first** (`docs/MODEL_TRIAL_03.md`). The staC read is exact and comes first; the model only puts
  the rows into words, and its words are marked as its own. A 2B model is enough for that. Improve the reads, not the
  prompt.
- **It opens on the work** (12 November, the owner left the choice here). At launch the Field is in front when the
  workspace has anything in it, with what waits selected; Esc goes to where the owner left off. An empty workspace
  opens on Home. Home's "Start: always Home" still means Home.
- **Small things that stay.** `poem` as the empty hint. Ingress and Egress. The pinned Trash. Home as a file browser.
  The game behind System (STRUTHIO ARCADE; its source is the STRUTHIO repository's `arcade/`, changed there and
  copied in).

## Where it stands

Graphite 0.4.3: 0.2a13 "After Midnight" plus the Field (0.3), then Stacy as the assistant answering in staC, the start
on the work, the shelf and the GPL (0.3.1), the desk that does (0.4), staC reading the desk, with trace and what-if (0.4.1), Stacy's doubt (0.4.2), and the look ahead, the brief and the owner's words (0.4.3). Passes 1 to 10 of the twenty-pass plan (`docs/BOSS_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`) are
built: the dark desk, the editable path, cascading menus that build staC chains, the Vulkan worker and memory
coordination, evidence preparation on the CPU, the model lifecycle, source collections, and PDF table to sheet to
report. Releases 0.2a8 to 0.2a13 then prepared the first ThinkPad install (offline kit, first-run workshop) and
settled the desk art; they also cut thin slices of later passes (the spreadsheet round trip, Open source row, Night
Shift, Method Press). `workbench/version.py` has one line per release.

Checked on 12 November 2026 in a cloud container, not on the ThinkPad: the nine release parts restore with
`INSTALL_LS.py`; `tools/check_release.py` passes; the window opens offscreen with no model; the Field draws a restored
worked case (After Hours 07) from its real records and opens its pages. The source is public in the STRUTHIO
repository on its own branch under the GNU GPL, version 2 only (`COPYING`); Stacy's artwork, the names and the game
copy are kept back (`RIGHTS.md`).

Never yet done, by every document in the tree:

- Graphite has not run on the ThinkPad (E16 Gen 2, Ryzen 7 7735HS, Radeon 680M, about 61 GiB shared memory, Debian 13
  at a text console). The offline kit is ready: `docs/THINKPAD_FIRST_INSTALL.md`.
- No model has answered on the ThinkPad, and the Vulkan path has not met the Radeon. (Two small models answered in the
  build container on 12 November: `docs/MODEL_TRIAL_03.md`.) No model file ships; the owner chooses one.
- Rust: asked about on 12 November ("I'm thinking rust soon???"). Not a rewrite. When the ThinkPad shows what is slow,
  new self-contained parts (the staC engine, indexing, evidence preparation) can be written in Rust behind the same
  dispatcher, the way the Linux kernel took Rust: new parts, one at a time.
- Twenty focused tests in five modules still fail because they assert the earlier look, layout and version.

## What comes next

1. **First boot on the ThinkPad** from the offline kit, with no model. Write down what actually happened.
2. **One real model** in the Brain room, on the processor and then on the Radeon. Record what the program reads back.
   The owner's choice for the first (12 November, voice-typed "Quinn 4.0 27B Quant 4 when it's available"): the Qwen
   family's 4.0 release at 27B, 4-bit quantised, once it exists.
3. **One whole journey with the model live:** datasheet to sheet to calculation to report (the first-run workshop),
   then a question over the prepared evidence.
4. **Connect the doing to the assignment loop** (`workbench/agent_loop.py`, which already records every step and keeps
   working while Graphite is closed): a job started from a sheet, its checks bound so that done means they pass, the
   owner's go for a waiting change in the Work block. Then the steps not offered yet: reviewing a sheet again from its
   page, deciding a held source, citing sources for a rewritten finding.
5. **Grow the Field and staC together** into the working desk: a key that starts a program in its full window from the
   shelf and brings its files back; what is in use and what was used last, so the desk knows what the owner is doing;
   every object kind (methods, files), staC lines that do
   more than read (the chain of steps that made a result, ready to run again on new material), wires that route around
   sheets, reading off the window's thread, and the way back from a full program.
6. **Then the plan's abilities, in its order:** full native programs from the desk (pass 11), a changed fact that
   travels (12), the assistant on any described job (13), getting the tools it lacks (14), web, mail and calendar on
   the owner's terms (15), specialist and creative routes (16), durable self-improvement (17), and the closing
   release (18 to 20). The passes are a map of abilities, not a schedule; measure progress by journeys that work on the
   real machine.

## Where the knowledge is

Read in this order: this page; the master specification (pages 1 to 15, then sections 70 to 76 for the desktop);
`docs/THINKPAD_FIRST_INSTALL.md`; `README.md` for install, start, backup, checks and packaging;
`docs/BOSS_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` for the passes. For how one mechanism works, read its own document in `docs/`;
documents written before 8 November describe the earlier look and names, and are right about mechanisms only.
`docs/DECISION_REGISTER.json` holds the reasons behind older choices.

The commands: test one module at a time with
`QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 -B -m unittest tests_integrated.test_graphite` (never discover);
`python3 tools/check_release.py` for integrity; after any source change

records.text:
# The resident agent loop (HATCH AGENT-01)

November 5, 2026 · UTC. The owner's direction (Commission v2.1 and the decisions of 2026-11-05, D19): Slate takes an assignment, works it one bounded step at a time with real tools, keeps a durable record of findings and open conditions, can be paused, resumed and stopped, and stays useful with the smallest model because explicit procedure comes first and the model only chooses among a few proposed next steps.

## The record

An assignment is an **investigation** (`workbench/investigations.py`: the question, claims as FINDING, CANDIDATE or QUESTION with computed evidence states, every step with its input digests, outcome and result digest, sources, checks, stop, refresh) plus one row in `agent_assignments` (same Kernel SQLite file): profile, request, context, plan, cursor, state, reason, budget, paused reason, model job. The investigation sheet (`investigation.sheet`) and the room Hatch ▸ Work ▸ Investigations & assignments show all of it. Nothing new was added as a store, scheduler or dispatcher.

States: READY (assigned), RUNNING (a driver is stepping it), PAUSED (Ledger closed, Master Stop or the owner), WAITING (the owner is needed: a question, a refused step, units that differ), DONE, STOPPED, FAILED.

## The step

`agent.step {id}` runs exactly one planned step: the profile's next operation is dispatched through the Kernel with a principal bounded to the budget's effects (read, or read and execute; never approve or candidate), the step is recorded in `inv_steps` **before** its result is interpreted (operation and arguments as the program, input digests, outcome, summary, result digest, seconds, authority), then the profile turns the actual result into claims and context, and the cursor moves. A refused or failed dispatch is recorded FAILED and moves the assignment to WAITING with the error in words; Resume retries it. Budget exhaustion is STOPPED with "Budget used: N steps, S seconds". `agent.run` repeats steps synchronously within limits (tests, command line); the desktop uses a timer driver (`workbench/agent_qt.py`) that calls `agent.step` while an assignment is RUNNING and yields to the interface between steps.

## Profiles

A profile (`workbench/agent_profiles.py`, interface in its docstring) is explicit Python: `plan` gives the first steps as registered operations or `helpers:<name>` local computations; `arguments` completes a step from earlier results; `interpret` turns a result into claims, context, `done`, `waiting`, further steps or `options`; `failed` says what to do after a refusal. This pass ships `operation_sequence` (an explicit plan, for tests) and `numbers_on_page` (`workbench/profile_numbers.py`): read the page → find the quantities with units (helper `quantities_from_text`) → sum them with a dimension check through `math.evaluate` → append the result paragraph to the page through `documents.edit` → bind a condition card to the exact input words. A request earns a profile by its words (`agent_loop.request_profile`: a verb such as add up, total, sum, count, a noun such as numbers, quantities, values, and a place such as on this page); a request no profile fits becomes a WAITING assignment that says so, with its own investigation, rather than a silent nothing.

## Where the model plugs in

Where a profile offers options, `choose_next` asks the local model only when more than one option is acceptable and a worker is READY: `brain.ask` in **choice mode** (added in this pass: the message lists the numbered options; the answer is one option number, schema-constrained, temperature 0, at most 24 tokens). The pick is taken only if the profile marks that option acceptable; otherwise the default is taken and the step says "model chose k, not acceptable here, default taken". Every consultation is a recorded step (kind MODEL_CHOICE: operation, job id, pick, decision, prompt); a rule-only choice is kind CHOICE. Measured in the build container (docs/MODEL_TRIAL_01.md): the 0.5B model chose poorly every time, the 1.5B model chose the plain case right; the rules therefore stay primary, and a better model simply picks better.

## Condition cards and helpers

A **condition card** (`workbench/conditions.py`, record kind `condition`) binds a written result to the block ids, offsets and quoted words it was calculated from on the saved revision. Every document write marks affected cards STALE (words changed or moved) or BROKEN (the result paragraph is gone); the page shows a quiet line with the word recheck; `conditions.recheck` re-extracts from the current revision, recomputes and rewrites only the result paragraph, bound again. A **helper** (`workbench/helpers.py`, record kind `helper`) is a procedure Slate uses, kept with its purpose, inputs, outputs, limits and source and counted on every use (uses, successes, failures, effectiveness), so effective helpers are reused and improved; this pass ships three module helpers (`quantities_from_text`, `sum_model`, `condition_card`), and the record shape already allows sandboxed Python helpers Slate writes later.

## The right column

`agent.status` gives five plain lines per assignment: working on (the request), doing now (the running or next step's purpose, or the reason it waits), found (FINDING claims with their evidence state), needs you (QUESTION claims and the WAITING reason), inspect (the investigation, the document, the condition cards). The Work block under Slate's face shows them with the words Stop, Pause, Resume and Inspect; the Related block beneath lists the owner's own records that share the page's words (`ledger.related`, word match, dismissable). Closing Ledger pauses running assignments ("Ledger closed"); Master Stop pauses them too; the Today page lists paused assignments with a resume word.

## Operations added and recorded

`agent.assign`, `agent.step`, `agent.run`, `agent.pause`, `agent.resume`, `agent.stop` (execute), `agent.status`, `agent.list` (read); `conditions.recheck` (execute), `conditions.list`, `conditions.get` (read); `helpers.list`, `helpers.get` (read); `ledger.related` (read). Extensions of recorded operations: `documents.edit` change `append` (a paragraph after the selected one; WORKSHOP-01's own addition), `brain.ask` mode `choice` with `choices` (SERVICE-01 baseline, recorded extension), `ledger.navigate` destination `investigations` (recorded extension). All are private to this computer for cloud proposals; the reads are journal observers.

## Boundaries that hold

No second dispatcher, scheduler or data store; zero workers, models or native tools started by the loop itself; the budget's authority is enforced by the Kernel's scope checks, not by asking a model to behave; every step is recorded before it is interpreted; stale or changed inputs are refused, never merged; the live model column is filled only by the trial records in `build/agent01_ui/model_trial/` and says where they ran.

# AGENT-02 · the three mechanisms in one page

November 6, 2026 · UTC. Operator's summary; the details are in docs/CONTINUE_01.md, docs/MODEL_TURN_01.md and docs/FILES_ABOUT_01.md.

| What | Where | Operations and settings | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A running assignment continues in the resident Ledger service while Ledger is closed; the desktop takes it back | `workbench/agent_loop.py` (driver, lease_until, service_steps, authority columns; `pump`, `pause_all`), `workbench/host_service.py` (tick, Master Stop), `workbench/agent_qt.py` (release on close, adopt on open, Today) | `agent.step {id, driver?}`, `agent.release {id}` (new, execute), `agent.status` rows gain driver, lease_live, lease_until, service_steps; setting `agent.continue_when_closed` (default on) | `tests_integrated/test_agent_loop.py`, `tools/check_continue_ui.py`, `tools/check_continue_service.py` (the real service) |
| A document edit the model proposes for the open page is applied at once, highlighted, undoable | `workbench/model_turn.py`, `workbench/document_qt.py` (`apply_model_edit`, the glow), `workbench/shell2.py` (the APPLIED card), `workbench/documents.py` (`EDIT_ORIGINS`), `workbench/instruction_matrix.py` (`APPLIED`) | `documents.edit` origin `SLATE_MODEL` (edit only); readback `basis: MODEL_PROPOSAL_CHECKED_AND_APPLIED`, `model_used: true` | `tests_integrated/test_model_turn.py`, `tools/check_model_turn_ui.py`, build/agent02_ui/model_trial (live, build container) |
| Files about something: a findings page from Files and Ingress | `workbench/profile_files.py` (registered in `agent_profiles.py`), `agent_qt.assign_from_page` | `agent.assign` profile `files_about`; reads `receiving.status`, `files.find`, `ledger.browse`, `files.get` (four at most); writes `documents.create`, `documents.edit` append | `tests_integrated/test_profile_files.py`, `tools/check_files_about_ui.py` |

Rules that hold across all three: one dispatcher (the Kernel), no new scheduler, store or process; every step recorded before it is interpreted; Master Stop is the one kill switch; the desktop has priority over the service; only a page edit applies by itself; nothing claims acceptance.

# Graphite 0.2a5 · BOSS P10

Ten of the twenty BOSS implementation passes are in this build. The new route takes a collection from Ingress through project search, then turns a reviewed PDF table into a sheet and an editable report.

## P08 · Keep a model ready

Use **Brain → Use model** to activate a registered GGUF. Graphite checks the weight file at load and binds that check to the running worker and the file's identity. Each turn checks that identity before using the worker. The Brain view shows the effective context, backend and fallback reason when available. **Restore previous** uses the saved model handover record. Stop invalidates earlier launch and rollback requests.

A source question can reuse the prepared prompt budget when the same owner asks the exact same question with the same frozen evidence on the same worker. Graphite asks the runtime to reuse its single resident slot and reports reused tokens only when the runtime supplies that count. Another turn, changed evidence or a replaced worker makes the next preparation start cold. Source records and work history live with the project.

## P09 · Give a project its sources

1. Bring a folder in through **Intake** and review the sources in **References**. Choose **Index admitted sources** to make those files searchable.
2. Open **Project Desk → Project notes → Attach collection…** and pick the collection. **Open collection** brings it back for review. **Ask Graphite → Prepare evidence** finds matching indexed passages with their source locations.
3. Choose **Export collection** in References for a ZIP in Egress. It contains ordinarily named source files, a readable collection summary and a catalog of source and project relationships. The summary lists omitted material. The collection and its export are useful with the Brain off.

The native export view publishes the verified ZIP when the worker finishes. A caller using registered operations can publish the completed export with `references.volume.publish`.

## P10 · Make a checked report from a datasheet

1. Select an admitted source in **References → Read technical PDF**. Select the table region and open **Review table**. For an image-only page, use the PDF view's OCR first.
2. Compare the candidates with the original crop. Fix values and units, retain the conditions, and choose **Save reviewed sheet**. The saved sheet keeps the PDF page, extraction notes and the reviewed values.
3. In the sheet, choose **Calculate and write report…**. For example, name the input cells `voltage=B2` and `current=B3`, enter `voltage * current`, and request watts. Give dimensionless values the explicit unit `1`. A missing unit needs a decision before the calculation runs.
4. Open the result in **Documents**. Edit or export it as you would any other document. **Sheet** and **Source page** reopen the inputs. When a selected value changes, Graphite marks the report for recheck. **Recheck** writes a new report from the current sheet and keeps the earlier one.

The review works on a selected table region with a bounded row layout. OCR and unusual tables can leave entries for you to resolve. The report carries both the reviewed source values and any later sheet edits.

## What ran here

- The model protocol check exercised a cold turn, a matching reuse request, a changed weight file and Stop during an earlier launch request. Live GGUF reuse, Radeon performance and ThinkPad operation are pending.
- A local test collection went through real Ingress, review, indexing, project search and verified Egress export. The exported source bytes matched the admitted originals.
- A native Qt walkthrough opened a text PDF table, an image-only page with real OCR, the editable sheet and the report. Exact local arithmetic gave **2.4 W** from **12 V × 200 mA**. Changing the sheet to **250 mA** marked the old report for recheck. The next report gave **3 W**.

See [the walkthrough observations](P10_captures/P08_P10_OBSERVATIONS.json) and the [table review](P10_captures/Graphite_P10_PDF_Table.png) and [report](P10_captures/Graphite_P10_Report.png) captures.

P11 connects full native programs to the desk and brings the owner back to the same work after an explicit handoff.

# Graphite implementation campaign

Twenty passes. Governing master: Graphite Master Specification v5 BOSS.

Graphite 0.2a6.post1 revises Visual Pass 1 on the P01–P10 implementation. See [the five-reference visual review](BOSS_VISUAL_PASS_01_REVISION.md) and [the halfway release](BOSS_HALFWAY_P10.md). P11 is next.

## Latest owner decisions

- The head shows the full active workspace path as directly editable text, without a surrounding box.
- Programs entries and dropdown menu commands participate in contextual cascading actions, alongside work objects.
- Use twenty substantial implementation passes for the entire master specification.
- No automatic test run after each pass; batch related work and use a quick launch-and-use check. Extra testing requires a concrete failure or data-integrity concern. No new test suites by default.

## Verification policy

No automatic tests per pass. Batch related changes and perform one quick launch-and-use check. Skip new tests for cosmetic changes. Reuse a small existing check only when an actual failure or specific data-integrity concern warrants it. No routine full suites, all-case reruns, model sweeps, or assertion-count targets.

## Passes

### P01 Build the native BOSS shell

Unify the current shell styling around charcoal, copper-orange, readable terminal lettering, restrained green signals, and intentional manga or ASCII spaces. Retire default cursive and reserved logo or corner-cat space. Provide Illustrated, ASCII, and Clean appearance choices without changing capabilities. Preserve reading scale, keyboard focus, reduced motion, and the owner's saved preferences.

Complete when: The actual Qt application opens in the new visual direction. Decoration can be reduced or removed, and working text, menus, files, and exports remain usable. Ship real widgets and separate artwork assets rather than a screenshot as the interface.

Dependencies: Supplied baseline.
Source anchors: shell2.py; reading_preferences.py; reading_profile.py; desk_qt.py; pane_qt.py; programs_qt.py.
State: IMPLEMENTED. Owner-host qualification remains pending.

Native charcoal/copper/green Qt chrome; optional Illustrated/ASCII/Clean ornament; named Work/Programs/System head, three writing modes, mirrored file/instrument panes. Stored legacy keys and reading preferences retained.

### P02 Make location and working objects coherent

Replace the old header title cluster with one borderless editable full path for the active workspace item. Support Ctrl+L, copying, Enter to navigate, and Escape to restore. Keep the complete address available without substituting an ellipsis. Extend current artifact bindings so selection, revision, location, and source identity stay consistent when switching work. Treat a database record or unsaved item truthfully instead of inventing a file path.

Complete when: Opening a file, changing tabs, navigating to a folder, and cancelling path editing preserve the right location and work. Programs and System remain reachable. Related artifacts can share a working surface without losing their individual identities.

Dependencies: P01.
Source anchors: shell2.py TopBar and PathBar; qt_app.py active_path; finder_qt.py; universal_viewer_qt.py; documents.py; object_context.py.
State: IMPLEMENTED. Owner-host qualification remains pending.

Full borderless path with Ctrl+L, Enter navigation and Escape restore; real file/folder paths and stable internal addresses for records and open unsaved work. Deferred command routes bind working identity, selection and revision.

### P03 Extend cascades to programs and menu commands

Give Programs entries and dropdown menu commands their own contextual actions. Ordinary clicks keep their familiar action; right-click and a keyboard or touch-accessible equivalent reveal relevant capabilities, parameters, source inspection, or a route into a chain. Bind those actions to the current artifact and supported operation. Extend Graphite's menus first and use actual application interfaces for native-program integration.

Complete when: A program entry, a dropdown command, and a selected object each expose useful contextual actions. The same operation carries the same target and revision checks through every route. Menus remain within the display and have predictable Escape, focus, and continuation behavior.

Dependencies: P02.
Source anchors: context_menu.py Target Entry providers and Router; programs_qt.py; menus2.py; hatch_qt.py; engineering_kernel.py; explore.py.
State: IMPLEMENTED. Owner-host qualification remains pending.

The contextual router handles program entries, native QMenu commands and contextual menu rows. Original QActions stay the ordinary click route. Secondary presses cannot activate an underlying menu action. Existing providers expose captured-work modifications.

### P04 Connect chains previews and the shared writing strip

Build on the existing staC chain builder to retain an editable sequence across menu openings, bind its inputs, preview its effects, run supported steps, and inspect the actual output. Consolidate Assistant, Terminal, and Log around the existing writing line; retain search through commands and keyboard access. Keep natural language and supported staC available through Assistant. Preserve real pause, stop, and process controls.

Complete when: The new desk can complete a real small chain and open its resulting artifact. A preview remains distinct from execution. Useful procedures can be retained through existing method records, and ordinary computer use still works with no model loaded.

Dependencies: P03.
Source anchors: chain_menu.py; stac/; context_menu.py; typebar_qt.py; console_qt.py; log_qt.py; qt_master_stop.py; system_menu_qt.py.
State: IMPLEMENTED. Owner-host qualification remains pending.

Retained chain tray, clickable stage prefixes, original cascade builder, read-only Kernel previews, source fingerprints, shared-strip editing, actual CSV and receipt saving, and existing kept-method menu. Changed sources refuse reuse; capped 200-row results cannot be exported as an apparently complete sheet.

### P05 Deliver the ThinkPad profile and Vulkan worker

Extend the existing model manager rather than add a competing inference system. Detect CPU, Radeon, usable memory, driver, Mesa, Vulkan, and runtime capabilities. Deliver or reproducibly build a pinned compatible Vulkan worker and its dependency route. Keep GGUF registration and a compatible CPU fallback. Show the effective backend and offload state from actual worker information.

Complete when: Graphite can configure and launch the supported Vulkan path on compatible hardware, preserve the current CPU route, and explain unavailable acceleration. Driver and firmware delivery uses maintained packages and retained notices.

Dependencies: P02.
Source anchors: brain_runtime.py; local_brain.py; brain_worker.py; model_settings.py; model_settings_qt.py; hardware_settings_qt.py; runtime manifests.
State: IMPLEMENTED. Owner-host GPU/model qualification remains pending.

Pinned Vulkan worker, actual host profile, saved launch preferences, observed-offload readback and one CPU fallback are delivered. The cloud reports no physical Vulkan device. Read docs/THINKPAD_VULKAN_P05.md.


### P06 Coordinate shared memory and foreground work

Implement the traffic cop through existing work ownership, agenda, worker controls, and model lifecycle. Account for weights, attention state, temporary allocations, CPU evidence, tools, and graphics in the one system memory pool. Prefer useful supported GPU inference while CPU preparation remains responsive. Keep priority, queue ordering, CPU niceness, and actual preemption limits distinct. Adapt resource containment to GPU virtual-address behavior.

Complete when: Foreground interaction can take priority at supported boundaries. Memory pressure, cancellation, failure, and fallback retain findings and correct worker ownership. The installed 64 GB is never presented as 64 GB of guaranteed GPU allocation.

Dependencies: P05.
Source anchors: agenda.py; agent_loop.py; local_brain.py; brain_worker.py; worker_boundary.py; job_priority.py; operations.py; host_service.py.
State: IMPLEMENTED. Shared-bandwidth, thermal and owner-host responsiveness qualification remain pending.

Resource admission now uses the existing queued worker and durable job record; foreground priority, model serialization and owned memory guards are delivered. Read docs/TRAFFIC_COP_P06.md.


### P07 Prepare useful evidence on the CPU

Join retrieval, indexing, typed extraction, exact arithmetic, units, dependency relationships, and relevant tool selection into intelligent data arrangement. Build a compact current evidence packet before a useful model turn, while letting model interpretation identify additional material or calculations. Preserve source conditions and unresolved meanings. Keep deterministic correctness separate from interpretation and engineering applicability.

Complete when: A model question can use observed calculations and current source references, retrieve omitted prose when needed, and identify the next consequential question. Changed inputs invalidate the affected preparation instead of quietly reusing a stale answer.

Dependencies: P02, P06.
Source anchors: knowledge_service.py; reference_service.py; math_service.py; math_backend.py; reason_graph.py; typed_artifacts.py; tool_selection.py; conditions.py.
State: IMPLEMENTED. Live model interpretation and owner-host qualification remain pending.

Ask Graphite prepares revision-bound source evidence and exact arithmetic before inference. The model receives
results within their declared conditions and supplied dependencies. Read or focus an omitted passage from the
same frozen sources. See docs/INTELLIGENT_DATA_P07.md.

### P08 Complete context cache and model lifecycle

Manage effective token budgets, prepared prefixes, eviction, streaming, worker identity, replacement, and rollback coherently. Verify model identity at appropriate lifecycle boundaries without needlessly hashing all weights every turn. Reuse established inference methods only where the selected model, backend, and pinned runtime support them: suitable precision, microbatching, attention, prefix reuse, speculation, or expert placement. Treat each as a compatible candidate rather than an obligatory imported engine.

Complete when: Model replacement preserves knowledge, temporary state is correctly invalidated or reconstructed, and stopped work stays stopped. Effective settings and the reason for fallback are inspectable. Actual usefulness and resource observations guide configuration; no promised speed multiplier or parameter-count guarantee is inserted.

Dependencies: P05, P06, P07.
Source anchors: local_brain.py; brain_runtime.py; brain_worker.py; model_turn.py; model_settings.py; tool_selection.py; current runtime interfaces.
State: IMPLEMENTED. Live model and owner-host qualification remain pending.

The resident worker binds load verification to the weight file's identity, reads back effective settings and invalidates old launch requests on Stop. Matching source turns can ask the existing runtime for single-slot prompt reuse.

### P09 Make the material collection useful and portable

Complete the file and collection experience around real locations, project associations, incoming material, source identities, local search, and readable exports. Preserve originals, revisions, Ingress, Egress, Trash, and established working-copy behavior. Index permitted project material without loading the whole collection into each model turn. Keep files, machine resources, and settings directly usable by the owner and assistant.

Complete when: A supplied collection can be brought in, found, opened, inspected, and exported with its relationships. Missing private project files remain a named input requirement. Records and source material remain useful without the conversation or a model.

Dependencies: P02, P04, P07.
Source anchors: files_service.py; files_qt.py; browse.py; finder_qt.py; receiving.py; working_copies.py; cabinet.py; knowledge_service.py.
State: IMPLEMENTED.

Project notes attach admitted collections. Evidence preparation searches their index with source locators and current revisions. The verified export includes ordinary filenames and a readable relationship catalog.

### P10 Complete documents sheets and PDF work

Finish the everyday artifact chain: read or OCR a PDF where needed, extract tables with units and conditions, build an editable sheet, calculate through suitable local tools, and produce an editable document or printable output. Preserve selected text during edits, formatting and undo where supported, numerical meaning, source pages, and unresolved extraction questions. Use mature document and spreadsheet engines.

Complete when: Datasheet to sheet to calculation to report is a real route through saved artifacts. Owner and assistant can alternate edits. A changed extracted value leads to the appropriate recheck; a scanned table or missing unit receives explicit handling rather than a fabricated value.

Dependencies: P04, P07, P09.
Source anchors: documents.py; document_qt.py; pdf_service.py; reference_service.py; office_service.py; office_runtime.py; math_office.py; office_math_runtime.py.
State: IMPLEMENTED.

Reviewed PDF table rows create an editable sheet with units, conditions and provenance. Exact calculations write editable reports from named cells. Changed inputs mark affected reports for recheck. Image-only pages use the PDF OCR route before table review.

### P11 Make full native programs part of the desk

Provide dependable native application launching, focus, ordinary windows, clipboard, file dialogs, and return to Graphite within a maintained Linux session. Connect compact work views through supported APIs, scripts, or explicit file handoffs. Keep full Blender, browsers, mail, office, and other installed applications reachable even where specialized automation is incomplete. Preserve manual use with the assistant off.

Complete when: The owner can operate a full application, return to the same task, and retain the actual saved or shared state. An explicit handoff reports its continuity guarantees. Installation is distinguishable from assistant-callable capability; universal foreign-window embedding is not required.

Dependencies: P02, P09.
Source anchors: native_sessions.py; desktop_services.py; workspace_services.py; universal_viewer_qt.py; explore.py; launcher.py; LS_XSESSION.sh.
State: PLANNED.

### P12 Follow edits across artifacts and applications

Unify revision and selection bindings across source excerpts, documents, tables, scenes, reports, and investigations. Connect source-to-result inspection, before and after, supported undo, staleness, and recovery. Refresh actual state after native application work. A preview, proposal, completed edit, and saved export retain separate meanings. Let related objects share the surface without freezing every task into equal columns.

Complete when: A manual correction reaches affected dependent work, an assistant change is inspectable, and returning from a native program reconciles the current artifact. A compatible retained method can be rebound to new material without borrowing old input values or execution claims.

Source anchors: typed_artifacts.py; reason_graph.py; object_context.py; change_sets.py; conditions.py; working_copies.py; investigation_service.py; context_menu.py.

### P13 Generalize the resident assignment loop

Extend the existing durable loop beyond its narrow built-in profiles. Carry an arbitrary supported assignment through relevant tool selection, incremental planning, actual execution, observation, revised interpretation, and a useful next action. Preserve goals, findings, attempted approaches, unresolved conditions, and budgets outside the context window. Continue permitted long work when the presentation window closes and resume coherently after restart.

Complete when: A supplied unfamiliar assignment can use supported tools and leave real work, an appropriate specific question, or a precise condition preventing progress. Pause, Stop, failure recovery, and completion reflect the actual worker. A completed calculation is not automatically a completed assignment.

Source anchors: agent_loop.py; agent_profiles.py; investigations.py; investigation_service.py; continuing_work.py; host_service.py; tool_selection.py; model_turn.py.
State: PLANNED.

### P14 Obtain missing abilities and retain useful tools

Discover installed software and existing supported operations before inventing a helper. When an assignment lacks an ability, establish an authorized acquisition or integration route, use mature software as a base, and return to the original task. Add dynamic helper development with inspectable inputs, outputs, dependencies, limits, and execution records. Consider retaining or promoting a recurring useful tool when the need appears again.

Complete when: A genuine capability gap can become a usable installed tool, adapter, or helper within the assignment's authority. Repeated need reuses or improves that work. Programs and menus expose substantial capabilities without flooding the launcher with every internal helper.

Source anchors: tool_atlas.py; tool_inventory.py; tool_selection.py; helpers.py; checked_methods.py; worker_tasks.py; package_service.py; integration_tools.py.
State: PLANNED.

### P15 Connect web correspondence and scheduling

Add useful web research, authenticated browsing, email understanding, mailbox operations, evidence-based correspondence, calendars, and commitment-aware scheduling through maintained integrations. Preserve thread identities, dates, accounts, sources, relevant permissions, and external acknowledgements. Include prepared online forms, record reconciliation, and clean paper letters where the task needs them. Keep imported material and local preparation usable offline; connect selected services for actual external work.

Complete when: Graphite can complete an authorized research or secretary chain with real artifacts and clear external state. Drafting, sending, acknowledgement, and delivery remain distinct. Reconcile an uncertain response before retrying. Obtain missing intent or access only when it is genuinely missing; a webpage or email does not grant new authority.

Source anchors: research_service.py; knowledge_service.py; reference_service.py; office_service.py; documents.py; agenda.py; existing browser routes and new supported service adapters.

### P16 Complete specialist and creative work routes

Extend the common interfaces and useful specialized adapters for engineering, CAD and Blender, compilers and software repair, images, audio and video, network investigation, translation, and demanding records work. Preserve native project formats and let one program produce inputs to another. Build task-relevant helpers when needed. Deliver roughly thirty programs' worth of useful ability through mature applications and supported operations rather than thirty rewritten applications.

Complete when: Representative complex assignments leave editable deliverables and source-linked results across installed tools. Geometry, electrical assumptions, calculations, and external project facts are assessed through their actual sources and tools. An engineering uncertainty or missing private dataset is retained explicitly rather than converted to an unsupported confidence percentage.

Dependencies: P10, P11, P12, P13, P14, P15.
Source anchors: Existing engineering and office adapters; kicad_tools.py; spice_tools.py; hdl_tools.py; first_stage_tools.py; network_watch.py; native_sessions.py; new task-driven adapters.
State: PLANNED.

### P17 Make improvement durable and recoverable

Connect observed friction and recurring work to a useful improvement process. Distinct observer, builder, and reviewer responsibilities can share one inference service and durable store. Retain candidates, compare actual artifacts or behavior where necessary, curate preferred methods, activate suitable changes within standing authority, and recover code and data together. Preserve failed attempts with their conditions and learn useful host configuration from ordinary work.

Complete when: A recurring limitation can lead to a retained method or software improvement with a clear basis, previous working path, and recovery behavior. An adopted change does not erase useful records or expand its own authority. Model replacement preserves the accumulated knowledge. Three cooperative roles do not require three resident LLMs.

Dependencies: P06, P08, P13, P14, P16.
Source anchors: helpers.py; checked_methods.py; study_service.py; experiment_runtime.py; reason_graph.py; update_service.py; existing worker and evidence stores.
State: PLANNED.

### P18 Converge the full journeys and capability coverage

Use the thirty-five assignment cases as a coverage and integration ledger, including all five four-application chains. Reuse observations accumulated while implementing the capabilities. Close missing handoffs, recovery, changed-input behavior, and ordinary manual operation across the same desk. Separate software completion, supported uncertainty, a missing input, and hardware or service qualification. Finish portable partial and whole-collection exports.

Complete when: Each case has an implementation owner and a stated capability route; delivered journeys point to real outputs or the precise remaining input or qualification. There is no automatic rerun of all thirty-five scenarios. New activity is limited to resolving an actual unestablished boundary or observed defect.

Dependencies: P12, P15, P16, P17.
Source anchors: All implemented artifact, application, assignment, method, and evidence boundaries; the case coverage ledger in this campaign.
State: PLANNED.

### P19 Build the maintained Debian delivery

Finish the minimal maintained Debian desktop profile, Graphite session, full native application access, bootable USB image, supported installation, persistence, and recovery. Include the compatible driver, firmware, runtime, application, and offline dependency route. Keep model acquisition and any separately licensed components explicit. Preserve the ordinary application upgrade route while delivering the complete system.

Complete when: A reproducible image or supported build recipe, installer, offline cache layout, dependency identities, notices, and recovery instructions are available. The system uses maintained Debian components; the project is not required to fork the Linux kernel. User data and supported native formats survive upgrades.

Dependencies: P05, P11, P13, P15, P18.
Source anchors: INSTALL_LS.py; INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh; START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh; LS_XSESSION.sh; package_service.py; deployment and release tools.
State: PLANNED.

### P20 Qualify the ThinkPad and ship the complete release

Collect the missing owner-host observations through normal use: install and session startup, display and input, full applications, actual Radeon backend and model, useful memory headroom, responsiveness, stopping, and continuation. Complete recovery and upgrade readback, reconcile the requirement and case ledgers, and ship the usable release, source, guides, and installer volumes at or below 15,000,000 bytes each.

Complete when: The final handoff states what is implemented, actually observed, and still blocked. Preserve the free-of-charge local core and existing rights and upstream notices. Owner-host acceptance is closed only by the actual machine observations. A missing laptop can leave that qualification pending while independent packaging continues.

Dependencies: P08, P17, P18, P19.
Source anchors: Current release registry and manifests; package_graphite.py; package_release_parts.py; existing install, backup, runtime, and readiness entry points.
State: PLANNED.

## Completion policy

A pass closes on delivered usable implementation and the relevant observed boundary, not a plan, screenshot, test count, or model assertion. Record live-model, native-application, account, and owner-host qualification separately. P20 owner-host acceptance remains open without the actual machine.

# Graphite 0.2a1 · the native BOSS desk

This is the first implementation checkpoint of the approved twenty-pass campaign.
P01–P04 are implemented on the supplied Graphite 0.1 native source. P05 is next.
The campaign and governing BOSS master are included in this project.

## Use it

The head is the full address of the active work, directly on its dark background.
Press Ctrl+L to select it, type or paste a path, then Enter. Escape restores the
current address. Relative paths start at the active file's folder. Folder paths
open the existing Finder; ordinary files open in the real viewer. Saved document
records use `graphite://documents/…`; open views without disk files have internal
addresses. They are not invented filesystem paths. The complete address remains
copyable and horizontally scrolls while editing rather than becoming an ellipsis.

Work opens the existing command families. Programs opens the actual capability
list. System opens the existing Game, owned Stop, process priorities, queue and
session controls. Corner logos and the peeking cat no longer reserve desk space.
The left trees are Files, Machine and Settings; their internal saved keys are
unchanged. Talk, Activity and Context keep the existing right-column functions.

Assistant, Terminal and Log share the bottom writing strip. Assistant still
accepts natural-language assignments and explicit staC on Ctrl+Enter. Terminal
uses the configured Debian shell. Log retains its event and network views.
Search stays available through Ctrl+K, a `?` prefix and the Work menu. Console
sizes remain in Work → Arrange → Console and the existing shortcuts.

Work → Arrange → Desk artwork offers Illustrated, ASCII and Clean. The illustrated
panel is a separate original SVG asset rendered by Qt; artwork never becomes part
of a document export. Reading size and reduced-motion settings remain available.
This checkpoint introduces no continuously running animation.

## Contextual commands

Ordinary clicks still open the original capability or run the original action.
Right-click a Programs entry or dropdown command to inspect it or open its
contextual operations. When a working passage or file is selected, the secondary
menu offers commands for that captured object. The existing document and file
providers supply those operations, including their revision checks. Menu, Shift+F10
and the existing contextual keyboard routes remain available.

A secondary press is claimed before a QMenu can activate an underlying action.
Deferred interface commands check the active identity and selection again. Saved
document revisions and selected Files entries are checked before those commands
run. This adds no alternate authorization path and no second dispatcher.

## Constructed chains

Choose “Build on the desk…” in a chain cascade. The tray stays beneath the work
after the menu closes. Each stage chip reopens the builder from that prefix.
Preview uses `language.parse` and the existing read-only `language.run` through
the Kernel. It records source fingerprints before and after calculation. Run
shows that inspected result in the existing console. Edit in strip uses the same
shared input; it does not add another place for ordinary assistant conversation.

Save sheet writes a new CSV under `Files/Slate/Chains` and a JSON receipt beside
it. The receipt retains the program, source operations and fingerprints, seed
binding, row count and output path. Inputs are not overwritten. A changed source
invalidates the old preview. A result at a detected source-view bound or the existing 200-row pipeline cap cannot
be exported as an apparently complete sheet. The visible table displays at most
100 returned rows and 20 columns; this display bound is stated in its tooltip.
Later full-data application work remains P10; this checkpoint does not silently
relax the existing pipeline bounds.

Keep method uses the existing named plain-text chain menu. This retains a useful
method for another input; it is not a claim of model training or general learning.

## What was observed

A brief native Qt offscreen walkthrough opened the desk, entered a real file path
containing spaces, cancelled a path edit, opened contextual routes from Programs
and a dropdown, calculated stock shortages, saved an actual derived CSV and receipt,
and refused to reuse a preview after its source changed. A document formatting
operation preserved the page words; a deferred interface command refused a changed
selection. The desk also opened at 1366×768 and the three artwork choices changed
only the ornament. Captures and a concise observation note accompany this build.

No automated unit suites, LLM trials or GPU benchmarks were run for this checkpoint.
Offscreen Qt does not establish physical keyboard/pointer feel, display comfort or
ThinkPad acceptance. Existing historical evidence describes the supplied baseline;
it is not a new acceptance result for the redesigned interface.

## Continue

P05 adds the ThinkPad hardware profile and compatible Vulkan worker. P06–P08 then
coordinate shared memory, CPU evidence preparation and the model/context lifecycle.
The current llama.cpp path is still the baseline CPU runtime. It has not been
relabelled as GPU acceleration. P09–P20 retain the rest of the approved destination.
The owner has already authorized continuing the campaign with minimal checking.
