# Graphite worksheet visual review

The Workshop Stock mockup depicts a worksheet mid-task. The first running screenshot was an editable calculation report. To separate the design differences from the different work, the comparison below uses the same real ODS workbook in P10 and in the revised desktop. The example rows belong to the walkthrough.

## Screen comparison

| Area | P10 on the same workbook | What the mockup calls for and how the revision handles it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Whole screen | Three panes already line up between the full-width bands. | Keep the three panes and make the work easy to follow from the source at left through the table and into the result at right. The two outer panes still share the same width and sizing rules. |
| Background | A cooler graphite gray under darker head and foot bands. | Use near-black charcoal with warm gray rules and cream text. Keep enough separation between the background, table header and raised menus to read each surface. |
| Head | The actual path is editable and the three menus are already at the right. | Keep the real path on the band. Use a thin amber rule and a character-cell grid beside Programs. Work and System have ordinary words. |
| Colors | Muted copper selection, cool text and green monitor readings. | Give amber the active row, cascade, route and Run chain. Give green the verified preview and source state. Include words and row marks alongside the colors. |
| Lettering | The path is mono. The sheet, pane tabs and most labels are sans. | Set the worksheet data, pane tabs, and cascade in IBM Plex Mono. Long-form document reading has its own font and size. |
| Left tabs | Files, Machine and Settings already exist. | Keep those three destinations with sharper lettering and a short underline. |
| File tree | The logical cabinet shows the Concern categories. The workbook's siblings are absent. | Put the actual containing folder and its files above the cabinet while the worksheet is active. Put the active workbook first and mark it with amber. Keep the underlying cabinet reachable. |
| File icons | The logical tree is mostly words with branch lines. | Add one-line ASCII type marks to the worksheet folder. The filenames and accessible file types carry the meaning. |
| Left margin and Trash | Space beneath the cabinet and a pinned Trash. | Add a small bracket sketch drawn with keyboard characters for the stock worksheet. Fit it above the existing Trash, which keeps its real count and drop target. |
| Workspace heading | The filename repeats in the address, breadcrumb, viewer heading and tabs. | Give the worksheet one title and a line that counts the selection. File views holds the original sheet, Hex, Details, Ask and Investigate. |
| Full spreadsheet | The viewer shows its normal file actions. | Put Full spreadsheet by the title. It opens the file in the system's associated application when there is one. |
| Sheet headings | A, B, C and D sit above a grid containing the heading row as data. | Make Part, Required, Available and Unit the headers in Worksheet. This is the existing staC data view of the file. The original sheet view remains reachable through File views. |
| Table width and density | The small table sits in the upper left with a separate filter field. | Stretch a small number of columns across the working area, right-align quantities and use fine grid lines. Wide tables can scroll. The original sheet view still offers sort and text filter. |
| Selection | The viewer can focus a cell. | Select whole rows, including nonadjacent rows, with native Qt keyboard and pointer selection. Amber and a greater-than mark identify the selected rows. |
| Cascading commands | The established chain menu starts from a file or existing chain. | Open a cascade from the current rows. In the stock example, choose Calculate, Required - available, then Keep positive. The named stock route appears when those columns are present. Any supported table can preview its selected rows or copy them as staC. |
| Connection from selection | Selection and chain are separate visual surfaces. | Draw an amber trace from visible selected rows to the tray and mark the chip and Run control positions. The trace follows selection, scrolling and layout. The actual popup remains a Qt menu. |
| Constructed chain | A general chain tray can appear beneath the active workspace. | Stage the actual bound program beneath the worksheet. The chips show selected rows, subtraction, filter and output. Each chip can put its prefix into the shared typing line. The menu retains the existing method and console routes. |
| Run and output | A chain can preview, show its result in the console or save a CSV. | Put Run chain at the end of the route. It uses the inspected result and writes a new CSV and a source receipt. The worksheet stays open so the result can be read next to its inputs. |
| Right tabs | Talk, Activity and Context. | On a worksheet use Preview, Activity and Sources. Talk is reachable from the preview and the typing line. Ordinary views get their normal inspector back. |
| Preview card | Activity and Timeline occupy the right while a general chain preview lives in the tray. | Show the real result at right with two columns for the stock recipe. Print the unit beside each amount. Show a total only when the contributing units agree. |
| Ready and stale | The general chain records its sources and checks them before use. | Bring the current-source state to the preview. The selected sheet and source digest travel with the program. Changing the file clears readiness, and a run or save rechecks the digest. |
| Panel artwork | A general illustrated header or text treatment exists on Today. | Put the original woman at a CRT below a ready result. Illustrated shows the halftone. ASCII renders the portrait in character cells. Clean removes both illustrations. The actual source label supplies the state. |
| Bottom strip | Assistant, Terminal and Log already share the line with real resource monitors. | Add compact prompt and log glyphs and the amber seam. Keep the readouts live. The mockup's sample ready badge is expressed by the worksheet's actual verified state. |
| Decoration and fit | Dock widths, text size and shortcuts are part of the running desk. | Use a static, sharp treatment with actual controls. Menus can move or flip to stay in the available screen area. The app uses its real path, files, tooltips, focus and size rules. |

## How to see it

1. Put a CSV, ODS or XLSX file in the workspace's **Files** folder or a subfolder. Open it through the viewer or enter its full path in the head.
2. In **Worksheet**, select rows. Use Ctrl to select rows apart from one another. Right-click the selection or choose **Row commands**.
3. With numeric Required and Available columns and Part and Unit headings, choose **Calculate → Required - available → Keep positive**. The chain previews on the right. Use **Run chain** to save the derived CSV and its receipt in **Files/Slate/Chains**.
4. **File views** opens the original workbook views. **Full spreadsheet** hands the file to the desktop's associated application. **Reload source** reads current bytes and starts a fresh selection. Set the ornament under **Work → Arrange → Desk artwork**.

The result uses Graphite's bounded file view and existing staC runner. The worksheet route is for files inside **Files**. The editable Office working-copy and P10 PDF-to-report routes have their own controls. Full application handoff and return are P11.

## Observed in Qt

The same workbook opened in both versions. The revised desktop selected Bracket A and Shade, opened the three native cascading menus, and previewed **40 pcs + 22 pcs = 62 pcs**. Run chain saved the two rows and a receipt bound to the source. A change to the workbook bytes refused the old program and cleared the ready state. The preview also opened at 1366 × 768, and Illustrated, ASCII and Clean were exercised. The cascade image places the visible Qt popups over the window capture at their actual positions.

| Capture | What to inspect |
| --- | --- |
| [P10 workbook](BOSS_worksheet_captures/Graphite_P10_Workshop_Before.png) | The old header, table and Activity placement with the same file. |
| [Worksheet and cascade](BOSS_worksheet_captures/Graphite_Workshop_Cascade.png) | Row selection, connected commands, staged chain and live result. |
| [Compact view](BOSS_worksheet_captures/Graphite_Workshop_Compact.png) | The same working surface at 1366 × 768. |

These are offscreen Qt observations. Display comfort and the system's external spreadsheet launcher await the ThinkPad.

# Work that continues while Ledger is closed (HATCH AGENT-02 · WI-A)

November 6, 2026 · UTC. The owner approved the next pass on 2026-11-05 ("Next pass approved") for the three items named at the end of AGENT-01; this is the first of them. Standing authorities: the Program Specification for Claude v1.0 and the Creative Implementation Commission v2.1 (no second dispatcher, shell runner, scheduler or data store; Master Stop is the one kill switch; never claim acceptance). Owner decision D19 holds: Slate acts freely inside an assignment and asks only for originals, network and outside effects.

## What the owner sees

An assignment Slate is working on no longer has to stop when Ledger closes. With the Ledger service running (Hatch ▸ Ledger services On; the desktop is attached to it) and the setting **Continue assignments while Ledger is closed** on (Settings ▸ Slate ▸ Assignments; on by default), closing Ledger hands the running assignment to the service, which keeps taking one step at a time. When Ledger opens again:

- Today's Waiting card says what happened: *While Ledger was closed, Slate took N steps on “…” · now done* (or *now running*, *now needs you*, *now paused*), with the word **inspect** (the investigation sheet) or **resume** when it waits or was paused; a paused one says why, as the AGENT-01 paused line does (*now paused (Master Stop)*, *now paused (The Ledger service stopped)*). The line stays for 24 hours after the assignment last changed.
- If the work is still running, the window takes it back about 1.5 s after it opens; from then on it steps at the window's own pace again. If a window that ended without handing the work over (a crash) left its 20-second lease behind, the reopened window looks again the moment that lease runs out and takes the work back itself (at most three such looks, so a second window that really is driving the work is left alone).
- While the service holds an assignment, the Work block's doing-now line begins *in the Ledger service ·*.

With the setting off, or with no Ledger service (the in-process desktop), closing pauses the assignment as in AGENT-01 (*Ledger closed*) and Today offers to resume it. Master Stop pauses every assignment, on both sides. When the service itself stops (Off, Reboot, shutdown), its own Master Stop on the way out pauses what it was carrying with the reason *The Ledger service stopped*; Today offers to resume those.

## How it works (no new scheduler, store or process)

The record is the AGENT-01 `agent_assignments` row with four added columns (an additive, idempotent `ALTER TABLE` in `agent_loop.ensure`): `driver` (`desktop`, `service`, or empty when released), `lease_until`, `service_steps` and `authority` (what the owner granted the work for the service's steps: the read and execute scopes, paths, tools and mode of the principal that assigned it, narrowed at hand-over to what the releasing principal holds). The step is the AGENT-01 `agent.step`, with an optional `driver` argument.

**The lease rule** (written in `workbench/agent_loop.py`'s docstring):

- A step by the desktop always proceeds and takes the lease (`driver` desktop, `lease_until` now + 20 s). The owner's desktop has priority, so reopening Ledger takes the work back.
- A step by the service proceeds only when no desktop lease is live; otherwise it is refused with `ASSIGNMENT_DRIVEN_BY_DESKTOP`.
- Every step renews the stepping driver's lease (`LEASE_SECONDS = 20`). A step the service takes adds one to `service_steps`, and its recorded inputs carry `{"driver": "service"}`, so the investigation sheet says who took each step.
- Nothing steps a PAUSED, WAITING or finished assignment, whichever driver asks.

**The hand-over.** `agent.release {id}` clears the driver and the lease (a READY assignment becomes RUNNING, because the owner asked for it to run; PAUSED, WAITING and finished ones are refused). The desktop's close (`qt_app.closeEvent`) calls it on every running assignment when the window is attached to the service (`ledger_bridge.kernel.is_host_client`) and the setting reads on (`ledger.settings.effective`); an assignment that cannot be handed over is paused instead.

**The service's side.** The resident service's existing 5 s loop already calls `Coordinator.tick_agenda`, which runs `continuing_work.pump` in its one daemon thread. That same thread now also calls `agent_loop.pump(kernel)`: one step each, as driver service, for every RUNNING assignment of any owner whose desktop lease is not live, at most eight per tick, with the owner's principal reduced to read and execute (never approve or candidate) and to the authority recorded on the assignment (`agent_loop.owner_principal`), kept inside the operator's ceiling by the same rule as the host's own delegation (`host_ipc.delegation`). So a command-line, MCP or JSONL caller that assigns and releases work never gains the desktop operator's paths through the service; the desktop owner keeps its own. (A record from before the column steps with the operator's paths only when its owner is the desktop owner, and with the Principal defaults for any other identity.) It does nothing when the setting is off, work is held (`work_trail.execution_held`) or the service is closing, and it checks all three again under the dispatch lock before every single step: Master Stop holds work before it takes that lock, so a batch already under way ends at the step in flight, and so does one under way when the owner turns the setting off or the service begins to shut down (`pump(kernel, guard=dispatch_lock, stop=closing.is_set)`). It holds the service's dispatch lock around each single step (so a desktop request never interleaves with one), and never raises: a step's own failure lands in that assignment's reason; anything unexpected becomes WAITING with *The Ledger service could not step it: …*. `Coordinator.master_stop` calls `agent_loop.pause_all` before it cancels jobs.

**The setting.** `agent.continue_when_closed` (boolean, default on, Slate ▸ Assignments, project private, owner only) is stored in the workspace's Kernel settings table (`ledger.agent.continue_when_closed`), where both consumers read it: the service on every tick (`agent_loop.continue_when_closed`; a row that is not a boolean reads as off) and the desktop at close (`agent_qt.continue_setting`). It is the 43rd setting; the 42 prior definitions are byte-identical (digest `c3126ee2…`); the single-key Set route is used, and the 17-key batch enum is unchanged.

## Operations, recorded

- **Added:** `agent.release {id}` (execute) → `{assignment, next}`; private to this computer for cloud proposals (`stacy_control.CLOUD_PRIVATE`); not a journal observer. Registry: 714 operations, 112 job tools.
- **Extended:** `agent.step` gained the optional `driver` (`desktop` | `service`, default `desktop`), a recorded extension of an AGENT-01 operation.
- **Status rows** (`agent.status`, `agent.list`) gained `driver`, `lease_live`, `lease_until` (when the live lease ends; empty when none is live) and `service_steps`.

## Decisions taken for the register

1. **The desktop has priority** (D19: the owner acts freely; the window the owner is looking at is the owner's own hand). A desktop step is never refused for a service lease; the service yields to a live desktop lease, and a reopened, attached window adopts running work.
2. **A 20-second lease**, renewed by every step: four service ticks or eighty desktop ticks. Long enough that the service never steps between two desktop ticks, short enough that work left by a crashed window resumes in the service within half a minute.
3. **Default on.** The owner asked for work that continues; the setting is the one switch to keep the AGENT-01 behaviour (pause on close).
4. **Service shutdown pauses with its own words** (*The Ledger service stopped*), not *Master Stop*, because Off and Reboot are not the kill switch; both run the same Master Stop path.
5. **Master Stop on the desktop is unchanged** (`qt_master_stop` keeps `driver.pause_all('Master Stop')`); the attached desktop then asks the service's Master Stop, which pauses everything else, READY assignments and other owners' included.
6. **The service acts with no more than the owner granted** (Commission v2.1: no new execution authority). The authority is recorded on the assignment when it is assigned and narrowed when it is handed over, rather than rebuilt from the identity, because the identity alone cannot tell the desktop operator from a command-line caller with the same name.

## Evidence

- `tests_integrated/test_agent_loop.py` (24 tests): the lease both ways, release, the pump to DONE on a numbers assignment with the setting on, nothing with it off or held, the pump's own failure words, `pause_all` across owners, the new status fields, an AGENT-01 table gaining the columns once; and from the independent review: the service steps with no more authority than the owner granted (a non-operator caller's assignment keeps the Principal default paths; release by a narrower principal narrows; the ceiling and read+execute bound whatever is recorded), the hold, the setting and the closing flag end a batch at the step in flight, a reopened window takes back work a crashed window's lease held once that lease runs out, and Today's line says why a paused assignment paused.
- `tools/check_continue_ui.py` (offscreen Qt, launchers held; `is_host_client` patched True on the window's Kernel for the close and for the adopt call only; the pump run in-process): 11 checks, captures at 1920×1200 and 1366×768, report `build/agent02_ui/continue/continue-ui.json`.
- `tools/check_continue_service.py` (no Qt; a real run of the resident process, started exactly as `host_client.ensure` starts it, in a disposable profile): the assignment released through the client reaches DONE from the service's own ticks with no desktop (about 25 s), the sheet's steps say driver service, a second one is paused *The Ledger service stopped* when the service shuts down, and the process ends with exit code 0. Report `build/agent02_ui/continue/continue-service.json`. The only process it starts is the service.

## What remains open

The owner-host run under the systemd user unit, the owner's display, and a live model are not exercised here; the service steps the explicit procedure only, and a pending model choice is polled by the service exactly as by the desktop. Today's non-resume rows are drawn by `TodayPage.fill` as a flat button that does not wrap, so at 1366×768 the long *While Ledger was closed* line is cut at the card's edge; a one-line change there (drawing it as a sentence with the word inspect, as resume rows already are) is proposed to the integrator. Nothing here claims acceptance.

# Graphite · daily guide

November 7, 2026 · Graphite 0.1. Graphite is the public name of the workspace (earlier Ledger & Slate); its assistant is Stacy, who speaks staC; folders, scripts and settings keys keep their earlier names. The owner's short guide for a working day: what the program does in this release. It does not claim owner-host acceptance: the ThinkPad, its display and inputs and the owner's model file are still to be tried. Installation is in the README and docs/MINIMAL_DEBIAN_INSTALL_01.md; how each part works is listed in RECORD_OF_DIRECTIONS.md, under Where the knowledge is.

## Start and stop

- From a text login on the minimal Debian machine: `bash START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh`. It starts the dedicated Fluxbox session with Graphite fullscreen and prints `Graphite ended with status N` when you leave. From an existing desktop the same command opens the fullscreen Office instead; `bash START_OFFICE.sh` opens the ordinary window.
- Graphite opens on the work. When this workspace has anything in it you start in the Field (below), with what waits for you selected; Esc goes to where you left off. An empty workspace starts on Home. Home's own choice "Start: always Home" starts on Home every time.
- Leave through the System menu (the pale Graphite symbol at the upper right) → Return to Debian (in the dedicated session) or Exit Graphite (elsewhere). Graphite asks about unsaved files, offers a return copy, stops its own model and tracked commands, then closes. The computer stays on.
- The same group holds Log out (this login session), Restart and Shut down (this computer). Each asks what leaving asks (unsaved files, the return copy), then asks you to confirm, naming what it affects. Nothing is stopped before you confirm, and Cancel leaves Graphite as it was. Then Graphite closes the ordinary way (the local model and tracked commands stop, running assignments pause, the session is saved) and only then asks the system itself (logind, through loginctl or systemctl, never sudo), because ending the session or the computer ends Graphite at once.
- When the system does not allow one of them, or Graphite is not running in a login session, its row says unavailable; F1, its tooltip and choosing it say why, and Graphite stays open. In the dedicated session nothing can answer the system's own permission prompt, so a Restart or Shut down that would need one is unavailable there: Return to Debian and use `systemctl reboot` or `systemctl poweroff` at the text login. If the system refuses at the very last moment, Graphite has already closed with your work saved and tells you why.
- Graphite services (the admission of new work) are separate from leaving: System menu → Graphite services → On, Off, Restart cycle Graphite's own services, never the computer, and keep the desktop open.

## The Field (new in 0.3)

Press **F9** for an overview of the work in this workspace: sources, reviewed sheets, calculations, pages, findings and open
questions as sheets, with wires that show what feeds what. Arrow keys follow the wires, Enter opens the real page, F9 comes
back to the same sheet, Esc leaves. Stacy's rail at the right shows the staC line for the selected sheet: S puts it in the
writing strip, Shift+Enter runs it. Ask Stacy about a sheet (its menu, or just type a question while it is selected) and she answers in
Talk: with no model she shows the staC that reads it and what the records say. Right-click a sheet (or press the Menu key) for what can be done with it. **P** shows every program and room as a shelf in six fixed columns
(Work, Think, Make, Build, Move, Set up): Enter opens one. N shows this computer's network the same way; W returns to the
work. With a model loaded Stacy reads the sheet first and then says the answer in her own words under the rows; say "this"
in your question and she takes the selected sheet. **D** asks the records what can be done about the selected sheet: the
steps show numbered, a digit takes one, a read runs at once and a change waits for your go (**G**, or Run in Talk; a
digit never approves). **C** checks the desk and says what waits; **1** then puts up what needs no decision of yours and
**G** is one go for the listed changes; the desk checks itself again. On the shelf, **F** offers a program's full window on
one of its files. A turned corner marks what changed in the last twelve hours. **T** traces the selected sheet back to its source and on
to what rests on it. With a calculation selected, ask "what if B3 were 320?": Stacy works it exactly and changes nothing.
In the writing strip `this` is the selected sheet (`this | count`, Ctrl+Enter), and `field.read` is the whole desk as
records (`field.read | pick waiting | select kind,title,state`). **X** doubts the selected sheet: Stacy puts exact questions to the records and shows what does not hold, what she cannot
tell and what holds; **D** then offers the step that removes a doubt, and **C** lists what she doubts across the desk.
"What if" also works with a sheet selected, by cell or by the row's words ("what if the pulse duration were 100?"): the
change is followed along the wires, nothing is changed, and the Field marks what would move until **Esc**. **B** shows the
desk written up as one page from the records; **G** keeps it as a page, and D on that page writes it again when the desk
has changed. **Backspace** goes back to the sheet you were on before. In the writing strip you can keep a staC line under a
word of your own: `word waits = field.read | pick waiting | select kind,title,state`, then `waits` (Ctrl+Enter), `words`
to list them, `forget waits` to let one go. Right-click a sheet (or the Menu key) for the same things as cascades: What if ›
a number › a value to try, Doubt it ›, Trace it ›, What can be done ›, Your words ›; choosing in a menu never approves a
change.
`docs/RELEASE_NOTES_0.4.3.md`, `docs/RELEASE_NOTES_0.4.2.md` and `docs/RELEASE_NOTES_0.4.1.md` have the details. `docs/RELEASE_NOTES_0.4.md` has the details. `docs/RELEASE_NOTES_0.3.md` has the details.

## The desk

The window is one symmetrical desk: two graphite bands, the head at the top and the writing line at the bottom, with warm paper between them, a pane at each side and your work in the centre. Both panes are one width (drag either edge and both follow; Settings → Workspace → Left column width sets both), and the desk is mirrored about the window's centre to the pixel. Lettering on the bands is pale, as if erased from the shading; words you can act on are eraser pink; the choice in use has a short yellow mark under it. Words you may skip (a caption, a note, an explanation) are in the script, and what you act on or read first stays in print; Arrange → Pleasantries in script turns the script off everywhere. The desk's measures are in docs/GRAPHITE_DESK.md, and its "Where things went" says where each older control went.

1. **The head.** Graphite at the upper left, in the script. Work · Revise · Tools · Arrange · Commands · Rules · Properties · Guide across the middle. Then CPU · GPU · RAM · TXT, each value under its name (TXT is the model's context in use, a dash until the runtime reports it). At the far right, the pale Graphite symbol opens the System menu (below).
2. **The left pane.** Three tabs, Machine · Cabinet · Settings, each a tree with connecting branch lines, and Trash, larger, at the lower right. Machine is this computer (processor, memory, storage, connections, devices, installed tools); every row's tooltip says where and when its reading was taken, and the Machine row's carries the one-line machine summary. Cabinet is your work by project: ideas, documents, assignments, questions, working copies. Settings is the shared registry Graphite reads too, under Workspace and Assistant. Nothing else sits in the pane: Import and Export are in Work, the cabinet's views and Refresh are under Arrange and on the tree's right-click, and Search finds records and settings by their words.
3. **The centre.** The real work. Documents, source files, calculations and workspaces open here. One Preview tab reuses itself; up to five pins stay; workspaces opened from a menu are rooms beside your Preview and never replace it. With nothing open the centre is the Finder (below).
4. **The right pane.** Three tabs mirroring the left: Conversation · Activity · Context. Conversation is talking with Stacy, the assistant: her answers, the staC she read them with, and Related lines. Activity is what Graphite did, what it got and what it needs from you, kept quiet: the Work block while an assignment runs, the services, one WORK line saying how much runs and waits (Work list opens the full list in the System menu), and the Timeline's last lines with Organizer, Return thread (Ctrl+Alt+R) and Follow latest. AI admission under Activity holds the AI ON / AI OFF switch: OFF refuses new AI requests only; files, tools and staC stay available. Context shows the files, selections and instructions in use, with usage when it is known.
5. **The writing line.** The lower band, as tall as the head: the cat at the left, Line · Half · Tall beside it, one long line to write in (its empty hint is `poem`), and the line's four modes at the right (below). Line keeps the centre reaching the band; Half and Tall open the working area above it. In a narrow window or at a large text size the band's words are set a little smaller rather than shortened, so every one stays whole.

The pointer is the Graphite mark's two facets aimed at eleven o'clock, the click at its tip. Text fields keep their I-beam, and the pane edges show the resize pointer while you are over them.

## The cat and the programs list

The cat at the lower left, pale paper on the band, opens the programs list: one click, even while it dozes, or Space or Enter when it has the focus (its tooltip says Open programs). It rests with graphite eyes, glances sideways with yellow eyes and a question-mark tail when you point at it, lifts a paw while the list is open, and closes its eyes after a quiet while. Under Reduce motion it changes pose at once.

The list is like the Programs folder of a Start menu: every program and capability Graphite has, one plain name and one small graphite icon each, A to Z (Agenda, Assignments, Calculator, Documents, Files, the KiCad, KiBot, ngspice, Yosys, nextpnr & Trellis and HDL checks, Laboratory, Local model, Memory, Methods, Office, Projects, Questions, References, Settings, Sources, Tool Atlas, Work trail), then Explore the workshop. Type a name's first letters to jump to it; Up, Down, Home and End move; Return opens; Escape closes. A row's word at the right says only what Graphite observed: open, N running or interrupted, needs setup (a program was not found), unavailable. F1 or the tooltip gives the full description: what opens, what Graphite can do there, what is missing. Opening a row runs nothing. Creating things is not in the list: New Idea (Ctrl+Shift+N) and New Project are under Work.

## The System menu

The pale Graphite symbol at the upper right opens the System menu, the programs list's mirror image (it opens downward from the right as the list opens upward from the left):

- **Game**: STRUTHIO, in its own window, paused at tick zero (below, The game behind the mark).
- **Stop all jobs**: the one stop for every job, model, assignment and capture Graphite manages (also Tools → STOP / KILL and Ctrl+Shift+F12). Programs Graphite does not manage keep running.
- **The process list**: active jobs as they started, then the queue. Each row's slider is its niceness, left more urgent and right nicer. The queue's order is a separate control: each queued row's place number at its left; drag a row, or use Earlier and Later. Each queued row says what it waits for.
- **Graphite services** On · Off · Restart: Graphite's own services, never the computer.
- Set apart: **Log out**, **Return to Debian** or **Exit Graphite**, **Restart**, **Shut down**, each with what it affects (above, Start and stop).

From the keyboard the symbol opens with Game under focus; Stop all jobs is one Down away.

## The writing line

One place to type. Ctrl+K puts the cursor there in Search from anywhere. Choose a mode with its word at the right, with Alt and a number, or by typing its lead character first on an empty line:

- **Assignment** (Alt+1): give Graphite work in your own words and press Enter. Typed staC, the structured commands pronounced Stacy, runs only when you press Ctrl+Enter, and the line says so while what you typed is staC; Enter never runs it. Up on the empty line brings back the staC you ran. A line starting with `/` runs an operation by name (Alt+3, or Commands → Run an operation…).
- **Shell** (Alt+5, or start with `$`): the line goes to your configured shell, in your Files folder; the word reads Bash when that shell is bash.
- **Search** (Ctrl+K, Alt+4, or start with `?`): files and their words, the cabinet, settings and commands, results under the line as you type; Enter searches everything.
- **Log** (Alt+6): above the line at Half or Tall, two streams chosen with the Events and Network tabs (below).

Choosing a mode never opens or closes the working area; running a line opens it at Half, and Line closes it.

## Log: Events and Network

**Events** is Graphite's own record of what happened, newest at the bottom, with Follow latest. Words in the line and Enter filter it. There are no notes: Log follows; it does not take notes.

**Network** is this computer's network as Graphite observes it, read from the system without privileges and without sending anything: each interface with how fast it receives and sends, and every open connection with the program that holds it. Type a host, a port, a program, a protocol or a state (`10.0.0.5`, `443`, `firefox`, `tcp`, `listen`) and press Enter to filter; words of one kind widen, kinds narrow.

Ctrl+Enter in the Network stream (or Capture… above it) captures packet headers with the line's filter. The first capture after Graphite starts asks once, saying exactly what is captured: headers only (addresses, ports, protocol, length, TCP flags, never what packets carry), this computer's own interfaces, never in promiscuous mode, at most 60 seconds or 2,000 packets, nothing leaving the computer. Stop capture ends it, and so does Stop all jobs. Capture needs the system's own capture tool: when it is not installed or not allowed, the stream says so and lists the steps for the administrator (Debian's wireshark-common and its group; `bash INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh --network-capture` adds the package); Graphite never runs them and never asks for a password. Capture only networks you own or may monitor.

Click an entry in either stream to pin it at the top while the stream moves on. **Ask Stacy about this** puts it in the line as an assignment's subject; **Follow this conversation** filters the stream to it.

**What Graphite can inspect.** During an assignment Graphite may read what the Network stream shows: the interfaces, the connections and the packets of the latest capture. Ask in Assignment, for example `what is talking to the network?` or `what ports are open?`, and it writes a findings page saying who talks to whom and what listens. It never starts a capture: when one would help, it proposes it, the assignment waits, and the proposal shows in Log, Network for you to start (or not). docs/NETWORK_01.md has the details.

## The right-click menu

Right-click anything you are working on, or press the Menu key or Shift+F10 for what has the keyboard focus. The menu names the thing at its top (a passage with its page and revision, a file or two files, a record, a job with its state, an event, a network connection) and offers what you can do to it right there:

- **Changes first**: on selected words Bold, Italic, Underline, Plain, the paragraph's style, Move to notes; on a file Rename, Copy to, Move to, Versions, Export, and Move to Trash last.
- **What its state allows**: a job's Inspect output, Pause, Resume, Stop; Agenda work's Pause, Resume and Stop. A greyed entry says why (Pause on a network capture, which the Kernel will not pause).
- **staC**: Inspect in the line puts the equivalent command in the writing line to read or change; Run runs it.
- **Capabilities that take it**: Compare revisions when two revisions of one file are selected, Compare with…, Extract, the program for its kind, the Tool Atlas, Ask Stacy about this.
- **The tree's own words**: Refresh, View as, New Idea, New Project, Import, Export.
- On an event: Ask Stacy about this, Show in Log, its job, Copy. On a connection or packet: Ask Stacy about this, Follow this conversation, Show the process, Copy address.
- On an empty place, the root menu: on Today and an empty part of the workspace it is the menu itself (Inquiries, the atlases, your kept chains, Start a chain from, the writing line's modes, Edit the Graphite menu, New Idea, New Project, Import); in a folder in Files, the Finder or the Library it is the first row, Root menu ›.

Everything goes through the same checks as elsewhere. A change is refused, with nothing done, if the page, file or job moved on since you right-clicked it. The result shows where it belongs: the page, the Compare room, the working area, the job's row. Run and Inspect output say "Not run" with the reason when staC refuses; they never say they ran. Text fields keep their own menu (cut, copy, paste).

## Home is the Finder

With no project attached and nothing open, the centre is a Finder window inside the same frame. The left pane is its sidebar: choose Today for what arrived, what waits for you, where you left off and Graphite; choose a storage mount under Machine, the Files row or a project's folder and the centre lists that folder, or open Places ▾ in the Finder's own bar (Today, Files, Ingress, Egress, Workspace, Program, each disk). With a project attached the same Finder is Home. Three views (Icons, List with Name · Date Modified · Size · Kind, Columns that open to the right) share one listing; a preview pane shows the chosen file's kind, size, dates, an image or the first lines of a text; the path bar at the bottom is clickable; the status line says how many items and how much space is free, observed on this computer. Enter opens (a text in the editor, anything else in the viewer), Backspace goes up, Space shows or hides the preview, Alt Left and Right go back and forward, typing selects by name. The Finder looks and opens; it never creates, renames, moves or deletes: those stay the Files room's own operations. Folders with more than 500 entries say so and offer up to 2,000.

## Ingress and Egress

Files come in through Ingress (`~/Concern/Office/Ingress` for the Office): drop them there or on the Office, and Today, the Library's ARRIVE section and the Office count them as new until you receive them. Files leave from Egress (`Files/Egress`): exports of documents, reviewed Office output copies, result pills and manufacturing or sharing copies with their SHA256SUMS start or land there. The names are the owner's; the older folders Arrived (and the 4.1 Inbox) and Exports are moved to the new names once, without overwriting anything, the first time Graphite runs on a workspace. Operation names such as files.export and receiving.* are unchanged.

## Writing a document with Graphite

The programs list → Documents opens a page. Write; it saves itself a moment after you pause (and before anything else touches it). Select words, go to the writing line, in Assignment, and ask in plain words: `make these words bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `make it a heading`, `heading 2`, `body text`, `code`, `plain`, `replace fox with cat`. These are direct edits Graphite makes without a model; its answer names the change and the saved revision. With a model loaded, a request the rules do not know goes to the model, and the edit it proposes for the open page is applied at once: the changed words glow pencil-yellow for a moment, the face shows APPLIED ON THE PAGE with undo, and Ctrl Z takes it back. If the page changed while the model was thinking, nothing is applied and the card says why. Anything else the model proposes waits for your Run. Ctrl Z takes any change back, Stacy's included, and `undo` or `redo` typed to her does the same. Anything it does not recognise goes to the model when one is loaded; without one it says so. Reopen a page from the list on the left or from the cabinet's Documents folder; every page is a saved revision with its history. Export… writes Markdown, HTML or plain text to Egress (Files/Egress). Keys on the page: Ctrl B, Ctrl I, Ctrl U, Ctrl 1/2/3 headings, Ctrl 0 body, Ctrl ` code, Ctrl S save now.

## Giving Graphite an assignment

On a page with quantities, ask in the writing line, in Assignment: `add up the numbers on this page` (a verb such as add up, total, sum or count; a noun such as numbers, quantities or values; and a place such as on this page). Graphite reads the page, finds the quantities exactly where you wrote them, sums them with a unit check, writes the total under your words and binds it to those numbers. The Work block at the top of Activity says what it is working on, doing now, found, needs from you, and where to inspect; Stop, Pause and Resume are words there, and Inspect opens the investigation with every recorded step. Units that differ become a question and the assignment waits for you. Change one of the numbers and the page shows a quiet line, a result on this page is stale · recheck; one word rechecks. Closing Graphite while it works: with the Graphite service on (System menu ▸ Graphite services ▸ On), the assignment continues in the service and Today says what was done while Graphite was closed; opening Graphite takes the work back. Settings ▸ Assistant ▸ Assignments ▸ Continue assignments while Graphite is closed turns this off, and then closing pauses it and Today offers to resume. Stop all jobs stops it on both sides. A request it has no procedure for becomes a waiting assignment that says so. Related, beneath the Work block, lists your own earlier records that share the page's words; dismiss what does not help. Assignments in the programs list (the cat) opens the room with all of them.

With nothing open, ask for files: `find files about pellets` or `what files do we have about the crate`. Graphite looks through Files and Ingress (Ingress by name only), reads the first lines of up to four of the best matches and writes a findings page; inspect opens it. Requests about the open page (`search this document for …`) go to the model instead.

## Writing elsewhere

Write directly into yellow passages: ideas, project intent, document titles, settings values, the return thread, the writing line. The X mark in the margin shows the line you are writing on; it is a setting (Settings → Workspace → Appearance → Writing marker) and goes still when Reduce motion is on. Owner prose uses the prose font and size from Settings → Reading; code keeps the code font.

## The local model

The programs list → Local model opens the Brain room: drop a GGUF file on it or choose one, and the pinned llama.cpp runtime (CPU build, included under runtimes/) serves it on this computer. No model file is included in the release; the room says which file is selected, qualified, running or stopped. Graphite's direct document edits, the machine view, the cabinet and every workspace work without a model.

Which file to fetch (both Apache-2.0, from the Qwen organisation's GGUF repositories on the public hub; both were run through Graphite's real operations in the build container, see docs/MODEL_TRIAL_01.md):

- Default: `qwen2.5-1.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf` (1,117,320,736 bytes, SHA-256 6a1a2eb6d15622bf3c96857206351ba97e1af16c30d7a74ee38970e434e9407e). It proposed the right document edit and the right plain next step.
- Minimum: `qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf` (491,400,032 bytes, SHA-256 74a4da8c9fdbcd15bd1f6d01d621410d31c6fc00986f5eb687824e7b93d7a9db). It answers in a sentence and loads in under a second, but decides poorly; the program stays useful with it because the loop's rules come first.

Place the file anywhere on the computer, register it in the Brain room (Add a model), then Use it; the room reports the qualification. Check the hash before trusting a copy: `sha256sum <file>`.

## Finding and checking

- Explore suggests capabilities for the selected record and opens the Explore room for a broad search: the programs list's Explore the workshop, Tools → Explore capabilities…, Explore in Activity for the selected record, or the right-click on a file or record.
- Settings → Workspace → Hardware category views remembers how each hardware pane lists its files.
- Run `python3 tools/check_release.py` from the program folder to verify the payload against `MANIFEST.json`, the seed and the live program against the recorded Graphite 0.1 registry (`docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json`: operations, job tools, settings, adapters); any difference is listed in words. `--self-test` adds the focused test modules one by one and `--ui` the offscreen window checks. A passing check is integrity, not readiness.

## The game behind the mark

Game in the System menu's list (the sharpened point at the far right of the head) opens STRUTHIO ARCADE 1.9.0 in its own window, in desk mode: keyboard only (no touch controls are shown), no title screen, and a new run waits on the pause screen at tick zero with the keys listed. ← → (or A D) flap left and right, ↑ W or Space flap hard, ↓ (S) darts, Esc pauses; a flap key starts the run and resumes it. Game over offers NEW RUN only (Space or Enter), paused at tick zero again. Desk runs save to their own run slots, apart from the web game's. The game window keeps its own storage on this computer, separate from the phone game (which stays as it is and keeps its saves and high scores on the phone), and Graphite serves the game at the same local address each time (127.0.0.1:47913), so the window's saved runs and high scores last from one session to the next. If something else holds that address, Graphite uses a free one for that session, and that session's saves stay with it.

## What is not yet in place

More assignments (an ARC calculation that follows a changed condition, datasheet to spreadsheet), Python helpers Graphite writes itself, real native application handover, and model replacement with rollback are the next passes; owner-host acceptance of the dedicated session, real models and native tools needs the ThinkPad.

# Documents · the shared page (HATCH WORKSHOP-01)

November 5, 2026 · UTC. The first route of the Creative Implementation Commission v2.1's simple demonstration: the owner types a paragraph in the centre, selects words, asks Slate in the typing strip to make them bold, sees the formatting change, keeps typing; saving and reopening retain the result; undo takes Slate's change back like any other. Everything here runs with no model; the model path is unchanged and receives the document and the selection as context.

## Where it lives

- `workbench/documents.py` — the store and the rules. A document is a Project Desk record (kind `document`, schema `ledger.document/1`) in the existing `desk_records`, `desk_history` and `desk_events` tables: a title and ordered blocks, each a paragraph with a style (Normal, Heading1, Heading2, Heading3, Code) and inline marks (bold, italic, underline) over character ranges. Marks are normalised to sorted, non-overlapping runs; overlapping input runs are unioned. Limits: 5,000 blocks, 32,768 characters per block, 2,000,000 characters in all.
- `workbench/document_qt.py` — the page. `DocumentsTab` is a retained room (Hatch ▸ Work ▸ Documents, Explore, the cabinet's action shelf, `ledger.navigate` destination `documents`): a list of saved documents, a yellow title passage, a marks row of pink action words (Bold, Italic, Underline, Heading, Subheading, Minor heading, Body, Code, Plain) and the page, a `QTextEdit` in the prose font with plain paste, a visible selection while the strip has focus, and Return ending a heading. Keys: Ctrl B, Ctrl I, Ctrl U, Ctrl 1/2/3, Ctrl 0, Ctrl `, Ctrl S.
- Filing: `workbench/cabinet.py` lists documents under Documents inside their project (or Unassigned); the cabinet record view shows the page's words; `explore.suggestions` offers the page for ideas, projects and documents.

## Operations (recorded additions)

| Operation | Scope | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `documents.create` | execute | A new page (title, optional project and plain text); an unnamed page is called by its first words. |
| `documents.list`, `documents.get` | read | Summaries; one document with its events and plain text. |
| `documents.save` | execute | Whole-page save against `expected_revision`; unchanged content is not a revision. |
| `documents.edit` | execute | One bounded change on one selection (`block`, `start`, `end`, quoted `text`): bold/italic/underline on or off, `clear`, `style`, `replace`. Refuses `REVISION_CHANGED` and `SELECTION_CHANGED`; records actor, words and the request in `last_change`. |
| `documents.interpret` | read | The explicit rules over a request's words (with the selected text when there is one). |
| `documents.render` | read | Plain, Markdown or HTML text of the saved revision (the page's Export… writes one of them). |

`documents.*` is private to this computer for cloud proposals; the reads are journal observers, the writes are journalled requests. The `ledger.navigate` destination enum gains `documents` (recorded extension).

## Revision binding

The page saves itself 1.5 s after typing pauses, when focus leaves it, on Ctrl S, before export, before any Slate request and when the tab closes, always with the revision it last saw. Slate's edit names the selection and quotes the words; the store checks both against the saved revision. On refusal the page reloads the saved revision and says so; unsaved words are repeated in the status line so nothing is silently lost. Two pages over the same document cannot overwrite each other (the later save is refused and reloads).

## Slate's turn without a model

`documents.interpret` resolves formatting requests by vocabulary: every word must be a filler, a formatting word, a style word or a negation, otherwise the request is left to the model path. Recognised: bold, italic, underline (and their removal: remove, not, un-), heading / heading 2 / heading level three / title / subheading, body text, code, plain / clear the formatting, replace x with y (narrowed to the words inside the selection). `undo` and `redo` typed to Slate work the page's own undo stack. The answer names the change, the revision, that no model was needed and how to take it back. Anything else: the existing `brain.ask` path with the document and selection as the open item; with no model selected Slate says so and lists the direct edits.

## Evidence

`tests_integrated/test_documents.py` (13 cases: model, rules, store, registry boundary, cabinet filing, the Qt page round trip and a two-page stale save) and `tools/check_document_ui.py` (offscreen: Hatch route, typed paragraph, strip request, bold on the page and in the store, continued typing, close and reopen, one undo stack across Slate's italic / undo / redo / Ctrl Z, the no-model answer, 1366×768, cabinet filing, zero jobs; three captures under `build/workshop01_ui/documents/`). The live-model turn, a real display and the owner host remain open.

## What is next on this route

The model turn (a loaded GGUF proposes `documents.edit` through the plan path and the owner sees it land), Slate writing new paragraphs under an assignment, a DOCX export through the existing office profile, the same binding for spreadsheet cells and selected design objects (WS01 across artifacts), and takeover/resume with retained drafts (WS03, WS04).

# P20 editable-document development checkpoint

Declared literal paragraphs/headings/native tables, Chinese/technical IDs,
source-bound working copies, Save/recovery and measured DOCX/PDF exports are
demonstrated. Extended Word fidelity/full owner Orange Book editorial/register
corpus remain OPEN. Measured renderer: LibreOfficeDev 26.8.0.0.alpha0, not owner
Debian-stable/GUI qualification. Broader P37 requirements below remain. No points
or source acceptance are inferred. See SLATE_PASS_20.md.

---

# DOCX campaign acceptance checklist

Retained owner direction: carry document work alongside the expanded Ledger and
Slate campaign. This checklist makes its acceptance explicit within core passes
17–20 and release Pass 37. Writing the checklist earns no feature points and
does not claim a new document editor.

P17 checkpoint: the PDF reader/citation/annotation foundation is implemented.
Unchanged DOCX paragraph/table-cell addresses, including Chinese, pass through
the extraction facade. Orange Book export source is preserved; its nine older
tests require sealed register/project inputs absent from this program-only
package and remain unavailable. Full editable-DOCX/renderer qualification is
still carried into P20 and P37; no new DOCX fidelity or Word pagination claim.

Current code already supports bounded, source-bound DOCX extraction with native
paragraph/table-cell locators, and Orange Book DOCX export. Original Word printed
pagination is not inferred from XML. Project chapters remain external in a
program-only release. Existing source review, Save and candidate rules continue.

- Preserve an unchanged original and its hash; retain native text/paragraph,
  table row/cell, Unicode and technical identifier locations in supported reads.
- Document supported structure and explicit losses for any proposed import,
  editing or export profile; do not imply full Word round-trip fidelity.
- Demonstrate a genuinely editable DOCX export with correct content and current
  source/evidence references, and disclose table/formatting limitations.
- Keep the Orange Book's editorial chapters, generated engineering status and
  accepted project revision distinguishable. Source drift must make currency
  inspectable rather than silently relabeling an old export.
- Keep generated DOCX and optional PDF tied to declared input hashes; measure
  the actual installed renderer before claiming PDF conversion or pagination.
- Verify explicit Save, fresh-process recovery and loss reporting on the
  declared host and profile. Imported active content remains inert.
- Retain the broader document ambitions in the campaign; comments, revision
  tracking, complex layouts or other extended features require named scope and
  acceptance cases before they are advertised.

This is an acceptance clarification of existing authorized work. It grants no
source acceptance, execution permission or physical engineering qualification.

# The second assignment: files about something (HATCH AGENT-02 · WI-C)

November 6, 2026. AGENT-01 gave the resident loop one assignment, numbers on the page. This item adds the second, and the first that needs no page: the owner types **find files about pellets** (or *what documents do we have on the frame*, *which drawings mention the hatch door*) to Slate, with or without anything open, and Slate looks through Files and Ingress, reads the first lines of the best matches and writes a findings page in Documents. The owner's own words choose it; no model is needed for any step, and when a model is loaded it only advises at one choice. Nothing here claims acceptance; the live-model advice and the owner's display remain open.

## How to ask

A verb, a kind of thing, a link word and the topic, in that order (explicit words; `profile_files.fits(words)`; never a model):

- verb: find · look for · look up · look through · search (for / through) · show (me) · list · what · which · do we have · have we got · are there · is there
- thing: file(s) · document(s) · docs · drawing(s) · sheet(s) · spreadsheet(s) after any verb (*are there any files about the brooder*, *what documents do we have on the frame*); *anything* / *something* only after find, look for, search or list, and never with the link *for*
- link: about · on · for · mentioning · mention(s) · called · named · regarding · concerning
- topic: the rest; at least one word that is not a stop word (letters of any script count: *Müller*, *ñandú*, *鸡蛋*). Up to three words may come before the verb (“Slate,” “please”), up to four between the verb and the thing (“me all the”), and *do we have*, *are there* and the like between the thing and the link. Trailing punctuation, quotes and *please*, *for me*, *thanks* are dropped. The owner's own letters are kept for the page title.

A request that points at what is open goes to the model path (which is given the page), wherever the pointing words stand: *this / that / these / those* before page, document, sheet, spreadsheet, drawing, file or one (*search this document for pellets*, *find anything on this page about pellets*, *is there anything about pellets in this file*, *which of these documents is about chickens*), a request ending in *here*, and a search of one page, sheet or drawing (*search the document for the word pellet*, *search the sheet for totals*; *search the files for grit* is still Files). So is a topic that only points (*this page*, *the document*, *it*) or names nothing (*something*). Everyday questions (*is there anything on TV tonight*, *do we have anything for a headache*, *is there something on my calendar*, *show me something about Python decorators*) do not fit. *add up the numbers on this page* is still the numbers profile: `agent_loop.request_profile` keeps the numbers rule first and then asks each registered profile's `fits` in registry order.

## The steps

Each is one registered operation, recorded on the assignment's investigation like every AGENT-01 step.

| key | operation | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| where | `receiving.status {}` | the Ingress folder's path and how many names wait there |
| find | `files.find {text, limit: 20}` | files inside Files whose name or words carry the topic. `files.find` is a plain substring search, so the text is the topic without a leading article and with a plural's ending taken off (*the pellets* → `pellet`, *boxes* → `box`; a word of four letters or fewer stays whole: *news*, *Mars*, *eggs*); a FINDING per match: name · place · size · changed · how it matched |
| find_word | `files.find {text: word, limit: 20}` | only when a topic of several words matched nothing as a phrase: once more with its longest word (*hatch doors* → `hatch`); the findings say “matched “hatch” by name” |
| ingress | `ledger.browse {path: Ingress, limit: 500}` | only when Ingress holds something: names that carry every topic word are a FINDING each, “waiting to be received, not read”. Nothing in Ingress is opened; a file whose word is only inside it is not found there. Nothing in Files and nothing in Ingress: one QUESTION (“Is it spelt differently, or kept somewhere else?”) and the assignment is done with “Found no files about … (looked at N files)”; no page is written. The QUESTION waits for this listing, so a match only in Ingress writes the page and asks nothing; when the listing fails with nothing in Files, the QUESTION is asked with the waiting words |
| read_1, read_2 | `files.get {path}` | the first line of the two best matches (a name match first, then readable kinds, newest first; a copy in Egress last). A table says its columns and rows, a drawing its first text, anything else its kind and facts |
| (choice) | none | while matches remain unread and fewer than four were read: *Write the findings page* or *Read one more match: <name>*, both acceptable. The default is to write; with a model READY `agent_loop.choose_next` asks it, and its pick is taken. Never more than four reads, whatever it advises |
| write | `documents.create {title, text, origin: SLATE}` | the page **Files about <topic>**, its first paragraph the request and the words searched for |
| lines_k | `documents.edit {append}` | one paragraph per match, best first, then Ingress, then “Looked in Files and Ingress on <date> · N matches · read M”; each bound to the revision the previous write returned |
| done | none | “Found N files about <topic>; the findings page is in Documents” and a FINDING with the summary. The page is not opened by itself: the Document word on the Work block's inspect line opens it |

Worst case: 20 matches, 5 names in Ingress, 4 reads and the retry make 35 steps, inside the default budget of 40 (a test checks the arithmetic). A findings page that moved on while Slate wrote it (the owner typed on it) is never merged: the step is refused by the store (`REVISION_CHANGED`), the assignment waits with “Resume writes a fresh page instead of merging”, and Resume writes a new page; the owner's page keeps what Slate had written up to then and the owner's words. With a read-only budget the finding and reading run and the write is refused with the step's words.

## Where it lives

- `workbench/profile_files.py` (new): `fits`, `topic_of`, `needle_of`, `stem`, `topic_words`, the `FilesAbout` profile and `PROFILE`. `needs = ()`. `done(state)` is overridden to finish only when interpret says so (see *Loop order* below).
- `workbench/agent_profiles.py`: registers `profile_files.PROFILE` exactly as `profile_numbers` is registered (UNAVAILABLE says why when the import fails). When `profile_files` is imported before `agent_profiles` (a tool that imports it directly), `agent_profiles` runs in the middle of that import and finds no `PROFILE` yet; `profile_files` then registers itself at its end. A test simulates that import order.
- `workbench/agent_qt.py`, `assign_from_page` only: a fitting request typed with no tab open, or on any tab, becomes an assignment with context `{}` when the profile's needs do not include `document` (the page is not flushed for it); the numbers profile keeps needing a page, and an unknown profile is treated as before (a page). The function's shape, answers and the AGENT-01 test of it are unchanged.

## Decisions

- **Explicit words choose it, no model** (owner decision 6: most steps are local computation; the model only picks among options). The model's only part is the read-more-or-write choice, with the rule default (write) primary, as the AGENT-01 live trial advised for the smallest model.
- **Two reads, then the choice; never more than four.** The plan's “at most four reads” and “options after the reads” agree only when the choice comes before the fourth read; two first keeps the page quick without a model and leaves the model two real choices.
- **Plural endings off, one retry by the longest word.** Without them *find files about pellets* missed `pellet_order.md` in the first trial run; both are still `files.find` reads inside Files, recorded and said on the page (“searched Files for “hatch door”, then “hatch””). A word of four letters or fewer keeps its *s*: cut to three letters (*news* → `new`, *Mars* → `mar`) it matched “needs new felt” and “March budget” and the page said “Found 2 files about Mars”. The cost: *find files about eggs* looks for `eggs`, not `egg`; a false “found” on the page is worse than a QUESTION that invites *egg*.
- **Words of any script.** Topic and Ingress names are split into letters and digits of any script, so *Müller* is not cut to `ller` (which matched “Keller invoice.pdf”) and a topic with no Latin letters fits.
- **Pointing words anywhere in the request, not only in the topic** (reviewer finding, AGENT-02): *search this document for pellets* had become a Files-wide search that wrote a page nobody asked for while the open page went unsearched. D19 keeps the page with the model turn; this profile takes only requests that name a subject and no open thing.
- **Ingress is listed only when it holds something**, and only by name (the plan: Ingress files are listed, not read). An empty or missing Ingress is reported as looked in (receiving.status said it holds nothing).
- **Nothing found: a QUESTION and DONE, no page** (an empty page would say less than the question).
- **The page opens from inspect, not by itself**: the done words say “the findings page is in Documents” rather than “open”, so they stay true when Ledger is closed and the Ledger service finished it (WI-A).
- Commission v2.1: no second dispatcher, scheduler, store or process; reads only (`receiving.status`, `files.find`, `files.get`, `ledger.browse`) plus the two document writes; no acceptance claimed.

## Loop order

Found during this work and integrated (AGENT-02): `agent_loop.step_once` now finishes an assignment by the default rule (the cursor past the plan) only when the step offered no options, so a profile's options after its last planned step are taken, not dropped. The profile still says when it is done itself, so it works either way.

## The right column

The Work block's Found line joins every FINDING; with one per match it reads as a long block at 1920 by 1200 and is cut at 1366 by 768 (captures 02 and 04). The plan asks for a FINDING per match, so the profile keeps them (the investigation sheet and the findings page carry them); the report proposes that the Found line show the last finding and “and N more on the investigation sheet” when there are more than three.

## Registry

No operation is added or removed. `agent.assign`'s `profile` enum is every registered profile, so it gains `files_about`: `['auto', 'files_about', 'numbers_on_page', 'operation_sequence']`. That changes the schema digest; test_machine's `RECORDED_DIGEST` and the shipped counts belong to the integrator. No setting is added.

## Evidence

- `tests_integrated/test_profile_files.py`, 16 cases: fits/topic_of (eighteen fitting requests with their topics, among them *Müller*, *ñandú* and *鸡蛋*; thirty that do not, among them every pointing request and everyday question above, each also checked through `request_profile`), request_profile routing (numbers still first), plural endings and words (four-letter words whole; *Müller* not `ller`), registration whichever module is imported first, the profile in `agent.assign`'s enum and the worst case inside the budget; on a disposable workspace (Files with matches by name, by words, a table, a copy in Egress and non-matches; Ingress with a match by name, a non-match, a match only inside a file and a hidden file) through `agent.assign` + `agent.run` with `ask_model` patched: DONE, the findings page's seven paragraphs, the eight findings, the CHOICE row “no model loaded; default taken: Write the findings page”, every operation in the allowed set, every `files.get` inside Files, `ledger.browse` only on Ingress; the model advising “read one more” every time (`ask_model` / `model_answer` patched) stops at four reads with two MODEL_CHOICE rows; nothing found; a match only in Ingress (page written, nothing in needs_you); nothing in Files and the Ingress listing failing (the QUESTION held back until then, then asked); *news* searched whole (not `new`); the longest-word retry; no Ingress listing when Ingress is empty; the moved page and a fresh page on Resume; a read-only budget; `assign_from_page` with no tab, on a page (context `{}`, not flushed), *search this document for pellets* on a page (None: the model path), the numbers request with no page (None), and a request that fits nothing (None). Kernel.launch, Kernel.submit and clip._request held; zero jobs.
- `tools/check_files_about_ui.py` (offscreen; `ARC_LEDGER_FILES_ABOUT_CAPTURE_DIR`, default `build/agent02_ui/files_about/`; JSON `files-about-ui.json`): seven checks — no tab open; “find files about pellets” typed in the strip with key events becomes a files_about assignment with context `{}` and Slate says “Working on it”; after two driver steps the Work block reads running and “Listing Ingress by name (step 3 of 5)”; the driver works it to DONE between events (12 steps, one CHOICE, reads inside Files only, the Ingress listing only); the Document word on the inspect line opens the findings page (revision 7, seven paragraphs, the roof note, the receipt and the scan absent); 1366 by 768; zero jobs, launches, submissions, provider requests and processes, no model. Captures `Ledger_Slate_AGENT_02_FilesAbout_01_Running_1920.png`, `_02_Done_1920.png`, `_03_Page_1920.png`, `_04_Compact_1366.png`.
- Reruns: `tools/check_agent_ui.py` (redirected with `ARC_LEDGER_AGENT_CAPTURE_DIR`) PASSED, 13 checks, 5 captures; `tests_integrated.test_agent_loop`, `test_related` and `test_conditions` green.

## Open

- The live model's advice at the choice (the loop's model path is patched in the tests, as in AGENT-01).
- The Found line and the loop-order change proposed above.
- `files.find` reads a file's words only for text kinds up to 2 MB; PDFs and office documents are found by name only.
- Owner display, owner host, acceptance: not claimed.
