# FINDER-01 · the Finder workspace (HATCH AGENT-01, UI-04)

Owner's words (November 5, 2026): "Don't forget that the empty workspace, if nothing is being worked on, is essentially
our Finder window or our Explorer of files on the computer, but mostly done in the Macintosh format. So we have always
information in the workspace. Even if nothing is being worked on, we can see the files that have been selected in the
left-hand column navigation tree."

## What the Finder is

With no document or room open, the centre of Ledger & Slate is a Finder window in the Macintosh shape. The frame does
not change: the left column, the Ledger Head, the typing strip and the right column stay where they are; the Finder
lives in the centre, where Today used to sit alone. Today is still there: it is the Finder's first place.

- **Code**: `workbench/finder_qt.py` (`FinderPage`), hosted by `workbench/empty_workspace_qt.show_home`; the listing
  operation is `ledger.browse` in `workbench/browse.py` (read scope, an observer, cloud-private).
- **`host._empty_home_page`** is the `FinderPage`; **`page.today`** is the existing `TodayPage` (greeting, capture box,
  four cards, the Waiting card's resume rows), unchanged in content. `host.finder` is the same page.
- **Toolbar** (top): back ‹ and forward › over a history of places, ↑ for the enclosing folder, the place's name, the
  view switch Icons · List · Columns, the Hidden word, the Preview word, and Places ▾.
- **Views**: one listing, three faces. *List* shows Name · Date Modified · Size · Kind, sortable by any column with
  folders always first. *Icons* shows tiles with the kind word under the name. *Columns* shows Miller columns from the
  nearest named place down to the current folder; choosing a folder opens the next column to the right; the preview is
  the last column.
- **Preview pane** (right of the listing): a drawn kind glyph or, for an image, a thumbnail read with a bounded
  `QImageReader` (longest side 512); the name; kind, size, modified and created (or "changed" with a note when the
  filesystem does not record creation); for a text under 64 KB the first forty lines, read-only. A folder's preview says
  how many items it holds and how much space its disk has.
- **Path bar** (bottom, where the Mac puts it): one word per segment, each a link to that folder. Under it the status
  line: "23 items · 118 GB available on this disk · observed from this computer". When the folder holds more than 500
  entries the line says "500 of 1,234 items shown" and a second line offers "show up to 2000".

## The places

Today · Files · Ingress · Egress · Workspace · Program · each storage mount. Files is the workspace's Files folder
(`files_service.root`); Ingress is the folder files come in through, read from `receiving.status` (`inbox`) with
`locations.ingress` as the fallback; Egress is `Files / files_service.EXPORTS`; Workspace is the window's root; Program
is the folder Ledger runs from; the mounts come from `ledger.machine`'s storage section. The names are the owner's
(Ingress and Egress: "we're going future"); the folders are resolved through those calls, never by a literal name.

## The left column is the sidebar

Nothing was added to the left column. What the owner selects there decides what the centre shows, while Home is active:

| Selected on the left | The Finder shows |
|---|---|
| the Today row | the Today place |
| a Machine ▸ Storage row (program folder, workspace, a mount) | that folder |
| the Files row, or a Library files row | the Files folder on disk |
| a cabinet project node that names a folder | its folder (no node does today; the hook is honest and idle) |
| anything else | leaves the Finder where it was |

The hooks are small: `navigation_qt.NavigationController.library_selected` (the Library's current row),
`machine_qt.MachinePage.activate` (storage rows) and `cabinet_qt.CabinetPage.clicked`. Each calls
`host.finder.show_place(...)`, which refuses while a document or room has the centre: the Finder never steals the
centre from open work. When the last tab closes, Home returns at the Finder's last place; the Today row (or
`open_destination(host, 'home')`) brings Today back, with the other places still in the history.

## What the Finder never does

- It never lists a folder itself: every listing is `Kernel.dispatch('ledger.browse', …)` with the read principal.
  `ledger.browse` reads the folder once with `os.scandir`, stats only the returned entries, never follows a symbolic
  link (a link is shown as a link, its size is its own), opens no file, writes nothing and starts no process.
- It never creates, renames, moves, copies or deletes. Those remain the Files room's own operations (Trash, versions,
  proposals). The context menu reads Open · Open in viewer · Copy path · Ask Slate about this file, with Show in Files
  and Change it in Files when the entry is inside Files; outside Files it says "Nothing changes here · Files keeps its
  own changes".
- It never keeps a second store. History lives in memory; the last place, view, preview and hidden choices are written
  to `session.state['finder']` through the existing session (a `session.py` default for the key is proposed to the
  integrator so the choice survives a restart).
- It never adds a colour: graphite words, the pencil-yellow folder glyph and selection wash, the eraser-pink underline
  of the words to act on.
- It never runs a model, a job, a worker or a provider. The check holds `Kernel.launch`, `Kernel.submit` and
  `clip._request` and counts zero of each.

## The keyboard

| Keys | Does |
|---|---|
| Enter | opens: a folder descends; a text inside the workspace opens in the editor tab; anything else opens in the viewer |
| Backspace, Alt ↑ | the enclosing folder, with the folder you left selected |
| Space | shows or hides the preview |
| Alt ←, Alt → | back and forward through the places |
| typing letters | selects by name (the views' own type-to-select) |
| double-click | opens, as Enter |
| right-click | the context menu above |

## The bound

`ledger.browse` returns at most 500 entries by default and 2000 at most; `count` is the number of entries the folder
holds after the hidden filter, so the status line can say "500 of 1,234 items shown" truthfully. A folder with more than
100,000 entries is read up to that bound and reported truncated with the count seen. Hidden entries (names beginning
with a dot) come only with the Hidden word on. The text preview reads at most 64 KB and shows forty lines; the image
preview reads a thumbnail of at most 512 pixels on the longest side.

## Decisions recorded for the register

1. **Today is the first place.** The owner's "we have always information in the workspace" is served by a Finder
   that begins at Today and keeps the greeting, the cards and the resume rows exactly as they were; the folders are
   the other places of the same window.
2. **The left column is the sidebar; nothing is added there.** "We can see the files that have been selected in the
   left-hand column navigation tree": selection on the left drives the centre, through three small hooks that act only
   while Home is active.
3. **Read-only by design.** Looking is `ledger.browse`; changing stays with the Files room's operations and their
   Trash, versions and proposals. The Finder writes nothing, not even a cache.
4. **The 500 / 2000 bound**, with a truthful count and the word that raises it, keeps a large folder quick without
   hiding that more exists.
5. **Ingress and Egress** are places named with the owner's words and resolved through `receiving.status`,
   `locations.ingress` and `files_service.EXPORTS`, never by a literal folder name.

## Narrow widths: every word whole (HATCH GRAPHITE-01, G-B, November 6, 2026)

At 1366 by 768 the AGENT-01 and AGENT-02 captures showed the toolbar clipping its words (the place name, "Colur",
"Hidc", "Prev"), the head's menu words clipping at the right ("Gui") and Today's card grid wider than the centre. Now:

- **Toolbar**: the words stay while they fit; under the bar's width the least-used fold into **⋯** in this order:
  Hidden, Places, Preview, then Icons · List · Columns. ⋯ holds the same choices as menu rows (Show hidden files, Show
  preview (Space), Places ▸, View as …), checked and enabled as their words are. The place name takes the room left and
  elides last, whole in its tooltip. A checked word keeps room for its bold face (theme2 draws a checked button at weight
  600, Qt sizes it at 400).
- **List**: Name keeps at least 150 px (at 14 pt, scaled); Kind folds first, then Date Modified, then Size. The preview
  pane shows all three. Date Modified, Size and Kind start at 120, 100 and 180 px at 14 pt and grow with the interface
  (154 px for Date Modified at 18 pt, where its title and "08 Aug 2026" need more than 120); a width the owner drags is
  kept, at every interface size.
- **Path bar**: the folders nearest the place stay whole; the leading ones fold into **…**, a menu of those folders. A
  last folder name too long for the whole foot elides in the middle (whole in its tooltip and in `path_words()`).
- **Columns**: a long name elides in the middle inside its column, whole in its tooltip; a column never scrolls sideways
  (the Columns view itself still does, by design).
- **Preview pane**: in a short window it scrolls down rather than drawing its lines over each other.
- **Today** (shell2.TodayPage, layout only): two columns of cards while two fit at their own width and 320 px each (at
  14 pt, scaled), otherwise one, sharing the width evenly, decided again after every fill; a card row never widens its
  card past its longest word (plain words wrap, a path may break after each "/", a row you open is the same words as a
  wrapping link, and the folder note beside a recent document wraps the same way, so a document five folders deep keeps
  its name a whole link).
- **The Ledger Head** (shell2.TopBar): the menu words fold into **⋯** from the right before they would clip; ⋯ opens the
  same menus. The fold is decided from the room the row can give the words when both end cells give up their slack
  (typebar.holder_widths' own rule), so it never feeds back on itself, and each heading counts at the width the layout
  draws it (its minimum width when that is larger than its size hint); at 1366 and 1280 nothing folds, at 1100 by 700
  Properties and Guide do, and from 1040 to 1400 px nothing scrolls or clips.

`tools/ui_fit.py` measures it: `whole_words(root)` lists every visible label and button whose words are wider than the room
the style gives them (less what an ancestor clips; a wrapped label needs only its longest word; a checked push button is
measured bold; a word squeezed to no width or cut off wholly sideways counts; a List's column titles are measured against
their sections), `regions(window, *parts)` splits the window's findings into the parts a check asserts and the rest, and
`side_scrolls(root, allow)` lists what scrolls sideways. `check_finder_ui` and `check_frame_ui` assert the whole window at
1920 by 1200, 1366 by 768 and 18 pt (captures and JSON in `build/graphite01_ui/fit/`); `check_frame_ui` also sweeps the
head from 1040 to 1400 px. Checked words outside the Finder keep room for the same bold face (`finder_qt.keep_bold_room`,
which applies `bold_room` again after a restyle): the left column's "Cabinet", "Machine", "Settings", "Logical cabinet" and
"Existing views", the right column's "Operations", the face row's words and the strip's selectors. `ui_fit.PENDING` (the
words allowed to fall short, by at most `PENDING_SLACK` px) is empty, so any clipped word anywhere in the window fails these
checks; the reports in `build/graphite01_ui/fit/` list none.

## Evidence

`tests_integrated/test_browse.py` (6 tests) and `tools/check_finder_ui.py` (offscreen, disposable profile, launchers
held; captures and `finder-ui.json` under `build/agent01_ui/finder`). Nothing in this document claims acceptance: the
owner's display and the real host remain open.

# HATCH GRAPHITE-01 · Graphite

The owner's design update of 2026-11-06 (decision D32): Graphite is the single public name for the workspace and its AI;
GRAPHITE on the startup screen; the sharpened graphite point replaces the Struthio mark; the unlabeled peeking cat
replaces the Hatch egg at the lower left and opens the existing menu. Internal identifiers, settings keys and project
paths stay as they are. The pass was delivered inside Graphite 0.1 (decision D34), which finished it; the section
"Finished in Graphite 0.1" at the end says what changed after the pass. Nothing here is owner-host acceptance.

## G-A · the mark, the startup screen and the cat

One new module, `workbench/graphite_brand.py`, paints everything with QPainter (no image files are read):

| Part | Where | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| The sharpened point | `paint_mark` | Two paper wedges converging to a point with a narrow gap between them and a short stroke past the tip, in the boot mockup's own proportions. Small sizes stay crisp: the gap keeps at least 1.25 device px at the wedges' wide end, the stroke at least 1.2 device px wide, and the stroke is left out where it would be shorter than 3 device px (only the 16 px icon); under 24 device px the tile's margin is 10%, not 15%. From 64 px, for the head's tile at device pixel ratio 2 and on the startup screen, the drawing is unchanged. |
| The head's mark | `shell2.Shell2.install` (the logo button) | The point on a 44 px graphite rounded tile on the same 54 px button as the bird; tooltip and accessible name **Graphite**. One click still opens the owner's STRUTHIO game. |
| The window icon | `qt_app.WorkbenchWindow` | The same tile painted at 16 to 256 px. |
| The startup screen | `launch.startup_screen`, called by `launch.main` | Graphite ground, the point in paper, GRAPHITE in spaced capitals. A frameless `QSplashScreen` centred on the screen, shown before `qt_app` is imported and closed by the first other window shown (the main window, or any dialog during the build, which never sits under it). No fade, so Reduce motion has nothing to stop. Any error means no startup screen, never a failed start; `--check` shows none. |
| The cat | `hatch_qt.HatchButton` + `graphite_brand.Cat` | The menu button itself: an unlabeled graphite silhouette with separately moving pupils, tail and right paw, 44 px high at 14 pt and following the interface size up to 1.4 (`typebar_qt.cat_tile`), standing on a short edge line. Tooltip and accessible name **Open menu**; the accessible description carries the service summary, the menu's choices (the words the old tooltip listed) and the F1 note. (HATCH DESK D2: pale paper on the band with graphite eyes and paws, named **Open programs**; it opens the programs list: docs/GRAPHITE_DESK.md.) |

The cat's poses (the owner's four):

- **Rest**: eyes forward, both paws on the edge, tail tucked away.
- **Hover**: a quick side-eye, the tail rises in a question-mark curl that is part of the tail (no dot), paws down.
- **Menu open**: the tail out of sight, the right paw lifted toward the menu, the eyes toward it. It wins over hover; the
  menu opens at once on click, Space or Enter, from any pose (one click from sleep).
- **Sleepy**: after 90 s with no input to the program and the menu closed, the head a little lower and the eyes closed.
  Hover wakes it into the side-eye.

When the menu closes the pointer decides: hover over the cat, rest away from it. A change moves six pose numbers in one
150 ms animation; under `reading.reduce_motion` the pose switches directly. Keyboard focus turns the edge eraser pink.

Decisions:

1. The pose logic is a pure state machine (`CatPoses`: open, then sleepy, then hover, then rest) over a table of pose
   numbers (`POSES`), tested without a window. It serves "choose the simplest implementation that fits the existing UI".
2. Input elsewhere in the program restarts the inactivity timer but never wakes a sleeping cat. Only the pointer on it,
   the menu or keyboard focus wakes it. This serves "keep the movement brief and tied to interaction". A pointer left
   resting on the cat lets it fall asleep too, and the next movement over it wakes it into the side-eye.
3. The hover wash and the eraser rule of the egg tile are gone. The cat's poses say hover and open, and the edge under
   it carries keyboard focus. The `menuOpen` property stays for the checks.
4. The menu, its rows, `LauncherKeys` and `DescriptorKeys` are unchanged. "Hatch" stays the internal name (module,
   object name, menu accessible names until the rename item).
5. The palette is graphite, paper and eraser pink only (shell2's values, repeated in `graphite_brand` so that the
   startup screen needs no window code; a test keeps them equal).

Evidence: `tests_integrated/test_graphite.py` (14 tests: the state machine, timing, Reduce motion, palette, mark
geometry, the mark crisp at 16 to 44 px, the tile arithmetic, a startup screen that cannot stop the start and closes before a failure message) and `tools/check_graphite_ui.py`
(offscreen, 11 checks, 16 captures and `graphite-brand-ui.json` in `build/graphite01_ui/brand`). `check_hatch_ui` and
`check_head_ui` now assert the cat and Open menu instead of the egg, the word Hatch and "Hatch launcher".

The wordmark beside the mark and every other public word are the rename item (G-C, below). The installers' shortcut icon
became the sharpened point in Graphite 0.1 (see the last section).

## The rename (G-C)

Graphite is the one public name of the workspace and its AI; the menu is "the menu". `version.NAME` is `Graphite`
(`SHORT` unchanged), so the window title reads Graphite, Home — Graphite or *file* — Graphite, and About, the wordmark, the
Leave dialog, the doctor's line and the launch failure say Graphite. The AI's words say Graphite and its pronoun is it: the
face, its tab and switch word, Today's card, the strip's destination word, Ask / Talk to / Message Graphite, the Work block,
"Graphite paused", "While Graphite was closed, it took …", new results "checked by Graphite", the agenda, the findings and
the model prompts ("You are Graphite…"). Program words follow: Graphite services, Exit Graphite, Graphite closed, the
Graphite service, Current Graphite host. Inventory: 673 literals read, 527 edits in 122 modules, 194 kept on purpose
(the list is in the G-C report's inventory).

Decisions:

1. Settings show Workspace and Assistant. During the pass the shipped release check compared every recorded setting
   definition byte for byte, so the definitions kept their words and a display table gave the settings page the public
   words (seven settings had Ledger, Slate or Hatch in a label, description or effect). Graphite 0.1 re-based the release
   check on its own record, so the definitions themselves now carry Graphite's words and the table is gone; the root keys
   `Ledger` and `Slate`, every settings key, default, kind and scope are unchanged, and `settings_registry.ROOT_NAMES` with
   `public(row)` still shows the two roots as Workspace and Assistant.
2. The AI switch (Operations ▸ AI admission) reads AI ON / AI OFF (tooltip and accessible name: new Graphite AI activity). "Graphite OFF" would
   read as the program going off.
3. Machine words stay and are shown in public words: the schedule reason `New Slate activity off` is shown as New Graphite
   AI activity off (`operations.PUBLIC_REASONS`); `Ledger services off` was already shown as the service summary.
4. Words already written stay readable: a condition card finds its result paragraph by block id, never by its words, so
   pages that say "checked by Slate" keep working; reasons stored before the rename ("Ledger closed") are shown as written;
   the face splits answers on both "(What Ledger knows:" and "(What Graphite knows:".
5. Kept on purpose: module, class, object and function names; operation names; settings keys and definitions; record
   actors and origins (SLATE, SLATE_MODEL, LEDGER); folder and file names on disk (Files/Slate, which Files explains as
   "Graphite's area (the Slate folder)", ~/Concern/Ledger, the Ledger menu file); signed release and manifest product
   identities ("Ledger & Slate"); the installer's file names, certificates and the application name; the knowledge seed's content and its
   model-facing label; file-format identities; the Struthio bird's history; "Hardware & Software Ledger" (a register); staC;
   the STRUTHIO game; the HATCH checkpoint name.
6. The strip's right column cap is 400 px at 14 pt (380 before; the same 1.4 ceiling): Graphite is about 30 px wider than
   Slate, and with G-B's proposed bold room for the checked destination word (applied here in `typebar_qt`) the right row
   stays whole from 14 to 20 pt. `ui_fit.PENDING` no longer lists the strip word.

Evidence: `tests_integrated/test_graphite.py` holds the rename guard tests: no
literal says "Ledger & Slate" except the listed compatibility identities; the window's modules say no Slate, Ledger or Hatch
except the listed kept words; the public name and internal identities; the settings roots shown as Workspace and Assistant;
words written before the rename stay readable; Today names the workspace; a new catalog's seed says Graphite and an older
one is shown so. `tools/check_rename_ui.py` (offscreen, 11 checks, 10 captures, `graphite-rename-ui.json` in
`build/graphite01_ui/rename`): Today with the head and strip, the menu, the face titled Graphite, the settings roots, the
cabinet with its concern, ledger and memory drawers open, Existing views and the `ledger` and `operations` dossiers, at 1920
by 1200 and 1366 by 768, over a catalog seeded before the rename. Every visible word is read, labels and the items of every
visible tree and list included (none says Slate, Ledger or Hatch, in any case, except lowercase identities such as
ledger.open), and every head, centre and strip word is whole (tools/ui_fit).

## Finished in Graphite 0.1

What the pass left open, and what changed with the release (November 6, 2026):

- **The centre at 1366 by 768 and 18 pt.** The right column's floor now gives the centre only what it lacks
  (`typebar_qt.CENTRE` 400, `centre_floor()`, `yield_to_centre()`, `TypeBar.least_width`/`least_need`): the quiet words of
  the strip yield first, so Home no longer scrolls sideways and Follow latest and Return thread · N stay whole
  (`tests_integrated/test_frame.py`, a narrow window takes the quiet words before the centre). Not yet: at 1280 by 720 and
  18 pt the centre is still about 67 px short; the left column would have to yield its quiet words too.
- **Bold room.** Cabinet, Machine and Settings (`settings_qt`), Logical cabinet and Existing views (`cabinet_qt`), Operations
  and the face row's Context and Graphite (`operations_qt`) keep room for their bold state (`keep_bold_room`), and
  `tools/ui_fit.PENDING` is empty: any clipped word anywhere in the window fails check_frame_ui, check_finder_ui and
  check_rename_ui.
- **Today's workspace name.** `TodayPage.fill` reused `name` in its Continue loop, so the greeting and THIS WORKSPACE showed
  the last recent file's name; the loop variable is now `title`.
- **Start and install words.** `START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh` prints `Graphite ended with status N`. The installers show
  Graphite: `setup_arc1.APP_NAME` (the shortcuts, the Apps & Features entry, setup's messages; Windows backups keep their
  earlier folder, `BACKUP_FOLDER`), and `unix_setup`'s launcher Name, the macOS bundle's CFBundleName and display name, and
  the Fluxbox menu entry (their file names stay, so an earlier install is updated in place). The shortcut icon is the
  sharpened point: `branding/graphite/graphite.ico` (7 sizes, 16 to 256 px, written by `graphite_brand.icon_files`) and
  `graphite_icon_256.png`.
- **The catalog seed.** A new concern catalog titles its `ledger` row Graphite (the id stays) and the `operations` summary
  says Graphite maintenance; a catalog made before the rename keeps its stored words and is shown as Graphite while the
  owner has not retitled it (`concern_catalog.shown`, the one place old seed words are mapped for display).
- **Settings words.** The definitions carry Graphite's words (decision 1 above).
- **Version.** `workbench/version.py`: NAME Graphite, VERSION 0.1.0, SHORT 0.1, so the title reads Graphite 0.1.
- **Under load.** check_graphite_ui (keyboard focus back on the cat) and check_paper_ui (a colour-share measure) wait for
  their condition instead of a fixed time.

# HATCH ACTIONS-01

November 2, 2026 · America/Phoenix

Complete checkpoint over OPERATIONS-01. The logical cabinet now presents a
compact **With this record** shelf and a right-click action menu. Both use the
same new read operation, `ledger.cabinet.actions`, available to local Slate and
the ordinary CLI/MCP command paths. This is a bounded contextual-action slice,
not a new scheduler, execution dispatcher, or model/native qualification.

## Selection and ranking

The read operation resolves the selected cabinet placement through the existing
owner-scoped `cabinet.get`. It returns only selected metadata, a digest of the
already-read saved record, ordered action metadata, and a signature. It does not
return the record body. Missing, private and stale identities receive one generic
unavailable response without echoing the requested ID or provider exception.

Order follows a declared rule: saved-record inspection; preparation of an
existing writing form when applicable; the provider's existing explicit read
checks; related workspaces from Explore's record-kind suggestions; all-capability
inspection. There is no numerical confidence, inferred method fit or model call.
Only the first three actions appear on the shelf; All actions and right-click
expose the complete same list. References retain both their placement ID and
canonical identity. A reference does not become ownership or project membership.

## Eligibility and invocation

States are READY, NEEDS_INPUT and UNAVAILABLE. Required scopes, Tutor mode,
registered read command contracts, presentation sources and workspace command
presence are checked. Unavailable actions remain visible with a specific reason.
Checks not performed yet are listed in the shared metadata and tooltips.
Opening a workspace does not establish native/runtime readiness.

Before any Qt action, the controller recomputes the model for the identity
captured when the shelf/menu was built. It refuses a changed signature and never
substitutes a later tree selection. The saved-record digest catches providers
whose note revision is separate from their tree object's revision. This digest
does not hash a master file or establish source freshness. The original command
still performs current provider, input and access checks; this is not a database
transaction spanning menu presentation and provider execution.

READ actions dispatch the exact existing read operation and show its current
result. Only registered read commands with valid arguments can be advertised as
reads. PREPARE actions focus the existing project/idea writing space and retain
its draft. The separate Keep/Create button submits writing. WORKSPACE actions use
the original Explore navigation with no automatic record binding, copying,
project reassignment or edited-input replacement. EXPLORE opens the retained
workshop. Failed cabinet opens now return None instead of a misleading prior
room. Existing cabinet record actions and all earlier routes remain available.

Discovery reads are passive metadata inspection. Existing dispatch auditing and
provider initialization can still write operational metadata; no claim of zero
SQLite writes is made. Cabinet actions are covered by the existing cloud-private
cabinet prefix and are an observer operation to avoid polling journal noise.

## Verification

- Nine new boundary tests passed; fourteen Cabinet regressions also passed.
  The initial combined run was 22 tests in 2.054 seconds; the final new-test run
  was nine tests in 0.739 seconds after adding the separately-versioned-note case.
  Distinct focused cases: 23. The historical full suite was not rerun.
- Eleven actual offscreen Qt checks passed. They cover the shared shelf/menu,
  writing preparation without creation, real tree context-menu event, captured
  target after selection changes, stale-menu refusal, draft preservation,
  unavailable actions, edited-source preservation, compact layout and poem.
- Five actual Qt PNGs are retained under `docs/ACTIONS_01`. The menu PNG is the
  actual separate QMenu widget; the other four are window captures. The missing
  workspace screenshot is a controlled source-observation fixture, not a claim
  that the delivered module is absent.
- UI fixtures create saved records and an edited disposable document. They start
  no worker, model, provider request, engineering tool or kernel job. Stop and
  actual OS priority controls are not exercised by this slice.
- Registry is 686 operations, 112 job tools, 26 settings, 15 workspace adapters
  and 12 authored method profiles. All 685 baseline operation schemas/scopes
  and all tool targets are unchanged. Explore now projects 825 combined entries.

## Remaining acceptance

HATCH remains 0/6 formally accepted; integrated remains 4/6 in retained evidence.
I05 exact-model/native and I06 owner-host acceptance remain OPEN. Offscreen Qt
does not establish ThinkPad, pointer-drag, live scheduling, owned Stop, real model
or native application ownership acceptance. Settings/memory adapter completion,
final launcher/menu review and lifecycle/session-exit work remain.

Next bounded slice: a clear session lifecycle/exit surface showing saved state,
unfinished writing and active owned work, through existing controllers. Preserve
all master protections, existing command paths and native acceptance boundaries.

# HATCH AGENT 01

November 5, 2026 · UTC

Complete checkpoint over WORKSHOP-01 under the Creative Implementation Commission v2.1. It builds the resident agent Slate is meant to be: an assignment becomes a durable investigation that he works one bounded step at a time with real tools, records as he goes, and can be paused, resumed and stopped; the first owner task (the numbers on a page) runs end to end with no model; condition cards bind a calculated result to the exact words it came from and read stale when those words change; helpers are kept with their record of use; the right column says in plain words what Slate is working on, doing now, found, needs and where to inspect; quiet connections list the owner's own related records while writing; and the smallest Qwen models were run live through the real operations in the build container, which found and fixed two defects in the reply path. The owner's own answers to the pass's questions are decision D19; the loop's design is docs/AGENT_01.md; the live trial is docs/MODEL_TRIAL_01.md; the requirement ledger is IMPLEMENTATION_LEDGER.json. Nothing here is owner-host, native-handover or physical acceptance; the live-model column holds build-container trials, labelled as such.

## What the owner decided for this pass (D19)

The agent loop first; Slate free inside an assignment's working area, asking only for originals, network and outside effects; closing Ledger pauses, the next start offers to resume; a model-proposed document edit inside an assignment applies at once, visibly and undoable; design for the smallest model; the X marker stays on; quiet connections in the right column; the numbers on the page as the first task; helpers reused and improved; the external provider off unless turned on; Hatch order and menu words unchanged.

## The loop (docs/AGENT_01.md)

`agent.assign` creates the assignment and its investigation; `agent.step` runs one planned step through the Kernel with a budget-bounded principal and records it before interpreting it; `agent.run` repeats within limits; `agent.pause`, `agent.resume`, `agent.stop` move the states READY, RUNNING, PAUSED, WAITING, DONE, STOPPED, FAILED; `agent.status` and `agent.list` read the five lines. Profiles are explicit Python; where one offers options, the model is asked in the new schema-constrained choice mode and its pick is taken only when the profile marks that option acceptable, every consultation recorded. The desktop driver is a timer that steps RUNNING assignments and yields between steps; Master Stop and closing Ledger pause them; the Today page offers to resume.

## The numbers on the page (the first task)

Hatch ▸ Work ▸ Documents, write a few quantities with units, then in the strip: "add up the numbers on this page". Slate reads the page, finds the quantities exactly where they are written (helper `quantities_from_text`, a fixed pattern and a spelling table, no evaluation), sums them with a dimension check through `math.evaluate` (exact arithmetic in the Kernel), appends "Total of the 3 quantities on this page: 16 kg · checked by Slate … · from: 12.5 kg, 3 kg, 0.5 kg" under the owner's words, and binds a condition card to those three spans. Units that differ become a QUESTION the owner sees and the assignment waits. Change a number on the page and the card reads STALE, the page shows a quiet line with the word recheck, the right column says needs you; recheck re-extracts, recomputes and rewrites only the result paragraph, bound again on the new revision.

## The right column, quiet connections and Hatch

The Work block under Slate's face: working on, doing now, found, needs you, inspect, with Stop, Pause, Resume and Inspect as words. The Related block: up to five of the owner's own records (ideas, projects, documents, investigations, assignments) that share the page's words, by word match, dismissable. Hatch ▸ Work gains Investigations & assignments (the existing investigation room; also a recorded `ledger.navigate` destination), and Inspect opens it.

## The Ledger Head, by the owner's request (D26)

Asked for mid-pass and done in it: the CPU, GPU, RAM and TXT monitors now sit in the Ledger Head beside one Nice menu; the separate Stop in the head is gone; the first row of Nice is the kill switch, bound to the existing Master Stop controller (the one stop for every job, model and assignment, same confirmation, same shortcut); every active or queued row below it has a niceness slider (left more urgent, right nicer, through the existing jobs.nice and agenda.nice operations) and the queue is dragged into order. Hatch is an unnecessarily large, standout tile with the owner's egg, like the unnecessarily large Trash at the bottom right of the left column. The head check (tools/check_head_ui.py) captures the head, the open menu and the tile at both sizes.

Also asked for mid-pass and done in it: with no project attached the centre is a Finder window in the Macintosh shape (workbench/finder_qt.py). The left column is its sidebar: Today shows the Today page unchanged; a Machine storage row or mount, the Files row or a project folder fills the centre with that folder in List, Icons or Columns view, with a preview pane, a path bar at the bottom and a status line (items, free space, observed on this computer). The listing is one new bounded read operation, `ledger.browse` (500 entries, 2000 on request; hidden files on request; symlinks never followed; private to this computer for cloud proposals). The Finder is read-only by design: it opens files in the editor or viewer and can hand a path to Slate; creating, renaming, moving and deleting stay the Files room's own operations. The Finder check (tools/check_finder_ui.py) captures the three views with the preview open at both sizes. docs/FINDER_01.md describes it.

The owner's third request of the day, the words Ingress and Egress for incoming and outgoing files (D28), is done the same way: the folders are renamed once on first run (Arrived or Inbox to Ingress, Files/Exports to Files/Egress) by the once-only move 4.2 already used, nothing overwritten; the Library rows, the Office page, Today's card, the Finder's places, the export and output-copy dialogs and the Pills folder say the new names; operation names and record identities are unchanged. tests_integrated/test_vocabulary.py holds the mechanical checks.

## The live model trial (docs/MODEL_TRIAL_01.md)

Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (Q4_K_M, Apache-2.0, hashes recorded) were registered, activated and asked through `brain.model.add`, `brain.model.use` and `brain.ask` with real worker processes and the pinned CPU runtime in the build container. The first live reply exposed an undefined name in the reply path and a plan prompt larger than a 2,048-token context; both are fixed (the plan prompt now carries a core set plus the tools chosen for the request). The 1.5B model proposed the right `documents.edit` and the right plain next step; the 0.5B model answered but decided poorly. Recommendation for the ThinkPad: the 1.5B file as the default, the 0.5B file as the minimum. No model file ships; the daily guide and README name the files and hashes.

## Registry, settings and preservation

All 690 SERVICE-01 scopes and the 112 job-tool targets are retained; the recorded extensions are `ledger.navigate` (destinations documents, investigations) and `brain.ask` (mode choice, optional choices); fifteen operations are added and recorded in this pass (agent.*, conditions.*, helpers.*, ledger.related, and ledger.browse for the Finder) over WORKSHOP-01's eight, so the registry reads 713; settings stay 42. `tools/check_release.py` reports the registry and settings sections as ADDITIONS_RECORDED against HATCH_AGENT_01_RESULT.json, and the historical I04 comparison documents the brain.ask extension. No second dispatcher, scheduler or data store was added.

## Evidence

The numbers are read from build/agent01_ui/focused-tests.json, build/agent01_ui/qt-checks.json and the reports under build/agent01_ui; HATCH_AGENT_01_RESULT.json copies them. The focused modules run one by one and include test_agent_loop, test_conditions and test_related; one new offscreen Qt check (tools/check_agent_ui.py) exercises the whole first task through the desktop: typing the page, the strip request, the driver's steps, the appended total, the stale line and recheck after an edit, Stop, pause on close and resume from Today, the Related block; every earlier shipped Qt tool is rerun with captures redirected under build/agent01_ui/regressions (reports kept, duplicate PNGs not packaged). Zero jobs, workers, models, providers or native tools in the tests; the live model trial ran separately and is recorded under build/agent01_ui/model_trial.

Numbers of this run: 326 focused tests in 24 modules passed (60 new cases over the INTEGRATION-01 focused log; test_launcher, test_service_lifecycle, test_operations, test_explore, test_settings_registry, test_hardware_settings, test_presentation_settings, test_settings_advanced, test_memory_settings, test_model_settings, test_install_media, test_startup_scripts, test_release_check, test_readiness, test_frame, test_paper, test_machine, test_documents, test_tool_selection, test_agent_loop, test_conditions, test_related, test_vocabulary, test_browse); 32 checks and 17 captures in the three new Qt tools (agent 13/5, head 7/5, finder 12/7), every one PASSED; 21 of 21 earlier shipped Qt tools rerun PASSED (none failed); registry 713 operations, 112 job tools, 42 settings; release check on the tree PASSED with registry ADDITIONS_RECORDED and settings ADDITIONS_RECORDED.

## What stays open

Background work with Ledger closed (the pass after; the pause-and-resume record is its foundation); Slate's model turn applied to a real page inside the desktop (the proposal path is live-tested, the application is mechanical); more profiles (a file investigation, an ARC calculation, the datasheet-to-sheet route); sandboxed Python helpers Slate writes; takeover and resume on one artifact; model replacement with rollback in one session; the owner host (display, input, the dedicated session, the owner's model file). Strict HATCH acceptance remains 0/6 and historical integrated 4/6; I05 open, I06 not started.

# HATCH AGENT 02

November 6, 2026 · UTC

Complete checkpoint over AGENT-01 under the Creative Implementation Commission v2.1. The owner approved the next pass, the three items named at the end of AGENT-01: work that continues while Ledger is closed, on the same record; Slate's model turn applied to a real page; and a second assignment. All three are built, checked offscreen, independently reviewed and fixed; the resident service and the small models were also run live in the build container.

## Work that continues while Ledger is closed (D29, docs/CONTINUE_01.md)

The resident Ledger service (Hatch ▸ Ledger services ▸ On) already ticks every five seconds for continuing work. That tick now also calls `agent_loop.pump`, which steps a running assignment that no desktop is driving: the same `agent_assignments` row and investigation, the same `agent.step`, recorded the same way, with `driver: service` in the step's inputs. There is no new scheduler, store or process. The desktop has priority: its step always proceeds and takes a 20-second lease, and the service steps only an assignment with no live desktop lease. The service holds the Coordinator's dispatch lock around each step and rechecks the work hold, the setting and its own closing before every one. It acts with the authority recorded on the assignment, never with approve.

Closing Ledger releases a running assignment to the service (`agent.release`) when the service is live and the setting `agent.continue_when_closed` is on (default on; Settings ▸ Slate ▸ Assignments). Otherwise closing pauses it, as AGENT-01 did. Master Stop on either side pauses every assignment. Reopening Ledger takes the work back. Today says "While Ledger was closed, Slate took N steps on …" with inspect, or resume when it is waiting or paused.

`tools/check_continue_service.py` starts the real resident service in a disposable profile, releases a numbers assignment to it, and watches the service finish it on its own ticks before shutting it down.

## The model turn applied to a real page (D30, docs/MODEL_TURN_01.md)

The owner decided in D19 that a document edit the model proposes applies at once, visibly and undoably. `workbench/model_turn.decide` checks one proposed `documents.edit` against the open page: the same document, the same revision, and a change the store accepts. When the model's place cannot hold the quoted words, the owner's selection is used and the sentence says so. The page applies the edit through the Kernel with origin `SLATE_MODEL`, which `documents.edit` alone accepts and which reads back `model_used: true`. It goes through the page's one undo stack as one step. The changed words glow pencil-yellow and fade; the glow is never saved. The face shows APPLIED ON THE PAGE with undo and the Right/Wrong marks, and the instruction matrix records the outcome against the proposal. Every other proposed operation keeps the Run/Edit words. A stale proposal is not applied, and the card says why.

The live page trial (docs/MODEL_TRIAL_02.md) ran Qwen2.5 1.5B and 0.5B through the real operations in the build container, and it found what the canned check could not. Under schema-constrained decoding both models filled every optional key of the change, so a "make it bold" proposal also replaced the words with nothing and added an empty paragraph, and the page applied it. The fix works at both ends. The model is offered one kind of change per proposal (one mark, a style, replace, append or clear, never an empty replacement). `decide` sets aside what rides along and applies one kind and one mark at a time. It replaces or deletes only the owner's own selected words, and a paragraph change applies only on the owner's paragraph; everything else waits for Run. An independent review measured the first version of the fix live and found four more holes, all closed. Page requests now also fit the owner's default 2,048-token context, which before failed every time. In the final run at that context, the 1.5B model applied bold, remove-bold and "replace lazy with sleepy" correctly, sent the heading request to Run, and changed no other word. The 0.5B model answers "bold" to almost everything, visibly and undoably. The rules still handle the common edits without any model.

## The second assignment: files about something (D31, docs/FILES_ABOUT_01.md)

With nothing open, `find files about pellets` becomes an assignment. Slate asks where Ingress is, searches Files, lists Ingress by name, reads the first lines of up to four of the best matches in Files, and writes a findings page that inspect opens. Explicit words choose this procedure, never a model, and requests about the open page go to the model instead. When a model is ready it only advises between reading more and writing. The loop now takes a profile's options after its last planned step instead of dropping them.

## Registry, settings and preservation

All 690 SERVICE-01 scopes and the 112 job-tool targets are retained. The registry reads 714: AGENT-02 adds `agent.release`. Its recorded extensions to earlier additions are `agent.step` (optional `driver`), `agent.assign` (profile `files_about`) and `documents.edit` (origin `SLATE_MODEL`). Settings read 43 with `agent.continue_when_closed`, recorded in docs/SETTINGS_INVENTORY_07.md. `tools/check_release.py` reports the registry and settings sections as ADDITIONS_RECORDED against HATCH_AGENT_02_RESULT.json. No second dispatcher, scheduler or data store was added.

## A slimmer tree (D33)

By the owner's wish for a slimmer project, the 66 regression captures of INTEGRATION-01 (17.6 MB) left the tree. Nothing pinned them: they were copies of captures earlier checkpoints ship, and they remain in the INTEGRATION-01 volumes and in git. Their JSON reports stay. The STRUTHIO · ARCADE game stays: it is the owner's Easter egg behind the logo and part of the recorded I05 baseline. The phone app's three image copies also stay, because the I05 baseline the release check verifies pins them.

## The owner's design update (D32, recorded for the next UI pass)

During this integration the owner chose Graphite as the new public name, with the sharpened graphite point as the mark and the peeking cat in place of the Hatch egg. As the owner asked, it is recorded and taken up as the next UI pass, after this checkpoint.

## Evidence

The numbers are read from build/agent02_ui/focused-tests.json, build/agent02_ui/qt-checks.json and the reports under build/agent02_ui; HATCH_AGENT_02_RESULT.json copies them. Each work item was implemented, then reviewed by an independent adversarial reviewer who reproduced every finding before it was fixed. Twelve findings were real and all were fixed; their probes are listed in the item docs.

The integration also fixed two things in the evidence itself. The AGENT-01 quiet-connections test left a parentless Related block alive. Its queued deletions crashed Qt inside the next Qt test once the new model-turn tests ran after it, so that test now closes what it opens. The Hatch check compared the Services row by its full words while the services lifecycle's one-second refresh could change them. It had passed by about a tenth of a second, and window startup is no slower in this pass (0.91 s against 0.96 s at the AGENT-01 commit). The row is now compared by its stable first word.

Numbers of this run: 379 focused tests in 26 modules passed (54 new cases over the AGENT-01 focused log; test_launcher, test_service_lifecycle, test_operations, test_explore, test_settings_registry, test_hardware_settings, test_presentation_settings, test_settings_advanced, test_memory_settings, test_model_settings, test_install_media, test_startup_scripts, test_release_check, test_readiness, test_frame, test_paper, test_machine, test_documents, test_tool_selection, test_agent_loop, test_conditions, test_related, test_browse, test_vocabulary, test_model_turn, test_profile_files); 34 checks and 11 captures in the new tools of this pass (continue 11/4, model_turn 11/3, files_about 7/4, continue_service.py 5/4), every one PASSED; 24 of 24 earlier shipped Qt tools rerun PASSED (none failed); registry 714 operations, 112 job tools, 43 settings; release check on the tree PASSED with registry ADDITIONS_RECORDED and settings ADDITIONS_RECORDED.

## What stays open

# Algorithm & Theory Atlas — ATLAS-02

Open **Tools → Algorithm & Theory Atlas**, or enter `/open algorithms`. Search a method name, purpose or assumption. The Method page gives its signature, domain, preconditions, guarantees, counterexample, cost, references and licence-review limits. Exact descriptor exposes the source bindings and canonical Kernel operation schemas.

**Try an example** is a scratch area. Choose a supplied example, optionally edit its JSON, and click **Check declared input**. This checks the finite profile; it does not save a problem, launch a solver or submit an engineering job. The Admission check page explains rejected inputs and outstanding obligations. Scratch edits are discarded when another example/method is selected; no master or working-copy file is changed.

## Initial corpus

| Profile | Existing implementation | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact dimensional arithmetic | `math.evaluate` | Supported typed scalar quantities and exact rational evaluation |
| Additive interval capacity | `math.schedule`, `methods.preview` | Constant additive capacity, half-open known intervals; learned methods retain their separate acceptance gate |
| Linear equalities | `math.solve`, fixed SYMPY backend | Local affine equality profile, exact witness recheck |
| Linear feasibility | `math.solve`, fixed Z3 backend | Local real/integer affine constraints, witness/infeasible/unknown |
| Rational normalization | `math.solve`, fixed SYMPY backend | Quantity expressions, no selected constraints, retained original denominator guards |
| Dependency impact | `reasons.impact` | Tracked dependencies in an owned saved reason DAG |
| Finite support/refutation paths | `reasons.evaluate` | Proposed finite graph, with receipt/current-source checks at execution |
| Linear optimization | Reference only | No objective or optimality adapter |
| Shortest path | Reference only | No qualified pathfinding adapter |
| Linear least squares | Reference only | No fitting adapter |
| Bracketed scalar root finding | Reference only | No numerical root adapter |
| Experimental design | Reference only | No automatic design generator |

The last five entries are explicitly **NOT_IMPLEMENTED**, even if a related library happens to be installed. The seven linked profiles reuse existing implementations; this pass does not implement five additional solvers or claim all twelve are executable.

## What a match means

`MATCH_DECLARED_PROFILE` means the supplied typed input satisfies the admission checks of that finite profile. `MATCH_WITH_OBLIGATIONS` means the input shape fits, with listed obligations still open. Neither is a successful solver result, a current-host qualification, a learned-method acceptance or an engineering conclusion.

`NEEDS_INPUT` retains unknown quantities/intervals or missing declarations. `REJECTED_INPUT` identifies a malformed or unsupported model, incompatible units, a zero denominator, a nonlinear form in the affine profile, an unsupported resource declaration, a missing graph node or a cycle. A problem owned by someone else or with a changed revision/context fails through the existing Kernel boundary; it is not relabeled as a mathematical counterexample.

Admission and implementation status are separate. For example, a linear equation may fit while pinned SymPy is unavailable. **LINKED** means the required direct source files, operation contracts and pinned optional packages are present. Every profile retains **NOT_CURRENT_HOST_QUALIFIED**. File/package presence and a matched example do not qualify an operation. Existing historical evidence is preserved, not silently promoted into the Atlas.

## Input forms

`algo.lookup` accepts optional query, task and expected_catalog_digest. `algo.get` accepts id and optional expected_catalog_digest. `algo.find_applicable` accepts context, optional algorithm and optional expected_catalog_digest. All three are registered read operations in the existing Engineering Kernel, also exposed by its CLI/MCP schemas and Slate discovery.

All contexts require task. Exact/equality/feasibility/normalization contexts accept a typed `arc.math-model/1` model. The existing mathematical validator enforces units, bounds, node order, supported operations and domain guards. Equality and feasibility admission reuse the existing affine checker. Unknown values remain unknown. Normalization preserves denominator obligations; cancellation cannot make an excluded point valid.

Resource contexts accept an owned saved problem binding (`id`, `expected_revision`, `expected_context_digest`), capacity variable, allocation/lifetime pairs and declarations using `checked_methods.DECLARATIONS`. Freshness and owner checks reuse `math_service.current` and `problems.check_bound`. The existing pure exact event sweep validates quantity dimensions, intervals and completeness. At most 32 allocations are admitted. The result does not certify the truth of owner declarations. Actual `math.schedule` persists its normal receipt and requires its existing scope; `methods.preview` still requires an accepted, currently qualified method version. Atlas admission bypasses neither route.

Graph contexts accept a supplied reason graph and, for impact, a node. Graph shape reuses `reason_graph.validate`. These are declared-input previews, not automatic saved graph creation or a check of the receipts mentioned by arbitrary JSON. Real receipt ownership, observation freshness and rule evaluation remain in `reasons.*` operations. A missing node or dependency is not evidence of no impact.

Unexpected fields from another profile are refused. Planned methods always return NOT_IMPLEMENTED; their reference assumptions are not advertised as validated input adapters. Context size is bounded at 128 KiB. Actual core/profile bounds remain narrower where applicable.

## Versions and authority

The corpus is `workbench/algorithm_corpus.json`, schema `ledger.algorithm-atlas/1`, version 1.0.0. Its finite code bindings are in `workbench/algorithm_atlas.py`; corpus text cannot add an executable module or a dispatch route. The catalog digest includes corpus content, direct implementation/validator sources, the guide and existing operation contracts. Passing an earlier digest rejects a changed catalog before selection. This covers declared direct sources, not every transitive dependency, imported model, operating-system package or hardware condition.

The corpus and its examples are authored engineering descriptions bound to code and references. They are not cryptographically authenticated theorems. Reference pages remain links, with concise offline descriptions; full upstream documents are not copied. External docs may describe newer or broader capabilities than the pinned local adapters. Executable scope is always the local code and contract, not the upstream library's marketing or API breadth. Dependency licences are retained under existing notices and not independently audited by this Atlas.

## staC

```
algorithms
algorithms | find "capacity"
algorithms | method interval_capacity
```

The finite embedded staC read extension forwards the existing caller principal. The upstream POSIX staC interpreter is unchanged. The general existing read pipeline can also use `algo.lookup {"query":"linear"}` and `algo.find_applicable` with typed arguments. Invocation/dispatch still comes from the same Engineering Kernel. No second execution engine, shell adapter, background scheduler or model profile is added.

## Focused validation and outstanding work

Development receipts in `docs/ATLAS_02` distinguish descriptor/admission examples, actual executions of existing mathematical implementations, UI interaction, registry preservation and package integrity. They do not qualify the owner's ThinkPad. Solver examples run only through the existing bounded pinned adapters when those dependencies are available. Screenshots use actual Qt offscreen rendering; they do not establish native display acceptance.

ATLAS-02 completes this bounded corpus/admission/browser implementation. It is additional H03 work, not completed H03. Typed Discovery IR, automatic valid method composition, operation-specific Tool Atlas probe promotion, full context menus and real native owner interaction remain open. HATCH acceptance remains 0/6. I05 actual-model/native acceptance and I06 owner-host qualification remain open while additive cloud development continues under the owner's current direction.

# HATCH CABINET-01 · poem

November 2, 2026. Full checkpoint over SETTINGS-02. The requested empty-field invitation is exactly `poem`.

## Writing invitation

The desktop's existing text-entry hints now use one `text_prompts.writing_prompt` helper: 114 existing Qt call sites in 57 source files, plus the new cabinet writing box. Search, conversation, command, title, notes and technical text-entry fields use the same invitation. Each field retains its semantic label; its former example remains in a tooltip and accessibility description. Changing context or switching among Slate, staC, Kernel, Find and Shell keeps the invitation. It never inserts a value, sends a message, changes validation, or changes a stored record. Read-only output hints retain their original status text.

Seven dynamic mobile companion entry hints and the pairing-code and generated records-browser HTML hints use `poem` too. The mobile shell cache has a new version so the next service-worker update can install the new interface. This verifies source behavior; live iPhone/owner-host acceptance remains open. Typebar status messages have their own visible console label so save/error feedback remains available while the typing placeholder stays `poem`.

## Logical cabinet

`workbench/cabinet.py` projects the existing Concern catalogue, Project Desk, working-copy and investigation stores into stable typed nodes. `ledger.cabinet` and `ledger.cabinet.get` are bounded read operations, owner scoped where the provider has owner identities. The existing Concern catalogue remains scoped to its connected profile. A declared filing relation is not a grant of access.

The new tree distinguishes the record's canonical identity from a display placement. Existing catalogue containment/maintaining relations select a deterministic primary placement, with additional declared placements shown as references. Project Desk projects contain views of their ideas, assignments and saved inquiries. Records with no declared project membership have an explicit Unassigned view. Working copies and older investigations have no project-membership field, so the tree does not guess a project from a path or from another project's reference. Records whose project lies outside a bounded snapshot appear as Other project work rather than being falsely reclassified as unassigned.

A second project's reference keeps its frozen source binding and resolves the same original target. It does not copy the record, change its owner or declared project, or move/overwrite a master. The tree reads stored metadata only: it does not refresh source hashes, declare an inquiry current, launch jobs, or run a solver. Opening a record permits explicit read actions such as checking inquiry bindings or rechecking a copy. Cycles, integrity failures, unsupported catalogues and projection limits are reported without migrating or repairing the underlying store.

The central Cabinet record room preserves an edited Preview. It reads original records and can save a new idea or create a project through the existing commands. Drafts are retained per node while this desktop remains open; Keep is required for durable writing. Selection, expanded branches, scroll and the existing-view switch are saved in validated Session presentation state. Filtering temporarily reveals matching branches, then restores the prior expansion state. The real `cabinet.sort` setting chooses natural or alphabetical sibling order without changing identity.

Existing views retains the previous catalogue, alternate views, tools, and workspace routes. Import and Export are separate fixed actions opening the existing receiving and outgoing-file controls. They do not perform a transfer automatically. Trash remains fixed outside the scrolling tree. Hidden legacy-library polling skips file walks and copy freshness checks while the logical cabinet is active.

## Verification

Evidence is under `docs/CABINET_01`: 42 focused backend checks (14 cabinet and 28 settings), 18 actual Qt offscreen checks, registry compatibility, prompt inventory, and three populated desktop captures. The UI run exercises two projects, unassigned work, a real source and working copy, a stale inquiry, a saved catalogue note with two placements, and an older investigation. It verifies draft and edited-Preview preservation, actual Keep behavior, original master bytes/mode, sort changes through Settings, search expansion restoration, old navigation rebuilds, the five typing targets, status feedback, Import/Export destinations, 1366 by 768 layout and clean Session/lease close. No job, model generation, provider request or engineering solver is run. JavaScript syntax and the mobile prompt helper's preservation of typed content and accessible labels were checked locally.

All 681 existing operation schemas and scopes and all 112 job tools remain unchanged. The two cabinet read operations bring the registry to 683; the real settings count is 26. Discovery's five protocol-bound service sources are unchanged. The full historical test suite was not rerun. Offscreen Qt and source checks do not qualify native handoff, a live model, or the owner's ThinkPad/iPhone.

## Remaining campaign work

The next coherent UI slice is the expanded capability launcher, menu organization/names, contextual command ranking and right-column monitors/queue. The current record room is an initial adapter; editing existing assignments and inquiries retains their existing workspaces. Object Glass can retain its prior file context while the cabinet selection is separately exposed to the desktop context reader; integrating that selection into the right-column presentation remains part of that UI work. Final wording, switch presentation and overall layout remain deferred owner-review choices.

The complete settings/memory adapter requirement remains open. HATCH acceptance is unchanged at 0/6; integrated acceptance remains 4/6. Real-model/native I05 and owner-host I06 remain open. The next step is to complete those UI pieces, then present the interface for a cohesive review before owner-host acceptance.

# Saved inquiries and Discovery IR — DISCOVERY-01

Open **Tools → Inquiries**, or use `/open inquiries`. A new inquiry needs a title, a question and one or more stopping criteria. Save revision records those words immediately; advanced structure is optional. Pin this workspace to keep unsaved edits while opening another Preview.

The Inquiry tab shows declared entities, dependencies, current status and why a binding changed. Optional structure contains editable JSON for sources, assumptions, hypotheses, constraints, candidate methods, proposed experiments, proposed claims, next actions and a budget. The visible title/question/stopping fields are the authority for those parts of the document. New inquiry and opening another saved inquiry replace the current editor; save work before switching. Check bindings preserves the editor buffer and does not advance its optimistic save revision. A competing save therefore requires reopening rather than silently overwriting newer work.

Checked predicates links existing numerical receipts. It never launches the calculation. Save draft changes first, select a target claim/hypothesis and a method in its declared dependency closure, then supply a reader, receipt/action ID, expected Boolean and note. **MATH** uses a completed math action ID, with a zero-based Boolean output index. **SCHEDULE** uses an exact schedule receipt ID and its fits predicate. The fixed adapters check owner, current inputs, model/argument identity and the selected method profile. Prepared actions without a completed receipt are refused.

## What the first IR contains

The canonical schema is `ledger.discovery-ir/1`, exposed by `discovery.schema` and in `docs/DISCOVERY_01/ir-schema.json`. It is an additive proposal format; the upstream staC grammar and legacy adaptive model profile are preserved.

| Collection | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| goal | Original question plus explicit stopping criteria |
| sources | Named existing Ledger addresses and their role; captured by existing owner-aware readers |
| assumptions | Explicit text, scope, HUMAN/MODEL/IMPORTED origin label and DECLARED/UNKNOWN certainty |
| hypotheses | Proposed testable interpretations, not accepted facts |
| constraints | Named Algorithm Atlas contexts: typed models, owned problem bindings or declared graphs |
| candidate_methods | Atlas algorithm ID plus constraint reference; actual definitions/contracts are captured from the Atlas |
| experiments | Proposed check questions, method references and predicted observations; not executable plans |
| claims | Proposed statement and scope with explicit dependencies; no caller-controlled success status |
| next_actions | ASK, PROPOSE_CHECK or REVIEW proposals; not scheduled or authorized actions |
| budget | Existing Desk budget vocabulary; recorded intent, not an issued runtime grant |

Keys are unique across collections; goal is reserved. Dependencies must exist and be acyclic. Every inquiry-dependent proposal also depends on the goal. Candidate methods automatically depend on their constraint, and experiments on their method. Unknown fields, arbitrary execution commands, forged observation collections and claimed CHECKED_FORMAL/CHECKED_NUMERIC statuses in proposal JSON are refused. Text must be meaningful, and structure is strictly bounded.

The supplied origin field is an authored classification, not verified authorship. The stored record's owner and actor come from the actual Kernel principal. Source roles and links do not prove that a numeric model was correctly extracted from a document. That interpretation remains reviewable.

## Store and history

`discovery.create` and `discovery.revise` use the existing owner-private Desk records, event log and immutable revision history. No database migration or new scheduler is added. Revise requires the current expected revision and explicitly recaptures source/method bindings. Observation records are immutable, linked transactionally with a new inquiry revision. Repeating the same current predicate/receipt/dependency/note combination returns the existing observation instead of creating a duplicate.

`discovery.list` gives private summaries with the existing limit/offset pagination. The desktop picker shows the newest 100. `discovery.history` returns revision summaries; `discovery.get` can select a historical revision without restoring it over the current one. Historical inquiry documents and observations remain accessible after edits. The UI history is a read-only summary; detailed historical reads are available through the Kernel API.

## Freshness and declared dependencies

The inquiry also binds its schema and direct validation/receipt-reader source files. A changed protocol binding makes the goal and its declared descendants stale; explicit rebinding does not make historical checks current. This is a direct-source check, not a complete transitive software/environment fingerprint.

Source bindings reuse Desk snapshots and freshness checks. For small file sources, exact bytes and SHA-256 are retained under the existing reader limits; larger sources retain the existing hash/projection notice. Current reads do not rewrite saved snapshots. Method bindings include the source-bound Atlas definition, implementation, dependency state and canonical contracts, with caller scope-eligibility removed from identity. A read-only user can inspect the same owned inquiry without changing its method identity.

Constraint contexts containing a problem binding recheck the owner's current problem revision/context through the existing math/problem readers. A changed/unavailable source, changed Atlas binding or stale problem marks the affected declared descendants stale. Independent branches remain independent. New definition/source snapshots are captured only on an explicit revision save.

Each observation also binds the entire declared ancestor closure of its target. Editing a relevant assumption, constraint, method, source, goal or target invalidates the earlier observation; editing an unrelated branch does not. Receipt readers are rechecked when the inquiry is opened. Their changed or stale result invalidates the related check. Old checks are retained as history. A new explicit valid check can be current while earlier checks remain stale; historical failures do not permanently prevent renewed investigation.

This is declared-dependency invalidation, not automatic causal discovery. Omitted dependencies remain unknown. Shared Atlas corpus/adapter files can invalidate several methods conservatively. Transitive software dependencies beyond the Atlas's stated binding coverage are not fully identified. No automatic recomputation occurs.

## Numerical checks and claim language

Only two fixed observation profiles exist in this first pass: exact Boolean mathematical outputs and exact additive schedule fits. An actual current predicate may receive **CHECKED_NUMERIC**, with MATCH or MISMATCH against the explicitly supplied expected Boolean. That grade belongs to the bound predicate, not the nearby free-text claim. A current but unresolved/unsupported calculation receipt remains OBSERVED_ONLY and UNRESOLVED, never a successful numerical check. Unexecuted preparation is not a receipt.

A mismatch is a counterexample to that declared predicate expectation. It does not prove arbitrary prose false. Proposed claim/hypothesis text remains HYPOTHESIS or REVIEW_REQUIRED; changed dependencies can make it STALE. The system does not mark prose CHECKED_FORMAL, SUPPORTED_EMPIRICAL, ACCEPTED_METHOD or completed merely because a receipt was attached. It also does not treat tool failure or unknown as hypothesis refutation. Every view reports that completion is not authorized by this foundation.

The current adapters verify that the selected method is an admitted profile and is a declared prerequisite of the target. MATH requires the same typed model digest and exact/SYMPY/Z3 backend as that method. SCHEDULE requires the same problem/revision/context, capacity and allocation/lifetime arguments. A numerically convenient receipt from another model is refused.

## Interfaces and scope

Eight registered Kernel operations are added: schema, validate, create, revise, list, get, history and observe under `discovery.*`. Save/revise/observe require execute scope because they write records. Other operations require read scope. Standard Kernel audit/activity effects remain. No operation issues an execution grant, runs an experiment, invokes a model or launches a solver.

Embedded staC read forms:

```
inquiries
inquiry INQUIRY_ID | inspect
inquiry INQUIRY_ID | history
```

The general existing read pipeline and CLI/MCP also use the same registered operations. There is no extra shell/evaluator, dispatch authority, job runner or copy of the operation schema. The existing adaptive ACTION whitelist and actual-model profile are not expanded by this pass. Local-model generation of an inquiry and the constrained experiment/method compiler remain later integration work.

Documents are limited to 128 KiB and the schema's bounded collections. Captured source/method bindings are limited to 1 MiB combined. At most 32 observation links are admitted per inquiry in this version. Underlying source/receipt readers retain their own narrower bounds. Closed/stale records are retained; no purge, rollback overwrite or claim deletion operation is introduced.

## Campaign status

DISCOVERY-01 completes this bounded typed-record, dependency-view and checked-predicate foundation. It is not a completed Discovery Kernel, H03/H04 acceptance or HATCH release. Planned experiments are still proposals. Formal/empirical claim review, automatic model-to-IR normalization, constrained method composition, operation probe promotion, and real native owner interaction remain open. The owner's ThinkPad, real-model and native acceptance gates remain pending under the current direction to keep cloud implementation moving.
