# HATCH EXPLORE-01

November 2, 2026 (America/Phoenix). Full checkpoint over CABINET-01 / POEM. This is the capability-launcher and menu slice of the Interface Companion, with the earlier Hatch workflows preserved.

## The new entrance

Explore sits at the bottom left beside the existing five-command Hatch. It opens a stable menu of 15 existing workspace adapters and a retained central workshop browser. The browser brings together these workspace routes, all 12 authored method profiles, all 684 canonical operations and all 112 job tools. The combined read view has 823 entries before filtering. Workspaces are the default category; methods, operations, job tools and the complete view have separate filters and bounded pagination.

The new `ledger.explore` operation is read only. It is a projection over the original capability catalogue and Algorithm & Theory Atlas, with presentation adapters for existing GUI factories. It creates no alternate store, execution dispatcher, grant, source record or learned procedure. An exact operation or tool opens its existing Tool Atlas contract. A method opens the existing Algorithm & Theory Atlas. A reference-only method is explicitly identified and offers inspection rather than execution.

Search accepts subjects, familiar tool names and exact operation IDs. It ignores a small documented set of common request words so a phrase such as “I want to test an idea” can find the actual inquiry controls. This is deterministic metadata matching, not an inference call, semantic proof or general natural-language planner. All editable entry hints retain the owner's exact invitation: `poem`.

## Work-aware suggestions

Opening Explore from a cabinet record carries its stable ID and caller-checked metadata. An idea or project offers questions, calculations and the existing laboratory; an inquiry offers methods and tool inspection; a working copy offers its established file and Office controls. Each suggestion explains its record-kind basis. It does not claim method applicability, a proven scientific result, or permission to execute. The record's original body is not copied into the projection.

Explicit read actions supplied by the cabinet, such as checking an inquiry's bindings, retain their original operations and caller checks. Search and selection do not run those actions. Unavailable or other-owner records yield a generic context notice without disclosing their ID, title, body or action list. Explore is included in the existing cloud-private operation boundary; local read-only inspection does not grant effectful scope.

## Presence, readiness and running state

Workspace source presence and registered family operations determine whether a GUI view can be opened. Tool prerequisites reuse the canonical passive native assessment: missing or incompatible tools need setup, detected files still need checks, and unassessed dependencies remain unassessed. Opening a view is separate from qualifying or running its instruments.

Active-job counters are bounded, owner filtered and based on stored Kernel jobs. Running and queued counts are reported separately; they do not claim live process ownership or CPU scheduling acceptance. Oversized or truncated metadata produces a visible counter notice. GUI “view already open” is derived from actual current workspace widgets. A source/registry check repeats before opening a frozen menu entry. The menu itself holds one snapshot steady while the owner chooses.

## Preserve the writing

Explore is an existing-policy Room. Its launches use the original factories inside a scoped retained-view context; newly created views stay open without replacing an edited Preview or consuming its five-pin allowance. Ordinary navigation outside that context retains its original policy. Reopening an existing inquiry never reloads or replaces its unsaved wording. A request for another method preserves edited scratch input and reports the pending request instead of silently overwriting it. Opening Calculate or Laboratory selects the corresponding genuine pane in the existing Project Desk problem sheet; it does not create a problem or run a tool.

Cabinet records also gain Explore this work. Selection, tree expansion, original identities and master protections remain in their established stores. This slice does not add durable recovery for unsaved buffers beyond the existing mechanism.

## Menu language

The top menu display proposals are Work, Revise, Tools, Arrange, Commands, Rules, Properties and Guide. Stable dictionary keys, original QMenu objects, QAction instances and keyboard shortcuts remain intact, including the legacy palette and Ctrl+K typing-bar shortcut. Explore is added to Tools. The original minimal Hatch remains New Idea, New Project, On, Off and Reboot through its existing routes; its service actions are not relabeled as Linux power controls.

The owner's later Interface Companion expands the capability-launcher role. Explore supplies that role while keeping the older Hatch entrance compatible. Final consolidation, launcher name/mark, menu wording and session-exit footer remain review choices. This pass does not implement unqualified Return to Debian, logout or host power controls.

## Evidence

`docs/EXPLORE_01` preserves 13 Explore boundary checks, 14 cabinet regressions and 15 actual Qt offscreen checks. The Explore checks were repeated after the search adjustment; the historical full suite was not rerun. Negative cases cover owner isolation, oversized counters, absent UI source, unavailable method corpus, reference-only methods, cloud restrictions, Tutor read scope, literal queries and bounds. The UI fixture preserves an edited source Preview, original file bytes, inquiry wording and method scratch; opens the real calculator and existing Atlas views; verifies stable menu targets and action identities; preserves cabinet selection and the five-pin policy; retains poem; and closes without jobs, provider requests or native tool invocations. Three actual screenshots include the 1366 by 768 layout and a scrollable detail panel.

All 683 prior operation schemas and scopes and all 112 tool targets remain unchanged. `ledger.explore` is the one added read operation. The settings count remains 26. Discovery's five protocol-bound service files remain byte identical to the baseline.

## Next

Move the existing machine monitors into the right column and connect Slate activity with the ordered operations queue, preserving the established Nice, ordering, dependency and owned STOP controls. This will also free header width on compact displays. Integrate the cabinet selection into the right-column presentation; Object Glass currently can retain its earlier file context while Explore separately carries the checked cabinet selection. Contextual command eligibility/ranking beyond the current deterministic suggestions, complete settings/memory adapters, native application handoff and the session-exit footer remain open work.

The owner can review the main UI once these pieces form a coherent whole. HATCH remains 0/6 fully accepted; integrated acceptance remains 4/6. Real-model/native I05 and owner-host I06 remain open. This cloud/offscreen slice does not establish a live ThinkPad, iPhone, model-choice, scheduler or scientific acceptance result.

INTEGRATION-01 (November 4, 2026): the five choices remain first; a Services row, capability groups and a session footer follow; see docs/HATCH_INTEGRATION_01.md.

WORKSHOP-01, DESKTOP-01 work item (November 5, 2026): the Explore word no longer repeats the six capability groups (Hatch is the doorway); it keeps Explore the workshop…, the For <record> suggestions and Find saved work…, and Return, Enter and F1 work on both popups. The Explore tab says Workspace available instead of Open workspace, shows the presentation kind in its Kind column and no longer prints registration totals; the Files row opens the Files workspace; see docs/HATCH_DESKTOP_01.md.

# HATCH INTEGRATION 01

November 4, 2026 · UTC

Complete checkpoint over SERVICE-01. This is the fourth and final estimated cloud development pass: focused integration and debugging across the completed HATCH slices. It integrates the accepted capability-launcher role into Hatch, closes the remaining per-category settings audit, repairs the service-cycle, Operations, installer and startup readback that the integration review found untruthful or fragile, and makes the shipped release check follow the HATCH checkpoint instead of failing on a historical comparison. Nothing here is native, HATCH, I05, I06 or owner-host acceptance.

## Hatch as the capability launcher

Hatch keeps its five original choices first: New Idea, New Project, On, Off and Reboot, with the same action objects, order and service routes. Below them a Services line shows the current service summary and opens the existing Background service room. Six capability groups follow: Work, Reason, Instruments, Programs, Knowledge and Configuration. Each row is one of the presentation adapters behind the existing read-only ledger.explore projection over the capability catalogue; the catalogue, the adapters and the workspace factories are the same ones Explore uses, and Explore the workshop… remains the broad discovery route. A separator and the session footer close the menu. Every entry is created once, so positions and identities are stable; opening the menu refills only the group submenus.

One service refresh and one ledger.explore read happen when the menu opens, and the menu holds still while it is open. The one-second service timer never reads the catalogue. Opening a row is navigation only: it goes through the existing open_instrument route, which rechecks availability and opens the original factory inside a retained view. Hatch dispatches no operation other than the read ledger.explore. If that read fails, the groups are hidden and one disabled row carries the message; the five choices, the Services line and the footer keep working.

A row shows only what was observed. Its text is the adapter title plus, in this order and only when true: unavailable (the row is then disabled), open, N running, N queued, N interrupted, and for the local model ready, stopped or no model selected. Its tooltip gives the description, the view state and tool prerequisite state, the owner's own job counts, the local-model state, the sentence "Qualification: not assessed on this host. Opening runs no tool." and the room statement below. Registration counts are never shown. The words mean exactly this:

| shown | asserts | does not assert |
| --- | --- | --- |
| row enabled | every module the route opens is present and the family has registered operations | that the view renders without error |
| unavailable | a required adapter module is missing or unsafe, named in the tooltip | — |
| Tools: Use existing controls | no job tool has this prefix | — |
| Tools: Not assessed | job tools exist without a native profile | readiness |
| Tools: Detected · checks remain | an executable was found on PATH or a pinned archive verified; version unmeasured | that it runs |
| Tools: Needs setup: a, b | passive discovery failed for the named executables or runtimes | — |
| N running / queued | the owner's durable job records in those states, bounded | live processes |
| N interrupted | the owner's job records in the Interrupted state | — |
| open | a center tab of that workspace class exists | that it belongs to the selected record |
| ready / stopped / no model selected | the local-model status: ready means the owned worker's process identity matches the selection | quality or context occupancy |
| Services · summary | the service-cycle snapshot summary; admission and confirmed stop stay distinct | that services are stopped when new work is merely held |

Six presentation adapters were added for the native tool families that already had tabs, navigation routes and passive detection: KiCad, KiBot, ngspice, Yosys, nextpnr & Trellis and HDL simulation. They form the Programs group, which is what makes "installed programs" a truthful part of the launcher: their readiness words come from the catalogue's existing passive detection, nothing is executed by opening a row, and version and licence stay unmeasured. In this container none of the executables is present, so each Programs row's tooltip reads Tools: Needs setup with the missing programs named (the row text itself carries only the title and the observed suffixes); on a host with the tools installed the same tooltips read Detected · checks remain. KiCad without an attached project shows the existing project-required dialog and says so in its tooltip. The adapter count is 21. Activity & receipts now opens the Work trail room, a real center tab, instead of returning the activity strip; Calculate & compare and Laboratory now require every module their route actually opens before they read as available; interrupted jobs are counted separately instead of disappearing from the counts.

Three defects in the shared Explore code were fixed on the way: the Explore button created five new submenus on every opening and never deleted them; the Explore tab left its result list disabled after a failed refresh; and a second New Idea stacked a second capture sheet instead of raising the visible one (closed sheets are now released as well). Group submenus now show their tooltips, which they never did. Both menus read the local-model state the same guarded way, so the same stored state gives the same word in Hatch and in Explore, and the word "state unavailable" appears only when the read actually failed. The catalogue read caches file digests by path, size, modification time, change time and inode, so a menu opening costs about 0.08 s here instead of 0.17 s; any change to the file recomputes. While the menu is open a service transition changes tooltips only; the Services line and the popup geometry hold still until the next opening, and a summary too long for the line is carried in full by its tooltip.

## Session footer decision

The footer has one live item and three items shown unavailable. The live item reads Return to Debian when the program runs under LS_XSESSION.sh, which now exports ARC_LEDGER_XSESSION=1, and Exit Ledger from an existing desktop or Windows, where no session of Ledger's own ends. It opens the existing Leave Ledger & Slate? review, whose default is Continue working, and then the ordinary close: Save or Discard for each modified editor, the return copy, local model and tracked command shutdown, session save and lease release. In the dedicated session the X session then ends and the Debian text login returns; the computer stays on, and START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh reports the exit status Ledger recorded. A service cycle in progress is recorded as interrupted, and the tooltip says so while a cycle is draining or stopping; Hatch → Off remains the graceful service stop.

Log Out, Restart Computer and Shut Down Computer are present so the footer keeps the shape the owner asked for, but they are disabled with a tooltip that says Ledger never logs out, restarts or powers off the computer and points to the console after Return to Debian. The reasons are recorded here: Hatch issues no operating-system session or power command (a hard boundary of this product); the dedicated session has no session manager, so logging out of a text login is the console's own exit; logind and polkit rights are unqualified on the owner host; Reboot already means Ledger services and a live Restart Computer beside it would make the word ambiguous; a power command would bypass the save prompts. The Hatch module imports no process facility and a test greps its source for one; the Qt check holds subprocess, os.system and QProcess.startDetached while every footer action is triggered.

The test the Interface Companion asked for: LS_XSESSION.sh runs START_OFFICE.sh once in the foreground, propagates Ledger's exit status, and its exit trap ends the window manager; no loop, unit, autologin or xinitrc restarts Ledger. A shell test with stubbed window manager and Office demonstrates it for exit statuses 0 and 3. This is a test result on this container, not owner-host acceptance of the minimal Debian startup, which stays open.

## Rooms by entrance and Off when already off

Workspaces opened from Hatch or Explore are retained rooms: inserted at the left, never replacing the edited source Preview, not counted among the five pins. The same workspace class opened from a top menu is a Preview or pin as before. This asymmetry protects the Preview on the most common entrance; it is now stated in the row tooltips, in the Pin tooltip and here.

Off is disabled while the recorded phase is already OFF, with a tooltip that says services are already off and On enables new work. This is a deliberate tightening of the Hatch enable rule: a second Off used to record a redundant cycle and two more journal entries without any observable change. The conservative rules for On during draining and stopping are unchanged.

## Service cycles and Operations readback

The service snapshot now reads only non-terminal job rows, so finished work no longer costs a process-identity probe per record every second; with three hundred completed records carrying exited worker identities the one-second drain costs about two milliseconds instead of seconds. Paused agenda and idle-study timers restart after a failed or interrupted cycle and whenever admission is observed enabled again, so a Settings re-enable followed by Resume no longer strands them until a restart. A corrupt or partial cycle row makes the service status unavailable without taking down the Operations queue, raising from the timer every second or repeating the status message every tick; the cycle row is validated field by field when read. A failure after a successful start no longer downgrades a completed cycle to incomplete; the restore request runs in its own guarded step and records its own failure. Save cancelled or save failed before a cycle is reported as "not started" rather than as an incomplete cycle. The hold message names running records that have no live worker. The service details room says observed running once an owned worker is seen for the requested model, and request failed when the request's job ended without completing. The On note no longer asserts phone state it did not observe. The lifecycle driver is stopped and joined when the window closes. Tracebacks are logged where the driver has to swallow an exception to fail a cycle. The ledger.operations result keeps every key; an unreadable cycle row now yields an unavailable services block instead of a failed read.

## Settings: the hardware category views

hardware.category_views is the forty-first genuine setting. It is the existing per-pane Auto view / Details / Thumbnails preference of the hardware overview, stored in the same connected-profile field it always used, with the same value shape and no migration. It appears under Ledger → Workspace → Hardware with its own map editor, is written through the single-key ledger.settings.set route with the row revision, and is read back map-aware: no open pane, applied when every open pane shows the saved mode, pending desktop otherwise. The panes write only on an explicit change, never on refresh, and follow an outside change (Slate, the editor, Undo, Default) without a second journal entry. The seventeen-key batch contract is unchanged and rejects the new key, as it rejects favorites. The forty prior definitions are byte-identical to SERVICE-01, proven by a text comparison in the tests; the operation registry digest is unchanged because settings are not part of it.

Profiles written before this pass carry an explicit Auto view entry for every pane that was ever visited; the editor round-trips those entries unchanged, so opening it is never an unsaved edit, and the summary counts only panes that are not at Auto view as customized. A refused pane save returns the pane to the saved mode so the readback stays applied rather than pending.

The remaining audit is closed in docs/SETTINGS_INVENTORY_06.md. The Orange Book automatic-update switch is the one other genuine preference found; it is explicitly retained in its original control with its reason recorded. Four connected-profile fields that were written but never restored (library sections, typing target, console mode and history, pill link) now have bounded loaders, and the console history is capped. The companion overlay's position fields are classified as live workspace state, correcting the earlier "retired" wording. Settings robustness was improved alongside: a corrupt priority file or a tampered Kernel-table row reads as a store-unavailable row that Default can repair instead of failing the whole settings read (a file the program cannot read at all is reported without that promise), Kernel-table values are validated on read, orphaned journal rows no longer break history, stale consumer receipts are pruned, and the visual-versus-policy readback rule is derived from each definition's store instead of a key list.

## Startup and installation truth

INSTALL_LS.py never prints a bare "Installed." again. Its final line names what happened: program extracted and verified, runtime imports verified, Debian prerequisites installed or skipped with the reason, minimal-session prerequisites present or missing, and that owner display and native or model qualification remain separate. It passes --yes to the Debian installer only when given, says beforehand when no terminal is attached, and reads INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh's new exit status 3 (PREREQUISITES_SKIPPED) honestly. Chunk metadata in RELEASE_PARTS.json is validated before anything is written, unreferenced chunk files are refused, a write-only chunk mode is refused and a missing mode falls back to ordinary file permissions, an unwritable containing folder is named before staging, an empty parent chain created by a failed run is removed, and every failure reads "Installation needs attention". --plan --extract-only lists the one step it performs and no start command. The restored tree from the SERVICE-01 media was compared file by file with the pristine tree after the change: identical.

LS_XSESSION.sh exports the session marker the footer reads and records Ledger's exit status in last-session.json under the state directory; START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh reads it after startx returns, prints "Ledger ended with status N" with the error log path when one exists, and exits with that status instead of startx's constant zero. It refuses arguments in the dedicated-session branch (they only work from an existing display), and it checks for an X server binary as well as startx, Fluxbox and the session bus. INSTALL_LEDGER.sh --quick prints the dedicated-session start line only when those commands are present. The launcher names its error log only after writing it and uses the product name in its alert. tools/package_release_parts.py now takes the checkpoint name as a required argument and places the start-here documents in the first volume. docs/MINIMAL_DEBIAN_INSTALL_01.md records all of it, including that --manifest-sha256 also pins copied USB media.

## Shipped checks and documentation

tools/check_release.py now routes by the manifest's hatch_checkpoint to tools/check_hatch.py. The new checker verifies the runtime payload and source bindings, compares the live registry against docs/HATCH_SERVICE_01_CAPABILITIES.json (generated in this pass from the unmodified SERVICE-01 tree, as its note says), compares the forty baseline setting definitions byte for byte, admits additions only when the checkpoint's RESULT records them, and reports the historical I04 comparison with its three documented additive extensions by name (work.investigate from I05, the ledger.navigate destination enum from ATLAS-01, ATLAS-02 and DISCOVERY-01, and ledger.settings.set's optional expected_revision from SETTINGS-01) instead of failing on the first of them. Its self-test runs a defined list of focused modules one by one and never a discovery over the whole folder. It states that registration counts and passing checks are not readiness or acceptance.

The four historical test failures were repaired: three stale literal settings counts now derive from the registry, and one historical module imports its fixtures by package path when run per module. The five historical Qt tools that aborted on stale literal counts or on the pre-cabinet navigator run again. README.md and GETTING_STARTED.md carry an INTEGRATION-01 banner with the current numbers above their historical layers and describe the shipped check as it now behaves; the six stage suites are listed as historical suites, four of which report documented additive schema extensions.

Definitions used in this document and its receipts: unchanged means identical bytes or schema; retained means still present, possibly different; extended means an additive schema change listed explicitly; added means a new definition recorded in the RESULT.

## Review before packaging

Every work item was reviewed by independent readers under three lenses before packaging: the hard boundaries (registry, settings, dispatcher, operating-system commands, fixed desktop controls, held launchers, historical evidence, acceptance words), correctness, and truthful readback. The readers returned thirty-one candidate findings, each with a path, a probe or a command; none was a boundary violation. Twenty-nine were real or cheap enough to fix and are fixed in this checkpoint (among them the Explore local-model word, the legacy Auto view entries in the new editor, the FAT-media installer message, the job-tool comparison and the legacy flags of the new checker, and captions that described tooltip text as if it were rendered); two were wording and were reworded. The service-cycle driver and the installer scripts were read line by line by the integrator as well.

## Focused evidence and limits

The evidence numbers for this pass are read from build/integration01_ui/focused-tests.json and the Qt reports there; HATCH_INTEGRATION_01_RESULT.json copies them. 205 focused tests passed in one per-module run of fourteen modules in 23.3 seconds: 76 cases are new (the four new modules launcher, hardware settings, startup scripts and release check, plus additions to the service-lifecycle, operations, settings-registry, settings-advanced and install-media modules) and 129 are related regressions. Three new actual offscreen Qt checks passed with 28 checks and 14 captures, each capture recorded with its hash and resolution: the launcher check (ten checks, seven captures, including the compact 1366 by 768 window), the service integration check (ten checks, four captures) and the hardware settings check (eight checks, three captures). All thirteen earlier shipped Qt tools were rerun green with their capture folders redirected under build/integration01_ui/regressions, so no historical evidence folder was rewritten; five of them had not been able to run at all since their literal counts went stale. Zero jobs were submitted, zero workers, models, providers or native tools started, and zero operating-system session or power commands issued; Kernel.launch and the provider request path were held throughout. The whole integrated suite was rerun by module as well: 321 tests, one failure, the I02 solver case that needs the pinned z3-solver this container does not have. tools/check_release.py reports PASSED on this tree after the seed and manifest rebuild, and its self-test PASSED over the same 205 tests.

All 690 public operation schemas and scopes and 112 job-tool targets are unchanged; the registry digest remains 9b28255cf4cd31117ece3edada8a737b569e9de996cbb32836e3b1040f92e1a1. The forty prior setting definitions are unchanged (their digest 2ee2a5ad6edc030ca98cf1d9e0d977ef3aaf1f637d0430214ecbcc6603fbfea5 is recorded in the SERVICE-01 capability baseline) and one setting was added. Packaging, volume sizes and the restored-volume checks are recorded in README_INTEGRATION_01.txt beside the release parts and in the discussion.

Four of the four estimated cloud development passes are complete. Owner-host validation and fixes remain, estimated at one or two passes when the ThinkPad and its inputs are available: the dedicated session start and Return to Debian on real display and input, the launcher's wording and density, real models and native tools, real service cycles with protected workers and owned Stop, pointer dragging, wireless and offline installation. Strict HATCH acceptance remains 0/6 and historical integrated acceptance 4/6. Exact-model/native I05 stays open and owner-host I06 has not started. Also open: the writing-marker experiment, the type bar's one-way minimum-width ratchet, and the host-client RemoteLink dialog's refresh after a coordinator-side revoke.

WORKSHOP-01, DESKTOP-01 work item (November 5, 2026): the five-choice-first order described above is superseded (HT01). The six tool groups lead Hatch; Explore the workshop…, New Idea, New Project, the Services row with a Ledger services submenu (the same On / Off / Reboot actions and routes) and the session footer follow, the footer’s three computer words being one disabled row marked not in this edition; every row carries the presentation contract (Opens · Slate can · Needs · Qualification · Context · Opening runs no tool) and the Programs rows are titled as Ledger’s checks; see docs/HATCH_DESKTOP_01.md.

# HATCH MEMORY-01

November 3, 2026 · America/Phoenix

Full checkpoint over RETURN-01. Existing private memory is now filed under
Ledger → Slate memory in the logical cabinet (or the cabinet root when the
catalogue has no Ledger object). Directions, Task memory, Procedures and the
Personality reference retain their original provider identities. No second
memory database, automatic collection, model training or execution authority
is introduced.

## Filing and reading

`memory.cabinet` is a shared read projection over the existing owner-filtered
`stacy_memory` table. The existing cabinet detail command resolves typed targets:
`memory:feedback:ID`, `memory:task:ID`, `memory:lesson:ID` and
`memory:profile:current`. Drawers are presentation views, not filesystem paths
or permissions. The original Memory and Settings workspaces remain linked from
the contextual action shelf; all earlier routes remain available.

The projection reads stored records with a 4 MiB cumulative payload budget,
128 KiB per record and at most 4,000 eligible rows; public result limit is
1–1,000 (cabinet default 300). It verifies stored digests and minimum shapes,
uses owner predicates before display, and skips corrupt records with a partial
view notice. Incomplete direction history disables guarded editing. No source
files, model inference or engineering/native tools run during browsing. Existing
Kernel operational auditing remains; this is not a zero-database-write claim.

Directions show saved wording, context, origin and history state: active,
superseded, undone, forgotten or incomplete. Profile state is reported separately;
an enabled profile does not establish actual model compliance or guarantee a
particular direction is selected in every response. A missing/corrupt profile is
not silently enabled or replaced. Imported reference bytes remain in the
existing store and are not returned as base64 by this projection.

Task filing retains the original task and checkpoint identifiers. Its explicit
Read task history action uses `memory.task`, with the original checkpoint/readback
and resume controls available in Memory. This slice does not reinterpret owner
task notes as measurements or evidence.

Procedure bodies are always withheld by the new browse/detail adapter, including
for previously reviewed procedures. It displays review metadata with bindings
NOT_RECHECKED. Check procedure sources invokes the existing `memory.lessons`
reader, which rechecks bindings and withholds unavailable text. A review label
does not establish source freshness, truth or permission to execute anything.
The original source-aware recall path is unchanged.

## Corrections and retained history

`memory.direction.revise` requires approve scope and is forbidden in Tutor mode.
The existing memory cloud-private prefix covers both new operations. Corrections
use a new caller-supplied event ID, an expected history digest, corrected wording
(1–300 characters) and an owner reason (1–200 characters). Blank wording/reasons
are refused by the existing text validators as well.

Inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, the adapter verifies the currently owned direction and
the complete inspected preference/context family, including reachable forgotten
history tombstones. A family change or inactive target blocks a new correction.
Unrelated contexts do not invalidate the inspected family. A matching event ID
may be retried without creating another event; different input under the same
ID remains a conflict.

The original feedback branch was extracted unchanged into `commit_feedback` so
both routes can use the same logic inside their own transaction. A correction
retains the prior agreement value and preference/context, uses the original
persistent owner-correction semantics, and supersedes the existing family while
leaving all prior event records untouched. The owner's reason becomes its
source reference. Existing Undo can remove the new correction from active
learning and reactivate the earlier directions. Forgotten text is not recovered
from its tombstone; separately retained recovery copies remain separate.

The cabinet editor uses a flat yellow poem passage and an explicitly labelled
reason. Revise this direction arms the shown history, then Keep correction and
history submits it. Historical/incomplete entries stay read-only here. There is
no direct overwrite of an old feedback row and no edit of the imported seed.

## Draft continuity

Unfinished correction text and its reason use the existing return-copy draft
shape (`text` and `title`; reason limit is within its 200-character title bound).
They survive record switches and a normal close/restart. The old history guard
is deliberately not silently recreated from a fresh record on reopening.
Recovered corrections have Keep disabled until the owner explicitly chooses
Use this shown history for the recovered correction. The backend still rejects
a further change after that review. Recovery writing does not itself apply a
memory correction.

The original code recovery, return thread, fixed Trash, visible Stop, monitors,
cabinet/settings navigation and five-item Hatch menu remain. No setting or
Explore workspace adapter was added; the new memory roles navigate to existing
Memory and Settings controls.

## Verification and limits

- 23 distinct focused checks passed in 3.858 seconds: nine new memory checks
  and fourteen Cabinet regressions. Cases cover private identity, mode/scope,
  cloud privacy, procedure-body withholding, stale history, unrelated contexts,
  idempotent retries, original Undo, forgotten/corrupt records and input bounds.
- Fourteen actual offscreen Qt checks passed. They exercise tree filing,
  correction saving through the original preference path, retained old words,
  pending drafts, stale edits, explicit refreshed review, procedure/task readers,
  fresh-desktop recovery and laptop layout. Five actual window captures are
  retained under `docs/MEMORY_01`.
- UI data is disposable: a small imported owner-reference fixture, explicit
  feedback, a task/checkpoint and a proposed procedure with an empty reference
  list. The missing-source behavior is a controlled boundary-test observation;
  the UI does not establish external-source freshness. No model, provider request,
  engineering/native tool, job submission, Master Stop or OS-priority change ran.
- The existing profile-context reader reflects the corrected direction, and
  the imported profile hash is unchanged. This proves the data path, not that a
  running model follows the direction. Full historical tests were not rerun.

Registry: 690 operations, all 688 baseline schemas/scopes unchanged; 112 job-tool
targets unchanged; 26 settings, 15 Explore workspace adapters and 12 authored
method profiles unchanged. Explore now projects 829 combined entries. Discovery's
protocol-bound files and all historical evidence remain unchanged.

HATCH remains 0/6 formally accepted; integrated remains 4/6 in retained evidence.
I05 exact-model/native and I06 owner-host gates remain OPEN. ThinkPad, live model,
native handoff, pointer dragging, live scheduling and owned Stop still need their
proper acceptance environment. The connected UI is ready for owner review.

Next bounded slice: expose remaining personality/memory configuration through
the shared settings hierarchy with current-value readback, preserving existing
approval, provenance and source-authority boundaries. Procedure/task editing
and profile import/review retain their established Memory workspace controls.

# HATCH MODEL-01

November 3, 2026 · America/Phoenix

Complete checkpoint over NAVIGATION-01. Three actual local-model launch defaults now appear under Settings → Slate → Local model: context tokens, CPU threads and memory cap. Saved defaults, pending requests, recorded selection and running-worker readback remain distinct. The original model registration, qualification, activation, restore, cancellation and reply-protection routes remain authoritative.

## Real defaults and explicit loading

The defaults are context 2048 tokens, four CPU threads and Auto memory (zero). Context accepts 512–8192; threads 1–32; memory is zero or 512–262144 MiB. These fields persist in the existing Kernel settings table as ledger.brain.context, ledger.brain.threads and ledger.brain.memory_mb, with the ordinary shared settings journal. They are genuine new launch preferences, not duplicate copies of brain.selection or brain.worker.

Apply, Default and Undo update a future launch preference. They do not rewrite the recorded model configuration, replace the worker, start inference or enable Slate. The existing expected-value/revision checks and atomic value/history commit remain. A manual memory value between zero and 512 is refused without losing the draft.

New default-only requests use the existing Brain panel's 2048/four/Auto defaults across all model submission routes. This unifies the former API thread fallback with the panel's explicit four-thread default. Explicit per-request options still override defaults. Earlier queued requests retain their original behavior.

The Settings panel offers Reload saved defaults, Restore previous model and Open model controls. Reload resolves the shown Auto preference and passes explicit options to the original Brain launch/watch route. An intervening displayed-state change requires review. Restore uses the original brain.restore operation and its recorded prior configuration. Model identity and registration remain stateful actions in the original model chooser rather than a fabricated scalar setting.

## Frozen requests and retries

At the existing Kernel queue commit, new activation and qualification requests receive a brain_launch snapshot. It merges saved defaults with explicit request options and applies the original configuration validator. Auto memory is resolved against measured RAM at submission. The existing architecture, template, declared-context and memory checks still apply.

The snapshot records concrete context, threads, memory cap and model identity. Running the job uses those values and rechecks the original configuration constraints. Editing defaults after submission does not change a waiting request. If available RAM later becomes insufficient, validation refuses the request rather than silently increasing its budget.

The original request_spec is unchanged, including the existing idempotency comparisons. A retry of the same request key returns the original job and frozen options even after defaults change. Direct jobs.submit, brain.model.use, brain.model.qualify and brain.restore share this behavior. Restore's explicit prior configuration takes precedence over current defaults.

Jobs queued before this pass have no snapshot. They keep their original request options and original configuration behavior. A malformed new snapshot or changed model identity is refused. No public operation schema accepts arbitrary internal snapshot fields.

## Current values and recovery

Settings reads the stored defaults, a bounded caller-owned request view, the last recorded selection and the existing worker receipt. Running values require both the calling owner's worker receipt and its matching process-start identity; they are not inferred from a stored selection or a queued job. An unknown, stopped, other-owner, mismatched or incomplete worker configuration supplies no effective value.

The view returns only model IDs, job IDs, numeric options and bounded state metadata. Worker credentials, key-file paths, ports and raw error bodies are withheld. Optional activity sharing omits the new model rows and definitions. Default cloud proposals refuse their explicit effective/history/write routes through the existing privacy checker. Reads remain caller-scoped and changes retain direct owner approval; Tutor mode cannot change them.

The original failed-handover path remains: a failed candidate can reload the previous live worker; owner cancellation leaves it stopped; an active reply prevents the handover from stopping that worker. A successful original restore probe adds its request ID to the existing worker receipt. The Settings view reports RESTORED_PREVIOUS only from that receipt while the owned worker is still observed. A failed restore does not claim running values. These are process/configuration receipts, not answer-quality or engineering qualification.

## The original model panel

The existing model controls read saved defaults into fields that have no local override. A local edit stays visible when a saved default changes elsewhere. Use saved launch defaults deliberately clears those overrides; Edit launch defaults in Settings returns to the canonical key. A local Auto override is resolved to concrete options before submission, including when the saved cap is manual.

The affected numeric passages use flat yellow writing surfaces, with no spinner buttons; the model chooser uses the paper action palette. The shared Settings editor retains its Room policy and source Preview. Its model status refresh updates request/worker information while preserving an edited default and its original revision. Settings drafts and local model-panel overrides remain desktop-local.

Model submission messages now say Requested model change/inspection/qualification or Requested previous model. Model-job labels describe activation/inspection/qualification with their actual event state; accepting a queued request no longer says that the model has already switched.

## Verification

Evidence in docs/MODEL_01 includes:

- 41 focused tests passed in 4.763 seconds: 13 new model/control boundary cases and 28 related settings regressions. Cases include atomic history, owner/Tutor/privacy, invalid values, frozen Auto/defaults, explicit overrides, direct jobs.submit, qualification, restore, idempotent retries, legacy jobs, corrupt optional data and saved/requested/worker separation.
- Controlled worker stand-ins exercise successful activation from frozen options, failed-candidate restoration, failed restore, cancellation and the running-reply guard. No real GGUF, native model process or model generation is used by these cases.
- 11 final actual Qt checks passed, with five screenshots including 1366 × 768. They exercise Apply/Undo/refusal, stale default revision, reload through the original panel, local overrides, retained source writing and compact controls.
- The final UI run holds every Kernel launcher. It submits one actual queued fixture request, observes its frozen fields, then cancels it. Zero worker processes, model generations, provider requests and native invocations occur in that final run.
- All 690 operation schemas/scopes, all 112 job-tool targets and all prior 31 setting definitions are unchanged. There are now 34 genuine connected settings. The registry digest remains 9b28255cf4cd31117ece3edada8a737b569e9de996cbb32836e3b1040f92e1a1.
- AST comparison verifies that the original Kernel is unchanged except for the atomic launch snapshot/validation relocation, and the model worker is unchanged except for its frozen-option reader and restoration receipt. The behavioral checks supplement that structural comparison.
- No full historical suite was rerun. Native execution, actual-model response quality, live scheduling and owner-host acceptance remain separate.

Complete packaging retains all earlier source, modes and evidence, including the prior 15-view UI review captures. It refreshes the existing source bindings and release manifest. Archive checksum and post-package preservation checks are recorded in the separate progress discussion.

## Next

This lands the model-settings portion of the four estimated remaining development passes. Next is the audit and connection of remaining presentation, favorites and view preferences, followed by final Hatch/desktop integration and a focused integration/debug pass. The numbered 15-view review remains available for owner wording/spacing choices.

HATCH acceptance stays 0/6; historical integrated acceptance stays 4/6. I05 exact-model/native and I06 owner-host remain OPEN while the ThinkPad is unavailable. This pass does not close those gates through metadata or simulated worker checks.

# HATCH NAVIGATION-01

November 3, 2026 · America/Phoenix

Complete checkpoint over SETTINGS-03. The focused workspace now keeps the left column aligned with Cabinet, Settings and checked Explore context. The owner can review 15 numbered actual application views together. This is a navigation and review slice; exact-model/native I05 and owner-host I06 remain OPEN.

## The three observed gaps

A real Qt probe reproduced three continuity problems in the preceding build: an explicit Settings destination could stay hidden by a previous filter, a focused Cabinet record could leave the left column showing Settings, and the Cabinet word could leave the Settings editor active in the center. NAVIGATION-01 connects those transitions through one small desktop controller.

The controller follows the current widget. Focusing Settings selects its current canonical setting key. Focusing a Cabinet record reveals its exact placement. Explore reveals only the checked context returned by its existing read operation; other workspaces retain the last cabinet anchor without declaring that the workspace belongs to it.

Following a view does not call its load_key or record-open form again. Settings values, draft revisions, cabinet writing and explicit read results remain with their existing widgets. A new Settings key or record still loads through its original route.

## Writing and the left column

Settings is now a retained Room, alongside Cabinet and Explore. Opening it from an edited source Preview no longer requires replacing that Preview. It does not consume any of the five pins or create a second Settings editor. Explicitly closing a workspace and its existing draft behavior retain their established controls. Settings drafts are still desktop-local; no restart recovery for them is added.

The Cabinet word returns to its retained record room without rereading over its form. If there is no retained record room, it opens the existing selected placement, or the cabinet root if that selection is unavailable. The Settings word retains its original shared editor route.

Explicit destination selection expands the required ancestor path and clears a filter only when it excludes that destination. Matching filters and unrelated branch folds remain. Resize handling keeps an expanded selected row in view; deliberately folded ancestors are not expanded by a resize. Selection and expansion continue using the existing validated Session presentation state. No navigation-history database or new preference is introduced.

The central record room now says FILED IN and shows its containing drawer path. The heading names the record itself. Show in cabinet refreshes the bounded cabinet projection and reveals the exact placement without reopening the form. The path follows placement parents; a second-project reference stays under that second project and continues resolving the same canonical record. It is not redirected to the owning home.

An unavailable or out-of-view placement clears the misleading current highlight and reports the bounded-view limit. It does not substitute another record or invent a filing relationship. Existing views and workspace search remain available. The controller reads existing metadata; source/master freshness and engineering applicability retain their explicit checks.

## Menus and review

The existing Work, Revise, Tools, Arrange, Commands, Rules, Properties and Guide proposals retain their original menu objects, actions, shortcuts and routes. The five-command Hatch and separate Explore entrance remain compatible. Their final naming, mark and consolidation are review choices. On/Off/Reboot still mean Ledger services; host logout/power behavior is not implemented by this slice.

The review includes Cabinet, a cross-project reference, memory Settings, a stale-edit message, Hatch, Work, Arrange, Rules, the record context menu, Explore, the method Atlas, Operations, Context, Return thread and a compact writing desk. See HATCH_UI_REVIEW_01.md for the numbered index.

All captures use real offscreen Qt widgets. Popup views combine the window grab with the visible live popup grab at its actual position. There is no generated mock interface. The review fixtures use disposable projects, an imported owner reference, source writing and three real pending Agenda records. No worker is running and no tool job is submitted. The pending queue illustrates scheduling metadata rather than live-process acceptance.

All empty writing invitations remain poem. The paper palette, fixed left-panel Trash, visible Stop, monitors and return thread remain available, including at 1366 × 768.

## Evidence

The evidence folder docs/NAVIGATION_01 contains the final navigation report/log, 15 captures, the related Explore regression report/log and captures, registry comparison and source coverage.

- 20 final navigation/Qt checks passed, including edited-Preview preservation, both draft types, exact revisions, filter/fold behavior, the Cabinet switch, reference placement, bounded-view refusal, stale Apply, popup rendering, Explore/Atlas routes, queue/context, return recovery and compact resize.
- 15 related Explore Qt checks passed. No backend implementation changed, no new unit suite was added, and the full historical suite was not rerun.
- Original source bytes/mode, imported-reference hash, idea ownership, the five-pin policy and Hatch routes were verified through the UI sequence.
- Provider requests, job submission and OS-priority changes were guarded and never called. No model generation or native application/tool invocation occurred. Pointer dragging, live CPU scheduling and owned Master Stop are not qualified here.
- All 690 operation schemas/scopes, all 112 job-tool targets and all 31 setting definitions compare exactly with SETTINGS-03. Registry digest remains 9b28255cf4cd31117ece3edada8a737b569e9de996cbb32836e3b1040f92e1a1.

Complete packaging refreshes the existing source bindings and manifest while retaining earlier source, modes and evidence. The external discussion records post-package archive checks without embedding a self-referential archive checksum.

## What remains

The connected UI is now ready for owner review by screen number. HATCH acceptance remains 0/6 and historical integrated acceptance remains 4/6 because the actual acceptance gates are distinct from implementation progress. I05 exact-model/native and I06 owner-host stay OPEN while the ThinkPad is unavailable.

Next development is the remaining local-model configuration adapters, with explicit requested, worker-effective, reload and restore states. Model activation and handover keep their existing authority and qualification routes. UI wording/spacing changes can proceed against the numbered review set. Final launcher consolidation, broader settings coverage and actual host/native acceptance remain explicit work.

INTEGRATION-01 (November 4, 2026): the five choices remain first; a Services row, capability groups and a session footer follow; see docs/HATCH_INTEGRATION_01.md.

# HATCH OPERATIONS-01

November 2, 2026 (America/Phoenix). Full checkpoint over EXPLORE-01. This connects the right-column observations and existing operation controls while preserving their original authority.

## The operations column

The right column now has Operations, Context and Slate faces. The original CPU/GPU/RAM/TXT monitor widget has moved from the header into a fixed strip above them. It stays visible while those faces change. The header has room for all eight menu words at 1366 by 768, and the original Master Stop button is visible at the upper right. Its existing QAction, shortcut, confirmation and owned-process controller remain in place. Nice remains available through its original popup route.

Operations contains local-model and admission status, an explicit cabinet-selection card, active jobs, the ordered Agenda, visible waiting reasons, accessible Earlier/Later controls and the existing priority controls. Its body scrolls at compact sizes. The existing Slate AI admission switch is retained behind AI admission, with its original store and behavior. It is no longer a permanent header toggle. The original Agenda and Work trail remain reachable.

The current cabinet selection is a named anchor, including while a file editor is active; it does not assert that the file belongs to that record. Context follows an active Cabinet/Explore record through a checked read of its original identity. It presents that record rather than an earlier Object Glass file. Returning to other workspaces retains the original inspector and Object Glass state and routes. Selection reads do not recheck source or master freshness.

## Shared read model

`ledger.operations` is the one new read operation. It composes the existing Agenda, work-admission and local Brain stores with a caller-checked cabinet selection and source-labelled host observations. Its compact queue records omit private program bodies and output snapshots. It is included in the existing cloud-private boundary.

The Agenda's existing view may reconcile due/missed scheduling metadata and initialize its component stores. The new projection preserves those established read semantics. It never starts a runner, submits a tool job, activates a model, changes priority or creates a grant. The supplied idle flag is observation context for queue checks; the actual runner rechecks its own environment at execution.

The Agenda's Kernel-job projection now reuses the canonical record-access filter, so another owner's private jobs are not disclosed through the right column or legacy Agenda/Nice views. Existing shared engineering records keep their original visibility policy. A dependency lookup also checks the item's owner, preventing a malformed cross-owner dependency from releasing an item based on another owner's record.

## Three distinct controls

Agenda position remains the persistent queue order. Dragging and Earlier/Later use the original `agenda.reorder` operation; crossing a scheduling tier adopts the destination tier, as the existing implementation specifies. The Agenda tier slider chooses now, normal or background. Background/idle requirements, dependency completion, future due time, pause, another running Agenda item, work holds, service admission and applicable AI admission are shown separately.

The first item passing those queue checks is named above the list. This is preliminary scheduling state; runtime, model, source and continuing-work grant checks remain authoritative. A blocked row stays in the owner's order with its reason even if another row passes the checks first. An ordered list is not permission to run an item.

Kernel job CPU nice uses the original `jobs.nice` operation and its 0–19 range. A queued value is labelled requested and applies at the next worker start. A verified running-process readback is labelled as an observation; an unverifiable, unsupported or unavailable process reports no live value and has no enabled adjustment control. Read-only/Tutor callers cannot be advertised as eligible to adjust priority. An OS refusal retains the actual readback and displays the refusal. A queued record with an old PID still shows its next-start request without measuring or modifying that old process.

CPU niceness controls CPU competition for tracked owned processes and verified descendants. It does not claim GPU, memory or I/O scheduling effects. The global Background CPU preference retains its existing owner-operated controller and next-use limitations.

## Observations

`host_observations.py` supplies bounded, Qt-independent readings of the current Ledger host. CPU utilization requires two valid increasing aggregate `/proc/stat` samples. Missing, reset or inconsistent samples clear the percentage. RAM uses MemTotal and MemAvailable from `/proc/meminfo`; invalid or unavailable readings remain unavailable. GPU uses the busiest reported value among the bounded DRM samples and reports missing driver access honestly.

TXT remains unavailable because this runtime does not supply trusted live context occupancy. A declared context capacity, completion count or file length is not substituted. Each model response carries a sample time and identifies the current Ledger host rather than claiming acceptance on the owner's ThinkPad. These fields measure observations, not settings or engineering qualification.

## Verification

Evidence is under `docs/OPERATIONS_01`: 13 operation/observation boundary checks, 13 Explore regressions, 15 actual Qt offscreen checks and three affected screenshots. Boundary checks cover missing/reset counters, TXT semantics, private job/context filtering, dependency and idle checks, cross-owner dependencies, paused/held/service-off work, reordered tier adoption, queued CPU requests, verified-process rejection, OS refusal and read-only/cloud restrictions. OS priority behavior is tested using controlled readback/refusal mocks; no live OS priority is changed.

The Qt fixture contains three Agenda items and two clearly documented job-state fixture records. It starts no worker. It exercises the real shared commands through keyboard sliders and Earlier, confirms dependency waits after reordering, preserves source bytes and an edited document, switches all three faces, verifies original Stop references without invoking Stop, renders compact layout, preserves poem and closes without a leftover desktop lease. Host CPU/GPU/RAM observations in screenshots are from the cloud session, not the ThinkPad. No provider request, model generation, engineering tool invocation or tool job is run. The full historical suite was not rerun.

All 684 prior operation schemas and scopes and all 112 job tools remain unchanged. The new read operation brings the registry to 685, and Explore's combined view to 824 entries. The 15 workspace adapters, 12 authored method profiles and 26 settings remain. The five Discovery protocol-bound source files are unchanged, and all earlier code and evidence are preserved.

## Next

The main cabinet, Explore/menu and operations surfaces now form a connected first layout suitable for a cohesive UI review. Remaining interaction work includes broader contextual command eligibility/ranking, complete settings and memory adapters, final naming/launcher consolidation, the session-exit footer and shared native application handoff. Actual pointer-drag, live OS scheduling/owned STOP, native GUI and exact-model acceptance still need their proper host cases; these offscreen checks do not close them.

HATCH remains 0/6 fully accepted milestones; integrated acceptance remains 4/6 in the retained evidence. I05 model/native and I06 owner-host gates remain open. Continue with a bounded contextual-action slice and consolidate the UI review, while preserving the existing grants, worker ownership and original-file protections.

# HATCH PRESENTATION-01

November 3, 2026 · UTC

Complete checkpoint over MODEL-01. Five existing favorite groups and the existing Concern catalogue view now have named adapters in the shared Settings tree. The registry contains 40 genuine settings. All 34 earlier definitions, 690 operation schemas/scopes, 112 job-tool targets and the original favorite eligibility catalogue are retained unchanged.

## Favorites with a visible home

Settings → Ledger → Favorites offers Work, Revise, Arrange, Tools and Guide. Each group has three ordered selectors using the original command labels. No favorite is a deliberate empty slot; an empty group stays empty. Apply validates the original eligible IDs, at most three choices and no repeated command within a group. Invalid and stale drafts remain available. Default and Undo use the same shared history as the other settings.

The canonical keys are favorites.file, favorites.edit, favorites.view, favorites.options and favorites.help. Their backing values are the existing Session toolbar_favorites groups File, Edit, View, Options and Help. Serialization IDs and group keys remain stable even where the current shell uses different visible words. The single-key Set route is shared by the legacy customize control, typed Slate and Settings. The original public batch contract remains restricted to its previous 17 Session keys; its schema has not expanded.

Commands → Favorite commands makes the saved choices useful in the paper shell. The menu adds the original QAction objects, preserving their shortcuts, enabled states, checks and command routes. Opening the menu does not trigger them. A command saved in two groups appears once in the combined menu, without rewriting either group. Membership refreshes before opening; a visible menu keeps its membership until it closes. The retired icon strip stays hidden.

A version-two marker distinguishes explicit current choices from old factory groups. Reading an old profile does not rewrite its bytes. Pre-versioned exact old factory groups retain their previous migration behavior. The first explicit favorite write normalizes the other legacy groups once, then records literal version-two choices. Selecting a group that happens to match an old factory group now remains intentional rather than silently being migrated again. Unknown IDs never become callable commands.

## Existing views without changing filing

Settings → Ledger → Cabinet → Existing catalogue view adapts preferences.view in the original connected Concern catalogue. Choices retain their existing IDs: works, offices, work and archive. The editor shows Properties & works, Offices, Work & ideas and Archive. The setting is scoped to that connected personal catalogue profile, which can be shared by different workspace journals. It does not move records, change source authority, rename identities or choose logical cabinet parentage.

The existing view chooser journals the same setting. Consumer synchronization updates its hidden selector, the visible Showing sentence and the original catalogue tree. A consumer-driven selector update does not write the setting again. The logical cabinet's saved selection and expansion remain intact; existing per-view expansion behavior is retained.

The optional store is read without initialization. Missing, corrupt or unsupported catalogue data marks this setting unavailable while other settings remain usable. A Set cannot create a replacement catalogue. The original SDK view setter and the shared adapter both stamp an opaque revision in the catalogue transaction, including same-value writes. Shared writes recheck that stamp at the actual SQLite write, so another workspace or a legacy chooser changing away and back still invalidates a stale draft and Undo.

## Delivery and readback

Session favorites retain the existing locked-profile delivery and journal recovery path. Catalogue and Kernel history are separate SQLite stores: there is no claim of one cross-database atomic commit. A private delivery receipt is written before the external catalogue change; the value and new stamp commit together in the catalogue, then the shared journal commits. Recovery records an interrupted delivered change only when its exact value and opaque stamp match. A before-write failure is not recovered as applied. A later conflicting change, disconnected catalogue or unavailable store is retained for review. Recovery never blindly replays a preference.

Settings distinguishes saved policy from desktop application. Favorites require a live matching desktop receipt. Catalogue application requires the original Existing views consumer. With no live consumer, effective remains unobserved. No model, provider, process-priority change or engineering job is launched by these settings.

## Focused evidence

- 44 focused settings tests passed: 16 new presentation/store/concurrency cases and 28 related shared-settings regressions. The full historical suite was not rerun.
- 11 actual Qt checks passed in an isolated offscreen application. All Kernel launchers and the provider entry point were held; zero jobs, model workers, generations, provider requests or native tools started.
- Five real captures cover ordered favorites, a rejected duplicate draft, the actual Favorite commands popup, the Offices catalogue presentation and the compact editor. Four are 1920 × 1200; the compact view is 1366 × 768. Popup evidence combines real window and visible popup grabs at their actual positions.
- Qt checking found and fixed an action-lifetime issue in menu clearing, a stretched single-value editor and a stale Showing sentence. Final checks preserve every original action, including the dock-owned Inspector toggle, and confirm that opening the menu triggers none.
- Registry comparison against the original MODEL-01 source confirms all old schemas/scopes, targets, 34 definitions and favorite IDs are unchanged. Digest: 9b28255cf4cd31117ece3edada8a737b569e9de996cbb32836e3b1040f92e1a1.

The paper palette, lowercase poem empty hints, fixed Trash in the bottom-right of the left panel, Stop, monitors, edited source Preview and return thread are retained. Final package verification and its checksum are recorded in the separate discussion after packaging.

## Boundaries and next work

This is development pass two of the four-pass cloud estimate following NAVIGATION-01. Two planned cloud development passes remain: Hatch/desktop service integration, then focused integration/debug and preparation for owner review. Further findings can change that estimate. Host validation/fixes are separately estimated at one or two passes once suitable owner hardware is available.

All-settings coverage is not declared complete. Per-category hardware display preferences remain in their original per-pane controls and require an adapter decision. Geometry, selected records, tree expansion and last surface are workspace state. Retired avatar position/collapse fields remain compatibility data. Runtime/deployment inputs and credentials keep their existing controlled routes.

Strict HATCH acceptance remains 0/6; historical integrated acceptance remains 4/6. Exact-model/native I05, owner-host I06, live scheduling, pointer dragging and owned Master Stop acceptance remain open. Offscreen checks and worker stand-ins do not close these gates. Continue with complete source/evidence checkpoints, preserve every prior capability and record, and keep all original qualification and authority boundaries.

# HATCH readiness and bounded checks

Run `bash HATCH_CHECK.sh` from the extracted program folder. It creates a new dated report directory, prints the missing prerequisites and saves `readiness.json` and `READ_ME.txt`. Exit 2 means a blocked prerequisite, failed diagnostic or cleanup needing attention; it is not a successful acceptance result. An existing output directory is refused.

The default command reuses Doctor, the math package pins, the Office/Java probe, protected Python and inference-runtime probes. It inspects an existing selected model through read-only SQLite, or accepts `--model /path/to/reference.gguf`. Model checks hash the explicit file with a 60-second hashing budget. No model weights or packages are downloaded, no workspace is initialized and no Kernel job or model generation starts. Small version/socket/display probes run locally; Office/Java probes retain their existing timeouts. The report identifies the current execution host without assuming it is the owner ThinkPad.

Example report command:

```bash
bash HATCH_CHECK.sh --model /path/to/Qwen3.5-4B-Q4_K_M.gguf --output /path/to/new-readiness-report
```

For a different installed Python environment, set `LEDGER_PYTHON` to its Python executable. Install the versions in the existing `requirements-math.txt`, `requirements-qt.txt` and `requirements-experiments.txt` through the selected environment's normal package setup when the report identifies them as missing. Qt Core/Widgets importability is shown separately from Doctor's complete desktop package metadata. Presence does not qualify behavior.

Explicit trials are available after the selected gate passes:

```bash
bash HATCH_CHECK.sh --run model-diagnostic --model /path/to/reference.gguf --output /path/to/new-diagnostic
bash HATCH_CHECK.sh --run visible-calc --output /path/to/new-visible-check
bash HATCH_CHECK.sh --run model-family --budget-seconds 3600 --model /path/to/reference.gguf --output /path/to/new-family
```

The diagnostic and visible check default to a 600-second runner budget. A full model family requires an explicitly declared budget; 3600 above is an example, not a promise that every host will finish in that time. The existing frozen cases, expected results, grants, duplicate guard and first-failed-case stop are unchanged. Model/runtime identity remains the retained I05 Qwen3.5-4B reference SHA256 and b11669 CPU runtime. Other models retain their normal Ledger entry points.

Passing `--run` explicitly requests the chosen existing checker and its isolated synthetic fixture. The checker creates fresh scoped work orders and owner grants within that fixture. It does not act on the owner's project workspace. The visible check opens real owned Calc windows on a connectable X11 host and performs its scripted takeover checks; it is not an offscreen substitute or a general owner-device qualification.

The supervisor retains stdout, stderr, trial intent and the checker's result. Budget expiry first interrupts the runner, then uses existing PID/start-token ownership checks to stop verified descendants. Cleanup uses existing Kernel cancellation and model-stop paths only inside the newly created fixture. If exit cannot be confirmed, `CLEANUP_REQUIRED` remains visible. Budget expiry produces `BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`, preserves partial evidence and never becomes a passed family.

Readiness and diagnostic receipts never overwrite historical results or promote I05, I06 or HATCH acceptance. A completed family still needs semantic/evidence review; native ownership evidence and owner-ThinkPad I06 qualification remain separate gates.

# HATCH RETURN-01

November 2, 2026 · America/Phoenix

Full checkpoint over ACTIONS-01. This slice adds a **Return thread** to the
activity footer, a retained central session room, and an explicit leaving review.
It gives unfinished cabinet writing a return copy and reuses the original code
recovery store. Saved return writing is distinct from project records, source
files, engineering evidence and model memory. It is never executed as a command.

## What the owner sees

- Return thread in the persistent activity footer, also Ctrl+Alt+R and a window
  action discoverable by the existing command palette.
- A yellow poem writing passage: Next time, begin here. Keep for return saves
  the note and cabinet drafts and keeps current code recovery copies.
- Still on the desk: current open work and buffer-edit state. Go to selected
  work navigates to the same live tab without replacing a buffer.
- Cabinet writing to continue: readable current cabinet labels, stored-versus-
  current recovery status, review of exact writing and checked record reopening.
  If a record disappeared, recovery writing remains readable/copyable; it is not
  silently assigned to another record.
- Recorded activity from the existing Operations read, labelled as stored work
  states rather than a verified census of live processes.
- Review leaving: Continue working is focused initially. Keep and close uses
  the ordinary close path with return capture. Close without a new return copy
  explicitly preserves the earlier stored copy and may lose newer thread/draft
  writing. Existing file-save prompts still apply. Closing LS leaves Linux on.

The page scrolls at laptop size. The original fixed Trash, host monitors,
Operations/Context/Slate, all Hatch items and the visible original Master Stop
remain. The return room uses graphite reading, pink actions and a flat yellow
writing passage. It introduces no new Hatch menu item or workspace setting.

## Shared saved state

`ledger.session.read` requires read scope. `ledger.session.keep` requires execute
scope and is forbidden in Tutor mode. Both are covered by a new cloud-private
session prefix. They route through the original Kernel/CLI/MCP machinery.
No new execution dispatcher, model worker or host-power operation is added.

The Kernel's existing workspace database holds one `session_handoffs` row per
principal identity. The row stores a note, cabinet draft IDs/titles/text, an
optional cabinet selection, a revision, a digest and a time. A read does not
create the handoff table. A keep validates the complete bounded payload and
compares the retained revision inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE. No-op keeps retain the
revision. A new keep increments it. Other owners and workspaces have separate
copies; no ownership is inferred from an ID in saved writing.

Limits: 8,000 note characters; 40 cabinet drafts; 60,000 text and 200 title
characters per draft; 256 KiB total canonical UTF-8 writing. Duplicate IDs,
extra fields, invalid modes, overflow and corrupt rows are refused without
truncating or overwriting the stored copy. SQLite non-text payloads and invalid
metadata are treated as integrity failures. A local digest is an integrity
check, not publisher authentication or evidence acceptance.

If a competing session has kept a newer copy, local writing remains in place.
Inspect stored copy reads its words without changing the current buffer or the
retained revision. Replace inspected return copy requires an explicit No-default
confirmation, then compares the exact inspected revision. Another intervening
change still blocks replacement. It never silently rebases a stale update.

## Desktop lifecycle

The controller restores the stored note and cabinet drafts into the existing
bridge draft map when the shell is installed. Returning to a cabinet record uses
that same map. No idea/project is created by restoration. ReturnTab can be
reopened through the existing deferred-tab mechanism after the controller is
installed; it does not override existing startup policy or recreate every old
workspace automatically.

Explicit Keep validates writing, writes dirty code buffers through the existing
RecoveryStore, then performs the guarded shared keep. Ordinary window close
runs existing concern/PDF and code-save decisions, then captures return writing
before shutdown steps. Return/recovery failure keeps the window open. The
explicit skip-new-copy choice bypasses only this new return-copy update, not
existing file prompts or ownership policies.

A relevant inconsistency is fixed: whole-window Discard now retains the code
buffer in RecoveryStore as tab-close Discard already did. It does not write the
source file, and final close cleanup does not remove that retained buffer.
The original model-stop, engineering shutdown, tracked command-tree handling,
execution lock, session/layout persistence and desktop lease close path remains.
Closing a client window is not a global cancellation receipt; separately hosted
work may continue, and actual owned-process Stop still uses its original control.

Coverage is explicit. Cabinet drafts and this note are kept at Keep or normal
close; changes since the last successful keep can be lost on a crash. Code
recovery retains its existing 2 MiB-per-buffer limit. Other workspace forms keep
their own save controls and are not claimed to be recovered by this slice. The
open-work list is bounded at 100 rows. This is not universal application hibernation.

## Verification

Nine focused boundary tests passed; the final run took 1.117 seconds. They cover
restart, owner/workspace/mode separation, revision conflict, no-op/clear behavior,
all-or-nothing bounds, malformed/non-text state and cloud-private rules.
Seventeen actual offscreen Qt checks passed. The runner opens two desktops in
sequence, checks a competing update through the real shared command, tests stale
and explicit replacement, cancels exit, forces a recovery-write refusal, tests
the explicit skip option and verifies a fresh desktop's restored writing and
recovery offer. Replacement confirmation uses a controlled Yes response. The
original recovery startup dialog's offer is observed with its modal interaction
suppressed; clicking its restore button is not new acceptance evidence.

Five actual Qt images show Thread, Compact, Leaving, Conflict and Returned. The
Leaving image is the actual dialog widget; the other four are window captures.
The UI fixture has two saved job-state records, with no running worker behind
them. No job is submitted, provider contacted, model run, engineering/native tool
invoked, Master Stop executed or OS priority changed. The full historical suite
was not rerun. Evidence is under `docs/RETURN_01`.

Registry: 688 operations; the 686 earlier operation schemas/scopes and all 112
job-tool targets are unchanged. Settings remain 26, Explore workspace adapters
15 and authored method profiles 12. Explore now projects 827 combined entries.
Discovery's protocol-bound files and all historical evidence remain unchanged.

## Remaining work

HATCH remains 0/6 formally accepted; integrated remains 4/6 in retained evidence.
I05 exact-model/native and I06 owner-host gates remain OPEN. Offscreen tests do
not qualify ThinkPad installation, native handoff, pointer dragging, live
scheduling, real model reasoning or owned-process Stop.

The connected interface is ready for a cohesive owner review. Next bounded
development: make Slate's saved directions and memory navigable alongside the
cabinet/settings hierarchy, with provenance and deliberate edit controls.
Complete settings/memory adapters, final menu choices and real-host qualification
remain; no completed cloud slice substitutes for those acceptance gates.
