# HATCH SERVICE 01

November 3, 2026 · America/Phoenix

Complete checkpoint over PRESENTATION-01. This pass integrates the existing Hatch On, Off and Reboot choices with durable cycle state, shared Settings history, graceful draining and visible Operations/service-detail readback. It also adds a verified release-parts installer, minimal Debian session scripts and the complete project specification requested by the owner.

## Service state and ownership

The trusted local service adapter stores its current cycle in the existing Kernel settings database. Off/Reboot atomically commit the cycle receipt and the false services-admission setting, including the normal shared setting journal entry. Running work is not emergency-held at this point. Queued jobs are cancelled by the original jobs.cancel route; running jobs, owned worker observations, tracked Qt commands and existing provider in-flight indicators keep the cycle draining.

Once drained, a guarded transaction applies the work hold and advances the cycle to stopping. Backend-owned model, console, desktop-tool and phone services close through their existing ownership paths. A narrow owner-only service_quiesce coordinator method covers backend-owned handles; it accepts only the current live stopping cycle. It is not a new public Kernel operation or an arbitrary RPC method dispatcher. The coordinator remains available as the service-control plane. No OS shutdown, logout or reboot command is invoked by Hatch.

Explicit On commits the supported work-gate release and admission update together with history. It refuses unresolved owned work when releasing a hold. A no-hold On does not cancel an already running job. Cancelled jobs are not replayed. Phone access remains off and no model is invented or started by On.

Reboot is the guarded second half of the same cycle. It may request the previously observed running model with its original configuration, using the original model action. Requested is distinct from running. Slate off skips that reload. A failed reload is separately reported. Every continuation checks the admission revision, work-gate epoch, cycle identity and live desktop. A newer Stop, Resume, even a same-value admission edit, another cycle or an absent desktop prevents the old automatic continuation. Reopening the programme never replays a pending Reboot.

Failed or corrupt cycle state is not silently replaced. Readback distinguishes admission-only holds from confirmed service closure, draining, stopping, interruption and changed decisions. Unknown state disables the Hatch service actions while retaining New Idea/New Project and ordinary inspection where their own stores remain available. Settings remain governed by their original definitions and scopes.

## Desktop and admission integration

Hatch retains its five current actions. Operations now shows service state separately from Slate/model state, and the existing Background service room provides details. New direct desktop commands, language/debugger starts or execution, console activity, phone starts and cloud replies respect the applicable admission checks. Existing close/inspection paths remain usable. Asynchronous queued cancellation and backend closure keep the desktop responsive during a cycle.

The real Qt walkthrough found a working-file save bug: the atomic replacement adopted temporary-file permissions. Save now preserves the original ordinary mode before replacement. The walkthrough verifies both saved text and mode through Off and Reboot. Service details is a workspace room, so it retains the edited source Preview.

## Installer and delivery

INSTALL_LS.py accepts a local release-parts directory or a pinned public HTTPS release manifest. It validates every part, restores hashed chunks for an individually oversized runtime, verifies the full payload and extracts into a new folder. It retains existing installation folders. Extract-only and plan routes invoke no package manager.

Offline mode requires a complete matching dependency cache with OFFLINE_FILES.json, debs and wheels. It refuses missing/unlisted/changed cache files and has no network fallback. The default desktop profile and optional suite profile reuse the existing Debian/runtime installers. Quick mode checks runtime imports, package integrity and source bindings without automatically repeating the extended historical walkthroughs.

START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh and LS_XSESSION.sh provide the manual dedicated X11/Fluxbox fullscreen route on existing Debian. They do not rewrite login or disk configuration. Actual apt/pip installation, wireless connection, display/driver startup, a bootable appliance ISO, public release hosting and the complete offline media cache remain unaccepted deployment work. See MINIMAL_DEBIAN_INSTALL_01.md for exact usage and requirements.

Every delivered ZIP is limited to 15,000,000 bytes. The pinned llama runtime archive is larger than one volume, so it is split into hashed transport pieces and restored before payload checks. The original runtime archive, its bytes and its hash are retained after installation. This preserves the complete programme while meeting the owner's part-size request.

## Complete specification and direction

LEDGER_SLATE_COMPLETE_PROJECT_SPEC_01.md and Ledger_Slate_Complete_Project_Specification_01.docx contain the long complete-product specification, including architecture, working copies, permissions, local Slate, staC, mathematical reasoning, documents, service controls, installation, UI appearance and acceptance. The Word document has 27 rendered pages with four actual UI illustrations. Its source is about 9,300 words. Every rendered page was visually reviewed; the inherited decorative title rule was removed.

The November 2 Interface Companion gives the launcher a broader capability-catalogue role. That accepted direction is retained explicitly. The five-action menu is the current implementation stage; Explore remains the current broad discovery route. Integration of that catalogue role into Hatch, the remaining all-settings audit and the writing-marker experiment remain open. The final development estimate must not erase these goals or turn registration counts into readiness claims.

## Focused evidence and limits

54 focused tests passed: 18 service authority/lifecycle cases, nine release-media/installer cases and 27 related Operations/shared-settings regressions. Eleven actual Qt checks passed with six captures. Three disposable durable job records exercise running/queued/completed states; no actual job was submitted. All Kernel launchers and provider entry points were held. No native tool, model worker, generation or provider request started. The real coordinator IPC/display/model and wireless installation remain owner-host acceptance work.

All 690 public operation schemas and scopes, 112 job-tool targets and all forty prior setting definitions remain unchanged. The registry digest remains 9b28255cf4cd31117ece3edada8a737b569e9de996cbb32836e3b1040f92e1a1. Full packaging, source binding, preservation, volume-size and restored-payload checks are recorded after packaging in the separate discussion.

Three of the four estimated cloud development passes are complete. One integration/debug pass is planned, with scope and findings allowed to change the estimate. Owner-host validation/fixes are separately estimated at one or two passes when the machine and inputs are available. Strict HATCH acceptance remains 0/6 and historical integrated acceptance 4/6. # HATCH SETTINGS-01

November 2, 2026. Full checkpoint over DISCOVERY-01, following the attached Interface Companion v1.0. The companion is preserved unchanged at `docs/HATCH_Interface_Companion_v1_0.docx`.

## Delivered boundary

The left panel now has separate Cabinet and Settings views. The real cabinet widget and its records remain intact. The Settings projection uses stable typed nodes with ID, parent, role, target, actual scope and provider. Ledger and Slate have separate roots; labels sort using case-insensitive natural order. Selection and expansion are validated and remembered independently of the cabinet. Trash remains in the fixed footer outside either tree's scrolling. Cabinet/Settings is a reviewable switch proposal, not a claim that its final presentation was accepted.

The center settings page uses a native yellow highlighted value passage and underlined eraser-pink actions, with graphite explanations. Native typing, selection, keyboard Undo and focus remain. A detailed definition and actual consumer observations are available under Detail. The old Tools category remains a genuine inventory rather than an editable setting. An explicit functional-ink flag keeps the legacy theme relighter from converting this surface’s pink action text back to graphite; older panels keep their existing behavior.

There are 18 existing typed settings, now described by canonical metadata and backed by their existing stores. The full inventory and remaining adapter coverage are in `SETTINGS_INVENTORY_01.md`. All genuine settings is still an open requirement.

## Shared changes, active effects and history

The page, CLI and deterministic Slate typed requests use the same Kernel settings operations and journal. `ledger.settings` keeps its existing schema name and legacy value field while adding stored/effective values, scope, application behavior, revision, history metadata, dependencies and typed navigation nodes. `ledger.settings.effective`, `.history` and `.restore` add explicit readback, history and default restoration.

`ledger.settings.set` retains its existing arguments and gains optional `expected_revision`. This fingerprint includes the saved value and latest setting change ID, so a value changing away and back still conflicts. The editor uses it automatically; `/set` does too. Legacy expected-value writes remain supported. Undo refuses a superseding revision and records restoration plus the original record's undone flag in one journal transaction. The existing external-profile delivery receipts still recover interrupted writes and undo receipts.

Saved visual values do not imply active desktop effects. Live consumer receipts include profile and process identity and require a desktop lease. Fonts show their resolved fallback. Startup changes stay pending until the next launch. CPU policy is reported as a next-work policy; no running OS priority, GPU, memory or I/O effect is claimed.

Drafts are retained per setting in the current desktop's bridge. They survive key changes, automatic refresh, Cabinet switching and preview replacement. A concurrent write updates the saved/effective display while retaining the highlighted draft and its original revision. Reload saved value is an explicit replacement of that key's draft. Draft retention across process exit is not implemented; Apply saves the actual setting.

The existing selected-settings ViewContext now follows the left key. Structured settings context includes saved/effective state and revision. Raw credentials are absent. Existing provider, AI admission and service-admission owner boundaries apply to Set, Default and Undo.

## Focused evidence

`docs/SETTINGS_01` contains the canonical definitions, registry compatibility check, focused unit result, actual Qt offscreen interaction receipt and three affected screenshots. Run the portable focused UI check with `python3 tools/check_settings_ui.py` when PySide6 is available. It uses disposable profiles and workspaces and saves its new evidence under `build/settings_ui`, or `ARC_LEDGER_SETTINGS_CAPTURE_DIR` when specified.

The checks cover direct keyboard edits; the real code editor consuming the changed font size; typed Slate parity and human Undo; changed-away-and-back revision conflicts; invalid values; scope/owner restrictions; recovery; draft survival; pending startup; key/expansion state; search; fixed Trash; legacy Tools access; and a 1366 × 768 offscreen layout. They create no jobs and run no model inference or engineering solvers. Slate:typed in the images is a deterministic command-path fixture, not a real-model acceptance claim.

## Continuation

Finish adapters for genuine advanced settings in the inventoried stores while preserving each store's authority and apply/reload behavior. Then migrate the cabinet through the proposed typed record/provider model, preserving master identities, alternate references, user selection and existing destinations. Review it populated with two projects, unassigned work, a source, a working copy and an inquiry. Import/Export separation remains part of that navigator slice.

The capability launcher expansion, distinctive top-menu names, adaptive context ranking, broader boxless document editing, right-column monitors/queue and native handoff are later slices. The companion supersedes the earlier five-command launcher limit; it does not make those later capabilities implemented. Names, X behavior, slider labels and the final left-switch design remain owner-review choices.

HATCH acceptance remains 0/6. Integrated acceptance remains 4/6, with the real-model/native I05 and owner-host I06 gates open. Offscreen screenshots do not qualify a ThinkPad, a real model's natural-language setting selection, native application returns, power/session actions or live process priority.

# HATCH SETTINGS-02

November 2, 2026. Complete checkpoint over SETTINGS-01, following `HATCH_Interface_Companion_v1_0.docx`. All earlier source, records, operations, job targets and historical evidence remain present.

## Result

The left Ledger/Slate registry now connects 25 genuine settings. Seven additions map to existing stores: incidental script text; left-column width; output height, visibility and selected page; Gemini model preference; and Gemini current-file sharing. The same highlighted editors, pink word actions, detailed definitions, revision guards, saved/effective distinction and Undo continue to serve these values.

A width change applies to the real dock and reads back actual width. Output height stays pending when the output dock is hidden; showing it applies and measures the request. Page choice targets the existing output tabs. The script choice now persists across Session reload and updates the actual presentation. The Cabinet/Settings switch, fixed Trash and existing cabinet data remain intact.

`ledger.settings.apply` adds a bounded Session batch operation. It validates every supplied key/value and every original revision before one Session file write, then commits the related journal entries in one Kernel transaction. There is no partial application when one key conflicts. Entries share a batch ID and retain per-key Undo. This operation accepts only the real Session keys; it cannot cross into Gemini credentials, admission, jobs, paths or grants.

The older reading dialog now uses this operation, and its unedited fields are preserved during concurrent changes. The existing prose-size shortcut, script menu and Gemini source-sharing control also use shared settings history. Remaining old controls are preserved; the full inventory identifies the unadapted boundaries.

## Provider preference behavior

Gemini preferences remain in their original file. Registry changes preserve the serialized credential field verbatim and never read/decrypt its contents for display or prompts. An opaque preference revision and a shared process/file lock prevent a stale same-value revision from passing across project Kernels. External delivery receipts distinguish a committed preference write from an unapplied no-op by that marker. A recovered write records history; it does not replay configuration.

The existing credential editor preserves preferences it did not edit and refuses conflicting changed fields. Its legitimate key handling remains separate from registry reads. The chat overlay reloads current preferences for each new request; an existing in-flight request retains the object it already captured. The actual overlay cache and sharing control synchronize from the file. These changes do not make an API request or activate a local model.

Both new Gemini settings retain direct owner-action requirements, including Default and Undo. Provider proposals and the compact local planning grammar do not acquire permission to change them. Invalid optional provider configuration is reported unavailable, with its editor disabled and drafts retained. Other Ledger settings remain available, damaged bytes remain untouched, and a new Gemini request refuses invalid preference configuration before making a call.

## Evidence and limits

`docs/SETTINGS_02` contains the 28 focused tests (14 prior settings regressions plus 14 advanced-boundary tests), 15 actual Qt offscreen checks, source/registry compatibility and three affected screenshots. Tests cover atomic batches and recovery, cross-project preference conflicts, credential preservation, owner restrictions, unavailable stores, draft survival, old-control parity, actual dock/font effects, 1366 by 768 layout and clean Session/desktop-lease close. The provider request function is blocked and asserted unused in the UI check. The run creates zero jobs, model generations or engineering-solver calls.

Use `python3 tools/check_settings_02_ui.py` with PySide6 for a new disposable run. Its default evidence directory is build/settings02_ui; ARC_LEDGER_SETTINGS_CAPTURE_DIR can select another output location. The three preserved images use explicit UI fixtures; the provider model text is not a real availability result.

All 680 prior operation schemas and scopes are unchanged. The added Session batch command brings the registry to 681 operations; all 112 job-tool targets remain. No full historical suite or long model trial was run. Actual natural-language selection with the changed settings catalogue remains an open real-model check. Offscreen Qt does not qualify native application handoff, owner-host behavior, session/power operations or live OS priority.

## Next

The next UI slice should build the logical cabinet with typed record/provider nodes and stable identities. Review it populated with two projects, unassigned work, a source, working copy and inquiry, preserving existing routes and each master record. Keep settings, Import/Export and fixed Trash distinct. The remaining model/memory adapters retain their inventory entries and existing authority until implemented.

The expanded capability launcher, distinctive menu names, contextual command ranking, broader editable-document treatment and right-column monitors/queue remain later work. Final names, X behavior, priority wording and the switch's presentation remain owner-review choices. HATCH acceptance is unchanged at 0/6; integrated acceptance remains 4/6. Model/native I05 and owner-host I06 gates remain open while cloud development continues with the ThinkPad unavailable.

# HATCH SETTINGS-03

November 3, 2026 · America/Phoenix

Full checkpoint over MEMORY-01. Five existing owner-memory preferences are now connected to the shared Settings hierarchy under Slate → Memory. Their values come from the original owner-scoped stacy_memory profile. There is no second configuration store and no new operation, job tool, worker, workspace adapter or Hatch menu item.

## Values and effect

The five controls are Use personality reference, Soft feedback half-life (days), Owner correction weight, Owner statement weight and Confirmed choice weight. Settings now contains 31 real connected preferences; the preceding 26 definitions retain their IDs, defaults, types, bounds and backing stores. See SETTINGS_INVENTORY_03.md for the current inventory and remaining work.

A missing profile is unavailable in Settings; it is not replaced with an enabled default. Import, delete, archive, task and feedback actions retain the original Memory controls. An unavailable or corrupt optional profile leaves the other settings available and does not replace profile bytes.

The enable default is true because the existing import operation creates enabled profiles. It is only a default for an imported profile, not a claim that a missing profile exists. Numeric defaults are the original half-life of 90 days and feedback weights 4, 2 and 0.5. Persistent owner corrections do not decay; the half-life applies to soft feedback accounting.

Readback distinguishes the saved value from the profile-context effect. Numeric parameters remain stored when the profile is off, while their effective value is unavailable. Enabling the profile does not load a model, grant permission for AI activity, alter model weights or prove that a response follows a preference. The existing local profile-context path consumes these parameters on its next eligible use.

## One guarded transaction

The adapter reads and validates the existing profile, including its stored digest, imported reference and parameter bounds. The profile token binds the calling owner and the complete inspected profile. Legacy configure/enable operations, an away-and-back edit and a delete/re-import invalidate that token even if the displayed scalar returns to the same value.

Apply requires the inspected revision. Within one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, it changes only the requested field through the original profile commit logic and writes the existing shared settings journal. Other parameters and the original imported reference remain intact. A refused journal write rolls back the profile update as well. No duplicate ledger.memory.* setting values or separate file-delivery journal are introduced.

The original profile branch was extracted into commit_profile. An AST comparison proves that its update body is unchanged and the rest of memory_service is unchanged except for that extraction. Feedback handling, source-aware procedure reading and original memory operations retain their existing routes.

Default uses the same guarded route. Undo is an owned, journalled new change: the selected change must still be latest for the key, and the complete current profile token must match. A newer change to another profile parameter therefore also blocks blind Undo. The owner can inspect current values and submit a fresh change.

## Caller identity and sharing

Kernel Settings reads, effective readback and history now carry the actual calling principal. New memory setting history is visible only to its actor; existing shared setting history semantics are retained. Memory changes require the existing owner boundary and are refused in Tutor mode. The generic internal value helper refuses private memory keys so consumers must choose an explicit caller-scoped read.

The optional shareable ledger.context activity snapshot omits these five values and their definitions. It reports that owner memory requires an explicit local read. Default cloud action proposals refuse broad Settings/effective/history reads that could disclose owner memory, direct private key access and private operations reached through pipeline or join sources. Narrow public setting reads remain available. This is a targeted privacy boundary, not a new blanket promise about every existing record or private_local operation.

## Desktop behavior

The five leaves use the existing typed Settings tree, distinct from cabinet record ownership. Apply, Default, Detail, Reload and Undo retain their established locations. Number writing uses an exact text passage rather than a rounding spinbox: a legal 1e-20 weight is displayed unchanged, and invalid writing stays visible for correction without changing stored values. Its hint is the exact lowercase poem.

An intervening profile change preserves the current draft and reports the conflict. Explicit reload reads the current owner profile before a new Apply. Settings drafts remain desktop-local; this slice does not add restart recovery for unfinished Settings writing. Stored profile values survive a fresh desktop through the existing store.

Fixed left-panel Trash, visible Stop, monitors, return thread, the paper palette and the five-item Hatch menu remain. No provider request, model activation, tool job or native process is needed to inspect these controls.

## Evidence and remaining work

Evidence is in docs/SETTINGS_03:

- Nine new boundary cases passed in 1.807 seconds. They cover absent/corrupt profiles, original storage, stale/away-and-back changes, owned Undo, default, private identity/history/context, precision/bounds, atomic rollback and valid cloud pipeline/join privacy cases.
- Twenty-eight related Settings regressions passed in 7.214 seconds: 37 distinct focused cases in total. The full historical suite was not rerun.
- Thirteen actual offscreen Qt checks passed. These include button interactions, conflict-preserved writing, Default/Undo, profile-off readback, tiny-number display, invalid writing, privacy and a fresh 1366 × 768 desktop. Five actual window captures are included.
- Registry comparison: 690 operations and all 112 job-tool targets unchanged; all old operation schemas/scopes and all old 26 setting definitions unchanged. Registry digest remains 9b28255cf4cd31117ece3edada8a737b569e9de996cbb32836e3b1040f92e1a1.
- The UI used a disposable owner reference. Zero model calls, provider requests, job submissions and native invocations were made. Stored preference readback is not actual-model compliance.

The complete archive retains earlier source and evidence. Packaging refreshes the existing source bindings and manifest; the external release discussion records the resulting archive size, checksum and post-package checks without embedding a self-referential archive hash.

HATCH acceptance stays 0/6; historical integrated acceptance stays 4/6. I05 exact-model/native and I06 owner-host remain OPEN. ThinkPad scheduling, pointer dragging, owned Master Stop and physical/native behavior are not qualified by these cloud captures.

Next is a cohesive UI review pass across launcher choices, menus, left-tree navigation and workspace transitions, with a consolidated screenshot review set. Remaining real configuration adapters include model reload/handover preferences, favorites/view choices and other presentation fields; they are not disguised as completed scalar settings here.

# Tool Atlas — first implementation

Open **Tool Atlas** from the Ledger navigator, or use `/open atlas` in the Slate command entry. Search for Calc, Python, KiCad, ngspice, a tool ID or an operation ID. Press Enter or Find. Use Operations / Job tools and Previous / Next to narrow the results.

The Passport tab explains prerequisites, required permission, source, licence status and known limits. Exact contract shows the registered argument schema and passive bindings. Selecting an entry never runs that tool.

Save passport snapshot records a private observation in the existing workspace database. Choose a saved passport and Check saved passport to compare its binding with the current adapter, contract, declared runtime and host session. A changed binding is STALE. Historical snapshots are retained. This pass does not add a database migration or rewrite existing records.

## Meaning of the status

All operation qualification states in this first implementation are **UNTESTED**. The existing catalogue's installed, available and permitted dimensions remain separate. A source file or installed executable does not prove operation success. An unchanged passport proves only that the bindings checked here match, not that the entire dependency environment is unchanged.

The snapshot covers the direct adapter source, exact argument contract, registered job target, declared passive runtime information, selected executable bytes when a command is declared, and platform/boot session. It does not cover all transitive Python imports, shared libraries, launcher dependencies, model weights, grant state, user arguments or engineering inputs. Systems without a boot-session identifier have a weaker platform-only host binding, explicitly recorded as a null session digest and HOST_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE when the other bindings match. Rebooting a Linux host invalidates its session binding conservatively. Job-level fixture/evidence adapters and their qualification promotion are future work.

## One registry and one execution authority

The Atlas adapts `engineering_kernel.CAPABILITIES`, `TOOLS`, `engineering_cli.schemas()` and `capability_catalog.catalogue()`. There is no duplicate dispatcher, independently editable operation schema or shell runner. Existing IDs remain unchanged. Search vocabulary is presentation metadata only. The six new Atlas commands are registered through the same Kernel and available to CLI/MCP/Slate command discovery.

`atlas.lookup` accepts query, kind (OPERATION / JOB_TOOL), limit (1–100) and offset. Search matches all words against IDs, required scope and the small explicit vocabulary.

`atlas.operation_schema` accepts name and optional kind; OPERATION is the default. It returns the exact operation contract or the job's existing `jobs.submit` route and registered adapter target. Job-specific options remain validated by the existing worker; no complete job-options schema is invented here.

`atlas.invocation` accepts operation and arguments. It validates argument shape using the existing contract and returns a structured call with `SCHEMA_CHECKED_NOT_DISPATCHED` and `runtime_authorization: false`. It does not check every argument-dependent permission/precondition, emit a shell command, or execute the proposed call. Required Kernel scope is not a complete effect model.

`atlas.passport.save` requires execute scope because it writes a new private Desk record. `atlas.passport.get` and `atlas.passports.list` require read scope and retain owner isolation. Listing returns historical summaries; opening rechecks freshness. The desktop picker shows the newest 100 snapshots; the Kernel list supports offset pagination for older records.

## staC read forms

```
atlas
atlas | find "KiCad"
atlas | operation math.preview
atlas | tool cad.drc
```

These are finite extensions to the existing embedded staC bridge. They produce typed read IR and forward the existing caller principal to the Kernel. No shell, extra execution stage, scope elevation or arbitrary generated program is accepted. The upstream POSIX staC interpreter is unchanged.

The general read pipeline also accepts registered calls such as `atlas.lookup {"query":"Python"}` through its existing `language.run` route. The chain-menu root has a Tool Atlas navigation link; object-specific compatible-operation filtering is not implemented in this pass.

## Scope and campaign status

This is **ATLAS-01**, an additive H03 foundation implemented while the owner's ThinkPad is unavailable. It is not completed H03 or a HATCH release. H01/H02 hardware/model qualification, Algorithm & Theory Atlas, checked probe promotion, typed compatibility matching, object-specific pipe menus, full native ownership and the release gates remain open. I05 actual-model/native acceptance and I06 owner-host acceptance are unchanged.

The new code is checked with focused boundary tests and an actual Qt offscreen UI capture. Offscreen UI capture does not establish a usable native Debian desktop. No model generations, native probe jobs or owner hardware acceptance are performed here.

To stop using the view, close its tab and continue through existing workspaces. Saved passport records remain inert, owner-private Desk history. For rollback, retain a backup of the current workspace database alongside the previous program checkpoint; do not delete the database or discard newer records.

# HATCH WORKSHOP 01

November 5, 2026 · UTC

Complete checkpoint over INTEGRATION-01 and the first delivery under the Creative Implementation Commission v2.1 (November 4, 2026), which continues from the latest working tree and asks for a usable installation first. It carries Gate one of the Program Specification for Claude v1.0 (the preserved five-part desktop and a truthful Hatch, usable with no model) and the first route of Gate two: a document in the centre that the owner and Slate edit in turns. The baseline was pinned as the specification's first actions require (BL01, BL02): the seven INTEGRATION-01 volumes match the intake hashes in the handoff, the handoff's derived restoration manifest restores all 1,491 payload files identical to the development tree, and an untouched copy was kept beside it. The requirement-to-evidence ledger is IMPLEMENTATION_LEDGER.json; the interpretation choices are docs/DECISION_REGISTER.json (D01–D17); the code map is docs/IMPLEMENTATION_MAP.md; the short daily guide is docs/DAILY_GUIDE.md; the document route is docs/DOCUMENTS_01.md; the machine view is docs/MACHINE_VIEW_01.md. Nothing in this checkpoint is owner-host, live-model, native-handover or physical acceptance; every acceptance case exercised here fills only the mechanical and offscreen column of the ledger.

## What the owner's direction changed

Commission v2.1 governs where it conflicts with the earlier specification's prescriptions: effort goes to implementation; checks are focused smoke checks of changed behaviour rather than sweeps; the gate order is a working order. The specification's decision register still supersedes four rules earlier checkpoints had built to, and this pass follows the newer decisions: Hatch is the primary doorway to usable tools and the five-choice first-item order is history; the machine overview and the Slate activity column stay visible beside the centre, so Home no longer hides the right column; the side columns are no longer forced to one width by a hidden-label ratchet; the left column is a machine and work navigator rather than only an office cabinet. Capabilities, records, routes and action identities are preserved while their presentation changes. Menu words, palette values, the X marker and priority labels remain provisional, reversible defaults for owner review (PD04).

## The permanent five parts (UI01, UI02, LP01)

The left column, the centre, the right column, the Ledger Head and the typing strip stay visible together. Home keeps the right column; Today sits in the centre. Each side column has its own two-way minimum derived from its own row of words (the left from Hatch, Explore and the console sizes; the right from the typing targets), scaled with the interface size; when the need shrinks and the column sat on the old minimum it comes back down; an owner-dragged width survives; both widths are remembered through the connected profile (layout.navigator_width and layout.simulator_width), and the saved widths reach the desktop at start. The workspace tab strip no longer moves with the current tab. Opening workspaces from Hatch keeps the edited Preview and the five-pin policy; a navigation event starts no job.

## Hatch as the tool doorway (HT01, HT02, HT03)

The capability groups come first: Work, Reason, Instruments, Programs, Knowledge and Configuration, then Explore the workshop…; below them New Idea and New Project; then the Services line (opens Service details) and a Ledger services submenu holding the existing On, Off and Reboot actions with their routes, identities and rules unchanged; then the live exit item (Return to Debian in the dedicated session, Exit Ledger elsewhere) and one disabled row for Log Out, Restart and Shut Down that carries the reasons in its tooltip. Every entry is created once; opening the menu refills only the groups; the menu holds still while open. At 14 pt the menu is 411 by 521 px and fits 1366 by 768 and 1280 by 720 in one column; at 18 pt it is 522 by 625 px and still one column.

Each row publishes its actual route, as the capability presentation contract asks: what opens (a Ledger-built workspace, Ledger's checks for a native tool, or application operations), what Slate can do there (the registered family operations with their scopes, six shown and the rest counted), what is missing (the executables passive detection did not find), the qualification state (not assessed on this host) and the current work context. The native-tool rows are named for what they open: KiCad checks, KiBot outputs, ngspice profiles, Yosys synthesis, nextpnr & Trellis, HDL simulation checks; none implies that the complete editor has appeared. Needs setup appears in the row text itself, not only on hover; a KiCad row without an attached project opens the existing project-required explanation, as its tooltip says. Opening a row is navigation; discovery starts no model, native tool, calculation or worker. Keyboard users open Hatch with Space or Enter, move with the arrows (Up from the first row wraps to the exit item, past the disabled power row), and read a highlighted row's descriptor with F1 or Shift F1 in the typing-strip note. The Explore word keeps the record suggestions, Explore the workshop… and Find saved work; the groups are listed in Hatch only. Work gains a Documents row.

## The machine and work navigator (NV01, NV02, NV03)

The left column switch reads Cabinet · Machine · Settings. A one-line machine strip stays visible above it in every view. The Machine view lists Processor, Memory, Storage, Connections, Devices and Installed tools, read from /proc, /sys and the filesystem with the source path and the sampled time of every reading, honest "none detected" and "unavailable" states, bounded sizes and no process started; the same readings are available to Slate through the added read operation ledger.machine, which is private to this computer (never offered to an external provider) and does not fill the journal. Work rows select the same record identities in the cabinet; no copy is made. The ARC project's hardware navigator stays under the project, distinct from the ThinkPad or container observations. Trash remains pinned at the bottom right of the column, outside the scrolling tree; Import and Export keep their routes. Documents file under their project (or Unassigned) in a Documents folder, and the cabinet record view shows a page's words.

## Paper interaction (VS01, VS02, VS03)

Writable passages are yellow and borderless: the New Idea sheet and the Home jot, the New Project title, the Slate composer, the document title, the cabinet and settings filters and the typing strip, with a visible selection colour on yellow and a bottom rule on focus. Owner prose (cabinet writing and intent, the return thread, the corrected memory direction, the document page) uses the prose font and size from Settings; code and JSON keep the code font. The empty hint remains the lowercase word poem. The X writing marker is a graphite mark in the page margin on the caret's line of the yellow writing passages (14 px, scaled with the passage font; a narrow form when the margin is tight); it blinks with a two-second period, is static when Reduce motion is on, follows the caret, never touches the text, the caret, selection, undo or copy, and is governed by the added setting appearance.writing_marker (default on). Its exact form remains an owner review item. The hardware category views editor grows with its content, keeps one scrollbar, names every combo and places Apply after the combos in the Tab order; the Service details room, the Brain tab state, the record menu heading and the Calculate fields read in words.

## One typing surface (CM01)

The strip's destination words are Slate, staC and Console, with Find and Kernel kept as quieter advanced words; the console target's key, prefix and history are unchanged. A context word at the right names the active work context (the open document, the selected record or the current workspace). The destination hint stays visible to keyboard users through the accessible description, and no status message lingers in the hint.

## The shared document (WS01, WS02, CM02, CM03, AI03 in part; AC03 and AC09 mechanically)

Hatch ▸ Work ▸ Documents opens a page in the centre: a Ledger-native document stored as a Project Desk record (kind document, schema ledger.document/1: a title and paragraphs with a style and inline bold, italic and underline marks), edited in a QTextEdit in the prose font with a marks row of pink action words and the usual keys. The page saves itself 1.5 s after typing pauses, when focus leaves it, on Ctrl S and before any Slate request, always against the revision it last saw; an unnamed page is called by its first words. The owner selects words, moves to the strip and asks Slate in plain words; `documents.interpret` resolves formatting requests by explicit rules (bold, italic, underline and their removal, heading levels, body, code, plain, replace x with y; undo and redo work the page's own stack) and anything else is left to the model path with the document and selection as context. A recognised request becomes `documents.edit`, which names the block, the offsets and the quoted words against the expected revision and refuses a stale revision or changed words; the change lands as a revision by SLATE and is applied to the page through the same undo stack as the owner's typing, so Ctrl Z takes Slate's change back like any other. The answer in the right column names the change, the revision, that no model was needed and how to take it back. With no model selected Slate says so and lists the direct edits he can still make. Reopening a page (from the list, the cabinet's Documents folder or the action shelf) reads the saved revision; Export… writes Markdown, HTML or plain text. Seven operations are added and recorded (documents.create, save, edit as execute; list, get, interpret, render as read); documents.* is private to this computer for cloud proposals; the ledger.navigate destination enum gains documents (recorded extension). The live-model turn, takeover and resume, other artifact kinds and a DOCX export remain open.

## The model's small tool set (Commission v2.1, first step of the agent loop)

When a request goes to a loaded local model in plan mode, `workbench/tool_selection.py` chooses up to six registered operations for the request's words by explicit matching over operation names, the capability families of the Hatch adapters (titles, descriptions, keywords, plus Machine, Notes, Mathematics and Agenda) and argument names; each comes with a one-line reason, and only read and execute operations are offered. The plan schema keeps its fixed direct set (now including documents.get and documents.edit) and adds the chosen contracts, so a 4B model reads a handful of relevant schemas instead of the registry. The owner still reviews and runs every proposal. This is untested with a live model here; `tests_integrated/test_tool_selection.py` covers the selection and the schema mechanically.

## The right column (LP01, LP03)

The held state is one sentence everywhere, taken from the service-cycle summaries; the small readings scale with the interface size; the Services line no longer shifts the column when it wraps. CPU, GPU, RAM and TXT stay compact with explicit unavailable values. Service and power targets keep their names: Ledger services cycle Ledger's own services; leaving Ledger is the exit item; Ledger never issues an operating-system session or power command. Slate's document edits appear in the activity because documents.edit is a journalled request.

## Registry, settings and preservation (AC14, ST01)

All 690 SERVICE-01 operation scopes and the 112 job-tool targets are retained; every schema is byte-identical to the recorded baseline docs/HATCH_SERVICE_01_CAPABILITIES.json except the recorded enum extension of ledger.navigate; eight operations are added and recorded (ledger.machine and the seven documents.*), so the registry reads 698. The 41 prior setting definitions are byte-identical and in order; one setting, appearance.writing_marker, is added and recorded (42); docs/SETTINGS_INVENTORY_07.md is the inventory. tools/check_release.py therefore reports the registry and settings sections as ADDITIONS_RECORDED against HATCH_WORKSHOP_01_RESULT.json. No second dispatcher, scheduler or data store was added; every new route resolves through the existing registered operations, the existing Project Desk store and the existing view factories.

## Installation for tonight (OS01 in part)

The release is the same shape as before: numbered ZIP volumes of at most 15,000,000 bytes with RELEASE_PARTS.json, INSTALL_LS.py and README_WORKSHOP_01.txt beside them. `python3 INSTALL_LS.py --usb . --target ~/Applications/Ledger_Slate_Workshop_01 --minimal-session --yes` extracts, verifies and installs the runtime on an existing minimal Debian with public dependency downloads; `--extract-only` restores without installing; `bash START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh` from a text login starts the dedicated fullscreen session and Hatch ▸ Return to Debian ends it. The pinned llama.cpp CPU runtime is included; no model file is included, and the Brain room says what is selected. The working records stay outside the replaceable program folder, so a new release folder beside the old one is the recovery route. The owner-host run itself (display, input, the dedicated session, a loaded Qwen) is pending the ThinkPad; see docs/MINIMAL_DEBIAN_INSTALL_01.md for every refusal and readback line.

## Evidence

The numbers are read from build/desktop01_ui/focused-tests.json and the Qt reports under build/desktop01_ui and build/workshop01_ui; HATCH_WORKSHOP_01_RESULT.json copies them. The focused modules run one by one and include the new modules for the frame, the paper vocabulary, the machine view, the documents and the earlier focused set. Five new actual offscreen Qt checks exercise the mechanical steps of AC01 (five parts visible through open, launch, maximize, switch, save, reopen), AC02 (Hatch with no model: a workspace, a checks route, a missing prerequisite, the services submenu, the footer; discovery runs nothing), AC03 and AC09 (type, select, bold by Slate from the strip, continue typing, save, reopen, one undo stack, the no-model answer), AC10 (machine, storage and device state, project links, Import and Export, pinned Trash, the settings hierarchy) and AC15 (pointer and keyboard operation, focus, disabled actions, reduced motion, poem hints, the X marker). Every earlier shipped Qt tool was rerun with its captures redirected under build/desktop01_ui/regressions and build/desktop01_ui/hatch_regressions, so no historical evidence folder was rewritten. Zero jobs were submitted and zero workers, models, providers or native tools started; Kernel.launch and the provider request path were held throughout.

Numbers of this run: 265 focused tests in 19 modules passed (59 new cases over the INTEGRATION-01 focused log; test_launcher, test_service_lifecycle, test_operations, test_explore, test_settings_registry, test_hardware_settings, test_presentation_settings, test_settings_advanced, test_memory_settings, test_model_settings, test_install_media, test_startup_scripts, test_release_check, test_readiness, test_frame, test_paper, test_machine, test_documents, test_tool_selection); 50 checks and 37 captures in the five new Qt tools (frame 12/10, hatch 11/6, paper 10/14, machine 8/4, document 9/3), every one PASSED; 16 of 16 earlier shipped Qt tools rerun PASSED (none failed); registry 698 operations, 112 job tools, 42 settings; release check on the tree PASSED with registry ADDITIONS_RECORDED and settings ADDITIONS_RECORDED.

## What stays open

The live-model turn on the document and Slate's agent loop over the Tool Atlas (choose a small relevant tool set, act, observe, revise, retain the method); calculations that follow a changed condition and the cross-application evidence loop (Gate three); long investigations that continue while the owner is away and stay resumable; takeover and resume on one artifact; model replacement, interruption and recovery; installation on the owner host and the display qualification (Gate four). Strict HATCH acceptance remains 0/6 and historical integrated acceptance 4/6; I05 is open and I06 has not started.

# Native HDL checks and recorded waveforms

Icarus Verilog, Verilator and Surfer are the seventh, eighth and ninth dedicated
native integrations. They use the existing shared Kernel, job grants, Stacy,
CLI/MCP, evidence, cancellation and hardware-centered navigation.

Open Motherboard → HDL · simulation / waveforms, or View → Hardware workspaces →
HDL · Simulation / Waveforms. Select the engine and profile, then Run profile.

## Exactly what runs

| Engine / profile | Native operation | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Icarus / RGMII | Original `tb_rgmii` with the original RX, TX, pump and DDR simulation cells | HOST_SIM, original pass/error messages and selected digital VCD signals |
| Icarus / SDRAM | Original `tb_sdram`, controller, calibrator and protocol model, default parameters | HOST_SIM, tile/stress/rejection/refresh checks and selected digital VCD signals |
| Either engine / pump | New adapter-owned bench around unchanged `eth_tx_pump` RTL | HOST_SIM, all 256 output words compared with an independently computed pattern |
| Verilator / RGMII | Native lint of `rgmii_rx` with the original DDR simulation cells | STATIC_CHECK, diagnostics with source/line/code; no simulation verdict |
| Verilator / SDRAM | Native lint of `sdram_ctrl` | STATIC_CHECK, diagnostics; no simulation verdict |
| Surfer capture | Actual native Surfer load, selected variables, saved state and image of a verified trace | STATIC_CHECK; rendering does not create a new simulation or timing verdict |

The available Icarus 12.0 passed the two original benches. The available Verilator
5.020 rejects the RGMII bench's named-fork-disable construct and the SDRAM model's
pull-up strength syntax. Those sources are not silently rewritten or replaced
to obtain a pass. The separate pump bench uses supported timed constructs.
It writes 512 known bytes with unrelated 80/125 MHz clocks, checks every one of
256 output words and emits the recorded sequence. `/compare pump` compares the
latest current Icarus and Verilator sequences. This is initialized transport
data agreement, not whole-design, four-state or cycle-by-cycle equivalence.

Existing hardware benches/models remain unchanged. The adapter-owned wrapper
only selects the top and signals to dump. No project Makefile is executed.
Verilator compiles its own generated C++ with a fixed generated build, never a
project-provided C++ harness or build recipe. Original source files, context,
adapter and portable waveform reader are hashed, copied and checked afterward.
HDL includes/macros, file/system IO, DPI/foreign-code hooks and source-supplied
native hooks require separate adapter review and are rejected by this profile.

## Stacy and command-line control

| Command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `/open hdl` | Open the shared workspace |
| `/hdl` | Read native availability and workflow scope |
| `/sim rgmii`, `/sim sdram` | Submit the corresponding Icarus job |
| `/pump icarus`, `/pump verilator` | Submit the shared transport check |
| `/lint rgmii`, `/lint sdram` | Submit native Verilator lint |
| `/compare pump` | Read agreement of the latest intact, current pump results |
| `/value JOB SIGNAL TICK` | Read an exact recorded four-state value from that job |
| `/wave rgmii`, `/wave sdram` | Capture native Surfer over the matching current Icarus trace |
| `/wave pump icarus`, `/wave pump verilator` | Capture the corresponding pump trace |
| `/qualify icarus`, `/qualify verilator`, `/qualify surfer` | Run that operation's capability cases |

Read operations are `hdl.inspect`, `hdl.report`, `hdl.value`, `hdl.compare_pump`,
`surfer.inspect` and `surfer.report`. Registered jobs are `icarus.PROFILE`,
`verilator.PROFILE` and `surfer.ENGINE_PROFILE`; qualification is `ENGINE.qualify`.
The same APIs are exposed by `python -m workbench.engineering_cli call` and MCP.
They keep existing execute grants, per-tool allowlists, Tutor read-only behavior
and provider proposal boundaries. Local commands need no provider key. No shell,
new programming authority or generic environment grant is exposed.

## Interactive Ledger trace inspection

The new portable SDK module `sdk/cli/arc1cli/hdl_waveforms.py` reads bounded
digital VCD and supplies four-state cursor values without Qt or a provider.
Waveform shows up to eight selected signals. Signals lists the original names,
widths, change counts and whether X/Z was recorded. Click the waveform, enter a
native tick, or use the slider/previous/next controls. Zoom and Fit change the
time window; cursor values always come from recorded events.

Completed traces are retained as verified `trace.vcd.gz` snapshots. Compression
preserves the exact native VCD bytes; both archive and uncompressed hashes/lengths
are recorded and verified. Native Surfer receives a verified decompressed copy.
This keeps retention compact and prevents later inspection from depending on a
large, mutable raw output file. Damaged archives are explicit, never displayed
as valid traces.

The time unit comes from the VCD timescale and is retained as integer femtoseconds
per native tick. X/Z are kept explicitly rather than converted to zero. Aliases
share the native value stream. Same-tick cursor reads use the last recorded
value; raw VCD retains its order. Dense regions are shaded rather than drawn as
falsely resolved individual transitions. Zoom reveals the events. This is a
digital trace inspector, not analog interpolation or delta-cycle reconstruction.

Inputs are bounded to 32 MiB VCD, 512 signal declarations and one million value
changes. Unsupported encodings, backwards timestamps, unknown identifiers,
unbalanced headers, inconsistent alias widths and linked paths are rejected.
FST/GHW are not implemented by this portable reader. Native Surfer supports more
formats, but this adapter deliberately consumes only the verified digital VCDs.

## Native Surfer view

More → Surfer native capture runs the actual Surfer executable with a fixed
adapter-owned command file. It loads a copied, hash-verified trace, selects a
small known set of variables and a bounded time window, saves native RON state,
and records the displayed variable tree. The saved state must name exactly the
requested signals and the exact relative trace file. An actual 1280×800 image
is captured after native loading; the viewer and display are then closed.

The Surfer capture page is this native image, with the original state and VCD
retained beside it. It is not an embedded interactive Surfer window. Ledger's
separate Waveform page provides the cursor/zoom controls. A normal local Surfer
installation can open the retained VCD or saved state for its full interactive
toolset. State files can contain the original attempt's relative file location;
decompress `trace.vcd.gz` to `trace.vcd` beside `surfer_state.ron` when using
that handoff. The archive retains exact original native bytes.

Capture currently qualifies on Linux with Surfer 0.7.0 (git 1cdbaa9), Xvfb, xauth
and Pillow. It uses an authenticated temporary X display and private HOME/config/
cache/temp locations, never the owner's desktop. No endpoint is published. It
does not read user decoders, state files or scripts. Surfer/native display
processes are part of the owned job tree. Other hosts must qualify their own
capture runtime; absent prerequisites are explicit. The portable Ledger trace
view still works without this optional native capture runtime.

## Runtime, evidence and limits

Install native tools separately and launch Ledger with their binary directories
on PATH. Icarus needs matching `vvp` and its `ivl` support directory. Verilator
needs matching `verilator_bin`, its normal share directory, GNU C++ and make.
The adapter handles a standard installation prefix explicitly; it does not
install tools or change existing tool pins. Optional Linux captures need Surfer,
Xvfb with its normal keyboard/font dependencies, xauth and Python Pillow.
Native binaries/data are not redistributed in the Ledger source archives.

Compiler/executable and observed support-data hashes are checked before/after
jobs. This is an observed tool binding, not an entire OS/dynamic-library closure
or a claim of an OS sandbox. Every HDL job repeats a small timed counter fixture,
checks real native VCD output and rejects a missing module. Every Surfer job
repeats a known VCD/state/capture case. Presence alone is not qualification.

SIMULATED requires normal native execution, exactly one expected pass marker,
no reported bench failure and a valid non-empty digital trace. LINT_CLEAN and
LINT_WARNINGS are separate from simulation; warnings remain visible despite
`-Wno-fatal`. RENDERED means native Surfer loaded/captured a verified trace.
QUALIFIED describes only capability cases. No cached verdict is reused.

Reports verify artifact hashes and rederive trace, diagnostic and sample
summaries from original native files. A cancelled/incomplete latest Kernel job
prevents falling back to an older trace for capture/comparison. Stale source,
damaged output and unavailable parents remain explicit. Stop job, `/cancel ID`
and the red Master Stop use the existing owned-process-tree controls, including
native compiler/model/viewer/display children. Cancelled evidence cannot be
relabelled as simulated or rendered. A new job restarts the UI monitor.

These are digital RTL/protocol models. Verilator's state semantics differ from
Icarus's four-state simulation. Bench-modeled throughput is not a measured PCB
speed. There is no board timing, CDC sign-off, full console cycle accuracy or
physical programming verdict. FAB, ROUTE release and programming remain HOLD.
Existing SDK, hardware, firmware, policy, tool pins and tests remain unchanged;
the new SDK reader and new tests are additions for independent source review.

Primary references: https://steveicarus.github.io/iverilog/ ,
https://verilator.org/guide/latest/exe_verilator.html ,
https://docs.surfer-project.org/book/ and its Commands chapter. The actual native
versions, help and retained operations—not current documentation alone—govern
this host's qualified capabilities.

# Implementation map · Program Specification for Claude v1.0 · Graphite 0.1

November 5, 2026 · UTC. Required by specification section 19: a short map tying each missing experience to the existing modules and the requirement IDs, kept current as passes land. Existing module names are starting points verified against the INTEGRATION-01 tree (commit fea2b5a); nothing here is a claim that the experience is finished. Under the Creative Implementation Commission v2.1 (November 4, 2026) the gate sequence is a working order, not a constraint: HATCH WORKSHOP-01 delivers Gate one and the first Gate-two route (the shared document) together.

**Where Graphite 0.1 stands (November 6, 2026).** Graphite is the public name of the program (earlier Ledger & Slate); "Hatch" below is the menu the cat opens (`workbench/hatch_qt.py`), "Slate" the assistant, now Graphite, and "the Ledger Head" the head. Gate one landed with WORKSHOP-01 and was finished by GRAPHITE-01 (the mark, the startup screen, the cat, the compact-layout fixes, the public rename; docs/GRAPHITE_01.md). Gate two's document route and the model's turn on the open page landed mechanically, with live small-model trials in the build container; native takeover is open. Gate three began with the agent loop, the numbers assignment and the files-about assignment. Gate four (HOST-01: model replacement with rollback, interruption, installation and the owner host) has not started. Every requirement's state, evidence and limits are in IMPLEMENTATION_LEDGER.json. Additive operations and settings are now verified against the recorded registry `docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json` (the release check); the evidence files of earlier passes named below and in the ledger left the tree at 0.1 and are in the project's git history and the owner's backups, and each named check writes its report again when run.

## Delivery in four gates (specification section 18)

| Gate | Pass name | Requirements | Acceptance exercised (mechanical/offscreen unless stated) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One: the five-part desktop and truthful Hatch usable with no model | HATCH WORKSHOP-01 (the DESKTOP-01 work items) | PD01, PD04, BL01, BL02, UI01, UI02, NV01, NV02, NV03, HT01, HT02, HT03, VS01, VS02, VS03, CM01, LP01, LP03, ST01 (readback), IM02, IM03 (presentation contract) | AC01, AC02, AC10, AC14, AC15 |
| Two: a supported rich document with fluid human/Slate turns | HATCH WORKSHOP-01 began it (Documents: `workbench/documents.py`, `workbench/document_qt.py`, docs/DOCUMENTS_01.md); HATCH AGENT-02 applies the model's turn on the open page (`workbench/model_turn.py`, docs/MODEL_TURN_01.md) and continues a running assignment in the resident service while Ledger is closed (docs/CONTINUE_01.md); takeover of a native artifact follows | PD02, WS01 (document selection), WS02, CM02, CM03 landed mechanically; WS03, WS04, AI03 (model turn), AI05, IM01 open | AC03 and AC09 mechanical without a model (`tools/check_document_ui.py`); the live-model column stays open; AC04 needs a display |
| Three: actual calculations and the cross-application evidence loop | HATCH AGENT-01 began it (the resident agent loop: `workbench/agent_loop.py`, `agent_profiles.py`, `profile_numbers.py`; condition cards `conditions.py`; helpers `helpers.py`; quiet connections `related.py`; the right column `agent_qt.py`; docs/AGENT_01.md) | RM01 (unit-checked sums), XD03 (stale on changed input, recheck), LP02 (five plain lines), AI03/AI04 (the step loop with the model as advisory chooser) landed mechanically; RM02–RM04, XD01, XD02, XD04, AR01 open | AC05 (actual exact calculation), AC07 (changed input → recheck), AC12 (pause, resume, stop; AGENT-02: continue in the service, `tools/check_continue_ui.py`, and the real service run, `tools/check_continue_service.py`) mechanical in `tools/check_agent_ui.py`; AGENT-02's second procedure, files about something (`workbench/profile_files.py`, `tools/check_files_about_ui.py`); AC06, AC08, AC17 open; the live-model column holds build-container trials only (docs/MODEL_TRIAL_01.md) |
| Four: inputs, interruption, model replacement, installation, owner host | HATCH HOST-01 | AI01, AI02, ST02, ST03, OS01, OS02, OS03, OS04 | AC11, AC12, AC13, AC16, AC18 |

## Missing experiences → existing code (Gate one)

| Experience the specification asks for | Requirement | Existing modules | What changes in DESKTOP-01 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both side columns, the Ledger Head and the typing strip stay visible while the centre is used; Home no longer hides the right column | UI01, LP01 | `workbench/empty_workspace_qt.py` (`show_home` hides `sim_dock`), `workbench/typebar_qt.py` (`align()` forces equal column widths and a one-way minimum), `workbench/qt_app.py` (`_apply_default_layout`, docks), `workbench/session.py` (`layout.navigator_width`) | Home keeps the right column; each column has its own two-way minimum and remembered width; saved widths reach the desktop; F11 stays reversible |
| Navigation keeps the artifact, selection, drafts and pins | UI02 | `workbench/workspace_tabs.py` (Preview, five pins, rooms), `workbench/control_qt.py` (`retained_views`), `workbench/explore_qt.py` (`open_instrument`) | Tab strip stops moving; launcher openings stay rooms; assertions in `tools/check_frame_ui.py` |
| Left column shows the machine and the work with inspectable identities; machine overview survives navigation; Trash pinned | NV01, NV02, NV03 | `workbench/host_observations.py` (CPU/RAM/GPU readers), `workbench/hardware_nav.py` (the ARC project hardware navigator, unchanged), `workbench/settings_qt.py` (`SettingsNavigator` switch Cabinet/Settings), `workbench/cabinet_qt.py` (record identities), `workbench/qt_app.py` (Trash placement) | New `workbench/machine_overview.py` (read-only /proc and /sys observations with source and freshness, `ledger.machine` read operation) and `workbench/machine_qt.py` (Machine page + compact strip); the switch reads Cabinet · Machine · Settings |
| Hatch leads with usable tools and tells the truth about each route | HT01, HT02, HT03 | `workbench/hatch_qt.py`, `workbench/explore.py` (adapters `VIEWS`), `workbench/explore_qt.py` (shared rows and tooltips), `workbench/capability_catalog.py` (passive detection), `workbench/service_lifecycle_qt.py` (On/Off/Reboot driver) | Groups first; New Idea/New Project, Ledger services and exit kept below; presentation kind per adapter (workspace, checks, operations) with truthful titles; descriptor tooltips (opens, Slate can, needs, qualification, context); needs setup visible on the row; keyboard open and F1 descriptor. HATCH DESK D2: the cat opens a flat programs list (`workbench/programs_qt.py`: every adapter A to Z by a plain name, Explore the workshop last, type-to-select); New Idea and New Project are Work entries (`menus2`); Graphite services and leaving moved to the System menu (`workbench/system_menu_qt.py`, `workbench/session_power.py`) |
| Paper language: graphite reading, yellow writing, pink actions, no bordered command boxes | VS01, VS02 | `workbench/theme2.py` (QSS2), `workbench/shell2.py` (`CaptureBox`, Slate composer), `workbench/project_desk_qt.py`, `workbench/settings_qt.py`, `workbench/calculator_qt.py`, `workbench/reading_preferences.py` (prose vs code fonts) | Writable passages converted; prose font on owner writing; poem hints where writing is expected; selection visible on yellow |
| The X writing marker as an optional, reversible presentation choice with reduced motion | VS03 | `workbench/reading_preferences.py` (`reduce_motion`), `workbench/text_prompts.py` (`poem` hint), `workbench/settings_registry.py` (41 definitions) | New `workbench/writing_marker.py` (margin X on the caret line, static under reduce motion) governed by the added setting `appearance.writing_marker` |
| One typing surface with an explicit destination and the active work context | CM01 | `workbench/typebar_qt.py` (`TARGETS` slate/stac/kernel/find/shell, `HINTS`), `workbench/console_qt.py` | Visible words Slate · staC · Console with Find and Kernel as quieter advanced words; a context word; no status message lingers in the hint |
| The right column explains work in one vocabulary and scales with the reading size | LP01, LP03 | `workbench/desktop_header_qt.py`, `workbench/operations_qt.py`, `workbench/operations.py`, `workbench/service_lifecycle.py` (`SUMMARIES`) | One held-state sentence from `SUMMARIES`; no hard-coded pixel sizes; service and power targets named as before |
| Settings stay one registry with truthful readback | ST01 | `workbench/ledger_control.py`, `workbench/settings_qt.py`, `workbench/session_settings.py` | One added setting recorded; `tools/check_hatch.py` reports the addition; inventory 07 |

## Gate two: what WORKSHOP-01 built and what remains

| Experience | Requirement | Modules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A rich document route with inline bold, selection, typing continuity, save, reopen, undo | WS02, AC03 | LANDED (no model): `workbench/documents.py` (record kind document in the Project Desk store, revision-bound `documents.edit`, rule-based `documents.interpret`), `workbench/document_qt.py` (the page, one undo stack for both actors), `workbench/shell2.py` (`SlateFace.direct_request`). Starting points kept for later depth: `sdk/cli/arc1cli/office_documents.py` (DOCX projection for export), LibreOffice via `workbench/office_runtime.py` and `workbench/native_sessions.py` for native documents |
| Selection bound to artifact, revision and permitted effects before a model reply | WS01, CM03 | `workbench/typed_artifacts.py`, `workbench/joined_qt.py`, `workbench/joined_work.py`, `workbench/slate_action.py`, `workbench/slate_reasoning.py` |
| Conversation joined to checked action in the active workspace | AI03 | `workbench/shell2.py` (`brain.ask` plan path), `workbench/investigations.py`, `workbench/continuing_work.py`, `workbench/local_brain.py` |
| Human takeover and resume on one artifact | WS03, WS04, AC04 | `workbench/native_sessions.py`, `workbench/working_copies.py`, `workbench/edit_storage.py` |

## Gate three starting points (for EVIDENCE-01)

| Experience | Requirement | Existing modules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Actual calculations with units, bindings and limits | RM01, RM02, AC05 | `workbench/math_model.py`, `workbench/math_service.py`, `workbench/math_backend.py`, `workbench/schedule_math.py`, `workbench/calculator_qt.py` |
| Cross-application loop: document → spreadsheet or mathematics → KiCad-related operation → report | XD01, XD02, AC06 | `workbench/joined_work.py` (the I05 Calc/Python/Writer chain), `workbench/office_runtime.py`, `workbench/kicad_tools.py`, `workbench/kibot_tools.py`, `workbench/evidence_compiler.py` |
| Dependencies and recheck after a changed input | XD03, AC07 | `workbench/reason_graph.py`, `workbench/typed_artifacts.py`, `workbench/checked_methods.py` |
| Evidence back to the model; revise an approach | XD04, RM03, RM04, AC08 | `workbench/investigations.py` (I04 adaptive path), `workbench/evidence_compiler.py`, `workbench/knowledge_service.py`, `workbench/memory_service.py` |

## Gate four starting points (for HOST-01)

`workbench/local_brain.py`, `workbench/brain_qt.py`, `workbench/brain_runtime.py` (model selection, registration, stop, rollback: AI01, AI02, AC11); `workbench/service_lifecycle.py`, `workbench/operations.py`, `workbench/agenda.py`, `workbench/job_priority.py` (AC12); `INSTALL_LS.py`, `INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh`, `INSTALL_LEDGER.sh`, `LS_XSESSION.sh`, `START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh`, `tools/package_release_parts.py` (OS01–OS04, AC13); `workbench/remote_service.py`, `workbench/remote_link.py` (ST03, AC16).

## Claim boundaries kept throughout

Operation counts and adapters are inventory, not finished applications (specification section 3). Offscreen captures and focused checks are mechanical evidence; the real model, real native handover, owner-host and physical columns of the implementation ledger stay open until their own evidence exists. No competing kernel, scheduler or data store is added; additive operations and settings are recorded in the registry record `docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json` (written by `tools/record_registry.py`) and verified by the release check, `tools/check_release.py`.

# Integrated campaign I01: one problem and a real source read

This candidate adds the first of six integrated math and software-use passes to the full Stage Six application. It targets the existing single-user Linux desktop workflow. The Stage Six features and historical records remain in the package.

## Try it

1. Extract into a new program folder and retain the previous program/workspace. Follow GETTING_STARTED.md for the Debian installer and launch command.
2. Open **Project Desk → Problem sheet → Start Clock Lab**. Choose a location in your home folder. Ledger creates a new `Clock_Lab_I01` folder there, imports a separate working copy through the existing ENGINEERING profile, delegates that copy to Slate, and opens its saved question. An existing example folder is never overwritten.
3. Read the **Question** page. Allocation lifetimes are UNKNOWN and have no numeric value. Goals, assumptions, questions, candidate approaches and typed placeholders are editable. The original request stays fixed. Saving creates a new revision.
4. On **Sources and results**, select Requirements and click **Read selected source and keep result**. The registered `work.read` operation reads the working copy. The saved receipt contains the returned text, exact byte count, source SHA-256, output digest, action contract and problem revision.
5. Close and reopen Ledger. Choose the saved problem. The original request, revisions, unknown variables and actual results remain. Reopening checks source freshness and never resumes an action automatically.
6. Edit a source in the working copy, then reopen the sheet. The saved observation remains visible and freshness requires review. A prepared action bound to the previous bytes is refused. Explicitly save the source selection in a new problem revision to investigate the changed input. Earlier evidence retains its earlier revision.

Any delegated profiled working copy can supply a relative UTF-8 text path on the Sources page. This first profile admits eight selected sources, up to the existing reader's 64 KiB per file. The full existing viewers and file operations retain their prior format support; this action profile does not expand the text reader to binary formats.

## What is connected

| Concern | Existing interface reused | I01 addition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ideas, projects and assignments | `project_desk` owner-scoped SQLite records, CAS revisions, history and events | `problem`, `problem_action` and `problem_result` record kinds in the same store; no new database migration |
| Selected source copies | ENGINEERING import, `copies` table, `edit_storage.workspace`, `work.read` | Copy/path/SHA-256/byte bindings, with delegation checked again before a read |
| Tool discovery | Capability catalogue, CLI schemas, declared handler map | Six relevant source-investigation operations, input/output descriptions and separate declared/installed/available/permitted/qualified dimensions |
| Actions and observations | Kernel schema validation, principal, audit and existing source reader | Problem revision/context digest, frozen operation schema and handler digest, exact returned snapshot, idempotent saved-result replay |
| Workspace UI | Project Desk and existing visual controls | Problem sheet with Question, Sources and results, and Tools pages |
| Model authority | Existing read-only PLAN proposal profile | Preserved unchanged. I01 source reads are explicit coordinator actions. The new model action profile belongs to I04. |
| Copy edits and originals | Existing Changes / Continuing work / publication checks | Preserved. I01 grants no new original-publication authority. |
| Launch and backup | Existing Debian installer, launchers, backup/restore | Preserved, with I01 verification added to the release-check entry point |

The complete baseline registry and schema fingerprint are pinned in `I01_BASELINE.json`. `I01_BASELINE_FILES.json` records every file from the supplied archive. `I01_DELTA.json` lists every intentional changed file and added file, and refuses deleted baseline files. Existing native tools and optional model routes remain registered. Presence, scope eligibility and one successful read do not qualify an engine.

## Problem and action contract

`problems.create` stores the exact request, goals, assumptions, typed variable placeholders, open questions, candidates, source bindings and optional project/assignment link. An assignment-linked question must retain that assignment's original request. Variables marked UNKNOWN cannot carry a value, including zero. These placeholders describe inputs; they do not yet implement dimensional arithmetic.

`problems.revise` requires both the current revision and context digest, keeps the original request, and appends history. Supplying sources explicitly binds their current working-copy bytes. Source content is treated as data and never conveys permission.

`problems.prepare` creates an action bound to the current problem and a selected source. It does not run the read. `problems.run` admits only the registered `work.read` contract with read effects. It rechecks owner, current problem revision, context digest, operation schema/handler digest, delegation, selected path, source size and source content digest. Kernel dispatch checks the caller's actual scope and the source reader's ordinary owner/path constraints. The actual result is frozen only after successful validation. A repeated run of a completed action returns its saved result without another read.

`problems.get`, `problems.list`, `problems.history` and `problems.tools` expose saved state to the same owner. `problems.get` returns current source freshness separately from historical observations. Read-only principals may inspect their records but cannot create/revise/prepare/run them. No arbitrary command, write effect, shell, scheduler, network grant or model self-authorization can be supplied through this profile.

## Frozen exercise

`examples/clock_lab/INPUTS.json` pins requirements in Markdown and one-page PDF, CSV memory/power/parts tables, an input-only XLSX, a native KiCad outline and an unexecuted Python stub. All data are invented. The workbook's lifetime values are blank with explicit UNKNOWN state. No native application has been inferred to work from the existence of those files.

The independent oracle is in `tests_integrated/clock_lab_oracle.json`, outside `examples/clock_lab/inputs`. The example copier uses a fixed manifest and excludes the evaluator. Tests independently check integer-byte and Decimal power calculations and a separately stated half-open lifetime variant. The initial task still lacks lifetimes and cannot acquire a feasibility verdict by assumption. Keeping the oracle out of the exercise is a fixture separation, not an adversarial security boundary against arbitrary repository reads.

## Verification

Run `python3 tools/check_release.py --self-test` with the installed runtime Python. It includes the existing six-stage checks and the I01 real-read/fresh-process check. `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests_integrated -v` adds seven focused tests for changed contracts, immutable unknowns, explicit source rebinding, retained evidence when sources disappear, delegation/path checks and the independent oracle.

`python3 -m workbench.problem_checks --ui` exercises the real Qt problem widgets offscreen when PySide6 is installed. Exit 2 with UNAVAILABLE means this host lacks that dependency; it is not a UI pass. The owner's display walkthrough and Debian ThinkPad qualification remain explicit acceptance work. `I01_RESULT.json` reports what actually ran on this execution host.

## Remaining integrated passes

I02 adds quantities, dimensional checks, bounded symbolic/constraint tools, actual Calc/Writer work and graphing calculations. I03 adds protected Python experiments, generic selected-board native checks, and finite evidence/reason graphs. I04 connects an adaptive model action/result/revision loop with scoped flexible grants. I05 adds reusable methods, transfer, linked artifacts and visible graphing/Calc sessions with takeover/resume. I06 performs real-model, unseen-task and target-host qualification and packaging.

The TI-style calculator should share the same units/expression/solver results as the reasoning tools. It is included in I02/I05/I06 rather than becoming a seventh campaign pass. I01 establishes durable context and observed software output; increased model reasoning has not yet been measured.
