# Integrated I02 mathematics and applications

This candidate connects an exact mathematical model, bounded SymPy and Z3 adapters, a What if calculator, and real Calc/Writer operations to the problem sheet introduced in I01. It retains the complete previous application. It targets the single Debian Linux Ledger desktop.

## Install and try

Extract the whole ZIP into a new program folder and retain the previous program and workspace. On Debian, run `bash INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh --math` as your normal desktop user. The math option adds the pinned Python math/document packages, Calc, Writer and a headless JDK. Existing system-package approval and offline behavior are preserved. If system prerequisites are installed, use `bash INSTALL_LEDGER.sh --math`.

The exact calculator and graph use the standard library. Normal Ledger startup remains usable without optional solvers or Office software. Missing dependencies are reported explicitly. Java 17 or newer with its source compiler module is required by the new UNO client; the Debian option installs a JDK.

1. Open **Project Desk → Problem sheet** and start Clock Lab, or reopen the I01 Clock Lab problem.
2. Open **Calculate** and select **Concurrent memory case**. The expression uses the saved quantities; its assumption states that the allocations are concurrent.
3. Click **Calculate and keep**. The checked comparison is false: 17 MiB exceeds 16 MiB in that declared case. The missing lifetime question remains visible. This is a conditional model result, not a verdict on every possible lifetime schedule.
4. Choose workspace for **What if**, from 0 to 10. The graph samples the same mathematical model. Its separately calculated exact linear boundary is 4 MiB. A sample graph does not prove arbitrary behavior between samples.
5. Select **Typical power estimate**, calculate, and obtain 1.25 W from 5 V and the declared 250 mA assumption. The maximum-current question remains open.
6. Click **Make checked Calc and Writer files**. A normal Kernel job opens a clean owned workbook, populates its cells, calls `XCalculatable.calculateAll`, reads actual formulas/values/errors, saves the workbook and reopens it. It creates the supported paragraph/table findings document, edits/saves it in native Writer, exports PDF and reopens the saved DOCX to check content.
7. The completed outputs are then copied into a new `Calculations/ACTION_ID` directory within the delegated working copy. This publication occurs after the job completes, preserving the existing source-change guard. **Open generated working files** opens that directory. Originals are never overwritten. An existing generated file with changed bytes is preserved and causes a conflict; a repeated publication of identical bytes is idempotent.

The saved calculation list retains old observations with their own problem revision and applicability. Save displayed problem edits before calculating. A changed source or problem makes an old action historical and prevents its execution against the new context. No calculation resolves the unknown lifetimes by inventing values.

## Mathematical profile

| Area | I02 behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Quantities | Existing time/frequency/voltage behavior retained; current, power and byte-based memory added. MB is 1,000,000 bytes; MiB is 1,048,576 bytes. Ambiguous KB is refused. |
| Compound dimensions | Products, quotients and bounded integer powers; V times A is power, and memory per time is distinct from memory. Incompatible addition/comparison/conversion is refused. |
| Exact values | Decimal or rational strings become Fractions in base units. The stored rational is exact. A nonterminating decimal display is marked approximate. Floats are never input facts. |
| Expressions | Ordered typed nodes for quantities, variables, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, negation, bounded integer powers and relations. Up to 16 variables, 128 nodes, depth 24 and degree 4. |
| Domains | Real/integer scalar declarations, optional bounds and retained nonzero denominator conditions. Unsupported interval arithmetic is not silently treated as scalar arithmetic. |
| Human entry | A bounded arithmetic syntax is parsed into those nodes. Calls, attributes, indexing, comprehensions and executable statements are refused. No Python eval or backend string parser is used. |
| SymPy | Constructed objects, exact normalization and bounded linear equalities. Underdetermined/free-variable results remain unknown. The adapter does not expose arbitrary nonlinear solving. |
| Z3 | A declared real/integer linear fragment, including inequalities. Variable products and variable denominators are unsupported. A feasible assignment is one witness, not a universal guarantee. |
| Witness checks | Solver assignments are checked against the original IR, bounds and denominator conditions. They cannot change a supplied known input. |
| Bounds | Solvers run in fixed child adapters with CPU/address-space/output/wall limits. Timeout/resource failure is UNKNOWN, not mathematical infeasibility. This is not the general experiment runner of I03. |

Backend states distinguish FEASIBLE, INFEASIBLE, UNKNOWN, UNSUPPORTED and UNAVAILABLE. Invalid dimensions/domains are checked separately. A false comparison can be a successful computation of an infeasible declared case. Process completion, parse/check verdict and evidential applicability are separate fields.

## Shared records and authority

New operations: `math.status`, `math.units`, `math.validate`, `math.evaluate`, `math.solve`, `math.preview`, `math.prepare`, `math.run`, `math.get`, `math.list`, `math.sweep`, `math.office.prepare`, `math.office.run`, `math.office.result`, and `math.office.publish`.

Pure mathematical reads remain read operations. Preparing/running durable observations and publishing owned output copies require execute scope. The shared Project Desk store holds new math action/result kinds with immutable problem/context/model/source bindings and versioned history. No new database schema or second scheduler is introduced. The new `math.office` job uses Kernel ownership, stable request keys, logs, cancellation and process-group termination. Its job request adds one optional `calculation` field to `jobs.submit`; previous fields and required parameters remain unchanged.

Each mathematical action pins its typed model, operation/schema, implementation hashes, assumptions, selected problem/source revision and backend. Known problem quantities and explicitly declared scenario quantities remain distinguishable. A successful computation is labeled a consequence of that declared model; it grants no physical qualification or original-publication authority.

The legacy model PLAN profile is unchanged. These calculator/Office actions are explicit coordinator operations. I04 introduces adaptive model action selection. No live-model decision or increased model intelligence is claimed in I02.

The read-only staC extension uses the same evaluator:

```text
math problem:PROBLEM_ID | calculate "voltage * assumed_typical_current" | unit W
```

The expression is quoted data for the typed compiler. The caller's real principal is forwarded. Compiling or previewing this program creates no write grant.

## Office profile and precision

The unmodified, hash-pinned LibreOffice UNO Java API JAR 25.2.0 is included with its MPL license and upstream POM/source reference. A fixed Java client receives data fields, not model-generated Java. The running native LibreOffice and Java versions are recorded per action. Documents load in an isolated profile with source document macros disabled and external updates disabled. This is a new generated-cell/paragraph/table profile; legacy Office adapters retain their existing interfaces and document-loss reports.

Calc uses native floating point. Each measured formula and numeric value is checked against the exact IR with an absolute tolerance of at least 1e-10 or relative tolerance of 1e-12. Both calculated and reopened observations must agree, and actual cell errors must be zero. Formula identities are checked. Stored input values are not labeled recalculation evidence. The Writer DOCX and its table are reopened and checked; PDF is an actual native export. Originals and arbitrary unsupported workbook/document features are outside this clean generated profile.

The execution host supplied LibreOfficeDev 26.8.0.0.alpha0, commit `2c87e51eeaa2b413ff4ae097b2705eea1995d8e5`, and OpenJDK 17. The tested JAR API version and native engine version are separate identities. The report records this limited compatibility evidence. The owner ThinkPad's installed build and visible session remain separately qualified; a successful development-host fixture does not establish them.

## Debugging and storage

An early full fixture wrote generated outputs during a worker job and correctly triggered the existing source-change guard. This was repaired by keeping native output under the job and publishing to the working copy only after completion. The guard was not weakened.

A separate early concurrent fixture reported a damaged Kernel database. Its exact corruption mechanism has not been established. The compressed synthetic failed database is retained under `tests_integrated/diagnostics` for diagnosis, never as a workspace/migration input. Kernel connection lifetimes now share a reentrant thread/process guard on Linux while retaining SQLite WAL, transactions and database format. Later checks include two concurrent writers, 250 concurrent reads, exact record counts, database quick_check, actual native-job cancellation and complete native round trips. This evidence supports the guarded candidate; it does not retrospectively prove the original failure mechanism or qualify the target host.

## Verify and recover

```text
python3 tools/check_release.py --self-test
python3 tools/check_release.py --self-test --native --ui
```

Use the installed runtime Python. The first command includes earlier six-stage/I01 checks, the connected mathematical case without Office, focused mathematical tests and the concurrency check. The second adds a real native Office round trip, native cancellation and real Qt calculator checks. Native checks may take over a minute. Missing optional dependencies prevent qualification rather than becoming a pass.

`I02_RESULT.json` and the pass discussion identify actual results and limits. `examples/clock_lab/I02_observed` contains actual synthetic Calc/DOCX/PDF outputs for inspection, outside the model-visible input manifest. Expected answers remain in the separate evaluator. The entire I01 package and all earlier features remain in this candidate. Keep the earlier ZIP and back up workspaces before opening them with a new program. There is no automatic database repair or silent retry of a cancelled native action. A new action uses new output identities; incomplete previous output is retained separately.

I03 adds protected general experiments, selected-board native checks and evidence/reason graphs. I04 closes the adaptive model feedback loop. I05 expands visible calculator/application sessions, reuse and takeover. I06 measures real-model unseen tasks and qualifies the Debian ThinkPad.

## Primary technical references

- SymPy parsing/evaluation boundary: https://docs.sympy.org/latest/modules/parsing.html
- SymPy exact objects and solvers: https://docs.sympy.org/latest/modules/core.html and https://docs.sympy.org/latest/modules/solvers/solveset.html
- Z3 arithmetic and its division semantics: https://microsoft.github.io/z3guide/docs/theories/Arithmetic/
- LibreOffice recalculation: https://api.libreoffice.org/docs/idl/ref/interfacecom_1_1sun_1_1star_1_1sheet_1_1XCalculatable.html
- LibreOffice document loading properties: https://api.libreoffice.org/docs/idl/ref/servicecom_1_1sun_1_1star_1_1document_1_1MediaDescriptor.html
- LibreOffice native command interface: https://help.libreoffice.org/latest/en-US/text/shared/guide/start_parameters.html

records.text:
# Integrated I03 experiments and explanations

Candidate 5.1.0a3 adds actual Python experiments, selected-board native KiCad checks, and finite support/refutation graphs inside the existing Project Desk problem sheet. It carries the complete I02, I01 and Stage Six program. It introduces no second scheduler, application, model PLAN grammar or generic record-write authority.

## Install and use

Keep the previous program folder and workspace. Extract the complete ZIP into a new program folder. On the Debian desktop, run `bash INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh --math --experiments` as the ordinary desktop user. This adds the pinned optional math/Office/Wasmtime packages and the distribution's KiCad. The selected-board adapter requires KiCad 9 or newer. If prerequisites are already installed, `bash INSTALL_LEDGER.sh --math --experiments` installs the optional Python dependencies. Existing offline and check-only behavior is preserved; include the new pinned Wasmtime wheel in an offline wheel folder. Missing tools do not prevent ordinary Ledger startup.

1. Open Project Desk → Problem sheet and start or reopen Clock Lab. Keep an exact **Concurrent memory case** observation under Calculate.
2. On Investigate → Experiment bench, click **Qualify Python on this host**. This executes boundary, fuel, memory, output and sparse-file probes. A detected package alone never grants qualified status. The receipt expires after 24 hours and is bound to the host, pinned distribution, embedding implementation and actual Wasmtime library.
3. Select the delegated working copy on Sources and results. **Create experiment in selected copy** creates a coordinator-owned Python stub and parameter file through the existing frozen Changes/journal mechanism. It cannot overwrite an earlier experiment. Existing Changes can edit the script; no new permission prompt is introduced for each internal step within this delegated copy.
4. **Freeze and run experiment** pins the exact script, selected inputs, parameters, problem revision, implementation and qualified runtime. The Kernel executes the selected script in WASI CPython. A real result JSON and CSV are created. The default Clock Lab experiment measures 17 MiB and reports that 17 does not fit inside 16 under the declared concurrent-allocation model.
5. Process exit, schema validity, source applicability and mathematical/design conclusions are separate. Failed attempts remain available. A script that exits zero but emits an invalid unit or schema is not admitted as an observation. **Keep generated outputs in this copy** publishes only retained generated output bytes into a new result directory after job completion. The originals remain separate.
6. **Check board and export outline** selects a `.kicad_pcb` from the same owned copy. A private immutable snapshot goes to native KiCad, which first reproduces the good and broken-outline DRC fixtures. The adapter captures actual native DRC JSON and an explicit single-file Edge.Cuts SVG export. The old ARC/R10 adapter and its project bindings are retained.
7. On Why and alternatives, select the saved exact memory comparison and an executed memory result. **Compare memory results** checks that this helper is using the saved concurrent-memory model and the saved MiB quantities. It proposes a finite graph with two alternative reasons. Each requires the explicit concurrency assumption. Advanced callers can propose other bounded graphs using registered operations.
8. Recompute after changing an input. The exact verdict can remain SUPPORTED while the experiment path becomes stale. The UI says **Verdict stayed the same. Reason paths changed.** It retains the earlier snapshot and shows the inactive path. A right-click menu derives actions from the selected retained path: open its owned receipt or preview its tracked consequences.

The lifetime variables remain unknown. This pass does not infer that the three allocations must overlap in every possible schedule. It does not make hardware measurements or approve fabrication.

## Qualified experiment profile

The execution host lacks usable Landlock and a user systemd session; a nested bubblewrap probe also failed. The pre-existing namespace/cgroup worker profiles are unchanged and are not presented as qualified here. I03 adds a distinct `ledger.python-wasi/1` profile. This is actual CPython bytecode execution inside a WebAssembly instance with capability-based WASI filesystem access. It is not Python AST parsing, a Python `eval` filter, or an unconfined native-Python fallback.

The complete CPython 3.13.17 WASI SDK 24 distribution is bundled without trimming its standard library. The archive SHA-256 is `ceec2512d4bf2d2377a4791603e9879329c9b6aa0e7514a19ef827cdefe3b274`. It is Brett Cannon's unofficial CPython WASI build, not a Python Software Foundation binary release. The full license and provenance descriptor are included. The optional native embedding is pinned to Wasmtime 50.0.1. No runtime is silently downloaded by the experiment runner.

| Boundary | Admitted behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Inputs | Exact selected files copied into a fresh private input tree; maximum 16 extra files, 1 MiB each, bounded total. The frozen Python script runs as `/inputs/experiment.py`; parameters are the explicitly frozen object. Extra inputs appear under `/inputs/selected/` with their relative paths. |
| Filesystem | Bundled runtime and selected inputs read-only; only the job's fresh output directory writable. Host home, workspace metadata, database, credentials and original files are not preopened. No inherited host file descriptors or environment. |
| Dependencies | Bundled CPython standard library. No arbitrary native extensions, pip installs, threads, native subprocesses or host shell. Native application adapters remain separate registered tools. |
| Network | No network capabilities or socket descriptors are supplied. TCP, UDP and Unix-socket attempts are tested as denied/unsupported. This is a guest capability boundary, not a claim of host network-namespace isolation. |
| Memory | 128 MiB guest linear memory; actual oversized allocation fails. This is not a cap on the trusted Wasmtime compiler or the embedding process's entire RSS. The module is fixed and hash-pinned. |
| Compute | 20 billion Wasm fuel units, plus a 30-second Kernel wall deadline including startup. Direct `jobs.submit` cannot extend the profile deadline. A smaller fuel probe must reach its loop marker before exhausting fuel. |
| Output | 2 MiB cumulative guest write budget, 128 guest file-open calls, bounded retained diagnostics. Host callbacks meter writes before performing them. File growth without writes, sparse seeks beyond the file-position budget, links and new subdirectories are refused. |
| Cancellation | Existing Kernel process group owns the trusted embedding process; cancel and wall timeout kill it. A stopped run never becomes a completed observation. Pause/resume is refused; prepare a fresh action. |

The WASI forwarding shim preserves the native WASI calling convention and the guest memory when metered callbacks re-enter WASI. The guest cannot call the unmetered forwarding functions directly. The profile has no authority to load arbitrary Wasm or host callbacks. Unsupported packages, versions, missing archives, changed hashes and failed qualification are explicit refusals.

## Observations, failure and context

New actions/results use existing owner-scoped Project Desk records and history. Inputs are retained through the existing content-addressed edit store. Three new job tools—`lab.qualify`, `lab.python`, `lab.board`—use existing Kernel request keys, logs, source-change guards, cancellation, stop control and restart behavior. `jobs.submit` gains one optional `lab` field; all previous fields and required arguments are preserved. No database migration or automatic repair was added.

A Completed lab job means the trusted coordinator finished retaining an attempt. Its `observation.state` can be OBSERVED, OUTPUT_INVALID or EXECUTION_FAILED; actual Python exit/trap is separate. Native board jobs distinguish COMPLETED process execution from NO_REPORTED_VIOLATIONS or VIOLATIONS. A native failure remains a failed Kernel job with retained logs and native attempt files. No stage converts a missing/failed observation into a successful premise.

The result JSON schema admits named exact rational-string quantities with checked units and booleans with unit `1`, plus explicit assumptions. Duplicate keys, floats as exact input facts, unknown units and malformed payloads are refused. Checking this schema does not prove that the script models the intended problem correctly. The connected demonstration deliberately executes a faulty threshold variant; its valid output conflicts with exact arithmetic and remains visible for correction.

Source files, source-copy delegation, problem revision, context and implementation are checked again at execution and result access. Old observations remain historical when those bindings change. Generated output is written under the private job during execution. Publication into a delegated working copy happens after completion, is idempotent for unchanged bytes and refuses conflicting existing bytes. This retains I02's source-change guard behavior.

The selected-board profile binds the actual installed executable/version, known program files, adapter and fixture outputs. It operates on selected embedded board geometry and stored zone fills. It does not refill zones, compare external footprint libraries, perform schematic parity/ERC, or establish physical correctness. KiCad 9.0.9 on this Ubuntu execution host passed the good/bad fixture pair and both SVG exports. The Debian ThinkPad's installed build must qualify independently. This host's temporary package layout is not embedded as a target installation path.

The ENGINEERING copy profile now explicitly admits `.svg`, so the native outline export can be kept in that working copy. CODE and the other narrower profiles retain their filters. Existing traversal, symlink, hidden/credential and original-publication boundaries remain in force. Board publication selects the actual board's DRC report and SVG, excluding qualification fixture reports.

## Finite reasons and Chronicle

The existing staC four-valued evidence representation supplies UNKNOWN, SUPPORTED, REFUTED and CONFLICT. The new calculator accepts at most 64 nodes, 128 acyclic rules, 8 premises per rule and bounded alternative paths/combinations. Rules combine joint positive or negative premises; separate rules retain alternative derivations. Unsupported cycles, dangling references, unsolicited attestation fields and undeclared assumption nodes are refused. Every recomputation currently traverses the whole admitted graph.

Only coordinator-checked comparisons of owned, completed, current math/Python/board receipts can supply observation bits. A model can propose labels, rules and graphs. It cannot submit observation bits, a reviewed flag, a completed job record or physical qualification through this interface. The interpretation of an arbitrary proposed inference is still **PROPOSED_RULES_NOT_APPROVED_FACTS**. Executing a script does not prove its semantics; agreement under one model does not prove physical truth. Each admitted atom retains its actual model/parameters/script and assumption context for review. A different problem revision/context is excluded.

Verdict, source applicability, reason paths and dependency coverage are separate. A stable verdict with changed support is a recorded event. An absent edge is never treated as proof that a change cannot matter: dependencies outside the declared finite graph remain UNKNOWN. Contradictions retain both directions rather than overwriting one result.

The existing Chronicle now also admits an explicitly validated `REASON_RECOMPUTATION` event. Existing read-event hashes and invariants remain intact. Full reason snapshots remain in the shared record store, referenced by their digests from the existing hash chain. The chain is local tamper evidence, not independent author identity or source truth. Saving a reason record and appending Chronicle use separate local transactions; a failed append returns PENDING without erasing the result, and `reasons.record` retries the append idempotently.

The GUI exposes the retained snapshot and a current preview. Reopening performs read-only dependency recomputation and does not resume execution. Older rule definitions/results remain in version history. The dynamic right-click actions operate on retained selected records, an incremental step toward the planned Fluxbox command-menu interaction model.

## Validation and remaining work

Run `python tools/check_release.py --self-test --native --ui --runtime` with the optional dependencies installed. The wrapper preserves the complete earlier check chain, including native Calc/Writer, source copies, Changes recovery, continuing work, exchange, signed updates, database concurrency and prior Qt views. It adds the connected Python/board/reason fixture, real cancellation, the real 30-second timeout, and actual Qt experiment/reason interactions. `python -m workbench.lab_checks --keep NEW_FOLDER --output REPORT.json` retains a fresh disposable connected exercise. It never launches a model.

The included observed examples and report are synthetic execution-host evidence, outside the input fixture. They are not model-visible oracle inputs or portable live receipts for a new workspace. The original I01 input manifest and previous deliverables are retained.

I03 measures implemented, observed tool mechanics. I04 adds the adaptive local-model action/observation loop, per-session working-copy grants and its compatibility profile. I05 adds methods/transfer and visible application sessions. I06 measures unseen tasks with the real local model on the target ThinkPad. No live model was invoked in I03 and no increase in model intelligence is claimed. Three candidate passes out of six is 50% of delivery milestones, not 50% of all validation or elapsed effort.

Primary implementation references: [Wasmtime Python API](https://bytecodealliance.github.io/wasmtime-py/), [CPython WASI distribution](https://github.com/brettcannon/cpython-wasi-build/releases/tag/v3.13.17), [CPython WASI platform documentation](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Platforms/WASI/README.md), and [KiCad 9 CLI](https://docs.kicad.org/9.0/en/cli/cli.html). Native tool help was checked again before using the explicit SVG export mode.

# Integrated I04 adaptive investigation

I04 meets its execution-host reference acceptance family. All three actual-model cases passed under one unchanged model/config/runtime/executor, and the final conditional wording was reviewed against actual receipts. The 35 focused tests and coordinator checks pass. ThinkPad and broader unseen-task qualification remain I06 work.

Candidate 5.1.0a4 adds a separate ACTION proposal profile and a bounded adaptive investigation inside Ledger's existing continuing-work executor. It preserves the complete I03/I02/I01/Stage Six program and the old read-only PLAN profile. Model proposals remain separate from execution permission and actual observations.

The candidate's current acceptance results are recorded in `I04_RESULT.json`. Native model trials, including failures, are distinct from scripted coordinator checks. A successful test of a permission or recovery mechanism does not establish adaptive model behavior.

## Use the investigation workspace

Install the full program as before. The I02 math and I03 experiment dependencies remain optional; no model weights are bundled or silently downloaded. Register and start an owner-selected GGUF in Brain. The existing pinned CPU runtime, authenticated loopback, template/tokenizer checks, model-file identity and resource guard remain in use. I04 admits the `qwen35` architecture to the read-only inspector's trial list; actual native loading/generation and task performance are still separately tested.

The frozen model configuration includes resident weight loading through the pinned runtime's `--load-mode none` option. The selected native address-space limit and host-memory preflight remain enforced. A successful load is separate from task acceptance.

Open Project Desk → Problem sheet → Investigate → Slate investigation. Reopen or create the problem with its known quantities, explicit unknowns and delegated working copies.

1. Select **Read and calculate** or **Working-copy tools**, review the step/time/token limits and click **Prepare investigation**. Preparation freezes the selected operations, copy identities, assignment, initial problem revision, model configuration and executor/schema bindings. It executes no tool or model decision.
2. Inspect the displayed scope and click **Start with this scope**. This uses the existing owner-grant mechanism once. Slate can make adaptive choices within that scope; it cannot add operations, copies, effects or resources to its grant.
3. The current uncertainty and predicted distinguishing outcomes appear above the frontier. They are Slate's proposals. The observation table shows actual completed operations, adverse outcomes and failures separately.
4. A consequential missing-input question pauses the investigation. Enter the requested half-open lifetime intervals and their time units, state their basis, and click **Supply these lifetimes**. These are owner-supplied inputs, not measured hardware facts. They create a new problem revision before another decision can use them.
5. Inspect retained alternatives, rejected/refined branches and the proposed finding. Right-click an observation for its actual receipt and the question it addressed. Use Pause, Resume or Revoke; the existing master Stop also retains its authority.

The **Direct response allowed** profile permits a response that needs no experiment. The default investigation profile requires actual current-context observations before a finding can finish. A model's text alone does not satisfy that policy. A proposed finding still requires review for interpretation and completeness.

## Exact instruments

`math.concurrent` compares the sum of selected saved scalar allocations against a saved capacity under an explicit concurrency assumption. The model supplies variable names, not copied numeric values. The existing exact IR, units, source bindings and durable math action/result records perform the calculation. It does not need lifetime values and does not imply that actual allocations overlap.

The ACTION argument grammar enumerates declared known quantity and lifetime names for these instruments. The model still selects the capacity, allocations and pairings. Numeric values or JSON interval values cannot masquerade as source names. The registered public tools retain their own complete input validation.

`math.calculate` offers the existing expression/solver profile as one source-bound call. The adaptive fragment requires saved variable names so that units and source identity survive the expression. A quantity result is not a constraint check. Literal-only calculations remain available in the existing calculator's own profile; they are not admitted as source-bound adaptive calculations.

`math.schedule` performs an exact rational sweep over explicitly supplied half-open `[start, stop)` intervals. Releases at a boundary occur before allocations there. It records selected quantities/lifetimes, peak demand, segment demands, capacity and assumptions. Missing lifetimes return UNKNOWN; they never become zero. Time units are converted exactly, allocations and capacity must share dimensions, and negative or empty/reversed lifetimes are rejected. The model cannot supply guessed lifetime values through this operation.

The adaptive schedule fragment waits until the declared lifetime inputs are known. Tool readiness can change when the owner supplies inputs; the original grant does not grow. The underlying public schedule API can report unknown selected lifetimes independently.

The scheduling model is additive. It does not model fragmentation, alignment, allocator overhead or indivisibility. It can establish a consequence of the supplied intervals and amounts, not a physical memory guarantee. The generic resource dimension supports later structural-transfer work, whose method/precondition qualification belongs to I05.

New math receipts remain in the existing owner-scoped Project Desk store. No mathematical source or model text can self-assign a passing hardware qualification.

## Separate ACTION profile

The legacy `slate.ask` tasks and PLAN allowlist are unchanged. PLAN still proposes read-only calls and does not execute them. ACTION uses the new `brain.action` job and current granted operation catalogue.

ACTION inference has two bounded phases. SELECT chooses a currently available operation, candidate key, uncertainty and expected distinguishing outcomes. ARGUMENTS fills that operation's schema and proposes any branch updates. Both are real model generations; the coordinator validates the complete assembled response before any action is executable. Neither a partial stream nor either phase by itself is an action.

SELECT explicitly presents ASK and FINISH alongside the tools. FINISH reports a conditional finding once current receipts resolve the full request and requested follow-ups. The model chooses when to use it; the controller does not replace a duplicate call with a fabricated final answer. Repeated unchanged calls still stop visibly.

The coordinator inserts fixed problem/revision bindings, reconstructs the complete registered call and validates its schema again. Copy IDs must belong to the grant. A native action must have been prepared by this same work order before it can launch. Result reads cannot select unrelated jobs or calculations. Working-copy application can use only a proposal created by this work order, with the existing exact proposal digest and change journal.

The prompt contains bounded source/current-problem data, current tool readiness, retained observation summaries, proposed alternatives and the remaining limits. SELECT sees tool descriptions and readiness; ARGUMENTS sees the selected tool's complete argument schema. Both phases see the actual observations. The full source/model/frame binding remains in the immutable request and is validated before and after inference. Completed operations and remaining unknowns are explicit feedback. Actual tool results are data, and source text cannot change permissions. Predictions and candidate explanations remain model proposals. JSON/schema validation does not prove the semantic truth of a model's interpretation.

Original-file publication, arbitrary host commands, installation, new grants and general scheduler mutation are outside this adaptive catalogue. The selected working copies retain their own read/write/execute policies and registered native profiles. I03's bounded standard-library Python execution and native KiCad/Office profiles remain separate instruments.

## One executor, durable checkpoints

Adaptive work uses the existing `flow_orders`, grants, steps, events and Agenda rows. No new scheduler, background timer, database schema or generic record-writing API is introduced. The new work profile freezes a catalogue and scope; the selected steps are added as the investigation proceeds. The legacy profile still freezes exact calls in advance.

The grant binds the operations, effects, copies, budgets, expiry, model configuration and executor/schema identity. Each branch and observation points to its problem revision/context. Owner answers create a new revision; earlier observations and branches remain historical. Current findings cannot cite stale-context results as their current support.

New actions select an active current branch. Historical and rejected branches remain available for inspection and properly cited interpretation, but cannot silently become the next active branch. The owner-answer revision introduces a current branch for the supplied inputs.

Before an action, a durable intent reserves its resources and identifies the step. A native model/application job receives a stable request key. The next decision waits for the actual completed/failed job result; a launched process never stands in for an observation. Registered result adapters validate their own files, exit status and schema/units. The coordinator records an immutable actual-observation digest in the existing record store and links it to the work step.

Adverse results and tool failures differ. A false checked constraint can support rejecting/refining a candidate for that recorded case. A timeout, parser error, missing dependency or cancelled job cannot refute the hypothesis. Rejection proposals must cite an actual adverse observation in the branch's context. The existing I03 four-valued evidence/reason views remain available; adaptive frontier status is not a new proof system or reviewed-fact authority.

Before continuing after a newly adverse observation, the complete ACTION proposal must include a cited branch interpretation. The model chooses REJECT, REFINE or RETAIN and supplies its reason. The coordinator does not choose that disposition or certify the reason's meaning. A response cannot reject a branch and simultaneously select that branch as its next active action.

Each action and observation retains the branch that the model selected to test. Required feedback addresses that tested branch. Updating a different explanation cannot silently count as interpreting the failed check. Citation lists are bounded by the available owned observations and reject duplicate entries.

ACTION uses its own strict, dependency-free schema-subset validator, including exact union selection, array bounds, unique citations and identifier patterns. Unsupported schema keywords stop validation. This validation runs independently after generation and again on reconstructed tool calls. The legacy PLAN implementation and allowlist remain unchanged.

Step, active-time, token, frontier, decision, failure, working-file and retained-observation limits are explicit. The model's fixed native memory budget must fit the work grant. Child tools retain their own execution/resource profiles. Controller retained-output accounting is distinct from native artifact limits, and the model's address-space limit is not a new aggregate cgroup guarantee for the whole desktop.

Unchanged duplicate calls stop with a recorded stall reason. Exhausted branches, changed inputs, incompatible executor/model versions, missing dependencies and exhausted budgets stop or wait visibly. The controller does not silently extend a grant, fill missing input or keep retrying indefinitely.

Reopening a record performs no automatic investigation step. An interrupted in-flight step is reconciled under the existing Agenda lock and requires explicit Resume. A completed working-copy application is recovered from the existing Changes journal; it is not applied twice. Uncertain partial applications require Changes recovery. Interrupted reads/calculations can repeat only after explicit resumption, with their reservations retained. Source/copy/model versions are checked again.

Pausing or revoking work cancels its pending owned job where applicable. Progress commits recheck the grant, epoch and current step so that a late result cannot overwrite a pause/revocation. A completed proposal is never authority to continue after its grant changes.

An owner lifetime answer writes the problem history and investigation checkpoint in one Kernel transaction. An interrupted answer preserves the old revision and pending question. The retry can commit one new coherent revision. Owner controls are checked again before a new intent, while collecting failed model jobs, during explicit resume and before reconciliation commits.

## Verification

`python tools/check_release.py --self-test --native --ui --runtime` carries the complete earlier regression chain forward and adds coordinator/interval/ACTION checks. These mechanics checks do not silently start or download a model. `python -m workbench.adaptive_checks` labels its injected-choice driver as coordinator-only, with zero model calls; it checks actual calculations, scoped writes, duplicate/stale/permission stops and fresh-process write recovery.

To perform new inference with explicitly supplied weights, run `python tools/check_release.py --self-test --native --ui --runtime --live-model /absolute/model.gguf`, or use `python -m workbench.adaptive_checks --live --model /absolute/model.gguf --keep NEW_FOLDER --output REPORT.json --ui`. The reference configuration and supported host budget must fit that model. The detailed report records the exact file/config/runtime identities and separates qualification of loading/text generation from task acceptance.

The case family starts with the 17 MiB concurrent demand against 16 MiB. Owner-supplied A/B lifetimes `[0,10)` and workspace `[10,20)` yield a 12 MiB peak. An unseen workspace start at 9 instead of 10 creates overlap and a 17 MiB peak. A valid adaptive demonstration must obtain the adverse result, ask for lifetimes, test the supplied variant and change its finding accordingly under the same recorded model configuration. Demonstration scripts, an attractive UI, valid JSON or a successful arithmetic tool alone do not establish that behavior.

Read the actual acceptance fields in `I04_RESULT.json`, `I04_MODEL_TRIAL.json`, and `examples/clock_lab/observed_i04/accepted/semantic-review.json`. The reference run includes both lifetime variants and a direct response with no tool calls. Its first post-checkpoint predecessor was rejected for an unsupported if-and-only-if claim; failed and paused runs remain historical. ACTION instructions now distinguish a sufficient tested case from necessity, uniqueness, optimality and guarantees. Read the included six-pass plan before starting I05. Early malformed, premature, duplicate or timed-out model attempts are not promoted into passing demonstrations. Broader unseen-task qualification and the owner ThinkPad's actual model/display remain I06 work. I05 connects typed application artifacts, checked methods, structural transfer and visible owner takeover.

# Graphite P07 · Intelligent data arrangement

Open **Project Desk → Ask Graphite**. Enter a question, select your assignment,
and add any extra source addresses. **Prepare evidence** runs on the CPU and
shows the selected passages, quantities, and gaps. You can do this with the
local model stopped.

## Put a calculation beside its sources

For an example, put “The warm rail is 12 V. The warm draw is 200 mA.” in a
workspace file named `rail.txt`. Add `files:rail.txt` to Extra sources. Enable
**Include an exact calculation**, enter `voltage * current`, and give it these
source quotes.

```text
voltage = 12 V
current = 200 mA
```

Set the result unit to `W` and the condition to “At the stated warm operating
point.” Preparation shows **2.4 W (12/5 exact)** and keeps the two source spans.
The condition travels with the result. If the question is whether a supply
can start the device, the warm calculation leaves the startup draw open.
When several passages contain a quote, use `name = files:rail.txt | quote` to
select its source. A still ambiguous quote remains a gap. The Kernel can also
bind by a retained passage ID.

## Follow the evidence

- Files and native documents keep their revision and text location. Use
  `namespace:ID` to search an already indexed, admitted reference collection.
  Reviewed reference packets keep their original passage locators, fact
  roles, variants, and conditions. Their address is `packet:ID`.
- Add `calculation:ID`, `reason:ID`, `artifact:ID`, or `condition:ID` to read a
  saved calculation, declared dependency graph, application output, or
  condition card. Each uses its existing applicability reader.
- The compact packet distinguishes unresolved quantities, reviewed facts,
  exact consequences, and scope. Preparation uses the existing reference
  index, ranking, quantity extraction, unit-aware expression engine, and
  read tool selector. It keeps numeric roles explicit and records suggested
  readers separately from actual observations.
- An answer turn receives the selected text and the calculation rows whose
  dependencies fit the measured model context. It can suggest one passage
  from a short catalog of omitted sources and the next question. **Read
  passage** shows the bound text. **Focus next turn** prepares a fresh
  selection from the same sources, with that passage first. You can edit the
  question before focusing, then choose when to ask the local model.
- The Kernel checks source revisions before and after inference, and when
  reading or focusing a passage. When a source changes, prepare again. The
  older packet remains available as a historical record. **Inspect context
  and result** shows the original bindings and what actually fit the turn.

Exact expressions use the existing arithmetic engine's supported dimensions.
Quantity mentions in other units remain visible for interpretation. Native
documents, source text, and reviewed reference facts can contain ambiguous
roles or conflicting conditions. The calculation and its evidence retain
those boundaries. Follow-up selection and interpretation quality depend on
the selected model.

This checkpoint uses a disposable local source and a short native Qt
walkthrough. The model handoff is observed with a held inference boundary.
ThinkPad and live model qualification remain pending.

records.text:
# Shared Ledger control and activity

This development review combines the command/settings foundation and Stacy's
desktop connection. It extends PySide6 and the existing Engineering Kernel.
No scheduler, source-promotion bypass, shell listener or physical programming
operation was added.

## Working surfaces

- Ledger → Settings opens live Appearance, Stacy, Workspace and Operations
  controls. Tools shows read-only executable discovery, separately from qualification.
- Ledger → Commands lists every registered Kernel operation with its actual
  argument schema and required scope. Desktop actions are also listed; connected
  navigation is distinguished from actions requiring their existing interactive UI.
- Ledger → Recent activity expands the bottom four-line activity tail. Follow
  latest, scroll-back pause, filtering and job-to-evidence navigation share the
  same retained event records.
- Tools contains Settings (Ctrl+,), Commands (Ctrl+Alt+K) and Recent Activity.
  The fifteen default ribbon favorites and maximum five pinned workspaces remain.

## Settings authority

The Qt-free `ledger_control` service adapts the current session reading profile,
workspace preferences, Stacy reaction preference and existing CPU priority
policy. Two new private Kernel preferences control Gemini proposals and sharing
of activity metadata. Credentials are never exposed by this registry.

Each setting reports its current value, default, type, limits/choices, scope,
effect and backing store. Updates validate before writing, support an expected
old value, and retain a bounded reversible journal. Undo rejects a change if
the setting has since changed. Existing unrelated session data is retained.
External CLI updates refresh the live desktop's managed preferences.

CPU background mode uses the existing scheduling implementation. Returning to
normal affects new work; the OS may keep existing processes at lower priority.

## Local commands

Local commands work in Stacy's overlay, dock entry and engineering conversation
without a provider key. Examples:

```text
/commands
/settings Operations
/set operations.priority background
/set reading.code_pt 16
/open brain link
/open workbench/engine.py
/build struthio.build
/jobs
/tail
/call workspace.job {"id":"REPLACE_WITH_JOB_ID"}
/undo REPLACE_WITH_CHANGE_ID
/stop
```

Some short natural requests have deterministic local mappings: "make the editor
text larger", "make builds run in the background", "open brain link", "what's
running" and "what changed". These are explicit convenience phrases, not an
offline general language model. Other language uses the configured chat adapter.

`/call OPERATION JSON` reaches the existing Kernel, preserving mode, scope,
tool, ownership, candidate and independent-acceptance checks. Direct local owner
commands have desktop-owner authority. Cloud proposals have read/execute scope
only and cannot accept sources or authorize candidate execution.

The existing CLI/MCP publishes the same new operations:

```text
python -m workbench.engineering_cli call ledger.commands
python -m workbench.engineering_cli call ledger.settings
python -m workbench.engineering_cli call ledger.settings.set --params '{"key":"operations.priority","value":"background"}'
python -m workbench.engineering_cli tail --lines 4 --follow
```

The JSON argument spelling above is for POSIX shells; other shells may need
different quoting. A navigation/open request returns PENDING_DESKTOP, not a
claim of completion. Its connected desktop acknowledges OPENED or reports
FAILED, CANCELLED or expiry. Intents contain only known navigation or validated
project-file opens, never arbitrary method names or execution requests.

## Gemini command connection

Enable "Stacy action proposals" in Ledger → Settings → Stacy. Each request
includes the current public command schemas, tool IDs and setting definitions.
The provider can propose at most three read/execute commands. The owner sees
the exact operation and JSON arguments and chooses Run listed commands.
Only then does the existing Kernel execute them. A proposal is not a result.

Activity sharing is a separate, off-by-default preference. When enabled, the
next request includes redacted recent events, effective settings, selected-object
metadata, active workspace and current job states. Source attachment keeps the
existing independent paperclip/source-sharing control. Activity collection makes
no background provider calls. Provider results and raw source are not silently
fed back into an autonomous chat loop.

Proposals cannot enable their own sharing/control preferences or undo privacy
preferences. A new conversation request, cancellation or Master Stop invalidates
older proposal buttons and pending replies. Live Gemini service availability is
not established by the deterministic transport fixture tests.

## Activity semantics

The bounded local stream projects the most recent 500 metadata events, uses atomic event files,
has stable cursors and reports gaps/truncation. Job events commit in the same
SQLite transaction as their state, including separate worker processes. The
stream combines these with existing GUI/agent
records, non-read Kernel request outcomes and job lifecycle transitions.
Recorded fields include event ID, time, actor, operation, lifecycle state and
optional job/evidence IDs. Detail strings are bounded and redacted; command
arguments, source contents and credentials are not stored by the new bridge.

REQUEST_COMPLETED means the Kernel request returned successfully. A submitted
job's lifecycle and engineering result remain separate. Historical activity is
not live health data or an instruction source. This is Ledger activity, not
complete operating-system telemetry. Privacy redaction is a defensive filter,
not a guarantee that arbitrary imported logs are safe to share.

Master Stop cancels pending presentation intents, fences new command sequences
and retains the existing job/process/session stop path. A service still finishing
is reported as unconfirmed rather than declared stopped. Active work keeps the
existing background-priority policy.

## Scope and validation

The new reusable services are Qt-free workbench modules shared by CLI/MCP and
desktop. Existing SDK contracts/runtime, hardware, firmware, tool pins, policy
and existing tests are unchanged. New acceptance coverage is in
`tests/test_ledger_control.py`. Changes to Kernel dispatch, audit metadata and
job-state recording are disclosed here for independent review.

The first KiCad native DRC adapter now uses this shared control path; see
`docs/KICAD_INTEGRATION.md` for its operation-specific qualification, snapshot
and native-result scope. Other native engines, owner-provider qualification and
physical qualification remain separate. The desktop action catalog explicitly
shows where full CLI parity still needs an adapter.

# Ledger and Slate expanded campaign

Owner authorized plan edition 2. Passes 13 through 37 plus independent acceptance. The assistant is Slate; staC retains its name. This is a prospective plan, not a claim that later capabilities are delivered. The original knowledge campaign remains 61%; expanded scope starts at 30.5%.

## Pass 13 Name migration and capability contracts

13.1 Current UI and new documentation say Slate; staC retains its name and historical provenance.

13.2 Old profiles and archived records open without losing identity or silently rewriting evidence.

13.3 Catalogue distinguishes declared, installed, available, permitted and qualified operations.

13.4 Missing tools, incompatible versions and denied permissions produce explanatory states.

13.5 GUI, CLI and Slate obtain the same checked capability descriptions.

## Pass 14 Context around the selected object

14.1 Component and job demonstrations resolve the exact selected identity across views.

14.2 Sources, evidence, gaps and relevant actions share that identity without leaking another profile.

14.3 Each offered action respects availability, source freshness and current permissions.

14.4 Navigation history, keyboard use, Focus Mode and Engineering Mode preserve context.

14.5 Restart and rapid selection changes never show a late result for the wrong object.

## Pass 15 Activity awareness and resource controls

15.1 An intent can be followed through authorization, execution, artifacts and displayed outcome.

15.2 Cancelled, interrupted, failed and completed work remain distinct after restart.

15.3 Master Stop terminates owned process trees and prevents automatic rearming.

15.4 CPU, memory, priority and budget controls report measured or explicitly unavailable instrumentation.

15.5 Secret redaction, bounded retention, dropped-event reporting and owner isolation are demonstrated.

## Pass 16 Archive intake and package transport

16.1 Inspect ZIP members and metadata without executing or admitting their contents.

16.2 Path traversal, symlink escapes, duplicate names, expansion limits and malformed archives fail safely.

16.3 Repeated admission is identifiable and does not duplicate or overwrite accepted originals.

16.4 Export manifests verify exact files and declare missing dependencies and encryption status.

16.5 Additional formats are qualified individually; unsupported and encrypted inputs are reported clearly.

Retained document acceptance: see DOCX_ACCEPTANCE.md for the explicit Word/Orange Book checklist within passes 17–20 and release Pass 37. It adds no milestone credit.

## Pass 17 PDF reading and technical evidence

17.1 Citations reopen the exact original hash and physical page, including printed-page differences.

17.2 Native text, tables and a Chinese passage retain technical identifiers and source locations.

17.3 A scanned-page OCR case records tool version, uncertain text and its original image.

17.4 Annotations survive restart and export without changing the source or becoming accepted facts.

17.5 Corrupt, restricted or changed PDFs and unavailable readers produce explicit gaps.

## Pass 18 Notes and knowledge base adapters

18.1 A declared Markdown and Org fixture preserves text, metadata, Unicode and attachment references.

18.2 Backlinks and block references survive supported round trips; losses are listed explicitly.

18.3 A real exported graph or vault qualifies the selected application version and profile.

18.4 Repeated import, rename, deletion and conflicting edits have deterministic reconciliation records.

18.5 Queries, plugins and embedded instructions remain inert until separately permitted operations exist.

## Pass 19 Engineering notebook and AppFlowy exchange

19.1 Text, source, requirement, table, query and result blocks retain their underlying identities.

19.2 Saved queries are read-only by default; effects require preview and existing authorization.

19.3 Explicit Save, unsaved recovery and block migration preserve content across restart.

19.4 A genuine AppFlowy export round trip or declared one-way import shows every unsupported block.

19.5 Notebook prose cannot overwrite an accepted source, requirement or Kernel result.

## Pass 20 Spreadsheets and engineering tables

20.1 CSV, XLSX and ODS examples preserve declared sheets, types, identifiers and units.

20.2 Formula text, cached results and measured recalculation outcomes are distinguished.

20.3 A BOM comparison identifies actual changes and links rows to exact component identities.

20.4 External editing and conversion use candidates, explicit saves and isolated office profiles.

20.5 Macros, external links and lossy conversions cannot execute or discard data silently.

## Pass 21 Code navigation and editor interoperability

21.1 Source navigation resolves exact files and revisions with useful symbol locations.

21.2 A qualified parser distinguishes structural findings from lexical matches and runtime truth.

21.3 VSCodium handoff opens the intended candidate and never silently edits canonical source.

21.4 Language servers, when included, run with declared file and execution permissions.

21.5 Changed files, missing servers, malicious workspaces and stale diagnostics are handled explicitly.

## Pass 22 Boards for work and investigations

22.1 Cards link to the actual task, requirement or job rather than a detached copy.

22.2 Dragging a card cannot fabricate job completion, test success or source approval.

22.3 Dependencies, blocked reasons and stale evidence remain inspectable from the board.

22.4 Filtering, keyboard use, saved layout and restart preserve the selected project context.

22.5 Export or import declares the supported fields and preserves source relationships.

## Pass 23 Claims and evidence dependencies

23.1 Claims preserve quantities, units, device grade, operating conditions and exact source locations.

23.2 Support, contradiction, applicability and review states remain independently inspectable.

23.3 A source change invalidates known dependents without marking unrelated claims stale.

23.4 Untracked dependencies and solver assumptions are explicit; no completeness claim is implied.

23.5 PSRAM and USB cases retain their host, source and physical proof boundaries.

## Pass 24 History and hypothetical changes

24.1 A timeline resolves actual sources, decisions, jobs and artifacts in their original context.

24.2 A hypothetical branch remains visibly separate from accepted project state.

24.3 Impact analysis lists known affected obligations and explicitly untracked consequences.

24.4 Promotion uses candidate review and owner acceptance, with comparison and rollback.

24.5 Restart, divergent edits and tampered chronology cannot silently rewrite accepted history.

## Pass 25 staC language and shared intent

25.1 Versioned syntax and IR preserve declared legacy compatibility or offer tested migrations.

25.2 Pipes preserve object types, units, source bindings and explicit read or write effects.

25.3 Ambiguous English requests require resolution before consequential execution.

25.4 GUI actions, written commands and translated requests reach the same Kernel checks.

25.5 Shell injection, forged approval and cross-owner references fail under actual permissions.

## Pass 26 Reusable engineering recipes

26.1 A recipe reproduces the PSRAM pilot with its actual tool and source fingerprints.

26.2 An unseen variation is chosen after method freeze and outside the teaching index.

26.3 An incorrect case fails its oracle and unresolved USB bindings remain unresolved.

26.4 Approval, revocation, budgets, interruption and restart prevent unauthorized or duplicated effects.

26.5 Owner activation follows recorded trials and independent review where required.

## Pass 27 Slate local reasoning and explanation

27.1 A real model answers the pilot questions with correct sources, conditions and uncertainty.

27.2 Short answers expand into technical evidence, operations and remaining proof obligations.

27.3 Grounded explanations are evaluated separately from deterministic retrieval and tool success.

27.4 Hostile source instructions and unsupported claims fail to acquire action authority.

27.5 Tokens, latency, memory, failures and cancellation are measured on the declared profile.

## Pass 28 External reasoning and frontier exchange

28.1 Complete a genuine Gemini exchange with actual usage, failures and disclosure records.

28.2 Complete an authentic request and return ZIP exchange; verify every source binding.

28.3 Missing, stale, forged or overbroad returns remain unaccepted with clear reasons.

28.4 Cancellation, retry and ambiguous network outcomes cannot silently duplicate external actions.

28.5 External advice becomes reviewed interpretation or a candidate, never automatic owner approval.

## Pass 29 Study and evaluated procedural learning

29.1 A study report separates sources read, hypotheses, tested procedures and accepted conclusions.

29.2 Unseen evaluation material stays outside the teaching corpus and selection process.

29.3 Procedure selection is measured against a declared baseline on additional cases.

29.4 Idle study obeys configured budgets and stop state; real host behavior awaits Pass 36.

29.5 Failures, supersession and unresolved questions remain searchable rather than being erased.

## Pass 30 Persistent memory and context clearing

30.1 Committed task state is read back before context is cleared.

30.2 Exact retrieval restores source locations, accepted decisions, gaps and unfinished steps.

30.3 Summaries link to originals and expose uncertainty or translation provenance.

30.4 Revoked sources, changed conditions and stale summaries cannot masquerade as current knowledge.

30.5 Retention, rollback and private namespaces prevent accidental evidence loss or cross-project exposure.

## Pass 31 Replaceable local brains

31.1 Two actual local models complete a controlled switch with identities and measured resource use.

31.2 Task, memory, decisions, presentation preferences and unresolved obligations survive replacement.

31.3 Malformed, incompatible or oversized models fail without destroying the working configuration.

31.4 CPU fallback works on a declared profile; AMD acceleration is separately measured if included.

31.5 Model rollback and dependency rechecks succeed without replaying completed jobs.

## Pass 32 Memory editions and verified restoration

32.1 Consistent database and full-text checks pass with complete external-source manifests.

32.2 A clean profile restores exact investigations, notebooks, procedures and source references.

32.3 Restore leaves idle disabled and does not resurrect live jobs, credentials or execution grants.

32.4 Corrupt, partial and incompatible editions fail without overwriting valid state.

32.5 Optional ISO is verified read-only; physical disc burning and readback require actual host evidence.

## Pass 33 Mattermost collaboration adapter

33.1 Actual channel and thread import preserves authors, timestamps, attachment hashes and server identity.

33.2 Pagination, incremental sync, edits and deletions reconcile without duplicates.

33.3 Access revocation removes future retrieval rights and marks dependent context appropriately.

33.4 Retry, reconnect and token failure expose accurate state without leaking credentials.

33.5 A draft handoff or explicitly authorized test post demonstrates the outbound permission boundary.

## Pass 34 Thunderbird and email intake

34.1 EML and mbox examples preserve headers, MIME bodies, attachment hashes and thread references.

34.2 HTML, tracking resources, malformed MIME and attachment instructions remain safely bounded.

34.3 One genuine Thunderbird export or scoped live profile qualifies the declared adapter.

34.4 Deduplication handles Message-ID collisions and repeated imports without assuming global uniqueness.

34.5 Private mail stays scoped; draft creation and any sending require their own explicit authority.

## Pass 35 Opus audio and Slate voice

35.1 Real capture and playback produce verified audio with duration and source identity.

35.2 Transcript segments link to audio offsets and expose uncertain words and model version.

35.3 Voice requests use the same staC preview and authorization path as typed requests.

35.4 Microphone permission, privacy, stop, cancellation and resource budgets work on the declared host.

35.5 Codec-only, transcription and synthesis support states are reported separately with measured limits.

## Pass 36 Owner ThinkPad workflow qualification

36.1 The owner completes an end-to-end object, notebook, evidence and authorized investigation workflow.

36.2 Short answers, technical expansion, readable scaling, keyboard access and explicit Save are usable.

36.3 Real input, focus, power and resource conditions control idle study and priority.

36.4 Master Stop, app restart, context clearing and recovery work without unwanted rearming.

36.5 Latency, retrieval quality, memory, CPU and model behavior meet predeclared host budgets.

## Pass 37 Distribution migration and recovery release

37.1 Fresh three-ZIP assembly, manifests, launcher and native UI checks pass on the declared profile.

37.2 Upgrade from Pass 12 and rollback preserve private data without silently reversing incompatible schemas.

37.3 Licence inventory, upstream notices and distributed dependency provenance match shipped bytes.

37.4 Privacy inspection finds no owner corpus, credentials, model weights or private development state.

37.5 Release notes identify qualified, unavailable, optional and blocked capabilities with their actual evidence.

## Retained acceptance

Original 12.5 independent case review remains OPEN. Independent protected-source review, actual ThinkPad acceptance, genuine model/provider qualification and real physical evidence remain separate. Expanded total: 200 points; legacy 65 available and 61 earned; new passes 125; final independent acceptance 10. No implementation credit comes from writing the plan.
