# MACHINE VIEW 01 · the left column's machine and work navigator

HATCH DESKTOP-01, work item WI-4. Requirements NV01, NV02, NV03 (spec §5), the context line of HT02, the mechanical
steps of AC10. Date: November 5, 2026. Nothing in this document is owner-host acceptance: every observation quoted here
was read on the development container, and the readers describe whatever machine Ledger runs on.

## What the owner sees

The left column now carries three views behind one switch bar, `Cabinet · Machine · Settings` (three pink action words;
the current one is set in weight with a pink rule under it, so the state is not said by colour alone). Above the switch
bar, in every view, sits the **machine strip**: one line, refreshed every 2 s, reading

    <processor> · RAM <used>/<total> · <free of the workspace mount> free · net up|down

for example `AMD Ryzen 7 PRO 5850U · RAM 9.8 GiB/62.7 GiB · 412.0 GiB free · net up`. Each value that cannot be read
is the word `unavailable` in its place; nothing is animated or estimated. The strip's tooltip and accessible description
name the sources (`/proc/cpuinfo`, `/proc/meminfo`, `os.statvfs` of the workspace mount, `/sys/class/net` operstate and
carrier) and the time of the sample. The strip elides to the column; it never widens it (its minimum width is 0).

The **Machine view** is a tree with a details pane under it:

    Machine
      Processor            model · cores · threads; logical processors; load average
      Memory               RAM in use of total; swap; a cgroup ceiling when one applies
      Storage              Ledger program folder and Workspace (path, mount, free); disks; mounted filesystems
      Connections          each interface: kind (ethernet, wireless, virtual, tunnel, loopback) and link state
      Devices              USB devices; input devices; display connectors
      Installed tools      the catalogue's native families: found on PATH or not, pinned archive verified or not
    Work
      <each project>       the cabinet's own project identities (project:<id>), pink links
    Settings               switches the column to the settings hierarchy

Choosing a row writes its words into the details pane: the label, `Observed HH:MM:SS · source <path>` (or the honest
state and its reason), then the observed values as words (bytes as sizes, flags as yes/no). Choosing a Work row selects
that very identity in the cabinet and opens its record room in the centre; choosing Settings shows the settings hierarchy
in this column and the editor in the centre. `Refresh machine view` re-reads everything; the page also re-reads itself
when shown after 30 s. Trash keeps its fixed place at the foot of the column, below the stack, outside every scroll
area; Import and Export stay as the cabinet's directional words above the tree (NV03). This file touched none of them.

## Honesty rules (NV01)

- Sources are `/proc`, `/sys` and `os.statvfs` only. No subprocess, no network, no `lspci`, `lsusb`, `ip` or `df`.
- Every item carries `source` and `sampled_at`. A source that is not present or unreadable yields an `UNAVAILABLE`
  state with the path and reason in words (`not present: /sys/bus/usb/devices`), never a blank or a guess.
- A section with nothing to list is a leaf (`Devices · none detected`, `Connections · unavailable`) whose details say
  why; no empty hierarchy level is shown. A bounded list says so (`· bounded`, `PARTIAL`).
- Addresses are not read: an interface is named by kind and link state only (`addresses: NOT_READ`).
- Installed tools are presence only: `shutil.which` for the catalogue's executables, the pinned-archive hash for the
  llama.cpp runtime and the Python WASI runtime. No tool is started; versions stay unmeasured; qualification stays
  `not assessed on this host` exactly as Hatch says it.
- The result's `basis` is `CURRENT_LEDGER_HOST_NOT_OWNER_HOST_QUALIFICATION`. The ARC project hardware (F133, D213,
  FPGA45, FPGA12, NOR, PCB) remains in `workbench/hardware_nav.py` under Work / Project; the machine readers never
  describe it, and the Machine tree never lists it. Physical and project views are therefore distinguishable by
  construction (AC10 pass condition, mechanical part).

## Sort rule (spec §5 "alphabetize comparable siblings with a documented rule")

Comparable siblings (disks, mounts, interfaces, USB, input and display devices, tools, projects) are ordered by the
natural key of their label: digit runs compare by value, letters case-folded, ties by id (`nvme0n1p2` before
`nvme0n1p10`; `eth0`, `lo`, `wlan0`; `Icarus Verilog` before `KiBot` before `KiCad`). Descriptive lines keep their stated
order: the Processor and Memory rows (identity, count, load; RAM, swap, ceiling) and the two Ledger paths at the head of
Storage, followed by disks and then mounts, each group natural. The three roots `Machine`, `Work`, `Settings` and the six
machine sections keep the schematic's order (physical to peripheral) rather than an alphabetical one; each section's
`order` field states its rule.

## Bounds

| list | bound |
|---|---|
| mounts, interfaces, USB devices, input devices (each) | 64 |
| disks | 32 |
| display connectors | 16 |
| partitions per disk | 16 |
| any word | 160 characters |
| bytes read from one `/proc` file | 256 KiB |

A whole `ledger.machine` answer stayed under 20 KB on the development container and is asserted under 512 KiB in
`tests_integrated/test_machine.py` for a fixture host with 70 interfaces and 100 input devices.

Storage excludes `loop*`, `ram*` and `zram*` block devices (pseudo or memory-backed, not storage) and lists mounts whose
device is under `/dev/` other than loop devices, plus whichever mount holds the program folder or the workspace even
when it is not device-backed (an overlay root in a container, for instance). Those two mounts are marked
`holds the program folder` / `holds the workspace`. Mountpoints are decoded from their octal escapes (`\040`).

## The operation `ledger.machine` (the one recorded operation addition of DESKTOP-01)

- Module `workbench/machine_overview.py`, the FIELDS / SCOPES / dispatch pattern every read module uses.
- Scope `read`. Arguments: optional `section` ∈ `processor, memory, storage, connections, devices, tools`.
- Answer: `schema ledger.machine/1`, `sampled_at`, `basis`, `host` (kernel release and host name from
  `/proc/sys/kernel`), `program_folder`, `workspace`, `sections[]` (id, title, state, items[], count, sources, notes,
  partial, order, sampled_at), `sources`, `limits`, `sort_rule`, `distinct_from`, and the counters
  `model_calls = network_calls = native_invocations = subprocesses = 0`.
- Item: `id, label, kind, state (OBSERVED | PARTIAL | UNAVAILABLE), source, sampled_at, values{}, reason?`.
- Registration: `workbench/engineering_kernel.py` imports the module (one line), merges `machine_overview.SCOPES` into
  `CAPABILITIES` (one line) and routes `op in machine_overview.FIELDS` in `Kernel._dispatch` (one line);
  `workbench/engineering_cli.py` merges `MACHINE_FIELDS` into `schemas()` (two lines). The kernel keeps three explicit
  tables for an operation (scopes, schemas, dispatch), so a bare import could not register it; `stacy_foundation.
  handler_map()` finds the module through the import as `workbench/machine_overview.py · dispatch ·
  DECLARED_FIELDS_ROUTE`. Earlier `ledger.*` reads (`ledger.explore`, `ledger.operations`, `ledger.cabinet`) were
  folded into `ledger_control.py`; that file belongs to WI-3 in this pass, so the registration went through the kernel
  tables instead. No second dispatcher, scheduler or store.
- Registry readback (`workbench.doctor.inventory()`): 691 operations; the 690 SERVICE-01 rows byte-identical; the 112
  job tools identical; schema digest `3976b8bc94370a1d91b915cade233ab29afabad2e29c69950452f634ca20b786` with ledger.machine alone, `e3523d01aef045f30605085ab1e8322a2b32f0d387de6dcb6248c385c23164f0` in the WORKSHOP-01 registry of 698 operations (baseline
  `9b28255cf4cd31117ece3edada8a737b569e9de996cbb32836e3b1040f92e1a1`). `tools/check_hatch.py` will say
  `ADDITIONS_RECORDED` once `HATCH_WORKSHOP_01_RESULT.json` lists `ledger.machine` under `added_public_operations`;
  until then it says the addition is unrecorded, which is the truth.
- Privacy note for the integrator: `ledger.machine` describes the host. It should join `stacy_control.CLOUD_PRIVATE`
  (beside `ledger.explore`) so an external provider is never handed it, and `activity.OBSERVER_OPERATIONS` so the
  Machine view's reads do not fill the activity journal. Both files are outside WI-4's ownership; proposed, not done.

## The switch and the session

`settings_qt.SettingsNavigator.show_view('cabinet' | 'settings' | 'machine')` drives the stack; the existing
`show(on)` keeps its meaning (on → settings, off → cabinet) for every caller in `navigation_qt`, `control_qt` and
`cabinet_qt`. `settings_navigation.mode` now takes the third word `machine`: WI-1 widened the loader
(`session.NAVIGATION_MODES = ('cabinet', 'settings', 'machine')`), so the chosen view is saved and the Machine view
returns at start exactly as Settings does. `settings_qt.PERSIST_MACHINE_MODE` (True) is the one switch to write
`cabinet` instead should a loader without the word ever have to read the file. The Qt check writes the mode and reads
it back through `Session.load`.

The machine strip is created by the navigator and inserted above the switch bar
(`box.insertWidget(0, strip)`), so it is present in all three views and independent of them (NV01: selection and
navigation never erase machine visibility). It reads `host_observations.memory()` (the same source as the right-column
RAM monitor), `machine_overview.cpu_model()` (cached a minute), `machine_overview.space(workspace)` and
`machine_overview.network_up()`; the whole tick is a handful of small file reads and one `statvfs`.

## V-24

The Settings filter (`QLineEdit#SettingsFilter`) is now the same yellow passage as the cabinet filter (background
`#f8edc9`, no border, bottom rule on focus, selection `#ecd7d5`); the check measures the share of its pixels in that
colour.

## Decisions taken (PD04)

1. Registration through the kernel tables rather than one import line or `ledger_control.py` (above). NV01/CM02.
2. Six machine sections in the schematic's order; natural order inside them; the Ledger paths first in Storage. §5.
3. `zram` excluded with `loop` and `ram` (memory, not storage). NV01.
4. Sizes in binary units labelled GiB/MiB/TiB, so a 64 GB module reads 62.7 GiB and nothing is rounded up. NV01.
5. Empty sections are leaves with a state word, not parents of a placeholder row. §5 "no empty levels".
6. A Work row opens the record room as a click in the cabinet does, after selecting the identity there; the cabinet view
   takes the column, which is the existing follow rule for record rooms. NV02.
7. The Machine view yields to the cabinet or settings view exactly when the Settings view did before (a record room or
   settings editor becoming current); the strip is what survives navigation. NV01.
8. `settings_navigation.mode` gains `machine` through the shared `Session.load` vocabulary (WI-1's `NAVIGATION_MODES`),
   so the Machine view is remembered like the other two; a documented constant falls back to `cabinet` for an older
   loader. UI02.
9. The current switch word is said by weight and a pink rule in addition to its accessible description. VS01/AC15.
10. Tool rows reuse `capability_catalog.native` and say presence only; the llama.cpp archive is verified by hash, never
    extracted or run. HT02/HT03.

## Evidence

Tests (per module, from the program folder with the venv interpreter):

    venv/bin/python -B -m unittest -v tests_integrated.test_machine

Six tests: missing `/proc` and `/sys` give honest unavailable states; a fixture host is read with bounds and natural
order and no process may start; the tools section reuses the catalogue families passively; short model names and sizes;
`ledger.machine` is a bounded read for the owner and a read-only principal with the schema fixed; the registry adds
exactly `ledger.machine`, keeps every baseline row and the 112 tools, and matches the recorded digest.

Qt check (offscreen, disposable profile, process guards):

    QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen venv/bin/python -B tools/check_machine_ui.py

Captures under `build/desktop01_ui/machine/` (or `ARC_LEDGER_MACHINE_CAPTURE_DIR`), report `machine-ui.json` with
`state`, `checks`, `captures` (sha256 and resolution), `strip_samples` and the zero-activity counters:

- `Ledger_Slate_HATCH_Desktop_01_Machine_01_Machine_View.png` (1920×1200) · the Machine view, Storage open, the
  workspace path selected, details with source and time
- `Ledger_Slate_HATCH_Desktop_01_Machine_02_Work_Link_Selects_Cabinet_Record.png` · the project chosen under Work: the
  cabinet shows the same identity selected, its room is open, the edited Preview is untouched
- `Ledger_Slate_HATCH_Desktop_01_Machine_03_Settings_With_Strip.png` · Settings from the switch under the same strip;
  the yellow settings filter
- `Ledger_Slate_HATCH_Desktop_01_Machine_04_Compact_1366.png` (1366×768) · the Machine view, one-line strip, Trash at
  the foot

AC10, mechanical part, exercised by the check: inspect machine/storage/device state (source and freshness in details);
project links select the same cabinet identity; Import and Export present; Trash pinned bottom-right outside scrolling
in all three views; the settings hierarchy reachable from the switch and from the tree; the chosen view written to the
session and read back through `Session.load`. The setting-change half of AC10
(ask Slate, read back stored/effective/pending) is the existing `ledger.settings.*` route and is not re-claimed here.
Real host and device observations for hardware claims remain the owner-host dependency the specification names.

# Ledger and Slate milestones

A pass is a bounded implementation and verification step. A milestone is an observable working capability assembled from its dependent passes. Several passes count as a milestone when the declared workflow is demonstrated, not simply when a pass counter reaches five.

| Milestone | Passes that assemble it | Observable result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 — Concern foundation | N1, N2/G1-G5, N3, P17 | Organize one concern, retain stable identities, read original evidence, save separate notes and keep shared jobs independent of desktop closure. |
| M2 — Shared reading | SW-001, P17, SW-002 | The owner reviews and publishes an exact view; a paired satellite reads the same identity/revision through an inert renderer with its own presentation. |
| M3 — Documents and working knowledge | P18, P19, P20 | Optional notes exchange, source-bound notebook blocks, engineering tables/BOMs and the declared editable-document profile work together with visible conversion losses. |
| M4 — Traceable engineering desk | P21, P22, P23, P24 | Navigate exact source, manage real tasks, trace claims/dependencies and compare hypothetical candidates without rewriting accepted history. |
| M5 — Grounded Slate reasoning | P25, P26, P27, P28 | staC (pronounced Stacy), reproducible recipes, actual local-model reasoning and genuine reviewed Frontier/Gemini exchanges share checked source and effect contracts. |
| M6 — Durable continuity | P29, P30, P31, P32, SW-003 | Evaluated study, exact-context resume, real model replacement, complete verified recovery and device reconnect preserve decisions and avoid duplicate work. |
| M7 — Hosted conversational office | N4, N5, P33, P34, P35 | Guided Debian hosting, a conversation-first satellite, optional collaboration/mail adapters and actual voice use one concern and service. |
| M8 — Owner-qualified release | SW-004, SW-005, P36, P37 | Resolve the conditional graphical bridge pilot, prove the real iPhone/home network and ThinkPad workflow, then rehearse installation/update/restore with independent acceptance. |

M1 has development demonstrations from the retained checkpoints. M2 has SW-002 development demonstrations on the declared native/browser profile. Physical iPhone, owner-host and independent acceptance remain OPEN. P18, P19 and P20 demonstrate the declared M3 development workflow; owner/independent acceptance OPEN. Next M4 spans P21–P24; next boundary P24. Later groups contain four or five passes as shown. These groups do not remove any original five-case pass requirement, conditional SW-004 pilot or independent/owner acceptance gate.

A development milestone is a reviewable capability on a declared profile. An owner-qualified milestone needs the actual ThinkPad/iPhone/network or other stated environment. Source/security acceptance remains separately OPEN. Fabrication, routing and physical programming remain HOLD.

There are 22 retained planned deliveries after this P20 development checkpoint. P17 participates in two milestone dependency chains and is counted once. G1–G5 were subpasses inside one N2 delivery. Milestone groups are unequal effort and cannot be converted into a new completion percentage. Historical 86/225 points remain unchanged.

Every pass handoff includes an approximately ten-minute discussion: where the project is, what changed, what was proved, what remains open, the next work, which milestone advanced and the final destination. State installation relevance and migrations plainly. Do not require a routine questionnaire to continue already authorized decisions.

The language remains **staC**, pronounced **Stacy (STAY-see)**. Slate remains the male bird.

records.text:
# Minimal Debian installation and startup

November 3, 2026 · America/Phoenix · written for HATCH SERVICE-01, startup and installation readback revised in HATCH INTEGRATION-01, words and packaging brought to Graphite 0.1 on November 6, 2026. Graphite is the public name of the program (earlier Ledger & Slate); the scripts, the installer file INSTALL_LS.py and the state folders keep their earlier names.

The product goal is a minimal Debian edition whose main visible workspace is Graphite. It should install from prepared USB media or pull a verified public release and its prerequisites over a working wireless connection. The current deliverable adds the application installer and a dedicated session launcher for an existing Debian system. A bootable Debian installer image, public release hosting and a complete offline dependency cache remain separate deployment work.

## What starts Graphite

The target is Debian 13 on the owner's AMD ThinkPad. No GNOME or KDE session is required. Python 3.11–3.13, the declared Qt runtime, display/input drivers and the existing programme dependencies are required. The dedicated session adds Xorg, xinit/startx, Fluxbox and a session bus. The optional minimal-session package group also includes NetworkManager and Mesa prerequisites.

From a local Debian text login, run `bash START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh` in the installed programme. It checks the session commands (`startx`, `fluxbox`, `dbus-run-session` and an X server, `Xorg` or `X`) and calls startx with the supplied LS_XSESSION.sh. That session starts Fluxbox without its toolbar/slit and opens the Office fullscreen. Exiting Graphite ends this dedicated graphical session and returns to the text environment. From an existing display it opens the fullscreen Office without starting a second X server. Normal `bash START_OFFICE.sh` remains available.

From a text login the script takes no arguments: `--doctor`, `--version` and similar options belong to `bash START_OFFICE.sh`, or to START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh from an existing display, where they are forwarded. Starting a whole X session to answer `--version` would be untruthful, so the text-login branch refuses arguments with a message instead.

Exit-status readback. xinit discards the session client's exit status and startx returns xinit's, so a plain `exec startx` would return 0 whether Graphite exited cleanly, crashed or never showed a window. LS_XSESSION.sh therefore runs START_OFFICE.sh once in the foreground, records `{"status":N,"utc":"…","log":…}` in `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/ledger-slate/last-session.json` (naming `launch-error.log` only when one was written during that session) and exits with N; a failure to write the record never changes the exit status. START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh removes the previous record before startx, reads the new one afterwards and prints one line, `Graphite ended with status N` (with `details: <launch-error.log>` when there is one) and exits with N, or `Graphite session ended; status not recorded (startx returned N)` when nothing was recorded. The session client's INT, TERM and HUP traps record 130, 143 and 129 the same way. A failed start writes its traceback to `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/ledger-slate/launch-error.log` (falling back to the folder beside the programme), prints it to the terminal, and the message names only a log file that was actually written.

LS_XSESSION.sh exports `ARC_LEDGER_FULLSCREEN=1` and `ARC_LEDGER_XSESSION=1`. The second marker is how the System menu (the pale Graphite symbol at the upper right; `workbench/system_menu_qt.py`, the words in `workbench/session_power.py`) knows it is running in the dedicated session: its leave row reads Return to Debian in this session and Exit Graphite from an existing desktop; it closes Graphite the ordinary way. The same separated group holds Log out, Restart and Shut down (HATCH DESK D2, the owner's brief): each first asks the leave flow's questions, asks for confirmation naming its scope (nothing is stopped before it), closes Graphite the ordinary way, then asks logind itself (`loginctl terminate-session`, `systemctl reboot` or `systemctl poweroff`, never sudo); logind's CanReboot and CanPowerOff decide whether they are offered. This session starts no permission agent, so where logind would ask for permission (`challenge`) Restart and Shut down read unavailable here and say to use `systemctl reboot` or `systemctl poweroff` at the text login after Return to Debian. START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh's existing-display branch exports only the fullscreen marker, so an existing desktop reads Exit Graphite. Nothing in these scripts restarts Graphite: when it exits, the X session ends and the text login returns.

The scripts do not rewrite login files, enable automatic login, partition a disk, change Wi-Fi credentials or reboot the computer. Native display, input, driver and owner comfort checks remain open until the actual host is available. A later appliance edition needs an explicit tested automatic-start policy and recovery path.

## Using the supplied ZIP volumes

Download every numbered ZIP (`Graphite_0.1_part_NN.zip`), RELEASE_PARTS.json and INSTALL_LS.py (the Graphite installer; its file name is kept) into one directory. Every ZIP is at most 15,000,000 bytes. They are inspectable ZIPs containing ordinary project files, with hashed chunks only for a runtime archive too large to fit in a single volume. The installer validates that chunk inventory before writing anything and restores the file automatically before checking the full payload. Do not treat a single volume as a complete programme.

First review a plan:

```bash
python3 INSTALL_LS.py --usb . \
  --target "$HOME/Applications/Graphite_0.1" \
  --minimal-session --plan
```

The plan writes and downloads nothing. With `--extract-only` it lists the single extraction step and no start command, because extraction installs nothing.

For a USB programme with public dependency downloads over an already working connection:

```bash
python3 INSTALL_LS.py --usb . \
  --target "$HOME/Applications/Graphite_0.1" \
  --minimal-session --yes
```

Use `--profile suite` to select the existing engineering, worker, math and experiment dependency groups. Desktop is the smaller default. Exact model files, licences, native tool/runtime profiles and their qualification remain separate. No model download or native acceptance trial is initiated by this installer.

Use `--extract-only` to verify and restore the complete project without invoking sudo, apt or pip. Target a folder on the computer, not the media:

```bash
python3 INSTALL_LS.py --usb . \
  --target "$HOME/Applications/Graphite_0.1" --extract-only
```

The installer stages the programme in a hidden temporary folder beside the target and moves it into place in one step, so the folder that will contain the installation must be writable; a read-only USB folder is refused with a message naming that folder before anything is written, and FAT or exFAT media, which cannot hold the programme's file permissions, stops the staging with a message that says so (the staging is removed and nothing is installed; choose a folder on the computer). A refused or failed installation removes any empty parent folders it created and leaves no staging behind. An existing target folder is retained; choose a new release folder. Working records remain outside the replaceable programme under their established paths. A failed dependency installation retains the verified extracted programme for inspection and says so.

`--manifest-sha256` pins RELEASE_PARTS.json for USB media too, not only for public downloads: pass the checksum from a trusted source when someone else copied the media and the installer refuses a manifest that does not match it.

What the installer says at the end. `--yes` is passed to INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh only when you gave it. Without `--yes`, the sudo prompt needs a terminal; when none is attached the installer says so before it starts, INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh skips the apt step and exits 3 with the line `PREREQUISITES_SKIPPED` after the runtime installer succeeded, and the final line reads it back. The final line always names what happened, for example `Program extracted and verified · Runtime imports verified · Debian prerequisites skipped (no --yes and no terminal for the sudo prompt) · Minimal session prerequisites missing (startx, Xorg) · Owner display and native/model qualification remain separate.` A start command is printed only when it would work: when the minimal-session commands are missing the installer prints the desktop start line and the INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh command that installs them instead of `bash START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh`. Every refusal reads `Installation needs attention: …` on standard error; a damaged manifest, chunk inventory or ZIP is a refusal, not a traceback.

## The optional packet capture

Log's Network stream (the writing line in Log mode) shows this computer's interfaces and connections without any extra package. Its packet capture runs the system's own capture tool, which a minimal Debian does not have. To add it, run `bash INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh --network-capture --yes` from the installed programme (INSTALL_LS.py does not pass this option; it is a separate, deliberate choice). It installs `wireshark-common`, which provides `dumpcap`, and nothing else: no Wireshark window, no group change.

Debian asks during that installation whether non-superusers should be able to capture packets. Answer Yes. Then the steps, in the words Log's Network stream uses (the administrator is root):

1. only if it did not ask, or you answered No: as the administrator, `dpkg-reconfigure wireshark-common`, and answer Yes: non-superusers may capture packets;
2. as the administrator, `usermod -aG wireshark <your login>`;
3. log out and in again, so the session carries the wireshark group.

The installer prints these steps, worded the same way and with your login, instead of running them. Graphite itself never runs them, never asks for the administrator's password and never changes the system's permissions: when capture is not possible, Log's Network stream says why and lists the same steps. What a capture keeps (header fields only: the capture tool passes at most 128 bytes of each packet, which after short headers include the first bytes of what the packet carries; Graphite's parser reads the header fields and drops the rest at once), that it is never in promiscuous mode and is bounded by seconds and packets, who may start one (only you; an assignment proposes and waits) and where its summaries live are in docs/NETWORK_01.md. Capture only networks you own or may monitor.

## Fully offline USB

A fully offline USB also needs OFFLINE_FILES.json and matching `debs/` and `wheels/` folders. This cache is not contained in the programme parts. Prepare it on a clean target-matching Debian environment so already installed dependencies are not accidentally omitted. Include all transitive system dependencies needed by the chosen profile and wheels for its exact architecture and Python version.

The inventory schema is `ledger.offline-files/1`. Its `files` object maps each relative path under debs or wheels to byte count and SHA-256. Unlisted files, missing wheels and changed dependencies are refused. The installer invokes apt with `--no-download` for supplied Debian packages and the existing runtime installer with pip `--no-index` for supplied wheels. Missing prerequisites fail rather than falling back to a network download.

```bash
python3 INSTALL_LS.py --usb /media/USB \
  --target "$HOME/Applications/Graphite_0.1" \
  --offline --minimal-session
```

The base Debian installation, wireless/display firmware and account setup must already be usable. Model weights remain separate, as do any external native runtime assets that the selected profiles require. The eventual bootable appliance USB should guide these base-system steps, but this checkpoint does not supply such an ISO.

## Public release download

The installer supports `--public-manifest` with a public HTTPS RELEASE_PARTS.json URL and mandatory `--manifest-sha256`. ZIP names are resolved relative to that manifest. It verifies transport sizes, ZIP hashes, restored chunks and the complete payload before running an installer. TLS verification stays enabled. No downloaded script is piped directly into a shell. The downloaded parts (about 77 MB) are held in the system temporary folder, which is a memory-backed tmpfs on Debian 13, until extraction completes.

A public Graphite release has not been published yet. Use a real published URL and its separately trusted checksum when hosting is established. The supplied private review links are not public release hosting. Programme checksums establish integrity relative to the supplied manifest, not publisher identity by themselves.

Wireless download requires a working connection before installation starts. Debian may require firmware for the actual wireless hardware. Use the official Debian installer/firmware route or a matching offline cache; no assumption is made about the exact ThinkPad wireless chip. No OS package installation, wireless configuration or X session has been run on the owner host in these cloud checks.

## Packaging the volumes

Two steps, both from the program folder. `python3 tools/package_graphite.py OUT` rebuilds the seed (`project/stacy_seed/current`, the program's own sources for staC), rewrites `MANIFEST.json` (`graphite_release` 0.1, `version` from `workbench/version.py`, every shipped file with its size and SHA-256) and writes `OUT/Graphite_0.1_full.zip`; `--dry-run` writes nothing and lists what would be shipped and how the manifest would change, `--manifest-only` rewrites only the seed and the manifest. From `build/` only Graphite 0.1's own evidence (`build/graphite01_ui`) and the live model-trial records (`build/agent01_ui/model_trial`, `build/agent02_ui/model_trial`) are shipped; what the Qt checks write there when run by hand stays local. Then `python3 tools/package_release_parts.py OUT/Graphite_0.1_full.zip PARTS_FOLDER "Graphite 0.1"` writes the volumes `Graphite_0.1_part_NN.zip` and RELEASE_PARTS.json. The release name is a required argument; the tool carries no default that could label a new release with an old name. The first volume carries the entry points (INSTALL_LS.py, the start and install scripts, MANIFEST.json), README.md, RECORD_OF_DIRECTIONS.md, the daily guide, this note and the complete specification. `tests_integrated/test_install_media.py` packages a fixture archive with small volume and chunk limits and restores it through the shipped installer, checking bytes and file modes.

## Quick installation and later acceptance

The new entry point selects `--quick`: install the declared dependencies, verify runtime imports, release integrity and source bindings, then show the startup commands. INSTALL_LEDGER.sh prints the `bash START_MINIMAL_DEBIAN.sh` line only when `startx`, `fluxbox`, `dbus-run-session` and an X server are present; otherwise it names the missing commands and the INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh command that installs them, and the Office start line stays. The original extended installer walkthroughs remain available when deliberately requested. Quick installation is not native, exact-model, protected-worker or owner-host acceptance.

Before appliance release, demonstrate a fresh Debian install, real display/input, a complete offline USB install, a public wireless install, actual GGUF inference, service cycling, recovery and an update preserving owner work. The complete project specification defines these acceptance requirements in detail.

Official sources checked November 3, 2026:

- [Debian installation guide](https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/amd64/install.en.html)
- [Loading missing firmware](https://www.debian.org/releases/trixie/amd64/ch06s04.en.html)
- [xinit and startx](https://packages.debian.org/trixie/xinit)
- [Fluxbox manual](https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/fluxbox/fluxbox.1.en.html)

# Live model trial · the smallest Qwen and the step up (HATCH AGENT-01)

November 5, 2026 · UTC. Where: the build container (4 logical CPUs, Intel Xeon at 2.30 GHz, 15.7 GiB RAM, no GPU), not the owner's ThinkPad. What ran: the real operations, real worker processes and the pinned llama.cpp CPU runtime (build b11669) that ships under runtimes/. Nothing here is owner-host qualification; the records are build/agent01_ui/model_trial/*.json.

## The owner's direction

"If you must test a model, let's build our program to work with the smallest, so that a model upgrade is multi benefit." So the trial used the smallest instruct GGUF of the Qwen2.5 family and then the next size up, with the same questions.

| Model | File | Size | SHA-256 | Licence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M | qwen2.5-0.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf | 491,400,032 bytes | 74a4da8c9fdbcd15bd1f6d01d621410d31c6fc00986f5eb687824e7b93d7a9db | Apache-2.0 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M | qwen2.5-1.5b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf | 1,117,320,736 bytes | 6a1a2eb6d15622bf3c96857206351ba97e1af16c30d7a74ee38970e434e9407e | Apache-2.0 |

Both come from the Qwen organisation's GGUF repositories on the public hub; the hashes above are the hub's own and matched the downloads. No model file is included in the release; the Brain room registers a file you place on the computer.

## What happened, in order

1. `brain.model.add` registered each file (a real inspection job, about 2 to 3 s); `brain.model.use` with context 4,096 and four threads loaded it and qualified it for CPU chat (0.5B in 0.7 s); `brain.status` read READY with a live worker.
2. The first `brain.ask` ever run with a live worker failed on an undefined name in the reply path. Fixed in this pass (workbench/local_brain.py). Nobody could have hit it without a model.
3. Plan mode then failed with CONTEXT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: the direct set's schemas alone were about 6,800 characters, more than a 2,048-token context leaves after the answer. Fixed: with a request in hand the plan prompt carries a core set of eight operations plus the tools chosen for the request's words (under 5,000 characters), and the trial activated with a 4,096 context.
4. Chat: both models answered in a sentence (0.5B in 1.5 to 4.6 s, 1.5B in 3 to 6 s).
5. Plan mode on "make the words quick brown bold" with the page and selection as context: the 0.5B model produced schema-valid JSON but chose knowledge.page; the 1.5B model proposed `documents.edit` with the document id, expected revision 2, offsets 4 to 15, the quoted words and a bold change. Its paragraph index was wrong (4 instead of 0); the store would refuse that selection as SELECTION_CHANGED rather than apply it to the wrong words.
6. Choice mode (added in this pass: `brain.ask` with mode `choice` and `choices` n answers with one option number, schema-constrained at temperature 0): the 0.5B model picked option 3 (read the page again) in every situation; the 1.5B model picked option 1 (sum the quantities) deterministically in the plain case, which is right, and still option 1 when the units differed, where asking the owner was right.

## What it means for the loop

The agent loop keeps explicit rules primary. A profile plans the steps and knows which options are acceptable in the current state; the model is consulted only where more than one option is acceptable, its pick is accepted only if the profile marks that option acceptable, and every consultation is recorded as a step with the job id, the pick and the decision. A better model simply picks better; the record and the safety are the same.

Recommendation for the ThinkPad: qualify the 1.5B file as the default and keep the 0.5B file as the minimum the program must remain useful with. Both run on the CPU path; the Brain room says what is selected, qualified and running.

## What stays open

The owner-host run (display, input, the owner's own model file), speed on the ThinkPad's processor, longer conversations, the model turn applied to a real page in the desktop (the proposal path exists and is covered mechanically; the live application is the next pass), and any claim about larger models.

# Live page trial (HATCH AGENT-02)

November 6, 2026 · UTC · the build container, CPU runtime b11669, not the owner host.

`tools/model_trial_page.py` (integrator tool, not shipped) registered each GGUF file through `brain.model.add` and `brain.model.use`, created a three-paragraph page through `documents.create`, asked `brain.ask` in plan mode with the words an open page gives the model (`document_qt.slate_context`, with AGENT-02's hint line), and applied what came back exactly as the desktop does: `model_turn.decide` against the page, then `documents.edit` with origin `SLATE_MODEL`. The reports are in `build/agent02_ui/model_trial/`, and the two earlier stages are under `history/`.

## What the trial found

Before the fix, both small models filled every optional key of the change under schema-constrained decoding. A "make it bold" proposal arrived as bold plus "replace with nothing" plus an empty new paragraph. The page applied it by itself and deleted the selected words; with the 0.5B model "lazy" became "Normal". It was undoable, but a model turn must never destroy words by itself. The canned offscreen check could not have found this.

| Model | Request | Proposed change | What the page did | Seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | bold selected words | `knowledge.page` | not applied: only an edit of the open page (documents.edit) applies by itself; knowledge.page waits for Run | 13.6 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | heading on the caret paragraph | `{"bold": true, "italic": true, "underline": true, "style": "Normal", "replace": "Normal", "append": "Normal"}` | not applied: it changes words but its selection holds none; select the words first | 12.1 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | replace a word | `{"bold": true, "italic": true, "underline": true, "style": "Normal", "replace": "Normal", "append": "Normal"}` | applied: made “lazy” bold and made “lazy” italic and made “lazy” underline and made the paragraph body text and replaced “lazy” with “Normal” and added the paragraph “Normal” after paragraph 1 | 12.0 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | bold selected words | `{"bold": true, "italic": false, "underline": false, "style": "Normal", "replace": "", "append": "", "append_style": "Normal"}` | applied: made “quick brown” bold and removed italic from “quick brown” and removed underline from “quick brown” and made the paragraph body text and replaced “quick brown” with “” and added the paragraph “” after paragra | 21.1 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | heading on the caret paragraph | `{"append": "", "append_style": "Normal"}` | not applied: the words it quotes (“quick brown”) are not at that place on the page | 21.1 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | replace a word | `{"append": "", "append_style": "Normal"}` | not applied: its selection reaches past paragraph 1 | 21.1 |

## The fix, and what its independent review found

The first fix narrowed the model's form of `documents.edit` to one kind of change and made `decide` set aside filled-in no-ops and refuse mixed kinds. Two read-only reviewers then measured it live and found more. With one optional marks object, the 1.5B model answered everything with a body-text style and the 0.5B model switched every mark on. The deletion guard checked only that something was selected, not which words. A paragraph change could land one paragraph off. At the default 2,048-token context, every page request failed before the model answered, because the plan prompt was too large.

| Model | Request | Proposed change | What the page did | Seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | bold selected words | `{"bold": true, "italic": false, "underline": false}` | applied: made “quick brown” bold | 12.1 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | heading on the caret paragraph | `{"bold": true, "italic": false, "underline": false}` | not applied: it names paragraph 4 and the page has 3 | 18.1 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | replace a word | `{"bold": true, "italic": false, "underline": false}` | applied: made “lazy” bold | 13.6 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | bold selected words | `{"style": "Normal"}` | applied: made the paragraph body text | 18.1 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | heading on the caret paragraph | `{"style": "Normal"}` | not applied: its selection reaches past paragraph 3 | 19.6 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | replace a word | `{"style": "Normal"}` | applied: made the paragraph body text | 22.6 |

The final rules:
- The model is offered one alternative per kind: bold, italic, underline, a paragraph style, replace, append or clear, with that key required, and no empty replacement or paragraph.
- `decide` sets aside what rides along, and applies one kind and one mark at a time.
- Words are replaced or deleted by themselves only when they are the owner's own selection.
- A style or added paragraph applies by itself only on the owner's paragraph, and a style the paragraph already has is no change.
- Anything else waits for Run, and the card says why.
- A request about an open page is offered only the page's operations and at most two small chosen ones, so it fits the default context.

## Final run, at the default 2,048-token context

| Model | Request | Proposed change | What the page did | Seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | bold selected words | `{"bold": true}` | applied: made “quick brown” bold | 7.5 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | italic selected words | `{"bold": true}` | applied: made “lazy” bold | 9.1 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | remove the bold | `documents.interpret` | not applied: only an edit of the open page (documents.edit) applies by itself; documents.interpret waits for Run | 7.5 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | heading on the caret paragraph | `{"bold": true}` | not applied: it changes words but its selection holds none; select the words first | 9.0 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | replace a word | `{"bold": true}` | applied: made “lazy” bold | 9.1 |
| Qwen2.5-0.5B | words the rules do not know | `{"bold": true}` | applied: made “quick brown” bold | 9.0 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | bold selected words | `{"bold": true}` | applied: made “quick brown” bold | 13.6 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | italic selected words | `{"style": "Normal"}` | not applied: once what changes nothing is set aside (paragraph 1 is already body text), it changes nothing | 15.1 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | remove the bold | `{"bold": false}` | applied: removed bold from “quick brown” | 15.1 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | heading on the caret paragraph | `documents.interpret, documents.save` | not applied: only an edit of the open page (documents.edit) applies by itself; documents.save waits for Run | 16.6 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | replace a word | `{"replace": "sleepy"}` | applied: replaced “lazy” with “sleepy” | 15.1 |
| Qwen2.5-1.5B | words the rules do not know | `{"bold": false}` | applied: removed bold from “quick brown” | 15.1 |

- Qwen2.5-0.5B: 4 of 6 requests applied by themselves; every word of the page is as it was (marks aside).
- Qwen2.5-1.5B: 4 of 6 requests applied by themselves; the words changed only here: paragraph 1 “The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.” → “The quick brown fox jumps over the sleepy dog.”.

## What this means for the owner

Nothing a small model proposes can now delete or add words on the page by itself, and everything that does apply is visible, glows, and goes back with one undo. The small models still pick the wrong kind of change for some requests. The direct rules handle bold, italic, underline, headings, body text and "replace x with y" without any model, so the model path matters for requests the rules do not know. On the ThinkPad, the 1.5B file stays the default to qualify.

records.text:
# The model turn applied to a real page (HATCH AGENT-02 · WI-B)

November 6, 2026. Owner decision D19: Slate acts freely inside an assignment and asks only for originals, network and outside effects; **a document edit the model proposes applies at once, visibly, and can be undone**. Before this item a `documents.edit` the model proposed waited on a Run/Edit card like every other proposal. Now, when the page it names is open in the centre and the proposal fits that page, it lands there by itself, is washed pencil yellow for a moment, and Ctrl Z or the word “undo” takes it back. Every other proposed operation keeps the review words. Nothing here claims acceptance; the live turn with the 1.5B model is the integrator's (kernel level, build container).

## Where it lives

- `workbench/model_turn.py` (new, no Qt, no calls). `decide(action, page)` returns `{apply, arguments, reason, notes, corrections}`; `page` is `{document, revision, blocks, caret_block, selection}` plus, from the page, each paragraph's words (`texts`). It applies only a `documents.edit` whose id is the open document (filled when missing), whose `expected_revision` is the page's (filled when missing; a different one is **stale** and refused), whose change is one the store accepts (`bold`/`italic`/`underline` on or off, `clear` true, `style`, `replace`, `append` with `append_style`), on a paragraph the page has, with quoted words that are at that place. A missing selection is the owner's selected words, or the caret's paragraph for a paragraph change. The model's place stands whenever it can hold the words it quotes; the owner's selection takes its place only when it cannot (a paragraph the page does not have, or offsets where those words are not). Every correction that changes where the edit lands or who it is recorded as is also in `corrections`. `words(result, action, model_id, corrections=…)` is the sentence Slate says, and it ends with those corrections, so they are on the card. `keeps_places(change)` is true for marks, clear and style only (no words changed, no paragraph added). `request_words`, `changed_range`, `not_applied_words` and `model_short` are helpers.
- `workbench/document_qt.py`. `DocumentsTab.model_page()` gives decide its page; `apply_model_edit(arguments, request, model_id)` saves the page first, decides, writes `documents.edit` with the model's origin and the owner's request, applies the same change through the page's one undo stack as **one undo step** (`apply_locally` opens one outer edit block; the paragraph style goes first, then the marks/clear/replace, then an appended paragraph, and the edit blocks `set_style` and `append_locally` open nest inside it, so one Ctrl Z or “undo” takes a combined change back whole; the style goes first so a mark in the same change is laid over the heading font, not wiped by it), syncs exactly as `slate_request` does (reloading the saved revision only when the local application differs, and then saying Ctrl Z does not reach it), refreshes the condition line, and washes the changed range (`flash`): one `QTextEdit.ExtraSelection` in `AMBER` stepping down from alpha 255 over 1.5 s in ten steps; under Reduce motion it stays 1.5 s at full strength and then clears. The wash is never a character format, so nothing of it is saved. The caret is left after the changed words, so a selection does not cover the wash. `slate_context()` saves a dirty page first (the model binds its proposal to a saved revision) and ends with one line the model can copy, under 200 characters: `To change this page use documents.edit with id <id>, expected_revision <n>, selection {block, start, end, text} and change {bold|italic|underline|style|replace|append}.`
- `workbench/shell2.py`, `SlateFace.poll` and `proposal_card`, plus `apply_on_page` and `applied_card`. For each proposed action: a `documents.edit` with a Documents page current goes to `apply_model_edit`; applied, its card reads **APPLIED ON THE PAGE** with the program, Slate's sentence, the word **undo** (`tab.slate_request('undo')`) and *Was this right?* Right/Wrong (the existing `mark()`); not applied, it keeps Run/Edit with the reason above them. Other operations keep Run/Edit unchanged. The request recorded on the page is the owner's words (the job's message before the open-item context). Two edits in one proposal, both written for the revision the model saw: a later edit follows the earlier ones onto the revision they made **only while every earlier one kept the places** (`keeps_places`: marks, clear, style). Then each paragraph index and offset means exactly what it meant when the model wrote it. After a replace or an append the later edit stays made for the old revision: decide refuses it as stale, and its card keeps Run/Edit, gives the reason and adds that an earlier edit in the proposal changed the page's words. A later edit with no revision counts as written for the proposal's revision. A stale revision is refused, never rebased. The cards scroll into view.

## What the small model actually proposes, and what decide does with it

In the AGENT-01 live trial (build container, `build/agent01_ui/model_trial/`), Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct Q4_K_M proposed `documents.edit` with the right id, revision, offsets 4–15, the quoted words “quick brown” and `{bold: true}`, but paragraph index 4 instead of 0 and `origin: HUMAN`. decide uses the owner's selection only because that place cannot be right: paragraph 5 does not exist on the page, and the quoted words are exactly the owner's selected words. Slate's sentence and the card then say “the model named paragraph 5, words 4–15, which do not hold “quick brown”; your selection in paragraph 1 is used”. A place that does hold the quoted words is kept even when the owner selected the same words elsewhere: “make the fox in the first paragraph bold”, with the second paragraph's “fox” selected, bolds the first paragraph's fox. The store checks the quoted words again against the saved revision. A selection with no quoted words relies on its offsets, and it lands only on the revision it was written for (or one the same proposal reached by marks and styles alone). The model may never sign as the owner: its origin is always replaced by the model's, and Slate says “recorded as Slate’s model, not HUMAN”.

## The origin

Integrated (AGENT-02): `documents.EDIT_ORIGINS` adds `SLATE_MODEL` for `documents.edit` alone; `documents.create` and `documents.save` keep `HUMAN`, `SLATE`, `IMPORTED`. `model_turn.ORIGIN` reads it and is `SLATE_MODEL`, so a model-proposed edit is stored as `DOCUMENT_EDITED_BY_SLATE_MODEL` and `documents.edit` reads back `basis: MODEL_PROPOSAL_CHECKED_AND_APPLIED`, `model_used: true`; a direct rule edit still reads `EXPLICIT_RULES_NO_MODEL`, `model_used: false`. This changes one operation's schema (the origin enum of documents.edit), recorded in the registry digest.

## The instruction matrix

Integrated (AGENT-02): `instruction_matrix.APPLIED = ('documents.edit',)`. A `documents.edit` with origin `SLATE_MODEL` completes the latest `PROPOSED` row for the same operation and document id within the link window, `SUCCESS` with the reason “applied on the page” or `FAILED` with the error; an edit with any other origin records nothing, exactly as before. The owner's Right/Wrong marks on the card still win over the automatic outcome. No store was added. `tests_integrated/test_model_turn.py` StoreReadback proves the readback and the link.

## Evidence

- `tests_integrated/test_model_turn.py`: 18 cases. decide (the live-trial proposal, filled id/revision/selection, caret paragraph, stale revision, another or no document, other operations, unknown changes and arguments, a paragraph the page does not have, quoted words not there, words changes needing words, binding the quoted words, a model place that holds the quoted words kept over the owner's selection, `keeps_places`, corrections in the sentence), words / request_words / changed_range, and offscreen against a disposable store: `apply_model_edit` (the store, the event, the wash existing and clearing, “undo” as a new revision, a stale proposal untouched, an appended paragraph through the undo stack); one “undo” restoring the blocks from before the edit after `{style, append}`, `{replace, append}`, `{bold, style}` and `{italic, append, append_style}`; and two edits of one proposal through `SlateFace.apply_on_page` (append then a paragraph style, and replace then an offset-only mark: the second is refused as stale and nothing lands on the wrong paragraph or words; a missing revision counts as the proposal's; two marks: both land where the model named them, the owner's selection of the second “fox” not pulling the first edit away). No model, no job; launch and submit held.
- `tools/check_model_turn_ui.py` (offscreen; `ARC_LEDGER_MODEL_TURN_CAPTURE_DIR`, default `build/agent02_ui/model_turn/`; JSON `model-turn-ui.json`). The request typed in the strip goes to the plan path; `brain.status`, `brain.ask`, `jobs.get`, `slate.progress` and `brain.result` are answered on `Kernel.dispatch` with a canned reply shaped like `run_reply`'s (and recorded in the matrix as `run_reply` records it); every other operation passes through. Eleven checks: the hint line in the message, the edit applied as a revision with the model's origin and the request, the paragraph index corrected and HUMAN not kept with both corrections in Slate's sentence on the card, the documents.get keeping Run/Edit, the wash fading from 255 in ten steps and clearing, no highlight in the document or store, Right marking the matrix row GOOD, the undo word as a new revision, Reduce motion holding then clearing, a stale proposal (the owner kept typing while the model worked) not applied with the reason and Run/Edit kept, a two-edit proposal through the strip (append, then a subheading for the old paragraph 2) whose second edit is not moved onto the new revision and keeps Run/Edit with the reason (no paragraph became a subheading), 1366 by 768, zero jobs/launches/submissions/provider requests/processes. Captures `Ledger_Slate_AGENT_02_ModelTurn_01_Applied_Wash_1920.png`, `_02_Stale_Not_Applied_1920.png`, `_03_Compact_1366.png`.
- Reruns, redirected (after the fix pass to `agent02_reruns/fix-B/`): `tools/check_document_ui.py` (9 checks) and `tools/check_agent_ui.py` (13 checks) PASSED; `tests_integrated.test_documents` green.

## The fix pass after the independent review (November 6)

An independent reviewer reproduced three defects in the first implementation. All three are real, and all three are fixed here.
- **The chain (high).** The second documents.edit of one proposal was moved onto the revision the first one made whatever the first one did. After an append its paragraph index named another paragraph (a subheading landed on the added line). After a replace its offsets named other words (“own” made bold). It now follows only after marks, clear and style; otherwise it is stale and keeps Run/Edit (`shell2.SlateFace.apply_on_page`, `model_turn.keeps_places`).
- **The owner's selection over a right place (medium).** decide used the owner's selection whenever the quoted words equalled it, even when the model's place held those words, and the note saying so was never shown. Now the owner's selection is used only when the model's place cannot hold the quoted words. Every correction is in Slate's sentence and on the card (`model_turn.decide` `corrections`, `words(…, corrections=…)`).
- **Two undo steps (medium).** A change with append was two undo commands, so “undo” left the style or the replaced words saved as a new revision. It is now one edit block (`DocumentsTab.apply_locally`). The style also goes first, so `{bold, style}` applies in place and is undoable instead of reloading the saved revision.
- **The origin (low).** It needs the store, which this item does not own. It is still open (see The origin).

## The live page trial (integration, November 6)

The live page trial (docs/MODEL_TRIAL_02.md) ran Qwen2.5 1.5B and 0.5B through the real operations in the build container, and it found what the canned check could not. Under schema-constrained decoding both models filled every optional key of the change, so a "make it bold" proposal also replaced the words with nothing and added an empty paragraph, and the page applied it. The fix works at both ends. The model is offered one kind of change per proposal (one mark, a style, replace, append or clear, never an empty replacement). `decide` sets aside what rides along and applies one kind and one mark at a time. It replaces or deletes only the owner's own selected words, and a paragraph change applies only on the owner's paragraph; everything else waits for Run. An independent review measured the first version of the fix live and found four more holes, all closed. Page requests now also fit the owner's default 2,048-token context, which before failed every time. In the final run at that context, the 1.5B model applied bold, remove-bold and "replace lazy with sleepy" correctly, sent the heading request to Run, and changed no other word. The 0.5B model answers "bold" to almost everything, visibly and undoably. The rules still handle the common edits without any model. The rules live in `model_turn.tidy_change`, `kinds_of` and `decide`, and in `local_brain.page_edit_schema`. `tests_integrated/test_model_turn.py` holds the exact live proposals (LiveTrialShapes) and the review's cases (ReviewOfTheFix).

## Open

The live turn with the 1.5B model on the kernel (integrator); `SLATE_MODEL` in the store and its readback (`documents.edit` says `EXPLICIT_RULES_NO_MODEL`, `model_used: False` for a model-proposed edit until then); a first edit with no `expected_revision` is filled with the page's current revision, so if the owner saved newer words while the model worked, only quoted words protect it; the matrix outcome for an applied edit; a model edit arriving while another tab is current waits on its card (it applies only to the page open in the centre); the owner display and host.

# Native capability integration status

This tracks the agreed fifteen-tool integration sequence. It describes dedicated
Ledger workflows, not merely whether a program is found on PATH. Existing
source editors, viewers, host/RTL jobs and SDK services remain available.

| Tool | Dedicated integration status |
| --- | --- |
| KiCad | Native DRC on bound R10 copies; retained findings, rules and qualification |
| KiBot | Source-checked component inventory and held fabrication-output candidates |
| ngspice | Reduced native DC/RC models, waveforms, measurements and numerical qualification |
| Yosys | Current R10 memory-enabled ECP5 synthesis; mapped resources, port preservation and native evidence |
| nextpnr | Bound current R10 routing, complete LPF pin coverage and separate reported internal-clock results |
| Project Trellis | Offline ECP5 packing/decode/roundtrip candidates; explicit package-proxy labels and programming HOLD |
| Icarus Verilog | Original RGMII/SDRAM bench jobs, shared pump check and four-state digital traces |
| Verilator | Native RTL diagnostics and timed shared-pump simulation; state-model limits explicit |
| Surfer | Verified native VCD load, saved state and captured views; separate portable Ledger cursor/zoom inspector |
| Freerouting | Later: isolated routing candidates and independent acceptance |
| FreeCAD | Later: native mechanical-model workflows |
| OpenSCAD | Later: parametric case-model workflows |
| sigrok | Optional: supported capture instruments and real acquisition evidence |
| openEMS | Optional: bounded electromagnetic models and explicit assumptions |
| KLayout | Optional: layout inspection within supported project scope |

The first nine dedicated adapters now exist. Their documented scopes are
deliberately different: a DRC finding, an output candidate and a reduced passive
simulation are not interchangeable evidence. ngspice does not mean that all R10
ICs, the full PCB or any physical target has been simulated or qualified.

Each following tool must use the existing Kernel, per-tool execution grants,
Stacy/CLI/MCP commands, cancellation, source binding and evidence. Presence is
separate from qualification. Use operation-specific positive/negative cases,
focused regression checks, actual screenshots and a fresh-package launch;
repeat broader tests only when a new change or failure justifies it.

The current authoritative architecture is R10 F133-B / D213ECV / ECP5-12F /
ECP5-45F, reaffirmed by the owner on 25 October 2026. The integration plan follows
those sources. Target changes require an explicit new decision. Native runtimes
are installed separately. Hardware, SDK, firmware, policy, pins and
existing tests remain protected, with source acceptance independent of a review
ZIP. FAB, ROUTE and physical programming remain HOLD.

Implementation details and limits are in `ECP5_IMPLEMENTATION.md`. The 45F uses
its CABGA381 source profile. The 12F uses the existing explicitly labelled
CABGA256 package proxy; TQFP144 and all physical hardware remain unqualified.

HDL scopes, runtime prerequisites and trace limits are in `HDL_INTEGRATION.md`.
Surfer captures are actual native views; the interactive Ledger VCD inspector
is a separate portable SDK / Qt view. Verilator lint is not a simulation pass.

# Left-column logic and structure — review 01

The owner asked us to revisit the logic used to build the left column while continuing HATCH. This review is part of DISCOVERY-01. It establishes a small shared shortcut catalogue and a concrete next design step; it does not claim that the entire navigator has been unified.

## What the current code builds

| Provider | Current responsibility | Consequence for the owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `control_qt.add_navigation` | Adds legacy workspace/tool links beneath the Ledger area | New features can land deep inside an older tools branch |
| `shell2.build_library` | Adds Today and the ARRIVE / FILES / LIBRARY / KEEP / SLATE / PROJECTS shortcut groups | Storage locations, type filters and work views appear together |
| `ConcernController.rebuild` and `concern_catalog.tree` | Render real Concern catalogue relationships and preserve legacy workspace access | This is a different ancestry model from the shortcut groups above it |
| `shell2.fit_library` | Automatically folds groups when vertical space runs out, while respecting stored open choices | PROJECTS is early in the folding order, which can hide useful work views |
| `menus2.rebuild`, the command catalogue and route adapters | Provide commands and workspace navigation | A menu destination need not become another tree root |

The Paper CONCERN heading and the Concern catalogue root are also assembled separately. Their labels should not be treated as proof of one shared parent/child relationship. The existing refresh path reconstructs the original tree before the Concern projection; this review has not established a duplicate-growth bug.

The ambiguity is structural: a row might be a real project object, a filesystem location, a filtered collection, an operational view or a command. Those roles need to be explicit. A Library type filter is an alternate way to find an existing record, not a new owner or a second copy of that record.

## Small changes in this checkpoint

- `workbench/navigator_catalog.py` now owns the Paper shortcut sections, the legacy workspace-link inventory, presentation roles and the existing fold order.
- Paper rows receive stable shortcut IDs and role metadata. Existing Qt destination fields, captions, counts and handlers remain intact.
- Inquiries appears as a saved-work shortcut in KEEP. Algorithm & Theory Atlas and Tool Atlas stay in Tools rather than becoming new Paper tree roots.
- Concern catalogue data, its IDs, relationships and view preferences remain under the existing provider. No project, file, notebook or original source is moved.
- Settings and Trash retain their fixed footer placement. No new Hatch commands are added.

This is a foundation for reviewing placement, not a finished new information architecture. The legacy list and Paper projection remain distinct views. Inquiries and the older Investigations workspace still overlap conceptually; the next design should provide a clear shared work entry and linked views without deleting old records or hiding existing functionality.

## Recommended organizing rule

The main structural view should answer **where the work belongs**. Type filters and file locations should be identifiable alternate views. Menus and context actions should answer **what can be done**.

| Kind of thing | Recommended home or view | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Concern / project / assignment | Main work hierarchy | Parentage represents actual responsibility or membership |
| Idea / inquiry / hypothesis / finding | The relevant project or an explicit Unassigned collection | A saved record has one identity; other views link to it |
| Source document / working copy / result | References under that work, with its provenance | A project link does not move or overwrite a master file |
| Files and folders | Files view | Show actual locations and explicit copy boundaries |
| Documents / code / boards by type | Library view | These are filters over records/files, not another storage hierarchy |
| Agenda / jobs / model state / instruction matrix | Slate operational view | Process state is distinct from knowledge or project ancestry |
| Atlases, calculators and tools | Tools menu and relevant context actions | Installing a capability does not automatically add a root node |
| Settings / Trash | Fixed footer | Configuration and recovery controls remain easy to find |

I recommend a project-centered work view with an explicit current-project scope, alongside Files and Library views. Concern remains the umbrella. Unassigned work stays visible until the owner chooses a project. Existing Properties & works / Offices / Work & ideas / Archive projections can remain alternate catalogue views, with the selection and scope stated clearly.

## Next navigator implementation step

Use one typed node description for rendering and routing: stable ID, parent ID, role, canonical target, scope, provider and allowed presentation actions. Keep an alias/reference distinct from an owning parent relationship. Rendering order and indentation must not silently define ownership.

Then adapt the existing providers into that description without replacing their stores. Preserve all existing destinations and expand/selection preferences through stable IDs. Make an active project and the selected item's ancestor path resistant to automatic folding. Explain why a node appears in the current view, and keep project-scoped collections distinct from workspace-wide or Unassigned collections.

Before changing the default arrangement, produce a concrete populated tree from the actual application: one project, a second project, unassigned ideas, an inquiry with stale evidence, a working copy and a running/waiting job. Review whether each item has a clear home and whether switching views preserves its identity. Use this as the next navigator pass rather than continuing to add independent root groups.

No new mathematical or model capability should be blocked by a cosmetic tree change. The current Discovery implementation remains intact, and the next method-composition work can consume its IDs independently of how the navigator presents them.

# Office CLI — one shared Ledger service

Run from assembled Arc_Ledger using Ledger's Python environment. --operator asks
for existing local scopes, not a permission bypass. Office requires actual
local desktop-owner. Do not expose Office through phone or provider operations.

```sh
python -m workbench.engineering_cli --root . --identity desktop-owner --operator call office.doctor
python -m workbench.engineering_cli --root . --identity desktop-owner --operator call office.list
python -m workbench.engineering_cli --root . --identity desktop-owner --operator call office.import.preview --params '{"path":"/absolute/path/parts.xlsx"}'
```

Responses are {"ok":true,"result":...}. Read the preview model/losses/source SHA
and digest. Put its actual id/digest into request.json (placeholders below):

```json
{"plan":"ACTUAL_32_HEX_PLAN","expected_digest":"ACTUAL_64_HEX_DIGEST"}
```

```sh
python -m workbench.engineering_cli --root . --identity desktop-owner --operator call office.import.commit --params-file request.json
```

The receipt document_id is an owner: identity. office.get accepts {"id":"ACTUAL_ID"}.
Use the returned revision as expected_revision. A save request contains id,
expected_revision and the COMPLETE actual document with only intended changes.
Retain sheet/block IDs. Each cell has type,value,formula,formula_dialect,
cache_state,number_format,unit. Numbers are decimal strings, Booleans true/false,
IDs text. Literals have formula null, dialect none, cache LITERAL. Formula caches
are STORED_NOT_RECALCULATED. A leading '=' alone does not make a text cell active.

```sh
python -m workbench.engineering_cli --root . --identity desktop-owner --operator call office.save --params-file save.json
cat save.json | python -m workbench.engineering_cli --root . --identity desktop-owner --operator call office.save --params-file -
```

These are alternative input methods. Obtain a fresh revision after a changed
save. Use either --params or --params-file, never both. Strict object JSON is
bounded to 2 MiB and parsed before coordinator startup. Duplicate members,
nonfinite numbers, symlinks and special files are refused. File/stdin avoids
shell argument limits without broadening the Kernel schema.

Explicit CSV preview example:

```json
{"path":"/absolute/path/readings.csv","csv":{"columns":{"B":"number","C":"boolean"},"units":{"B":"V"},"header_rows":1}}
```

BOM: office.bom.preview with actual .kicad_pcb path, then reviewed import.commit.
office.bom.compare takes id/expected_revision and returns native links or unresolved
rows, not approval. Ordinary XLSX rows are not automatically native CAD bindings.

An operation starts with office.operation.preview:

```json
{"id":"ACTUAL_OWNER_ID","expected_revision":"ACTUAL_SAVED_REVISION","mode":"recalculate","format":"ods"}
```

Inspect model, losses, environment and digest. Send its plan/expected_digest to
office.operation.run using a JSON file. Poll jobs.get with {"id":"ACTUAL_JOB_ID"};
read office.operation.result with {"job":"ACTUAL_JOB_ID"}. Retry returns the same
job; a later edit makes the old result historical. Failed/interrupted jobs remain
visible. Recalculation runs actual Calc on the declared profile and never commits
its output over saved working data.

Modes: export, recalculate, edit. Table exports: csv/ods/xlsx; CSV requires the
selected sheet ID. Recalculation's demonstrated output is ODS. Document exports:
docx/pdf. Edit preparation: ods/docx; native desktop launches the actual editor.
To adopt an external candidate, call office.candidate.preview with id,
expected_revision,path; inspect differences/losses, then office.candidate.commit
with the reviewed plan/digest. Source drift or pending recovery refuses commit.

To retain an output call office.output.copy with job,file,expected_sha256 and
absolute destination, using the result's actual filename/hash. Same extension
and NEW destination required. Originals/existing files are never overwritten.
Historical outputs remain labeled historical. Office opens only clean projections.

Recovery: office.draft.save takes id,writer (32 hex),base_revision,document;
office.drafts takes id; office.draft.discard takes id/writer. Drafts are not saves.
Changed bases require review/merge. Pending drafts block conversion/acceptance.

office.from.notebook takes notebook/expected_revision. office.from.book uses real
attached editorial inputs. Derived documents retain source revision/currentness;
editing them cannot overwrite the notebook or accepted project revision.

Real CLI qualification covers separate processes on one coordinator, preview/
commit, file and >128 KiB stdin save, actual Calc, cache/measurement separation
and idempotent replay after later edits. Owner-host/independent acceptance OPEN.

# Settings inventory 07

The one current settings inventory of Graphite 0.1 (November 6, 2026). It was first written for HATCH DESKTOP-01 and
extended in AGENT-02; Graphite 0.1 folds in the classification of every preference outside the registry (from the earlier
inventories 01 to 06, which left the tree) and brings the words to Graphite. The file keeps its name because the program
names it: `ledger_control.settings()` reports its coverage as "43 genuine settings; remaining coverage is recorded in
docs/SETTINGS_INVENTORY_07.md".

There are 43 genuine connected settings, `workbench/settings_registry.SPECS`; the live count is always `len(SPECS)`. The
settings page shows two roots, **Workspace** and **Assistant** (`settings_registry.ROOT_NAMES` over the unchanged root keys
`Ledger` and `Slate`). Since Graphite 0.1 the definitions themselves carry Graphite's words (labels, descriptions and
effects); keys, defaults, kinds, scopes, stores and root keys are unchanged, as the owner's rename asked. The release check
records every definition's digest and the settings digest in `docs/GRAPHITE_0.1_REGISTRY.json` (written by
`tools/record_registry.py`) and lists any added, removed, changed or moved definition in words.
