| workspace.startup | Workspace → Workspace → Startup | "last" | Connected session profile | Session view_preferences |

## The two newest settings

**appearance.writing_marker** (DESKTOP-01; Workspace → Appearance → Writing marker; Off / On). It is the reversible,
quiet-motion-aware form of the owner's decorative X that the Interface Companion asked to keep (specification VS03). The value is a boolean, default true. The consumer is the window's one marker controller (`workbench/writing_marker.py`): while an opted-in yellow writing passage has keyboard focus, a small graphite X (1.25 × the passage font's x-height, so 12 px on 14 pt code and 10 px on 14 pt prose) is drawn in the page's own margin on the caret's line and blinks with a 2 s period, half the caret's rate. The passages that opt in are the cabinet's title line and writing passage, the memory direction correction (the same cabinet writing), the New Idea sheet (Home and the Jot it down dialog), the Settings string value and the return thread; the source editor is refused, and no search or console field carries it. The X is painted from the page's own paint event, so the passage, its document, undo, selection, caret and click areas are untouched and the accessible tree gains no object. `reading.reduce_motion` wins over this setting: the X stands still and no timer runs. Application is immediate: a Set, Undo or Default from Slate, the CLI or the Settings page reaches the controller on the next desktop tick through `sync_profile`. Readback is a controller receipt (`requested` the saved choice, `effective` what focused passages show, `motion` blinking / static / off, `passages` the number opted in): `APPLIED` when the saved choice is what the desktop shows (a static X under Reduce motion is applied, not pending), `PENDING_DESKTOP` otherwise, `NO_LIVE_DESKTOP_READBACK` without a connected desktop. New keys use single-key Set/Default/Undo; the existing batch schema remains exactly 17 keys. A profile without the field, or with a foreign value, reads as the default and is never rewritten by reading. The `Session.load` loader for the field belongs to WI-1 (workbench/session.py); until it is present a saved false is on disk but a fresh Session reads the default, which `test_paper.py` reports as skipped rather than passed.

**agent.continue_when_closed** (AGENT-02; Assistant → Assignments → Continue assignments while Graphite is closed; Off / On).
The value is a boolean, default true, project private, owner only, single-key Set (the public batch enum stays 17 keys). Two consumers read the same Kernel settings row: the desktop's close (with the Graphite service, internally the Ledger service, live and the value on, a running assignment is released to the service instead of paused) and the service's 5 s tick (`agent_loop.pump` steps released assignments only while the value is on, and rechecks it before every step). A stored value that is not a boolean reads as off. See docs/CONTINUE_01.md and decision D29.

## Classification and remaining audit

The per-category audit enumerated every persisted preference and state outside the registry: the connected Session
profile, the Kernel `settings` table, project-private files under `.ledger/`, personal profile files and environment-driven
options. `QSettings` is not used anywhere.

| Existing field or control | Classification and treatment |
| --- | --- |
| Session `writing_marker` (new in DESKTOP-01) | Genuine boolean presentation preference, adapted as `appearance.writing_marker` (above). It is the reversible, quiet-motion-aware form of the owner's decorative X; it never changes editing behaviour, so it is public presentation state in `ledger.context` and a cloud proposal may Set it like favorites. |
| Hardware category_views: Auto view, Details, Thumbnails | Adapted in INTEGRATION-01 as `hardware.category_views`; the editor now sizes its frame to its rows up to a cap that scales with the interface size, runs its Tab order pane by pane into Apply, and names each combo for assistive technology (DESKTOP-01, V-08 / ACC-06 / ACC-07 / ACC-10). |
| Orange Book `auto_refresh` (`.ledger/orange_book_enabled.json`, checkbox "Automatic updates", default from `docs/orange_book/bindings.json`, env override `ARC_LEDGER_DISABLE_BOOK_WATCHER`) | Genuine boolean preference, previously absent from this table. Retained in its original control (Orange Book panel checkbox); not adapted in INTEGRATION-01, reason: project-private boolean with an env override and a watcher consumer; candidate for a later slice. |
| Window geometry, dock state and engineering split state | Saved workspace arrangement, retained by the original restore paths. No scalar setting invented. |
| last_surface, selected_nav and current record | Runtime workspace/navigation state, retained without changing record identity. |
| Per-view tree expansion, selected tree node, scrolling, settings/cabinet navigation and Library section folds | Navigation state; preserve existing projection and persistence behavior. |
| clip_position and clip_collapsed | Workspace arrangement state of the live companion overlay (`ClipAssistant.retired` is False; the overlay is shown in workspaces and hidden at Home, and these fields are read and written by its own drag and collapse controls). An earlier inventory called them retired compatibility fields; that wording was wrong. No scalar setting is advertised; the original controls stay. |
| library_open, type_target, console.mode, console.history, pill_link (Session) | Written on every save but never restored before INTEGRATION-01 (dead persistence). INTEGRATION-01 adds bounded loaders in `Session.load`: `library_open` (≤ 50 section → bool), `type_target` (one of slate, stac, kernel, find, shell), `console.mode` (one of the five console pages), `console.history` (≤ 50 typed lines per page on load and on save; the live console still keeps 200 in memory), `pill_link` (host:port or [ipv6]:port). Navigation state and a deployment input; none is a registry value. |
| Journal `ledger.change.*`, receipts `ledger.settings_runtime.*`, desktop intents `ledger.ui.*`, `ledger.session_path`, desktop catalog/context, work gate, service cycle, brain selection/worker/handover, model registrations, dialogues, `remote_enabled`, `deployment.profile` | Journal, observations, stateful actions, working records, binding and deployment inputs with their existing routes. `history()` now tolerates journal rows of retired keys (`orphaned`, never undone); receipts of desktops whose lease is gone are pruned on the next publish; a corrupt `operations.priority` file or a tampered Kernel-table value is one `STORE_UNAVAILABLE` row (`repairable`: Default replaces it) instead of a failed `ledger.settings` read. |
| Model identity, registration, load, qualification, restore and stop | Existing stateful actions. Three launch defaults remain shared settings with separate requested/running readback. |
| Memory import/archive/delete, owner correction and source review | Existing owner-scoped actions; five existing memory preferences remain shared and private. |
| Credentials, environment/deployment inputs (`ARC1_WORKBENCH_CONFIG_HOME`, `ARC_LEDGER_*`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `LEDGER_PYTHON`, remote-config.json, pill link) and runtime pins | Existing controlled configuration and deployment routes; no arbitrary path/value editor. |
| Legacy Tk `workspace.json`, catalogue `expanded`, object glass history, activity, caches and locks | Compatibility data, navigation state, working records and caches; not preferences. |
| CPU/RAM observations, jobs, queues, records and qualification results | Observed runtime state and working records, not preferences. |

Source sharing, rights, model qualification and engineering acceptance retain their original boundaries. The five shared
memory preferences and three local-model defaults keep their privacy checks (owner only). Forty-three connected settings
describes this audited registry; it does not close every settings, menu, launcher or owner-host review item. Evidence:
`tests_integrated/test_settings_registry.py`, `test_settings_advanced.py`, `test_hardware_settings.py`, `test_paper.py`, the
settings section of the release check, and `tools/check_hardware_settings_ui.py` and `tools/check_paper_ui.py`. How each
slice of settings came to be is in docs/HATCH_SETTINGS_01.md to _03.md, HATCH_MODEL_01.md, HATCH_PRESENTATION_01.md and
HATCH_INTEGRATION_01.md.

records.text:
# Five concern groundwork passes — G1 through G5

Development checkpoint following N1. The owner authorized five implementation
passes using the researched defaults, followed by reassessment. These five
bounded passes form the expanded N2 groundwork delivery. They do not close five
unrelated retained campaign milestones. Independent protected-source/security
acceptance and owner-host qualification remain open.

## What changed

G1: Slate faces inward from either side of the workspace. Approved source pixels
are unchanged; direction is a render transform. Real events can admit a short
notice/acknowledgement pose. A one-shot timer returns to rest. Input, quiet,
reduced motion, hidden/collapsed views, and cooldown suppress cues without
queuing them. The existing 800 ms actual-job poll remains separate. The retired
portrait/fairy presentation controller is no longer attached to the desktop bird.
Continuous idle movement and the standalone Living Library sprint are not added.

G2: A portable SQLite concern catalog gives works, offices, projects, collections
and notes stable IDs. Named containment and office relationships create several
entrances to one item. Renaming and unlinking preserve the item and its notes.
Containment loops and stale note/name writes are rejected. Future schema versions
are refused without rewriting their original bytes.

G3: The navigator offers Properties & works, Offices, Work & ideas, and Archive.
The default is Properties & works. Expansion is retained separately by view;
filter-induced expansion is temporary. Existing hardware and tool entrances are
retained, including all fourteen devices, seven areas and five pinned workspaces.
Counterbalance is a planned declaration, not an imported or implemented game.

G4: Selecting an item opens its working area: Overview, Notes, Links, Sources.
Create an item, link an existing item, rename, or change its lifecycle. Sources
record saved file identity and SHA-256 in the explicit current directory. A check
can show current, changed, unavailable, or another directory. Updating the stored
reference is explicit. Files are never relocated by reorganizing the catalog.
Source links neither admit a document nor accept a claim or rights instrument.

G5: A visible working-context strip follows catalog items and associated existing
workspaces. Saved dossiers retain their identity across restart. Explicitly saved
notes and titles join the existing search palette. Recovery drafts stay separate
from committed notes. The concern overview offers a consistent catalog backup.
Native controls compact at narrow widths while notes retain usable space.

## Use it

Choose a view above the tree. Click an item to open its working area. Use New item
for a note, project, work, collection or office. Link existing creates another
entrance; it does not make a separately editable duplicate. Links lists both the
container and maintaining office. Removing a selected link keeps its item.

Open Notes and type. Save note or the existing Save command commits the note.
The dot on its tab identifies an unsaved draft. A debounced local recovery copy
does not commit that draft. Closing an edited working area asks Save, Discard or
Cancel and reports whether a recovery copy was retained. Recover draft loads a
chosen copy for review; Save remains explicit. Reload saved retains an unfinished
draft when recovery succeeds. If another view changed the saved note, copy wanted
text, reload the current saved note, and paste the intended edits; stale Save
cannot overwrite the other view. Pin and keep an edited workspace when opening
other items, using the existing five-pin policy.

Type in the left search field to filter the current tree. Enter opens the
existing search palette. It now includes saved catalog titles, descriptions and
notes, with stable item targets. Recovery drafts are deliberately excluded from
search. FTS5 is used when supported; otherwise catalog search explicitly falls
back to titles/descriptions. Source-file full-text/OCR indexing is still the
retained document campaign, not a claim made by this catalog.

Sources supports ordinary files up to 32 MiB in the current explicit working
directory. Private runtime directories, escaping/linked paths and changed reads
are refused. References in another directory are not silently rebound. Check
selected source rechecks saved bytes; Open source uses the existing desktop
document path. Large archive inspection and real-corpus admission keep their
existing separate controls and limits.

Ask Slate opens the existing conversation and, only in an empty input, prepares
an unsent question prefix naming the current item. It never sends on its own.
Attention metadata contains no note body or source contents, grants no tools,
and is not automatically exported to paired devices or providers. Local/Gemini
behavior and explicit attachment settings keep their existing controls.

## Private state and recovery

The catalog lives beside the existing OS session profile in
`concern/catalog.sqlite3`. It contains organizational records, relationships,
saved notes, source locators/digests, local preferences and separate recovery
drafts. It references the existing work; it is not a replacement Genesis rights
register, Engineering Kernel database, or accepted-source store.

Back up catalog & notes uses SQLite's online backup and integrity check and
refuses to overwrite an existing destination. It includes saved notes and
recovery drafts. It is not a complete Ledger edition: preserve the existing
`.ledger` records, full OS profile, original sources, models and prior program.
For a manual catalog restore, close Ledger, preserve the current catalog and its
sidecars as a set, and use a verified backup as the catalog in a separate test
profile before replacing the intended profile. Never copy a live database alone
over an open catalog. A guided combined restore remains P32 work.

Older programs ignore this new catalog; they cannot display these new working
areas. Keep the complete profile and original program for rollback. Existing
private records and hardware source identities are not migrated or rewritten.

## Limits and next work

This is a native Debian-target development checkpoint using pinned PySide6 6.8.3
on a controlled Linux host. It is not measured ThinkPad/display performance,
iPhone/cellular qualification, a new public listener, always-on service, local
model answer qualification, live Gemini exchange, or a complete multi-project
execution system. The selected organizational context does not change the
Kernel's attached execution root. These retain their campaign work.

R10 authority, physical HOLD, no-eMMC/no-microSD, input/save/stop rules and existing
caller/source guards remain. No original protected SDK, test, policy, hardware,
runtime pin, or historical artwork is changed. New protected additions are
`sdk/cli/arc1cli/concern_catalog.py`, `sdk/cli/arc1cli/slate_attention.py`, and
`tests/test_concern_groundwork.py`. Independent review is required for acceptance.

## Research basis

The implementation follows one-item/multiple-collection patterns, native
model/view separation, SQLite transactions/FTS/consistent backup, and restrained
mixed-initiative presentation. It adds no dependency on the surveyed products.

- https://www.zotero.org/support/collections_and_tags
- https://www.devontechnologies.com/blog/20230524-duplicates-replicants
- https://doc.qt.io/qt-6.8/model-view-programming.html
- https://doc.qt.io/qt-6.8/qtreeview.html
- https://sqlite.org/fts5.html
- https://www.sqlite.org/backup.html
- https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/principles-mixed-initiative-user-interfaces/

The owner requested reassessment after these five passes. Next priority proposed
for discussion is N3's shared always-on service, using this context/catalog
foundation. No further pass is implied to have been implemented here.

# N1 — A readable, shared workbench foundation

Development candidate for the unified campaign. Independent protected-source
and security acceptance remain open. This is the first of 30 planned remaining
deliveries after P16; 29 remain after this development delivery. The earlier
core/window milestone baseline remains 86/225; no new percentage is inferred.

## Read from a comfortable distance

View > Reading and Layout (also retained under Tools) separates interface,
navigation, prose, and code sizes. Prose and interface fonts may differ. Code
uses a separately selected fixed-pitch face, with a reported local fallback if
the requested family is unavailable or unsuitable. Existing OpenDyslexic OTFs,
licence, source record and hashes are unchanged and checked when loaded.

The dialog has a scrollable control area, live prose/code previews, a larger
reading preset, explicit Apply, and Close. Preview does not save. Apply persists
in the existing OS profile. Ctrl+Alt+= and Ctrl+Alt+- adjust prose only. Source
text, selections, undo history and explicit-save rules are preserved. Paragraph
spacing applies to rendered QTextBrowser documents; ordinary labels retain
native Qt line metrics. New views receive the saved roles as they appear,
without a polling loop or reading/collecting their contents.

Legacy profiles retain their chosen interface, navigation and code sizes; prose
inherits the old interface size when no separate prose setting exists. New
profiles start at 14 pt interface, 15 pt navigation, 16 pt prose and 14 pt code.
All new settings also appear through the existing shared settings catalogue and
validated set/undo operations. No new operation scope is introduced.

The extended reading fields are understood by N1. An older P16 reader can ignore
this extended reading profile and fall back to defaults; retain the earlier OS
profile together with private-state backups for a faithful rollback. N1 does not
rewrite old evidence or private project identity.

## One presentation vocabulary

Organizer and Object Glass use the same native summary surface over a pure SDK
projection: title/status, short summary, context, known links, attention and next
step. This is presentation of existing checked reads. It grants no permission,
creates no engineering evidence, and does not establish completeness or truth.
Object Glass keeps its existing object/revision/history checks and real actions.
Both compact and full views scroll, including when text is enlarged. Raw technical
detail remains available. Unavailable objects carry no old link counts or bindings
in the new projection. Caller changes clear the organizer's summary as before.

Existing menus, shortcuts, fourteen devices, seven areas, five pinned workspaces,
and explicit Save remain. Fullscreen remains F11; the startup-surface choice is
not changed. Focus layout keeps Slate available inside the workshop.

## The retired characters

N1 uses the unchanged approved bird's resting pose in desktop Home/workspace
entrances, assistant perch, conversation portrait, and active asset preview/icon.
The desktop does not offer the old fairy presentation/cameo menu. Historical
character files and legacy storage names retain their bytes for compatibility;
the earlier upstream art/test records are not rewritten. The desktop perch polls
actual existing job state at 800 ms and repaints on state change, not at a 60 Hz
idle animation rate. N1 adds no event-driven bird motion or sprinting. N2 supplies
that richer bird/conversation integration. Older phone artwork/routes are not
modified or remotely expanded in this desktop foundation pass.

No owner seed, Poe corpus, notebook, model weights or private state is imported
from Living Library into the program. Only its unchanged key-pose PNG, asset
metadata and a local provenance note are added.

## Scope, evidence and recovery

The target is Debian 13 ThinkPad plus an iPhone satellite. Native development
walkthroughs use pinned PySide6 6.8.3 on Linux, not the owner's physical display.
No new always-on daemon, public listener, TLS deployment, phone conversation,
model quality result or hardware improvement is claimed here. Those retain their
campaign passes. Physical FAB/ROUTE/programming stay HOLD; R10 source authority
and no-eMMC/no-microSD rules remain unchanged.

New protected addition: sdk/cli/arc1cli/workbench_view.py. New focused checks are
protected additions. Existing protected SDK, policy, tests, hardware and pins
retain their bytes. The portable projection and GUI changes need independent
acceptance; implementing-agent evidence cannot provide that acceptance.

Preserve the private .ledger state and OS profile, originals and previous
program. This program-only source release contains no private user data. Use all
three N1 ZIPs in one fresh parent; do not mix P16/N1 parts or replace an active
private database with an empty release. Assembly recreates exact missing aliases
only after all supplied files and part identities match.

Next: N2 Slate bird behavior and expandable information surfaces; N3 service
foundation; retained P17 PDF evidence and SW-002 document views. All subsequent
toolbox, staC, model, pills, memory, mail, collaboration and voice requirements
remain in the unified campaign.

records.text:
# N3 — shared background service

Development candidate for Debian 13. Independent source/security acceptance,
actual ThinkPad systemd/Unix-socket checks and phone/model/network qualification
remain OPEN. This document supersedes the proposed N3 status in the older
groundwork addendum. The cumulative build includes N1 and G1–G5.

## What changed

`engine.engineering(root)` now attaches Linux desktop, JSONL, engineering CLI,
MCP and staC clients to one headless coordinator. The existing Engineering Kernel
still owns SQLite job records, request keys, scoped candidates, execution grants,
source hashes, recovery, model handover leases and actual tool processes. There
is no second job table or replacement scheduler. Job workers instantiate the
existing Kernel directly for their already admitted job.

The service owns in-memory console handles and the existing optional phone HTTP
listener. Desktop window closure detaches instead of sending `brain.stop`.
Local reply observers also detach without cancelling their durable job. Results
remain in their existing Kernel records. Existing foreground graphical previews
and desktop command processes still stop on desktop closure.

Tools > Background service opens a native status/control workspace associated
with Ledger in the concern. It reports current work admission, jobs, model and
phone listener state, distinguishes detached startup from systemd supervision,
and provides Reconnect, Master Stop, Resume and Stop service. A scrolling body
keeps the controls usable in narrow windows. Phone controls now start/stop the
service's listener; no phone-server QProcess belongs to the desktop lifetime.

## Lifetimes and recovery

| Event | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Close a tab or desktop window | Keep shared jobs/model/listener; keep explicit save and recovery rules. |
| Reopen the desktop | Attach to the same service and existing records. Do not replay submissions. |
| Disconnect after sending a request | Report an uncertain outcome. Inspect records; a deliberate retry uses the same exact request key. |
| Master Stop | Persist the existing work hold, revoke phone sessions, cancel work, stop verified workers/models/consoles, retain the coordinator. |
| Resume work | Use the existing owner operation. Admit new requests; do not replay jobs, rearm idle work or reopen the phone listener. |
| Stop service / orderly host shutdown | Quiesce work and revoke access; stop the coordinator after cleanup. Work remains held. |
| Service crash and restart | Reconcile existing workers by PID/start identity. Adopt a surviving worker; do not launch it twice. Mark a stale unclaimed queue entry interrupted through existing recovery. |
| Host power loss | No process can keep running. On the next start, reconcile records; do not automatically execute interrupted mutations or load a model. |

Service startup does not select, download or load model weights. The existing
model manager's sequential handover and durable control lease are reused. A
real-model ownership/performance claim still needs the later declared model
qualification; this pass does not substitute a dummy model for that evidence.

An exclusive, root-specific flock in `.ledger/service/coordinator.lock` prevents
two coordinators from owning one execution root, including when clients request
different transports. A failed listener startup releases that lock without
master-stopping existing work. Reconciliation that cannot safely establish
ownership holds new work and reports a recovery error.

There is one execution root in this pass. Concern organization can name many
properties, but selecting a property does not redirect execution into another
project or confer new authority. Existing private profile/presentation helpers
retain local SQLite access; the service boundary centralizes dispatch and
worker/listener lifetime. It is not a claim that every local presentation write
has become a remote API or that a desktop has become a thin network-only client.

## Local boundary

The Debian default is a private pathname Unix socket, under a short per-account,
per-root directory in `/tmp`. Directories must be owned and mode 0700; sockets
are 0600. Both ends inspect Linux SO_PEERCRED. Older owned `.ledger` parents may
be tightened to 0700; symlink/foreign-owned state is refused. Ordinary sources
are not moved or permission-expanded.

The authenticated local OS owner may request a bounded delegation. The
coordinator validates the label, scopes, source prefixes, tools and mode against
the existing owner's ceiling, then issues the Principal used by dispatch. Each
operation message contains only method/arguments, not a replacement Principal.
Repair-review scope stays separate from execute/approve. Read-only and provider
callers retain their restricted grants. The paired phone uses its existing
transport-issued Principal and operation allowlist on the same dispatch lock.

This is a same-OS-account trust boundary. It does not sandbox arbitrary programs
already running as that owner. Model/provider text cannot request arbitrary
Python, SQL, shell commands or a host lifecycle method through the existing
capability schemas. No new remote operation or remote owner scope is introduced.

Framing uses bounded UTF-8 JSON: 2 MiB requests, 16 MiB responses, finite numbers,
no duplicate members, a nesting bound, connection timeouts and 16 concurrent
connections. No pickle, object deserialization or SQL endpoint exists. The
handshake checks protocol, execution-root identity and the declared service-code
edition. A different edition is refused; close clients and stop the previous
service before replacing the program. In-flight mutations are not retried by
the client. Existing exact job request keys still decide deduplication.

An explicitly selected alternative is available with
`ARC_LEDGER_HOST_TRANSPORT=loopback`. It binds only 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port,
requires a fresh 256-bit token in a 0600 file beneath the same 0700 directory,
and retains all delegation/Kernel checks. The token is absent from status,
stdout and audit. It rotates at restart. This transport is not HTTP, public
hosting or the phone listener. There is no automatic fallback to it. Clients and
service must select the same transport.

The development sandbox denies AF_UNIX socket creation. Real-process and native
tests therefore explicitly used authenticated loopback. Actual Unix socket
creation/peer-credential rejection and systemd boot/logout behavior remain owner
host gates. Unit syntax was checked with `systemd-analyze verify`; no real
ThinkPad service installation or public listener was performed.

## Debian controls

Run from the installed Arc_Ledger directory, using its Python environment:

```sh
python3 -m workbench.host_cli start
python3 -m workbench.host_cli status
python3 -m workbench.host_cli master-stop
python3 -m workbench.engineering_cli --operator call ledger.work.resume
python3 -m workbench.host_cli stop
```

`status` never starts a service. Normal desktop/client startup can start a
detached coordinator. This lasts independently of the window; it does not by
itself enable boot startup or keep the ThinkPad awake. Reconnect explicitly
establishes a replacement connection after service loss, without replaying a
previous request.

For a supervised user service, first stop a previously detached instance. Review
the generated unit before enabling it. From the installed program directory:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
python3 -m workbench.host_cli unit --output ~/.config/systemd/user/arc-ledger.service
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now arc-ledger.service
```

The generator refuses overwrite. It records absolute program/interpreter/profile
paths, Type=exec, Restart=on-failure, a restart limit, UMask=0077,
NoNewPrivileges=yes, a 45-second shutdown limit and KillMode=mixed. The main
process gets a graceful cancellation interval; systemd can then kill remaining
processes in that unit's control group. A unit naming a moved program directory
must be regenerated/reviewed during update. The service cannot make a stopped
computer, sleeping laptop, missing ISP route or untrusted phone certificate
reachable.

`loginctl enable-linger` for the owner account can let its user manager start at
boot and persist after logout. Its actual authorization and behavior belong to
ThinkPad deployment checks. Full setup, certificate lifecycle, network diagnosis
and product-guided updates remain N4/P32 work. No mandatory Cloudflare component
has been added.

## Storage and updates

Jobs, evidence, candidates, provider disclosure records, model selections and
sessions remain in their existing `.ledger` stores. The concern catalog remains
beside the OS session profile. No durable record is migrated into a new host
database. The new service directory holds only the coordinator lock and bounded
startup diagnostics. The transient socket/token endpoint is not an execution
grant to preserve or restore. Do not include credentials, live endpoint tokens
or active grants in a portable recovery edition.

Existing explicit source saves still use the shared SQLite promotion transaction
and preserve recovery copies. Existing staged application update CLI first
requires closed desktops and finished/cancelled jobs, then stops the service and
holds its exclusive coordinator lock during the original update/verification
procedure. It does not update beneath a live coordinator. The built-in old
unittest tool runs its tiny disposable fixtures in explicit embedded Kernel mode;
shipped protected tests are unchanged. Normal clients use the host boundary.

## Development evidence and limits

New tests cover framing, private endpoints, delegation, edition rejection,
parallel exact-key requests, disconnect ambiguity, crash/adoption, stale queue
recovery, CLI/MCP/staC continuity, real local pairing, Master Stop and persistent
hold/revocation. They use real service/worker processes. A controlled delay in a
disposable intake-tool copy makes lifecycle observation deterministic; the
shipped intake tool is unchanged. The native walkthrough exercises real Qt
controls at 1040/1366/1920 widths, actual desktop closure/reopen, a running intake
job, the local phone listener, dirty note/source preservation and owner Resume.

Retained focused Kernel, model-authority, stop primitives, N1/G5 organization,
reading, object and package tests are run separately in explicit embedded mode.
The unchanged 28-observation N1 and 33-observation G5 native scripts also pass
through the real shared-service boundary, including cross-process reading
settings, Focus/Home behavior, identity and recovery. Together with the 27 new
service observations, this is 88 native observations in explicit service mode.
The old `MasterStopQt` class requires sealed Struthio C project sources absent
from this program-only delivery; its setup failed when attempted. Those cases
are recorded unavailable, not weakened or declared passed. New native tests
exercise this pass's changed desktop/service stop path using declared fixtures.

Fresh three-part assembly, stock release UI/privacy, launch and byte-preservation
checks are required before delivery. Final counts and receipts accompany the
package. Independent acceptance remains OPEN. No live Gemini request, weights
inference, real iPhone/cellular, actual ThinkPad performance or physical hardware
claim is made.

## Research basis

These primary references informed implementation; they do not independently
certify this code:

1. [systemd 257 service configuration](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/257/systemd.service.html): long-running service type, restart policy and bounded lifecycle.
2. [systemd 257 kill procedure](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/257/systemd.kill.html): mixed/control-group semantics and remaining child cleanup.
3. [systemd 257 loginctl](https://www.freedesktop.org/software/systemd/man/257/loginctl.html): user lingering across boot/logout.
4. [Linux Unix sockets](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/unix.7.html): pathname length, file permissions and SO_PEERCRED.
5. [Python fcntl](https://docs.python.org/3.13/library/fcntl.html): exclusive nonblocking flock.
6. [SQLite WAL](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html): same-host concurrent connections; it is not a database to mount directly over the phone network.
7. [Jupyter Server security](https://jupyter-server.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operators/security.html): local servers still need authentication; authentication and authorization are separate. The explicit loopback design borrows that principle, not Jupyter code or its HTTP stack.

# Slate Pass 13 Naming and capability catalogue

The assistant is now Slate. staC retains its name. Current desktop headings, menus, labels, accessibility text, new greetings and local/provider system instructions use Slate. Historical conversations, source packets, identity strings, operation names, file paths and stored setting keys remain compatible. Old /open stacy knowledge and /settings Stacy continue to work; /open slate knowledge and /settings Slate use the same records. No source or profile is accepted merely because its name changes.

Open Ledger commands or Slate Knowledge > Capabilities. The short result distinguishes declared, installed, available, permitted and qualified. Technical capability details expands the exact schema, source bindings and reasons. /catalog QUERY and ledger.capabilities.catalog expose the same record through Slate and the CLI. /find and /describe retain their existing scope-filtered response contracts and add the same assessment.

The catalogue checks declared handler files and bounded prerequisite identities without running native tools, calling a provider or submitting a job. It lists registered job tools and passive runtime observations. Detected executables have unmeasured version compatibility. The pinned local-runtime archive is checked against its existing pin, but native loading and a model are not qualified by that check. A missing or unsupported runtime remains explicit. Components without a complete dependency profile stay unassessed.

Permitted means operation-scope eligible only. Actual parameters, ownership, tool grants, source admission, path restrictions, approval, stop state and current resources remain the dispatch boundary. A conditional command is not ready to execute. No qualification receipt adapter is supplied in this pass: all catalogue qualification states remain UNASSESSED. Existing test artifacts remain available through their original services and retain their original scope; the catalogue does not promote them to a broad feature claim.

The three discovery surfaces share a portable SDK assessment and one host adapter. Original schemas remain readable. New descriptive fields do not alter permission scopes or execute registered commands. Older foundation fields retain their legacy meaning and qualification labels for compatibility; current UI reads the explicit assessment instead.

The owner-approved expanded plan is docs/LEDGER_SLATE_CAMPAIGN.md. After the five Pass 13 development checks, expanded milestone completion is 33% (66/200 points). Original knowledge-campaign completion stays 61%. Check 12.5 and independent protected-source and owner-host acceptance remain OPEN. Pass 14 will compose existing sources, evidence, gaps and actions around the selected object. No hardware, firmware, ROM, personality, model weights, project admission or routing is changed here. iPhone development remains deferred; its existing static assistant label is updated for naming consistency only.

# Pass 14 — Object Glass

Select a source-map component or net, a job in Engineering, a requirement in the current register, or an opened saved file. The existing Inspector shows a short Object Glass summary, exact object and revision identifiers, source/evidence counts, gaps and relevant read actions. Technical detail is collapsed initially. View > Object Glass (Ctrl+Alt+O) opens the same context in a center workspace, including in Focus layout. No second assistant or engineering authority is created.

The source-map demonstration uses preserved ARC-1 R10 reference identities. A map component keeps its exact map and native identity; another map containing U23 is a different context. Reference snapshots do not become the accepted current design. Native-current component/net and requirement routes require an attached project. Program-only releases explain that prerequisite. A file context describes saved bytes, with an explicit separate state for an unsaved editor buffer; binary and large files have no generic text action.

Object Glass composes existing authorized reads. Sources, evidence, unresolved gaps and actions are bound to one object/revision. Private jobs, map connections and run outputs keep their existing owner checks. Every offered action is read-only and is checked again for current source identity, actual arguments and caller permissions before and after its read. Passive capability assessment remains distinct from qualification. This pass adds no engineering execution grant, source promotion or remote transport operation.

Three shared local operations serve GUI, CLI and Slate: ledger.object.inspect, ledger.object.current and ledger.object.action. /object explains the last saved selection for the current caller. /object followed by a selector JSON object inspects an explicit target. For example: /object {"kind":"job","target":"<32-character job ID>"}. A source-map component adds its map ID: {"kind":"component","target":"U23","map":"<map ID>"}. /call and the existing Kernel CLI remain available. Short replies are deterministic summaries of checked source/record observations, not claims of model reasoning.

Back/Forward history retains at most twenty locators, observed revisions and object identities in the private operating-system profile, separated by project path and caller. It stores no source contents, cached grants, answers or evidence payloads. A cold restart reauthorizes and rechecks sources. Changed sources show a stale state; Refresh advances bytes only for the same identity. A replaced native identity requires explicit reselection. Clear context clears this navigation history; it does not delete engineering records or memories.

Async requests clear the previous displayed payload immediately. A selection ticket includes the current caller/permission fingerprint and generation. Late results for older selections or another caller are ignored. Permission changes clear the active context. Source checks are snapshots, with periodic revalidation and an explicit recheck on every action; they are not continuous observation of arbitrary external programs.

The four authority roles remain intact. Independent review, actual ThinkPad/Windows and real iPhone/network qualification remain open. Physical ARC-1 fabrication, routing release and programming stay HOLD. Private originals, model weights, personality and memory editions remain separate from the program.

See ARC1_DISCOVERY_PRACTICE.md for the owner's rule on retaining engineering improvements revealed while developing Ledger. Next is SW-001 logical windows, followed by the dependent core activity-awareness work. The window campaign remains planned until its own checks pass.

# Pass 15: follow the work

This development candidate supplies the five Pass 15 checks. Core milestone
progress is 76/200 (38%); windows remain 5/25 (20%); combined progress is 81/225
(36%). Independent acceptance is OPEN. These are development milestone weights,
not estimates of effort or confidence in engineering answers.

## Use

Open Ledger active > Work trail, or Work trail in the Recent activity row. Choose
an intent to see Intent, Scope check, Work, Artifacts and Outcome. Inspect job
opens the existing Object Glass. The technical detail disclosure is optional.
`/trail` lists recent owner intents; `/trail <id>` inspects one; `/resources`
reads host headroom and existing controls. No remote/PWA operation is added.

Scope check describes Kernel mode/scope validation. Exact-source execution,
object visibility, grant checks and acceptance remain their existing gates.
Request RETURNED, job Completed and outcome PROCESS_SUCCEEDED are separate facts.
Exit zero by itself is not an experiment PASS. Missing evidence/currentness stays
unavailable. Historical jobs can be inspected with ledger.trail.job without
inventing an earlier intent. No old journal or evidence row is rewritten.

Artifact SHA-256 observations check current project bytes against the registered
evidence. CHANGED, MISSING_OR_UNAVAILABLE and NOT_CHECKED_BUDGET remain visible.
An observation is not an immutable filesystem snapshot or source acceptance.
Selection is bounded to eight jobs, 64 artifacts and 64 MiB of registered bytes
per inspection; omitted artifact counts are retained in technical detail.

## Stop and resources

Master Stop first persists a project job-admission hold, then performs the
existing owned-process cancellation, idle inhibition and remote revocation.
The hold survives restart. Newly queued jobs cannot cross it into execution.
Resume work requires approve scope and no remaining Running/Queued jobs. It
admits future requests; it replays zero jobs, does not rearm idle study and does
not enable the phone link. Reads and reconciliation remain available while held.
Other desktop launchers retain their existing explicit controls: the new hold
is the Kernel job boundary, not an OS-wide application freeze.

CPU reuses the portable sampler: measured aggregate Linux host activity or an
explicit waiting/stale/unavailable state. Memory reuses the host probe and its
container ceiling. Neither number claims Ledger-only or ARC-1 utilization.
Priority selects the existing normal/background policy; normal applies to new
work and does not raise a process already lowered by the OS. Study and Brain
buttons open their existing reviewed budget controls. Per-job CPU/RSS is not
instrumented in this view; no universal CPU/RAM cap is claimed. Existing tool
deadlines and resource limits remain authoritative.

## Privacy and retention

New trails are owner-only even for another approver. Consequential Kernel
requests are correlated with actual saved jobs in the same job transaction.
Passive read polling is omitted. Trails copy no arguments, goals, source text,
stdout/stderr, model paths or credentials. Presented strings use existing
redaction. The prior general activity journal remains project metadata under
its existing local trust boundary; this pass does not turn it into a tenant
event service or bound its historical retention.

The new trail projection retains at most 256 requests per owner, with up to
eight job links each and four KiB per request. Old returned or interrupted
requests may be trimmed; jobs/evidence are preserved. Pruned and dropped counts
are explicit. If every retained request is active, new trails are dropped and
counted. Storage failures leave a current-process gap count and a redacted,
owner-correlated journal recovery marker; recoverable markers remain visible
after journal reconciliation. A missing process identity presents an interrupted
request without rewriting the stored row. Unknown OS identity stays uncertain.

## Validation and next work

Five focused acceptance cases cover real controlled process/artifact correlation,
cold-process states, owner isolation/redaction/retention/gaps, persistent hold and
explicit resume, and measured/unavailable resources. Existing Kernel and owned
process checks are reused. A native pinned-Qt walkthrough and fresh-package
receipts accompany the release. Controlled fixtures are not native ARC-1, model,
phone-network or owner-host qualification.

The new portable SDK contract and five new tests are protected additions pending
independent source/security acceptance. Existing protected SDK, policy, tests,
tool pins and hardware bytes remain unchanged. Case review 12.5 and all previous
open qualification gates remain OPEN. Physical FAB/ROUTE/programming remain HOLD.
Next is core Pass 16 archive intake surfaces. SW-002 follows core Pass 17 document
views; SW-003 follows recovery Pass 32. No original requirement is removed.

records.text:
# Pass 16: package desk and an organizer that follows the work

Development candidate; independent acceptance remains OPEN. Core progress is
81/200 (40.5%), windows 5/25 (20%), combined 86/225 (38.2%). The organizer improves
the same pass without adding milestone points or removing campaign requirements.

## Start with an intention

View > Workbench organizer (Ctrl+Shift+J), Ledger active > Organizer, or the
Organizer button beside Recent activity opens a responsive task desk. It groups
existing workspaces into Bring in, Understand, Build & prove, and Follow through.
Search narrows tasks and your next items. Focus narrows the lane. Cards reflow
from two columns to one as space narrows. Existing menus, fourteen devices,
seven workspace areas, explicit saves and the five-pin limit remain intact.

Next on your desk is a bounded view of the caller's inspections, nonterminal or
failed jobs, held work and reference queues. It opens existing controls; it is
not a scheduler, automatic folder mover or universal project inventory. Up to
eight inspections, twenty visible jobs and sixteen owned libraries contribute
to at most twelve next items. Completed/cancelled jobs remain in Work trail.
An inspected package with an existing ready copy leaves the copy suggestion;
unfinished reference decisions appear at the library instead. The package desk
can locate that review batch again without inventing another copy or approval.
Local desktop navigation requires the desktop owner; read-only staC views retain
the actual caller. New private screens clear metadata on a caller change.

## Inspect, copy for review, then admit

Package desk inspects an external ZIP without extracting, executing or admitting
its contents. Choose Inspect ZIP, view the file inventory, hashes, encryption
status and transport observations, then explicitly choose a private library and
Copy / locate review batch. The existing intake job performs the copy. Open
reference review for the separate admission decision. A manifest claiming that
files were previously approved cannot grant local admission or source promotion.

Repeated copies of identical ZIP bytes into the same library locate the existing
ready batch or request. They do not overwrite accepted originals or silently
rerun interrupted work. The exact archive digest is checked at inspection, copy
request and worker publication. Changed originals require another inspection.
Path-deduplication and accepted-path conflicts retain the original intake rules.

Inspectors retain at most 32 checksummed owner receipts, paginating inventories
100 members at a time in the UI. Read scopes can read their own receipts, not
arbitrary external paths. Inspect/copy require approve scope. Private source
paths remain outside public receipt responses. These are observations of bytes
at a time; Refresh reads stored receipts and does not imply a new scan. The
inspector reacts to work-hold epoch changes; Master Stop does not rearm a copy.

## Qualified package scope

ZIP Store and Deflate are qualified here. Input is bounded to 128 MiB, 10,000
entries, 64 MiB per expanded file, 512 MiB expanded total, 1,000:1 member expansion,
8 MiB central/transport metadata and a 20-second cooperative inspection deadline.
Parsing and metadata processing remain bounded; this is not an OS sandbox.
Path traversal, aliases, duplicate directories/files, file/directory collisions,
links, special entries, malformed metadata, CRC corruption and resource overflow
fail closed. No member is extracted to a supplied path.

Encrypted members are explicitly ENCRYPTED. ZIP64, multipart ZIP, additional
compression methods, 7z/tar and other package formats are unqualified and remain
UNSUPPORTED. Individual documents still use their existing intake adapters;
OOXML/DOCX is not reclassified as a generic package here. No optional decoder,
password prompt or external archiver is silently invoked.

The existing ZIP import route now performs this preflight too. Its original
snapshot/namespace/review policy remains the authority. Intake rule fingerprints
include the new reader: existing policies/accepted references can become stale
and require their existing explicit policy review rather than automatic renewal.

## V1 transport integrity

Exports include exact original hashes/sizes and decision receipts, declare no
encryption, and are read back before atomic publication without replacement.
Inspection verifies the exact declared member set and decision/input linkage,
and reports missing or changed declared dependencies. Generic ZIPs have no
declared dependency graph; they are not assumed complete.

VERIFIED transport means content consistency, not a signed origin, trusted
external approval, engineering acceptance or physical qualification. Imported
decision receipts are reference data. Original catalog bytes and accepted sources
are not replaced by an export or its inspection.

## The same vocabulary in staC

The existing Kernel staC bridge gains finite typed read adapters:

```
desk
desk | focus bring-in
desk | focus understand
desk | focus build
desk | focus follow-through
desk | find "review"
package 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef | contents
package 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef | gaps
```

Replace the example package ID with one of your own receipts. The organizer can
run a read directly and display its summary. `/desk` and `/packages` read the
same models; `/open organizer` and `/open package desk` request navigation.
Compile declares WorkbenchOverview, PackageInventory or PackageGaps and read
effects only. Runtime forwards the real Principal to the existing Kernel. No
copy, admission, tool execution, shell expansion or authority appears in this
grammar. This is a Kernel bridge extension; upstream POSIX staC 0.6 grammar and
historic engineering IR/digests are unchanged.

## Acceptance and next work

Six new focused cases cover the five package gates plus shared organizer/staC
privacy. Eleven existing intake/staC checks are reused. A pinned-Qt walkthrough
uses actual local controls and controlled intake/export workers, checks responsive
layout and caller clearing, and accompanies fresh-package verification. The old
810-check campaign is not rerun. New protected SDK/test additions await independent
review; existing protected source bytes remain unchanged.

Back up the private .ledger database and OS profile; memory editions do not
automatically include these new inspection tables. They are additive, but the old
program does not implement this preflight. Keep originals and the prior program
when rolling back. No private corpus or model is included in the release.

Next: core Pass 17 PDF reading and technical evidence, followed by SW-002 document
views. DOCX_ACCEPTANCE.md remains binding within passes 17–20/release 37. Twenty-one
core and four window passes remain. Case review 12.5, source/security, owner host,
model/provider and iPhone/network acceptance remain OPEN. R10 F133-B / D213ECV /
ECP5-12F / ECP5-45F remains authoritative; physical FAB/ROUTE/programming stay HOLD.

# P17 — exact PDF pages and separate working annotations

Development candidate, 27 October 2026. This cumulative edition includes N1,
expanded N2/G1–G5 and N3. Independent source/security acceptance remains OPEN.
Twenty-six retained planned deliveries remain; SW-002 is next. Historical
86/225 milestone points are unchanged. Development observations are not a new
completion percentage or physical qualification.

## Using the reader

Open Slate's Exact References, choose an admitted PDF and use **Read technical
PDF**. Indexing is needed for passage search; the new page reader itself checks
the admitted original directly. Open original location on a PDF passage now
opens that same central reader at the passage's physical page. Non-PDF original
views retain their existing behavior.

Previous, Next and the physical-page selector navigate the original. Fit width
and 125/150/200% zoom alter only the view. Original page, Native text, OCR and
Source / tools remain separate. Narrow workspaces use wrapping command rows,
vertical content and scrolling; Focus reading gives the page more space. The
right Inspector follows the checked page identity. Slate remains the existing
quiet inward-facing male bird. The concern tree and fourteen-device/seven-area/
five-pin policy are preserved.

Drag a page region, select a note kind and write your annotation. **Save note**,
global Save and Save All explicitly commit it. Changing page, replacing a
Preview or closing the window offers Save, Discard or Cancel for dirty notes.
Discard retains bounded recovery; Recover draft loads it for review without
committing. Notes survive desktop and service restart. Master Stop preserves
both committed annotations and unfinished prose. An orderly service stop holds
new work; Resume work and Check original explicitly permit a new rendering job.

Copy citation produces a checked JSON citation for Open citation. It contains
the namespace/item identity, full original SHA-256, zero-based physical index
and normalized region. The display uses one-based physical page numbers.
PDF metadata labels and the printed label actually seen on the paper are
different fields. Printed labels are not guessed. An owner's printed-label note
is displayed as an observation; conflicting observations remain visible.

## Evidence and authority

The portable SDK measures original bytes and parser/tool profiles. The original
stays in the existing intake vault; page images, native positions and OCR are
rebuildable derivatives. No original PDF is rewritten or decrypted. Links are
inert. JavaScript, launch/active actions, embedded-file and other checked active
features are held, never executed. These checks are not a universal PDF malware
detector or a replacement for the same-account operating-system trust boundary.

Each original has stable page identities independent of extraction offsets and
printed labels. Normalized rectangles refer to the top-left of the cropped,
rotated rendered page. Poppler word coordinates are corrected for the rotated
page dimensions; the controlled rotated/cropped case checks them against raster
ink. Text layout retains table/figure context and technical identifiers on the
qualified examples. It does not reconstruct table-cell semantics, guarantee
reading order or certify every symbol. The 2001 NIST source exposes imperfect
native font spacing; compare the image or explicitly request OCR.

Page rendering and OCR use the existing Kernel job mechanism and shared headless
service. A cached result must match the completed job's evidence, current
original admission and exact page-image hash before it is shown. Changing the
source, revoking admission, deleting an original or altering a derivative
withholds the old image/text. Late page results cannot replace a newer selection.
No new scheduler or database is introduced.

Annotations and recovery use two tables in the existing private Kernel SQLite
store. Notes have original/page/region anchors, integrity digests and optimistic
versions. Recovery is separate, bounded to 32 writer/page entries per item and
owner; the latest ten for a page can be inspected. Notes neither populate the
accepted-fact table nor confer source approval. Export library volume includes
indexed originals, existing facts/links and explicitly saved owner annotations.
Recovery drafts are excluded. Verification checks original bytes, passage
identity and annotation structure/anchors; it imports nothing automatically.

The nine new PDF routes are typed, scope checked and namespace restricted.
Paired-phone operation exposure is unchanged; SW-002 will extend the shared
document surface separately. Private PDF routes are excluded from cloud command
proposals, including typed-pipeline/direct-job bypasses. They remain available
to authorized local clients. This also preserves the existing bounded Gemini
metadata proposal path as the command catalog grows. No source or note is
automatically sent to Gemini, a Frontier model or another service.

## Measured tools and limits

| Tool | Actual development profile | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PySide6 | 6.8.3 | Native desktop; offscreen Linux walkthrough |
| pypdf | 6.17.0, existing vendor pin unchanged | Original structure, labels and bounded security checks |
| pdftotext | 24.02.0, executable hash recorded | Native UTF-8 text and positioned words |
| pdftoppm | 26.05.0, executable hash recorded | Cropped page raster |
| Tesseract | 5.3.4, executable/model hashes recorded | Explicit per-page OCR |

These are separately measured tools, not a claim of a single installed Poppler
release. Other host profiles are inspected when used and need their own
qualification. Existing dependency pins are preserved. Debian's optional
`poppler-utils` supplies both Poppler commands. For optional English OCR an owner
may install `tesseract-ocr` and `tesseract-ocr-eng` through Debian's package
manager. Chinese OCR additionally needs the chosen `chi_sim` or `chi_tra` language
data. This pass installs or downloads none of those tools or language files.

Only English OCR data was installed here. Chinese native text was tested;
Chinese OCR was deliberately reported unavailable. OCR never silently changes
languages. Every OCR word has its engine score and image rectangle. Scores below
85 are highlighted; **all** OCR text remains unverified. A high engine score is
not a probability of correctness, and low-score highlighting is not a measured
accuracy rate. Scanned symbols, units and diagrams require image comparison.

The reader bounds originals to the existing intake size, 512 pages, 4 MiB
decompressed page streams, 8 MiB native/TSV text, 6,000 words per page and a
2,000-pixel maximum image dimension. The worker has memory/file limits and
timeouts. Corrupt, encrypted, active, oversized, unsupported and missing-tool
inputs fail explicitly. Larger or unusual PDFs require a separately reviewed
profile; no silent repair or lossy conversion is advertised.

## Qualified examples and remaining gates

The genuine corpus receipt identifies the exact downloaded bytes, original URLs,
tool hashes and observations:

* Espressif ESP32-S3 Chinese datasheet v2.2: 83 physical pages; Chinese passage
  and technical identifier, pin table on physical 17 and pin-layout figure on 16.
  Full copyrighted source, text and page images are not distributed in this build.
* NIST FIPS 197 original 2001 edition: 51 physical pages. Physical page 9 carries
  printed page 5; the PDF has no declared page-label tree. This is not the 2023
  editorial update. Its native font-spacing limits are recorded.
* Archived NIST FIPS 46 (1977): 22 pages, historical withdrawn scan with an old
  text layer. Physical page 4 was explicitly re-OCRed from its raster; the tool,
  English model, word scores, uncertainty and original image identity are retained.
  Its use is a reading test, not a cryptographic recommendation.

Four declared authored PDFs cover table/figure context, physical/metadata/printed
pagination, a true image-only page, encryption and rotated/cropped coordinates.
The native walkthrough exercises actual Qt controls and actual Kernel workers,
recovery, export, source drift, process restart and Master Stop. The unchanged
N1/G5/N3 native walkthroughs are retained against the shared service. Detailed
counts are in SLATE_PASS_17_VERIFICATION.json and the accompanying review folder.

The development sandbox denies Unix sockets; real-service tests explicitly use
authenticated loopback. Actual ThinkPad Unix credentials, systemd boot/logout,
screen resolution/performance, real model/provider, iPhone/cellular/home hosting
and physical hardware acceptance remain separate. The source is a development
candidate. No independent reviewer or owner-host qualification is fabricated.

## Upgrade and DOCX continuity

Keep the previous program and complete private state. Stop the old shared
service before replacing an edition. N3 edition checks now include MANIFEST.json
so a published PDF/dependency-module change cannot attach to a stale coordinator.
Use all three matching P17 archives in a fresh folder; never mix delivery parts.

One existing protected SDK file changes: `intake_profiles.py` now allows a passive
OpenAction destination/GoTo while continuing to hold executable actions. The real
Chinese datasheet uses a passive Fit destination; the prior blanket check wrongly
held it. **The intake rule fingerprint therefore changes for existing receipts.**
Older admissions become stale and require explicit review under the new rules;
no receipt is silently accepted, rewritten or migrated. Refresh source review
and make the owner decision, then explicitly rebuild affected reference indexes.
Original-byte identities and saved annotations remain separate from extractor
versions. New SDK/test additions and exact before/after hashes are disclosed in
the source-change report; independent acceptance remains OPEN. Existing tests,
hardware, policy, runtime pins and historical art are byte preserved.

The existing DOCX paragraph/table-cell extractor and Orange Book DOCX export
source are preserved. The DOCX facade regression confirms native Chinese table
addresses through the existing worker. This pass does not deliver a full Word
editor, faithful Word pagination or a qualified DOCX-to-PDF converter. Nine
historical Orange Book tests need sealed register/project inputs absent from
the program-only package and are recorded unavailable. The retained
DOCX_ACCEPTANCE.md checklist stays active across P17–20 and P37.

## Primary references

* [pypdf 6.17 extraction documentation](https://pypdf.readthedocs.io/en/6.17.0/user/extract-text.html): memory, scanned-page and positioning limits.
* [Tesseract command-line documentation](https://tesseract-ocr.github.io/tessdoc/Command-Line-Usage.html): explicit languages, TSV boxes and word scores.
* [Qt for Python 6.8 QPdfDocument](https://doc.qt.io/qtforpython-6.8/PySide6/QtPdf/QPdfDocument.html): evaluated native alternative. This implementation reuses headless Poppler and does not add a QtPdf dependency.
* [Espressif original Chinese datasheet](https://www.espressif.com/sites/default/files/documentation/esp32-s3_datasheet_cn.pdf): exact edition hash retained in the receipt.
* [NIST original FIPS 197 download](https://csrc.nist.gov/files/pubs/fips/197/final/docs/fips-197.pdf) and [historical FIPS 46 scan](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/Legacy/FIPS/fipspub46.pdf): declared reading corpus only.

records.text:
# P18 — optional notes and knowledge-base exchange

28 October 2026. Cumulative development checkpoint based on verified SW-002.
staC is pronounced Stacy (STAY-see). Slate is the male bird. Independent
source/security and actual owner/device acceptance remain OPEN. Hardware
fabrication, routing and physical programming remain HOLD.

P18 begins M3 — Documents and working knowledge. P19 notebooks and P20
tables/editable documents still assemble that milestone. Next is P19;
24 retained planned deliveries remain. Historical 86/225 points are unchanged.

## Use the desk

Open Concern or another concern working area. On Overview, choose **Notes
exchange…**. This is an optional toolbox; no owner vault is assumed. Choose an
explicit source folder and a declared profile. Use a new collection in this
working area, or an existing exchange collection for reconciliation. Existing
collections must use their original profile.

Preview exchange reads bounded files without creating saved notes. Select a
row for exact inert incoming text and metadata. Review exchange details lists
ignored configuration/files, attachment hashes and static-link results. Changing
folder, profile or collection clears acknowledgement.

Review, acknowledge and Commit reviewed exchange. Notes become ordinary saved
notes in the existing concern catalog. Existing search finds them. Open working
note reaches its existing Notes editor, explicit Save/Save All, recovery drafts
and optimistic versions. No second editor or source admission is introduced.

Saved collections shows text, metadata, backlinks, source paths and state.
Export creates a new ZIP and never overwrites a destination or source folder.
Manually extract into a new folder for a later explicit preview. P18 does not
automatically extract untrusted ZIPs or watch/synchronize folders.

## Profiles

| Profile | Supported exchange | Explicit limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| markdown-v1 | UTF-8 .md, restricted front matter, basic static Markdown/wiki links | Same-profile text, not full CommonMark rendering or universal conversion. |
| org-v1 | UTF-8 .org, file keywords, static file/ID links | No Babel, includes, calls, macros, agenda or computation. Anchors remain unverified. |
| obsidian-v1 | Markdown vault subset, wiki/relative links, attachments | No configuration/plugins, Dataview, Canvas, live embeds or full block runtime. Actual application qualification remains open. |
| logseq-og-v1 | File-graph Markdown/Org subset, page properties, static block IDs/references | Not Logseq DB/SQLite/EDN. Queries/renderers stay inert. Actual application qualification remains open. |
| joplin-md-v1 | Markdown/front matter, exported relative note/resource links | Real Joplin CLI 3.7.1 demonstrated; no JEX, encrypted/sync database or universal version claim. |

Metadata interpretation supports simple scalar fields and lists. Complex YAML,
duplicates, tags and aliases retain original text with explicit gaps; no YAML
object construction occurs. Metadata is data, never a permission instruction.
Unknown syntax remains inspectable. Unedited original note bytes are retained
as reconciliation bases and restored on same-profile export. Working text
normalizes BOM/CRLF to UTF-8/LF; edited exports report this change.

Links are exact and case-sensitive. Unsupported nested/escaped syntax can remain
unresolved. Heading/block anchors remain attached but unverified, except the
declared static Org/Logseq ID lookup. Missing, outside-profile, external and
ambiguous references are explicit. External URIs never open or fetch. Embeds
are references. Code/query text never executes or confers authority.

## Reconciliation

Each source collection retains stable note identities. Match by a Ledger export
key within that collection, then current path, then an unambiguous exact-byte
rename. Rename plus edit without a stable exported key cannot always be inferred;
a new note and missing upstream reference appear instead. Identical-content
ambiguity never silently merges notes.

Unedited local notes can receive reviewed upstream updates. Local changes or
recovery drafts hold conflicting incoming text separately. The saved working
note remains untouched. Reimporting the same held version adds no versions.
A newer incoming version is refused until the current conflict is resolved.

Review incoming conflict displays both texts. Separate acknowledgement enables
Keep local note or Use incoming note. Resolution binds the incoming hash and
expected saved-note version. Applying incoming text is refused while a recovery
draft exists. Keeping local rebases the observed upstream version without
accepting an engineering fact.

Upstream deletion marks its source missing, retaining the saved note. Removed
attachments remain available for surviving local references and are explicitly
marked upstream-missing. Unchanged reconciliation does not advance generation.

Rename history can resolve an old path without rewriting original text. These
aliases travel in ledger-notes.json. Other applications may require updated
links; export reports that gap. The sidecar preserves Ledger identities and
catalog titles, not universal application semantics. Catalog title changes do
not rewrite an original note header.

## Authority, bounds and storage

Reusable behavior lives in sdk/cli/arc1cli/notes_exchange.py. The existing
catalog SQLite database owns saved notes and additive exchange tables. Upstream
bytes are reconciliation bases, not another mutable working copy or accepted
source vault. Existing catalog SQLite backup includes these tables and blobs;
it remains a catalog backup. P32 must include them in complete recovery.

Ten typed Kernel routes expose profiles, collections, preview, selected incoming
note, commit, saved collection, saved note, conflict review, resolution and
export through the shared coordinator. Private data requires the actual
desktop-owner profile with read scope; preview/commit/resolve/export additionally
require approve scope. The native desk refuses mismatched desktop/service
catalog profiles.

No phone route, scheduler, model worker or provider permission is added.
Private exchange routes are excluded from cloud proposals and supported typed
pipeline indirection. The HTTP allowlist is unchanged. Later conversation and
sharing work must retain explicit disclosure and privacy.

Scan bounds: 512 files, 512 directories, 128 notes, 128 KiB per note, 8 MiB per
attachment and 32 MiB total. Maximum 512 references per note, 2,048 per graph,
32 aliases per note and 32 collections. Unsupported/oversized sources fail.
Hidden/application configuration and unsupported files are listed and excluded.
Symlinks, special files, escaping paths and unsafe manifests are refused.
Allowed opaque assets: PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/PDF/TXT/CSV/BIN. Storing/exporting their
bytes grants no source acceptance and never automatically opens them.

Eight distinct pending previews are retained. A new preview of the same source,
profile and destination supersedes its old pending preview. Pending previews
expire after one hour. At most 2,048 durable preview/commit records are retained
before an explicit limit. Committed-plan retries return the existing receipt.
Parser/catalog fingerprints, source hashes, local note/draft state and
collection generation bind a preview. Late source drift rolls back the entire
transaction.

Export includes current saved text, retained assets, identity metadata, hashes
and conversion/loss warnings. Recovery drafts, unresolved incoming copies,
configuration/plugins and credentials are excluded. ZIP files have ordinary
data permissions and no automatic execution. Export is a checked snapshot.

## Evidence and open gates

All five original cases remain: declared Markdown/Org fidelity; backlink and
block-reference round trips; genuine application export; repeat/rename/delete/
conflict reconciliation; inert queries/plugins/instructions. Final counts are
in P18_VERIFICATION.json and Slate_P18_Review.

Actual Joplin CLI 3.7.1 created, tagged, attached and exported the controlled
notes. Ledger retained Chinese metadata, resource bytes and note links. A clean
Joplin profile imported Ledger's exchange contents and re-exported them. These
are authored qualification notes, not an owner vault or general fidelity proof.
Joplin is a developer-only tool; no Node/Joplin runtime is bundled with Ledger.

Native Qt 6.8.3 and the real coordinator demonstrate the desk, existing Save/
recovery, conflict review, aliases, deletion, export, three widths and restart.
Actual ThinkPad performance, iPhone/Safari/HTTPS/cellular, real model/provider
and independent acceptance remain open. Historical sealed-project test gaps
remain disclosed. Existing protected SDK/tests/policy/hardware/pins/artwork are
unchanged relative to SW-002; protected additions are separately disclosed.

## Primary references

- [Joplin terminal](https://joplinapp.org/help/apps/terminal/)
- [Joplin front matter](https://joplinapp.org/help/dev/spec/interop_with_frontmatter/)
- [Obsidian links](https://obsidian.md/help/links)
- [GNU Org links](https://orgmode.org/manual/Link-Format.html)
- [Logseq DB/file distinctions](https://github.com/logseq/docs/blob/master/db-version.md)

Primary specifications informed the profiles. Actual receipts establish tested
behavior; a format specification alone does not qualify an application.
