records.text:
# P19 — Engineering notebook and Marginalia

This cumulative development checkpoint builds on verified P18. It joins working
prose to source, note, requirement, table, query and result identities without
creating a competing engineering authority. Native Qt is the owner editor; no
new phone or cloud access is added. staC remains pronounced Stacy (STAY-see).

## Use

Open a concern working area and select Overview > Engineering notebooks.
Create a notebook, Add idea, or Attach reference. Reference selection
previews the actual current record and requires an explicit review acknowledgement.
Attachment adds a draft block. Save notebook, global Save and Save All use the
existing explicit-save hooks. Reordering preserves IDs. Removing a saved block
archives its existing catalog note; it does not erase its saved body or history.

Inspect reference is available on saved blocks. The Reference tab shows readable
content/currentness; Record details exposes exact structured locators and hashes.
Changed referenced bytes or
record versions show STALE with no substituted record; missing or unauthorized
records show UNAVAILABLE. Review current binding previews a new binding in the
draft and requires Save. The notebook caption never writes the referenced file,
register, admission or job. Working requirement notes explicitly say they are
not accepted register facts. A real register reference requires an attached
engineering project and a valid existing register record.

Run read query is explicit and read only. Only bounded saved-note search and accessible
job listing profiles exist. There is no arbitrary SQL, shell, arbitrary Kernel
operation or effectful imported query. Keep query result records an immutable
reading identity. It rechecks the referenced rows when inspected; if a known
dependency changed, content is withheld. It is a historical reading: later new
matching rows are not automatically added. A query creates a private read/audit
snapshot, not an engineering job or accepted fact.

## One catalog and recovery

The schema is `arc.notebook/1`. Notebook headers and every block have existing
catalog object identities. Current body/title live only in the existing notes
and objects tables, so ordinary saved-note search/editing remains coherent.
Additive notebook tables store order, typed references, reviewed hashes, origin,
separate writer drafts, previous document versions, immutable read snapshots and
import receipts. History/originals are snapshots, not a second current note body.
An external edit in the normal Notes editor invalidates stale notebook saves.

Unsaved typing stores a bounded recovery draft after activity, separate from
the saved notebook. Review recovery compares a draft with current saved content;
matching bases can be recovered into an unsaved editor. Changed bases stay
available for comparison, without an automatic overwrite. Save is still required.
Discard affects this writer; unrelated recovery writers are retained. Catalog
backup includes the additive tables and original bytes. Complete-edition recovery
and exact context resume remain later campaign work, not a new P19 claim.

Limits are explicit: 32 notebooks, 64 active blocks, 256 retained blocks per
notebook, 16 KiB prose per block, 96 KiB document/draft, 16 draft writers, 4,096
historical document versions, 1,024 read snapshots per notebook and 128 KiB read
payloads. Limits refuse rather than silently truncate saved prose. Source views
are bounded previews and disclose truncation; hashes cover complete bounded
files. CSV is literal strings, up to 100 preview rows and 32 columns; formulas
are not evaluated. Typed sheets, units, BOM comparison and recalculation are P20.

## Marginalia role

An explicitly selected existing Marginalia HTML/JSON/MD/Org/text file may be
linked as its canonical original. The link records locator/name/hash and shows
bounded inert literal text. Ledger does not execute HTML/JavaScript, rewrite the
original, scan a personal corpus or start two-way synchronization. New notebook
ideas are separate working notes. A changed or missing original becomes stale
or unavailable. No standalone Marginalia file/application was identifiable in
the supplied materials; qualification uses a clearly authored representative
HTML fixture, not an invented claim of an unseen application port.

## Declared AppFlowy exchange

`appflowy-editor-json-v1` is a ONE-WAY import of AppFlowy Editor's document JSON:
`document.type=page`, nested child nodes, and text delta in data or attributes.
The official exporter serializes `editorState.document.toJson()`; it does not
establish compatibility with arbitrary full AppFlowy workspace/cloud exports.
Choose Import AppFlowy JSON, inspect blocks/losses, acknowledge, then commit.
Exact bytes, rules fingerprint, destination revision and a late read are checked
atomically. A retry returns its receipt. Reimport of the same original at the
same destination preserves saved local edits rather than overwriting them.

Paragraph, heading, lists, todo, quote, code and divider text become literal
working blocks. Flattened nesting, unrendered inline/other attributes, extra
fields, unsupported embedded/noninsert operations and unknown blocks are listed
as losses. Origin retains source hash/type/path/available node ID and attributes.
Unsupported blocks remain inert; foreign query blocks cannot become executable
queries or accepted records. Exact original bytes remain separately inspectable
and backed up. Strict duplicate members/IDs, size/depth/operation limits, changed
sources, ambiguous attributes, symlinks and special files fail explicitly.

Genuine evidence is the public author's `tttt.json` reproduction attached to
AppFlowy Editor issue 1134, dated 2025-08-05. Exact application version is UNKNOWN
(author wrote latest). The 2,817-byte export SHA-256 is
`fff7c396b623e98ce6608c55e54c1cb6439566d9d28346b654e766a7bb1cdf20`.
Its 22 blocks preserve every literal text string and source path; 19 formatting/
nesting losses are reported. Full application runtime was not executed here.
The producer build and creation path are not independently attested.
The third-party original/text is not redistributed; review includes its source
URL, hash, content-free receipt and a script taking an explicit local download.
Separate authored fixtures exercise unsupported/query blocks. No full-app,
round-trip, plugin, live sync or general version/fidelity claim is made.

Primary references:

- https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/appflowy-editor
- https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/appflowy-editor/blob/main/example/lib/home_page.dart
- https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/appflowy-editor/issues/1134
- https://github.com/AppFlowy-IO/appflowy-editor/blob/main/documentation/importing.md

## Authority, upgrade and qualification

All 13 notebook operations require the existing actual desktop-owner identity
and read scope. Mutations additionally require approve. Underlying Kernel reads
retain the caller; private output ownership, file containment, original intake
admission and register availability are checked through existing contracts.
Notebook routes are excluded from existing phone HTTP allowlists, Gemini tools
and typed-pipeline indirection. There is no new provider/model dependency.

Use all three matching P19 ZIPs in a fresh parent. Stop the old coordinator;
preserve its program and complete private state/catalog before switching. The
new catalog tables are additive. Rollback uses the matching previous program
and pre-update private-state backup. Existing SW-002 re-pairing/per-view refresh
and pre-P17 intake re-review/index rebuild rules apply when crossing those
editions. Never infer source/engineering acceptance from the import or prose.

P19 cases 19.1–19.5 are development demonstrated on the declared profiles:
actual identities after restart, read-only queries, separate save/recovery,
genuine declared one-way AppFlowy import and separation from referenced records.
Exact focused tests, native walkthroughs and retained receipts accompany this
edition. Existing protected SDK/tests/policy/hardware/pins/art are byte-preserved
relative to P18; new SDK notebook.py and test_notebook.py are disclosed additions.
Unchanged unavailable legacy cases retain their prior disclosures and are not
counted as passing. Actual ThinkPad/iPhone/home-network/model performance and
independent acceptance remain OPEN; physical FAB/ROUTE/programming remains HOLD.

P19 advances M3; P20 is next and its planned grouped milestone boundary.
23 retained planned deliveries remain. Historical 86/225 is unchanged.

records.text:
# Ledger & Slate — P20 working Office desk

P20 assembles the declared M3 development workflow: notes exchange, source-bound
notebooks, typed tables/BOM comparisons and editable paragraph/table documents.
Owner/independent acceptance remains OPEN; physical FAB/ROUTE/programming HOLD.
22 retained deliveries remain; next P21 begins M4, with its boundary P24.
Historical 86/225 points are unchanged. staC is pronounced Stacy (STAY-see).

## Native workflow

In a concern working area choose Overview > Office tables and documents. Preview
an explicitly selected CSV, XLSX, ODS or DOCX, inspect the model and losses, then
acknowledge to create a separate working copy. Original bytes are immutable in
the private catalog. External source currency checks its SHA-256. No directory
scan, personal corpus import or automatic source rewrite occurs.

Named sheets have stable IDs and typed cells. Edit cell exposes type, literal,
formula/dialect and unit. CSV columns default to text so 000123 stays an identifier;
type/unit/header mappings are explicit. A visible Unit column is more portable
than per-cell metadata. Notebook table references retain actual Office/sheet IDs
and reviewed revisions; later changes become stale rather than substituting data.

Documents contain editable paragraphs and native tables. Saved-notebook and
attached Orange Book copies are explicitly derived working documents. Their
source revision/currentness is inspectable; editing them grants no original or
engineering acceptance. Missing project/editorial inputs are reported honestly.

Save/global Save/Save All commit against the expected revision. A 650 ms draft
timer stores separate writer recovery. Another writer's recovery is not erased
by this writer's save. Save before conversion. Existing Catalog backup includes
new tables, originals, history and drafts. Complete cold restore remains later.

Recalculate previews saved inputs, formula restrictions, losses and measured
tools. Run uses an existing private Kernel job. Stored caches and measured Calc
results remain separate. Recalculation never saves over the current working copy.
Compare/import a candidate and commit explicitly to adopt it. Output copy creates
new files only. Source/model/rules/runtime drift invalidates the reviewed plan.

Prepare editor copy creates a clean ODS/DOCX candidate. Open editor requires a real
desktop display and separate LibreOffice profile. Native QProcess tracking joins
the existing stop/close controls, without an editing countdown. Headless preparation
is not owner GUI qualification. Review/import the externally saved candidate.

BOM import reads actual KiCad PCB footprint UUIDs/tstamps, references, values and
footprints. Comparison links each changed row to its exact native identity and
source hash. Altered/unknown identities remain unresolved. It neither edits the
board nor accepts a design. Public-demo qualification is not ARC-1 authority.

## Declared profiles

CSV/XLSX/ODS readers use the Python standard library and do not calculate. Ledger
stores exact decimal strings, actual Booleans, text IDs, ISO calendar values and
Excel serial/date-system metadata. Clean ODS explicitly styles Boolean/date/time
cells. Calc outputs are reread: sheet/identifier/Boolean/unexpected type loss
fails a job; numeric/calendar normalizations are recorded. Fictitious Excel
1900-02-29 is refused as a calendar projection. Original metadata remains intact.

Only bounded same-sheet numeric A1 arithmetic and SUM, PRODUCT, MIN, MAX, ABS,
ROUND, AVERAGE, COUNT are projected as formulas. Unknown/network/DDE/external/
cross-sheet/shared/array formulas are outside that profile. Recalculate refuses
them; plain export may literalize definitions only with explicit loss reporting.
No eval, macro execution, active-part copying or implicit external fetch occurs.
Actual Calc precision is measured floating point, not exact Ledger decimal math.

Charts, complex layouts, merged structures, formatting fidelity, links and active
parts are explicit losses, not universal Office fidelity. Per-cell units remain
Ledger metadata: use a Unit column for portable exchange. CSV writes one selected
sheet, reports type/unit/format loss and escapes formula-looking text.

DOCX supports literal paragraphs/headings/native tables, Chinese and technical
IDs. python-docx exports editable tables, repeated headers and readable Letter
pages. Images, fields, footnotes, comments, revision tracking, complex layout and
original pagination are outside the profile. Foreign active content is inert.
Orange Book uses the same writer; editorial and accepted engineering revisions
remain separate. The full owner's editorial/register corpus is absent here and
its full acceptance stays OPEN; the nine older unavailable cases remain uncounted.

Bounds: 16 MiB input; 1,792 KiB model; 8 sheets; 2,048 rows; 64 columns; 20,000
populated cells. Bounded ZIP/XML expansion and entity refusal apply. Documents:
5,000 blocks, 20,000 cells, 16 table columns. 32 working documents; 256 prior
versions/document; 16 recovery writers; 1,024 durable plans. CLI files/stdin:
strict JSON object, 2 MiB, no duplicate keys/nonfinite values/special files.

## Setup and CLI

Existing Qt/PDF/tool pins remain. In the SAME Python environment used by Ledger:

```sh
python -m pip install -r requirements-office.txt
```

For actual conversion/recalculation/PDF/editor use normal Debian Calc/Writer:

```sh
sudo apt install libreoffice-calc libreoffice-writer
python -m workbench.engineering_cli --root . --identity desktop-owner --operator call office.doctor
```

These are owner-host instructions, not a claim they ran there. Reading tables
and writing clean ODS/CSV need no Office app. DOCX writing needs python-docx 1.2.0.
No Office/Node/AppFlowy runtime is bundled. Actual development renderer measured:
LibreOfficeDev 26.8.0.0.alpha0, build 2c87e51eeaa2b413ff4ae097b2705eea1995d8e5.
That exact alpha evidence is not an owner-version recommendation or Debian-stable
qualification. Doctor measures the installed executable, version, hash and fonts.

Read OFFICE_CLI.md: file/stdin requests avoid shell argument limits. CLI and Qt
share the same 19 Office operations, jobs, catalog and revision checks. Actual
desktop-owner plus read is required; mutations require approve and execution
also execute. No phone/cloud/pipeline permission was added. Clean Office inputs
use unique private profiles with Very High macro security, empty trusted paths
and scoped fontconfig; no HOME changes.

## Update and review

Extract all THREE matching P20 ZIPs into one fresh parent. Stop the old coordinator
and retain matching old program plus COMPLETE private state before switching.
Catalog additions are additive; downgrade with that backup. Earlier crossed-
edition intake-review, pairing and publication migrations still apply. The
existing prepare/launcher refuses missing/mixed parts and restores nine aliases.

One existing protected file changes: sdk/cli/arc1cli/notebook.py adds the typed
Office-table target. Existing tests, hardware, policy, pins and art stay byte-
preserved relative to verified P19. New SDKs/tests and optional dependency pin
are disclosed in patch/hashes. Independent acceptance remains OPEN.

See P20_VERIFICATION.json and Slate_P20_Review for actual evidence. ThinkPad
Debian/stable Office/interactive editor/systemd boot/logout, actual models,
providers, iPhone/cellular/home hosting and physical board remain separate.
Primary references and exact fixture provenance are in the technical report.

## Open development runtime anomaly

Intermittent assembled sandbox runs returned malformed engineering SQLite databases, including before new Office work.
A clean diagnostic run and a complete clean assembly repeat passed the same
combined workflow; actual engineering/Catalog integrity checks then returned ok.
The cause remains UNRESOLVED; passing reruns are not a fix. No owner data was
accessed or repaired. This remains a DEVELOPMENT CANDIDATE: retain your working
installation and complete matching backup. It is not an owner-qualified update.
See Slate_P20_Review/runtime_anomalies.json.

# Record sharing and paired device boundary

This debug pass closes generic API paths into owner-scoped Slate jobs. General engineering jobs and evidence retain their existing project read semantics. Slate job families brain, intake, references, knowledge, study, memory and research are owner-scoped; an approve scope is not a private read grant. No new sharing toggle can override this classification. Generic jobs.get, jobs.list, evidence.read, evidence.list, workspace.job and workspace.search use the same checked reader. Private evidence is checked against its parent job; orphaned or contradictory private evidence is unavailable.

Generic files.read and queued ledger.open cannot bypass the owner boundary through build/brain, intake, references, knowledge, study or investigations run paths. An output needs the corresponding owned private job. This guard is not a complete filesystem sandbox. Local code running as the OS account retains that account's access. Local project activity still exposes redacted operational metadata, and this pass does not introduce a tenant-isolated event service.

Malformed shared engineering evidence remains inspectable so existing staC correlation checks can reject its broken linkage. Reading that record grants no qualification. Private orphaned evidence remains unavailable.

Paired-device /api/call now exposes only the reviewed PWA operation set. New local operations require deliberate transport and object-authorization review before they are added. Both the view and owner pairing profiles retain their scope checks. Neither profile automatically obtains access to desktop-owner private assistant data. The optional remote owner profile still has its previously explicit engineering approval capability; this pass does not remove that existing owner choice or create a new approval grant.

Policy version 2 binds the operation set into session policy. Previous-policy pairings are invalidated at service restart and require pairing again. Revocation, expiry, changed grants or a disabled service during a request prevent response publication. A Kernel effect that committed before revocation is not undone; a disconnected client must reconcile using the original idempotency key. The five existing remote tests remain unchanged. No listener, certificate, VPN, Xpra bridge, OS account or public cellular deployment is installed by this debug pass.

The original general-job fixture confirmed shared project reads, rather than proving all job reads were erroneous. A second reproduction on actual brain.respond fixtures confirmed the private payload gap. The patched tests use isolated synthetic data. No claim of a breach or real owner-data exposure is made. Historical jobs, evidence and originals are not rewritten. The incoming Slate Windows design will build on these explicit rules.

Core campaign remains 33%. This corrective pass earns no new feature milestone credit. The approved five-pass window campaign adds 25 planned points alongside the core's 200, giving combined progress 66/225 or 29.3%; the window track is still 0/25. Independent source and security review, owner ThinkPad and real device/network acceptance remain open.

# SW-001 — Logical windows

Development candidate, independent protected-source and security acceptance OPEN.
The core remains 71/200. This pass supplies five window development checks: 5/25.
Combined milestone progress is 76/225, or 33.8%. No model, phone, network or hardware
qualification follows from these points.

## Use in Ledger

Open View > Object Glass (Ctrl+Alt+O). Select a supported component, net, job,
requirement or saved file. In the center view's Slate Windows section, enable
resumable windows and choose Keep view. Reload lists saved opaque IDs;
Restore reopens the same checked identity. Refresh in Slate Windows explicitly advances
source bytes for that same identity, invalidating all prior publication grants.
A changed native identity requires reselection. Close in Slate Windows deletes only its
view metadata, publication grants and presentation state.

The initial renderer is an overview: object identity, observed source revision,
title, authority, source/evidence counts and up to eight gaps. It contains no
source text, evidence payloads, owner credentials, arbitrary HTML, action arguments
or engineering execution controls. Native source/evidence renderers and the mobile
Window Deck belong to SW-002. No new HTTP endpoint or PWA operation is exposed in
this pass; existing paired-device operation policy and PWA bytes are unchanged.

Paired devices remain different principals. Publishing requires an actual live
paired-device identity and an explicit local-owner approval for one window and
revision. The desktop offers Publish overview and Revoke for a selected paired
device. This prepares the checked broker grant; it does not add a mobile renderer
or enable remote transport. Never launch the CLI as desktop-owner for a device.
Revoking a pairing, changing its grants or expiry, revoking publication, refreshing
the source binding or disabling Slate Windows denies later device reads.

## Local API / Slate

The existing CLI/MCP and Slate /call share ten Kernel operations:
ledger.windows.status/configure/open/list/snapshot/refresh/close/publish/revoke/present.
Use /windows to list accessible views and /window sw_HEX to read one exact ID.
Use the full 32 hexadecimal characters produced by the broker.

Open takes selector, expected_object_id and expected_revision from
ledger.object.inspect. Snapshot takes window_id. Refresh and publish require
expected_revision from the saved overview. Publish additionally takes device
(the real remote.sessions identity). Configure takes enabled. Revoke takes
window_id and device. Close takes window_id.

Present accepts window_id and a presentation object with overview view, scroll,
zoom (0.5–3), and collapsed. It writes only the current authenticated principal's
presentation metadata under read scope. No caller-supplied owner or presentation
recipient is accepted. Desktop/phone layouts never alter the source revision or
another device's layout. Future renderers must not treat presentation as intent,
approval or source truth.

## Storage, bounds and checks

Four additive tables in the existing private Engineering Kernel SQLite database
hold window metadata, owner feature flags, explicit publication bindings and
per-principal layouts. The default is disabled. There is no second scheduler,
source database, viewer process or model worker.

At most 32 windows per owner, 16 publication recipients per window, 17 presentation
rows per window, 16 KiB per window record and 16 KiB per returned snapshot; relevant registered artifacts are limited to 64 MiB per dependency check.
Reopening the same exact object/revision reuses its ID. The record stores only
locators, bounded overview metadata and dependency seals; original source bytes,
technical payloads and executable actions are not copied.

Owner capture uses the actual caller's existing Object Glass checks. Published
reads revalidate sealed source connections, native/reference identities, selected
originals, relevant job/evidence/artifact bytes and reader fingerprints. They never
construct the source owner's Principal or open the owner's map API to the device.
Authorization and source dependencies are rechecked at publication. This is a
checked snapshot, not continuous observation. An authorized stale view returns no
title, selector or technical content; only its owner receives the old revision
token needed for an explicit refresh.

Opaque IDs confer no permission. Missing and inaccessible IDs have the same error.
Actual operating-system account access remains the local trust boundary, as before.
The limited publication projection is deliberate; sharing a full source or evidence
view will require its own SW-002 authorization/projection review.

## Disable and recovery

Disabling clears the owner's publication grants and recipient presentation rows;
it preserves all jobs, evidence, sources, windows and owner layout. Re-enabling
restores no device grants. Refresh also clears publication grants and recipient
layouts. Close and revoke remain available while disabled. A cold process reads
the registry without submitting jobs or restoring execution grants.

To roll back, disable the feature, close Ledger and return to the retained Pass 14
program with the private-state backup. The additive tables may remain; Pass 14
ignores them. Do not replace an active private database with the empty release.
Preserve the private database and OS profile: existing memory editions do not automatically include the new window tables.

The original four uploaded files and all pre-existing protected SDK, policy,
test and runtime-pin bytes remain unchanged. The new portable SDK contract and
five-case test module require independent acceptance.

## Focused evidence and next work

Five new acceptance cases reuse the existing map fixture. They exercise a controlled
U23 reference, cold-process restoration, filtered publication, unknown/foreign IDs,
mid-read revocation, source drift, refresh/republication, separate layouts, quotas,
disable/re-enable and unchanged remote operation boundaries. This is development
evidence on a synthetic reference, not the private real 649-component project.
Two existing Object Glass checks and five existing remote checks are the focused
regression set; the previous full 810-test campaign is not rerun.

The native walkthrough uses pinned PySide6 6.8.3 on local Linux with offscreen
rendering. Actual owner Debian/Fluxbox, Windows, iPhone and network acceptance remain
OPEN. No new ARC-1 enhancement is established; the existing PSRAM and D213 USB-mux
leads remain retained with their original limits.

Next: core Pass 15 activity awareness and resource controls. SW-002 follows Pass 17
document views; SW-003 follows recovery Pass 32. Keep all remaining core, document,
memory, voice, mail and collaboration requirements intact.

records.text:
# SW-002 — shared reading and Window Deck

Development checkpoint, 28 October 2026. Independent source/security and actual
owner ThinkPad/iPhone/network acceptance remain OPEN. This cumulative edition
includes N1, expanded N2/G1–G5, N3 and P17. The language stays **staC**, pronounced
**Stacy (STAY-see)**; Slate is the male bird.

## Milestone and next work

SW-001, P17 and SW-002 assemble **M2 — Shared reading**. The owner reviews a
source-bound view, publishes it to one paired device, and that device reads the
same identity/revision through an inert renderer. M2 is demonstrated on the
declared development profile; its actual owner/device gates remain open.

A milestone is a demonstrated workflow across its dependency passes. A counter
does not automatically create one after five passes. See MILESTONES.md and
docs/milestones.json for all eight capability groups. The next grouped
boundary is M3 after P18, P19 and P20: notes/knowledge exchange, notebooks,
engineering tables and the declared editable-document profile. Twenty-five
retained planned deliveries remain after SW-002. Historical 86/225 points are
unchanged; neither the groups nor development checks invent a new percentage.

Every handoff includes an approximately ten-minute discussion of present state,
next work, milestone movement and final destination. Routine implementation
decisions continue under the owner's existing autonomous-development direction.

## Desktop workflow

Enable resumable windows in Object Glass. Select a supported component, net,
saved file, job or requirement; Keep view retains its checked identity. The
existing Publish overview remains overview-only. **Preview / share content**
opens the new native read-only renderer. Choose Object, Sources or Evidence;
Candidate review additionally requires a job linked to a real draft candidate.

Prepare preview reads under the actual local caller's existing authority.
The dialog shows the exact bounded reading content, source identity and content
digest. Choose a live paired device and explicitly acknowledge reviewing that
content before **Publish reviewed view** enables. Publication grants the
overview and the selected content view atomically. Changing the selected view
or device clears the acknowledgement. No engineering action or source acceptance
is performed by publication. Revoke removes all views for that window/device.

P17's reader now has **Share page view**. It can retain an already completed,
original-bound page job as a logical PDF window. Its native review dialog shows
the checked original page raster in a scrollable tab alongside the reading
content, before publication. If saved windows are disabled,
the desktop explicitly offers to enable them; it does not silently enable
sharing. The PDF preview includes physical page, original hash, native text,
optional explicitly requested OCR and the checked page raster. Private PDF
annotations and recovery drafts are not included in this profile.

The retained window list accepts both ordinary object windows and PDF windows.
Restoring a PDF window opens its reviewed shared-content dialog. These are
reading snapshots; they do not follow a desktop selection automatically.

## Satellite workflow

Pair through the existing owner-hosted endpoint. **Views** opens the Window Deck.
A read-scoped pairing alone sees no unpublished window. An overview grant alone
does not reveal Sources, Evidence or PDF content. The owner must publish each
supported view explicitly for that particular paired identity.

The deck uses the same window, object and source-revision identities as the
desktop. Source/provenance details can be expanded while reading content takes
priority. Technical text, Unicode, source strings and diffs are rendered as
literal text. There is no arbitrary HTML/Markdown execution, link navigation,
iframe, remote desktop stream or command runner in a shared content view.
PDFs are displayed as checked PNG derivatives, not active PDF documents.

Zoom and scroll belong to the authenticated reader and selected view. They
cannot alter another device's layout or source truth. Presentation saves and
foreground checks revalidate publication. Closing/hiding, connection loss,
expiry, revocation or a failed current-view check clears the reading surface;
an unavailable result never substitutes an old cached excerpt. The existing
foreground session poll checks an open deck view at its 15-second interval.
Already received information cannot be retroactively erased from a recipient.
This pass is not the later SW-003 replay/follow/reconnect qualification.

The active satellite uses the existing approved Slate bird pixels in its
welcome surface, navigation and new install icons. Historical girl/fairy asset
files retain their original names and bytes. The manifest now names Slate and
allows portrait and landscape. The licensed bundled CJK font supplies a fallback
when the browser lacks an appropriate local font. No new artwork or font model
is downloaded into the product.

## Authorization and records

Seven typed operations extend the existing Kernel registry:

| Operation | Scope | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ledger.windows.pdf | read + approve | Keep an existing verified owner PDF-page result as a logical window. |
| ledger.deck.preview | read + approve | Prepare exact content under the actual caller. No publication. |
| ledger.deck.publish | read + approve | Publish the reviewed content digest to one live paired identity. |
| ledger.deck.list | read | List the current caller's published windows/views. |
| ledger.deck.read | read | Read one explicitly published, revision-bound content projection. |
| ledger.deck.image | read | Read the matching checked PDF raster through that view's grant. |
| ledger.deck.present | read | Save only that caller's bounded scroll/zoom. |

Only the last four are added to the HTTP transport's operation set. The previous
protected record_visibility SDK operation set is byte preserved. The new
portable SDK declares the exact four-route addition and validates the bounded,
inert projection format. Tests inspect the actual transport union, not merely
the old SDK constant. Existing pairing path/tool/approval scopes are unchanged.
Even an old owner-profile phone cannot publish views through the transport.

Private deck routes are excluded from cloud proposals, including supported
typed-pipeline indirection. Local clients remain subject to Kernel scopes and
object ownership. No owner Principal is constructed on a phone's behalf.
Owner capture uses actual owner reads; later device reads use the reviewed
projection and direct verification of its sealed dependencies.

Three additive tables in the same private Kernel SQLite database hold bounded
preview projections, explicit per-view grants and per-principal view layouts.
They are rebuildable publication data, not a replacement original-source store
or scheduler. No new job tool or model worker is introduced. PDF reading jobs
remain the existing P17 jobs, started by the owner before publication.

Content is bound to the window/object ID, source revision, window generation,
content digest, renderer fingerprint and live pairing/session fingerprint.
Current original admission, relevant job/evidence/artifact bytes and publication
are checked again on use, including late checks before returning results.
PDF result JSON must match the completed Kernel evidence and image hash. Image
responses are bounded and hashed again in the browser before display.

The existing limits remain: 32 windows per owner and 16 paired recipients per
window. There are five content kinds, at most 24 blocks and 96 KiB per projection;
each text block is at most 48 KiB with explicit excerpt reporting. Image limits
remain P17's 6 MiB and 2,000-pixel maximum dimension. Unsupported binary text,
large projections or unavailable sources produce explicit gaps. PDF OCR remains
unverified and table positions do not become semantic cell reconstruction.

Refresh, close, revoke and disable remove the applicable content grants and
reader layouts. Refresh/disable clear prepared projections; re-enabling does not
restore publication. Jobs and original sources are preserved. New table coverage
must be included in the retained P32 complete-recovery qualification.

The HTTP request parser now uses the existing strict JSON reader, rejecting
duplicate members and non-finite values. Host/Origin/CSRF, HttpOnly/SameSite
cookies, rate limits, no-store API responses, CSP and current-session checks
remain in place. Only allowlisted static assets are served. Browser storage
caches the interface shell, not the new content, API responses or page rasters.
These controls are development evidence, not independent security certification.

## Upgrade boundary

Stop the previous coordinator before replacing an edition and keep complete
private-state backups. Use all three matching SW-002 archives in a fresh folder.
The changed paired-device transport policy invalidates older pairing sessions:
pair again and explicitly publish the desired views. Existing SW-001 windows
need owner refresh/review under the changed reader fingerprint; no old overview
grant silently expands into a content grant. P17's earlier intake-rule migration
still applies when upgrading from an edition before P17.

No existing protected SDK, tests, policy, hardware, runtime pins or historical
branding are modified relative to P17. New protected additions are
sdk/cli/arc1cli/window_views.py and tests/test_window_deck.py. Independent source
acceptance remains OPEN. The source-change receipt gives exact before/after
hashes for all modified and added files.

## Verification profile and limits

The actual-browser walkthrough uses Qt WebEngine 6.8.3 / Chromium 122.0.6261.171,
not a DOM mock. It exercises 320×700, 390×844 and 844×390 layouts, actual HTTP
pairing/cookies/Origin, native owner preview/publication, a controlled U23 map,
hostile UTF-8 text, actual candidate diff data and an authored original PDF.
The shared service and page worker are real processes. The declared candidate
job is interrupted and unexecuted; no compiler result is fabricated.

The native owner and browser run in separate processes, matching the desktop/
satellite architecture. The combined-process developer harness was unstable;
the separated harness exercises both surfaces without changing product checks.
The browser uses software rendering in this sandbox. Its OS sandbox is disabled
only in the isolated developer test process; no such setting enters the product
or a user's phone. Two missing developer shared libraries were extracted into
a temporary developer path, with receipts; they are not product dependencies.

Controls and summaries are measured at a minimum of 44×44 CSS pixels in the
tested layouts. This is a selected accessibility check, not a claim of complete
WCAG conformance. Browser images are private visual-inspection artifacts and
are not distributed. Native Qt preview and machine-readable observations are
included. Final counts and fresh-assembly checks are in SW002_VERIFICATION.json
and the review folder. Historical unavailable project-dependent tests remain
disclosed and byte preserved.

Actual Safari/iPhone/Home Screen behavior, trusted owner HTTPS, Wi-Fi/cellular,
sleep/reconnect, practical latency and actual ThinkPad setup remain SW-005/P36
and related retained gates. A graphical bridge remains the conditional SW-004
pilot. There are no live Gemini requests, real weights inference, public
Internet deployment or physical hardware acceptance in this pass.

## Primary research

* [W3C target size enhanced](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-enhanced.html): the 44 CSS-pixel target informed the measured controls.
* [OWASP frontend security](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Web_Frontend_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html): untrusted API/source text uses textContent and known structures; URL/style contexts are handled separately.
* [Playwright browser profiles](https://playwright.dev/docs/browsers): browser binaries are version-specific. Its optional development download failed here; actual-browser evidence instead uses the separately identified installed Qt Chromium engine.
* Existing SW-001, P17, N3 and the owner-supplied window architecture retain the source-of-truth identity, explicit publication and lifetime requirements.

# Slate Windows campaign integration

The owner authorized the uploaded ARC Slate Window System Architecture v1.0 campaign. Both supplied copies have identical extracted content. We retain core passes 13 through 37 and insert SW-001 through SW-005 by dependency. Slate is the assistant name throughout this implementation plan. These additions supersede blanket deferral of iPhone development; actual device and network acceptance remain required before a mobile release.

SW-001 follows Pass 14 selected-object context: typed window identities, per-caller object authorization, filtered snapshots, bounded registry and source revision checks. Prove U23 restores by opaque window ID, guessed IDs disclose no private metadata, source drift withholds content, per-device layout stays separate, and disabling the feature preserves existing jobs and PWA behavior.

SW-002 follows SW-001 and Pass 17 document views: mobile Window Deck and native object/source/evidence renderers. Prove correct object and revision, text-only rendering of hostile content, touch-size controls in portrait and landscape, explicit review previews, and actual browser evidence. Phone-size emulation is development evidence; actual iPhone behavior remains a separate gate.

SW-003 follows SW-002 and Pass 32 recovery: reconnect, sequence/reset behavior and explicit follow mode. Prove fresh grant checks, stale approval invalidation, bounded replay with snapshot fallback, one durable job under a repeated request key, and independent device scroll/zoom/focus. Streaming transport remains a later measured choice.

SW-004 follows SW-003 and requires an owner host: optional graphical bridge feasibility and restricted pilot. Prove a dedicated restricted identity, one harmless read-only viewer, disabled clipboard/file transfer/printing and other unnecessary features, private transport and bounded resources, and documented exact-version licence/deployment plus disable/recovery results. Adoption is conditional; any decision to omit the pilot requires a recorded scope amendment. It cannot be marked passed from an unexecuted command example.

SW-005 follows SW-003 and any adopted SW-004 bridge, before core Pass 36 closes: actual iPhone Wi-Fi/cellular and security qualification. Prove trusted HTTPS and owner-network reachability, sleep/resume and network transition recovery, prompt revocation and stale-intent denial, measured latency/resource results with samples and percentiles, and independent security plus owner acceptance. No mandatory third-party relay is introduced. Network configuration and certificate provision are owner-host tasks when this pass begins.

Each SW pass has five completion checks, one point each. Current SW-001 development progress is 5/25; core is 81/200 (40.5%) after Pass 16. Combined programme is 86/225 (38.2%). Independent acceptance remains open. The original addendum began at 66/225 before Pass 14 and window implementation. Independent core acceptance requirements remain intact. Debug pass 13D adds no milestone points. Fabrication, routing release and physical programming remain separate HOLD decisions.

Primary source: owner-supplied ARC_Slate_Window_System_Architecture_v1_0(2).docx, with identical extracted text to copy (1). Its proposed broker, endpoints, transport options and budgets are design inputs, not deployed capabilities. Original architecture document remains unchanged.

records.text:
# Stacy Ledger knowledge foundation

Pass 1 gives Stacy a source-bound account of Ledger itself. It extends the
existing PySide6 application and Engineering Kernel. A deterministic reader
demonstrates the packet and answer contracts. Local LLM inference, durable
journal recovery, quarantine admission, learning and study remain later passes.

## Open and use

Open **Ledger → Stacy knowledge**, **Tools → Stacy Knowledge**, or ask Stacy
`/open knowledge`. The existing command catalog, CLI and MCP expose the same
eight read operations. Tutor mode may read the foundation; it gains no new
execution or source acceptance authority.

* `/knowledge` reports the seed and actual registry counts.
* `/seed reading.code_pt` searches the indexed seed.
* `/capabilities boot` reports registration, scope and sampled missing inputs.
* `/explain settings reading.code_pt` explains the effective selected setting.
* `/explain commands boot.inspect` explains the actual command prerequisites.
* `/explain hdl rgmii` explains the named profile and passive runtime discovery.
* `/explain` or `explain this window` uses the actual current supported selection.

Settings, command and HDL profile selectors are the supported ViewContext
surfaces. Other views produce an explicit unsupported-context response. The
HDL descriptor does not claim to interpret an unselected trace or signal value.
The knowledge tab can reopen the last supported selection for inspection.

## Knowledge and capability status

The portable seed holds a JSON catalog, a SQLite FTS5 index, an input manifest
and, in the exported ZIP, copies of the declared public Ledger sources. It
contains command schemas, setting definitions, reviewed documentation and the
explicit owner intent below. Private profiles, credentials, unsaved buffers,
model weights and hardware/vendor sources do not enter this seed.

Owner intent: Stacy understands Ledger first, explains selected program data,
uses registered tools and retains evidence-backed knowledge independently of
replaceable model weights. Durable awareness, rule-based intake into a clean V1,
custom reference volumes, checkpoints, idle study and manual Frontier research
ZIP exchange remain the agreed later work.

Every seed read checks catalog/index integrity and current hashes of its narrow
declared input set. Changed inputs yield STALE; missing originals yield
SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. A damaged seed yields INVALID. These are integrity and
source-identity states, not independent technical acceptance or publisher
authentication. No whole-project-current claim follows from this fingerprint.

The capability manifest covers the current operation registry and its declared
handler links. It distinguishes HANDLER_UNRESOLVED, BLOCKED_MISSING_INPUT,
OUTSIDE_SCOPE, NEEDS_ARGUMENTS and REGISTERED. Registration and authorization
do not prove that a native runtime exists or that an operation is qualified.
The first prerequisite profiles cover boot.inspect and hardware.proof.inspect.
The Stacy reader wrapper returns structured blockers without changing the
protected original hardware, SDK, tests, boot readers or P8 sources.

## Provider contract

A foundation packet carries a supported view, effective data, source hashes,
unknowns, a read-only scope and a packet digest. The deterministic provider
returns structured field claims and source IDs. The validator rejects changed
values, invented locators, another packet identity and proposed execution.
The explanation text is rendered from those checked fields. This verifies
field support, not unrestricted natural-language entailment or LLM quality.

## Reproduce the local seed

```text
python -m workbench.stacy_foundation build-seed --export build/stacy/ledger_seed.zip
python -m workbench.engineering_cli call stacy.seed.status
python -m workbench.engineering_cli call stacy.explain --params '{"view":"settings","selection":"reading.code_pt"}'
```

Seed authoring is an explicit local maintenance command. No read operation
writes a seed, runs a native binary, calls a model provider or promotes source.
The shell quoting above is POSIX syntax. Use the normal launchers on the owner
machine and preserve existing installation and approval instructions.

## Completion estimate and next pass

Pass 1 is one of eight delivery passes. After its acceptance checks, the
milestone-count estimate is approximately 13 percent. This is a planning
estimate, not measured feature coverage or a probability of correctness.

Pass 2 adds the durable journal, per-consumer cursors, catch-up across the
current 500-event limit, visible awareness gaps, atomic state/event commits
and control coverage across the declared workflows. The present activity tail
continues to use its existing retention and is not relabeled as durable memory.

# Stacy born Pass 10 — source-linked engineering map

Development candidate. The knowledge campaign advances from 10% to a 25% target after the five source-map checks have evidence. Independent protected-source acceptance, current-project engineering acceptance and owner-host qualification remain open. The earlier eight-pass software estimate stays separately at 90%.

## What this adds

Open Ledger active > Source connections > Engineering map. Attach the separate ROM, inspect the preserved locked project ZIP, and explicitly select its V1 reference snapshot using the preceding Source connections controls. In Engineering map, refresh the sources, choose that snapshot and ROM, and build a source map. These actions use the existing Engineering Kernel scheduler, cancellation, evidence and private database. No project source is restored or promoted.

The map reuses NetGraph and shares a Qt-free KiCad S-expression reader with the existing inspector. It correlates netlist component references, schematic UUIDs, values and footprints with original native schematic symbols and PCB pad/net assignments. Each endpoint retains pin, net and pad UUID. A component graph path preserves intervening components but does not establish current flow, switch state, routed copper or physical operation.

The original native export receipt is compared with the exact preserved schematic and netlist hashes. Its matching state is historical corroboration, not a fresh KiCad export on this host or independent engineering approval. Missing or contradictory identities remain visible. Unconnected schematic pins with unassigned PCB pads are distinguished from a named-net disagreement.

Select Part, Net, Trace native path or Evidence. Short summaries are followed by optional Technical map details. The displayed equivalent staC command reads the same Kernel relationship and source revision. No new top-level workspace, device or pin allowance is introduced.

## Source relationships and honest gaps

The schematic Value is preserved separately from the exact MPN declared in the native PCB properties. The footprint is an identified design package, not confirmation that the purchased part fits. Device grade and operating conditions begin UNVERIFIED.

Vendor candidates require an exact MPN mention in preserved document metadata and a currently available original hash. This is a candidate relationship, not reviewed document applicability. Document grade, conditions and package still need engineering review. An owner may record a document selection through knowledge.map.configure, but that record remains an owner declaration rather than an accepted manufacturer fact.

Existing software bindings retain their explicit archived origin. Additional code locations are bounded lexical identifier mentions with exact file hashes and line numbers; they are not promoted into validated implementation mappings. Draft requirements remain draft. Full RTL/firmware interpretation and accepted test-oracle binding are subsequent engineering work.

The real reference pilot includes USBMUX_SEL (U23, J10 and R62) and the PSRAM data/control interfaces. PSRAM clock names on either side of an intervening resistor remain distinct. No D213 GPIO is invented. The map does not claim that the historical loader discrepancy still exists or has been fixed; that is a Pass 12 investigation.

## Recorded evidence and stale scope

Evidence is referenced through actual owned Kernel jobs. The staC 0.6 witness checks record links and classes. The map additionally rehashes registered artifact bytes and exposes the original job revision, candidate, outcome and oracle artifact. A successful process or source-map job is not controller compliance. Missing approved test oracles and requirement bindings remain gaps.

A map is owner-scoped and points to its exact source connections, generations, reader and registered graph artifact. Every read rechecks those bindings, with a second publication barrier. A changed archive, revoked source, altered artifact, reader update or generation change makes the map unavailable until rebuilt.

The configuration contains bounded operating conditions, owner document declarations and existing oracle/job references. Updating it requires approval and the expected current revision. Changes create a new view revision. Commands or packet candidates pinned to the preceding revision return STALE. The impact policy is conservative: the entire map view is invalidated; precise per-conclusion dependency reduction belongs to the Evidence Compiler. Untracked impact is not asserted safe.

Each explicit build creates a separate map edition, preserving native component identities and the preceding map. A failed or cancelled build cannot overwrite an earlier usable map. Replaying the same Kernel request key returns the existing invocation; restart reads stored records without resubmitting jobs. Old observations remain historical, never automatically current.

## staC integration

The supplied cumulative staC 0.6 source is integrated with provenance retained. Legacy IR meanings and digests remain versioned. Its new short commands and recorded Kernel witnesses do not launch jobs.

The Ledger bridge adds a small finite read grammar:

    source ROM_CONNECTION_ID | search "APS3204L" | take 5
    source ROM_CONNECTION_ID | originals
    map MAP_ID | part U45
    map MAP_ID | net USBMUX_SEL
    map MAP_ID | trace U23 J10
    map MAP_ID | trace U40 U45 on PSRAM_SCLK
    map MAP_ID | evidence
    map MAP_ID | status
    map MAP_ID@VIEW_REVISION | part U45

Replace identifiers with the real private IDs shown in Technical map details. The bridge forwards the authenticated caller and existing scopes. A model-created owner field cannot substitute for identity. The existing embedded staC panel, JSON CLI and MCP use that same bridge. The standalone staC batch CLI also routes map/source commands through it; the legacy REPL remains its original engineering grammar. These are read requests, not shell commands or a second execution framework.

## Limits and privacy

Each map artifact is capped at 8 MiB, its metadata at 64 KiB, and each owner at 16 maps. Archive inputs retain the preceding compressed/expanded limits; selected parser inputs have 16 MiB per-file and 64 MiB total limits. Source workers retain finite CPU/memory/time limits and cancellation. Query traces exclude power nets and retain the existing twelve-hop bound. Exact source and archive checks have a measurable local cost; no ThinkPad performance is inferred from this host. Native qualification uses a local Linux filesystem. SQLite WAL state on cloud or network-mounted workspace storage is unqualified; an attempted development run there produced a malformed test database, which was preserved separately. Owner data was not involved.

ROM, locked project archive, user personality seed, model weights, credentials, original vendor passages and private map state remain outside program packages. The personality seed remains a private presentation reference; it grants neither engineering authority nor execution permissions. Character stays curious and candid; short answers and expandable technical detail remain the UX direction. ThinkPad study reports remain local; iPhone development is deferred.

## What remains

Pass 11 compiles these relationships into one versioned EKP contract with frozen source bindings, claim locations, requirements, evidence classes, contradictions and budgets. Pass 12 qualifies the PSRAM and USB investigations, including unseen variations and independent review. Pass 13 connects actual local/provider reasoning and reviewed procedures. Pass 14 qualifies combined real-model replacement, memory editions and cold recovery. Pass 15 qualifies the actual ThinkPad workflow and independent protected-source acceptance.

Longer-term notes are preserved as acceptance direction: Knowledge Diffs, candidate falsification questions, a private engineering curriculum with held-out cases, historical source reconstruction and measured procedural benefit. Existing services supply the learning function; no parallel execution authority or model-weight training is introduced.

Official native format references: https://dev-docs.kicad.org/en/file-formats/sexpr-pcb/ and https://dev-docs.kicad.org/en/file-formats/sexpr-schematic/ .

# Stacy born Pass 11 — Evidence Compiler

Development candidate. This pass advances Ledger and Stacy using ARC-1 questions as software acceptance cases. It does not alter hardware, firmware or canonical project sources. Five declared compiler gates target 45% of the separate knowledge campaign. Independent protected-source acceptance, current engineering acceptance and owner ThinkPad qualification remain open. The earlier eight-pass implementation estimate stays separately at 90%.

## Use it

Open Ledger active > Source connections > Evidence Compiler. First connect the separately preserved ROM and build the V1 reference engineering map using the preceding tabs. Refresh, select a map, enter the component, question and an optional literal source lookup term, then Compile evidence packet. U45 and tCEM are useful starting values. Compilation is a registered, cancellable Engineering Kernel job; it never invokes a model or executes imported project code.

The default view gives a short source/gap summary. Evidence, Sources and Uncertainties expose different authorities. Select a source to reopen its checked excerpt and locator. Open selected original PDF page starts the existing bounded original-page reader/render job. Technical packet details expand the complete JSON. Save packet is an explicit local save to a new file; it does not grant external disclosure.

The displayed `packet ID | inspect` command returns exactly the same checked packet through the caller-aware staC bridge. `sources`, `gaps` and `why` select presentation intent on the same result; they do not create another packet or launch a job. The standalone batch CLI and the embedded staC bridge share these reads. The legacy REPL remains its existing grammar. Stacy can use the registered Kernel operations and existing `/call` conversation command. Ordinary English engineering reasoning is Pass 13 work.

## One versioned packet authority

The compiler extends the existing `arc.reference-ekp/1` family to `arc.reference-ekp/2`, stored in the existing private `ref_packets` table. A separate integrity receipt binds each v2 record to its owner, actual compiler job and registered packet artifact. It is a verification receipt, not a competing evidence store. Existing v1 packets and historical `arc.stac.ekp/0.2` packets retain their schemas and meanings; they are not silently upgraded or accepted as v2 evidence.

Every invocation has a separate ID, job and timestamp. The context digest excludes those invocation fields. Equivalent frozen source, map, page and evidence inputs produce the same canonical context digest. Canonicalization is the existing ARC JSON byte profile, not a claim of RFC 8785 compatibility. Fact, passage, page and legacy-input ordering is deterministic.

The context contains a question, exact map revision, native component/MPN/package identities, source passages with hashes and native/page/line locators, declared relationships, draft requirements, reviewed reference facts if explicitly supplied, hypotheses, actual Kernel evidence references, conflicts, gaps and budgets. Identification, document applicability and engineering compliance are independent fields. Native grade remains UNVERIFIED; owner grade and condition declarations are preserved as declarations. A source-map oracle reports correspondence; it cannot pass a controller requirement.

## Sources, facts and uncertainty

Document candidates come from exact MPN metadata matches or explicit owner document declarations. The bounded lookup selects at most two original pages automatically. An explicit request can choose up to four associated pages. Search text only locates a page: the compiler reextracts selected text from the current, hash-verified original using the shared original reader. Original identifiers, page labels and Chinese text remain preserved. OCR and translation are not invented. A missing association or lookup match produces a visible gap rather than an unsupported answer.

Native excerpts retain schematic UUID, PCB UUID, exact board/archive identities and their registered map location. Up to three source-code excerpts preserve exact file hashes and line ranges, with their association labelled as an unreviewed lexical mention. Native net membership does not establish signal direction, electrical conduction or physical behavior. Up to twelve draft requirement records and software declarations retain their source identities; omitted items are labelled. Full relationships remain available through the engineering map.

The optional `source_packets` field imports up to three current, caller-authorized v1 reference packets. Their passage IDs and reviewed quantities stay intact. Their original admissions, review state, exact conditions and units are rechecked before use. Imported facts do not automatically apply to the selected fitted component. Hypotheses remain separate from reviewed facts. Conflicting exact quantities or opposing support in the identical subject/property/variant/condition/role context stay visible. Standard and extended grades and different operating conditions are not merged. Quantities such as 3 us and 3000 ns compare exactly without floating-point rounding.

No bare numeric datasheet limit is automatically extracted or approved from a PDF table. Accepted current requirements, source-to-implementation mappings, reviewed controller test oracles and physical measurements remain explicit proof obligations. The grade-sensitive PSRAM and D213 loader/mux investigations are qualified in Pass 12, including unseen variations and independent review.

## Freshness, permissions and bounded work

Reads recheck the private receipt, actual completed owned compiler job, recorded packet bytes, compiler/extractor fingerprint, map revision and source generations, original page hashes, legacy admission/review dependencies, and current recorded job/oracle/artifact bytes. A second boundary after slow evidence reads rechecks source and condition state. Changed or revoked inputs withhold all cached packet text. A prior edition is retained as history rather than overwritten. Packet identity is not permission, and a model-supplied approval or owner field is rejected.

Compilation requires the actual caller's read and execute scopes. It cannot execute project candidates, widen approval or accept source. Local exports additionally require approval, preserve existing files and recheck the packet. Cloud proposals cannot retrieve or compile private packets directly or through the typed language; this pass grants no Gemini/Frontier disclosure. Local reasoning can propose only calls allowed by its existing principal. Citation validation checks locator membership only, explicitly leaving semantic entailment and technical truth unverified.

The default full JSON export cap is 64 KiB; the caller may choose 8–128 KiB. This includes envelope aliases for legacy adapters. Oversized output fails before publication. Other bounds are four original pages, thirty-two native pins, three code excerpts, thirty-two passages, three legacy reference packets and 256 stored compiler invocations per owner. Truncation is named in gaps; the full map is not deleted. Worker CPU, memory, timeout, cancellation and Master Stop remain under the existing Kernel. There is no implicit retry, provider call, code execution or archival admission.

## Release and qualification

The program still ships as three ordinary ZIP overlays. Extract all three into the same fresh parent folder, merging Arc_Ledger; do not concatenate them. Assembly checks all receipts and refuses missing or mixed releases. Source corpus, personality, weights, credentials, private maps and packets stay outside the program ZIPs. Previous program and private-state backups remain available for rollback. Fourteen devices, seven workspace areas and five pin slots remain unchanged. ThinkPad study reports stay local; iPhone work is deferred.

The release receipt records retained checks, new compiler checks, actual Qt/Kernel jobs, independent process recovery and fresh-package privacy/launcher checks. Native qualification uses local Linux filesystem state and an offscreen Qt display. Network/cloud-mounted SQLite WAL, actual owner ThinkPad, Windows, GPU/runtime replacement and live providers remain unqualified. All SDK additions, test additions and existing source changes are disclosed for independent acceptance. Policies, hardware, runtime pins and pre-existing tests are not changed.

Next: Pass 12 engineering investigations (target 65%), Pass 13 grounded reasoning and reviewed procedures (80%), Pass 14 combined memory/model recovery (90%), and Pass 15 owner-host release qualification (100%). These percentages are milestone estimates backed by the named development gates, not proof of engineering answer accuracy or board readiness.

# Stacy born Pass 12 Engineering investigations

This development pass adds bounded, reproducible engineering investigations to Ledger and Stacy. ARC-1 supplies preserved source examples. The program continues to ship separately from its private source corpus, model weights and personality. Independent source acceptance and physical hardware qualification remain open.

The campaign plan assigns twenty points to five Pass 12 checks. Four demonstrated development checks can raise the knowledge campaign from 45% to 61%. A separate independent review supplies the remaining four points toward the 65% target. Automated checks and the implementing author's review cannot supply that independent acceptance.

## Start an investigation

Open Ledger active > Source connections. Connect the separate ROM, select the preserved V1 reference snapshot, build its engineering map and compile a packet for the part using the preceding tabs. In Investigations, Refresh, choose the packet and choose PSRAM timing oracle or USB mux assumption. Run selected case requires the current owner's read, execute and approve scopes. Cancel investigation and Master Stop use the existing Engineering Kernel.

For PSRAM, use a U45 packet and the preserved APS3204L-3SQNA-SN vendor original. The initial case uses a 40 MHz controller clock, 256-byte write and starting address 900. The optional bounded variation allows whole MHz clocks from 40 to 50 MHz, 64–256 bytes and addresses from 0 to 4096. These are controlled host case inputs, not an accepted hardware configuration. Icarus Verilog and its vvp runtime must be installed separately and available on PATH; the empty program does not include their binaries. Missing tools fail clearly without creating a passing case.

For USB, use a U23 packet whose native selector net is USBMUX_SEL. The investigation compares a direct-D213 control hypothesis with native net membership and the preserved loader's callbacks. That hypothesis is a question, not a fact accepted from a previous chat.

Results start with a short assessment. Results, Sources and Uncertainties expose experiment outcomes, exact original locators and limitations. Select a source to reopen its freshly checked excerpt. Technical investigation details expand the full record. Save report writes a new local JSON file after rechecking dependencies. The displayed `investigation JOB_ID | inspect` command returns the same checked report through staC or the standalone batch CLI. `gaps` and `why` retain that same result and mark presentation intent; they do not execute another investigation.

## PSRAM case and source interpretation

The method reopens the original manufacturer PDF, not the ROM search excerpt. It checks physical pages 1, 6, 26 and 27: nominal part identity, ordering/temperature range, Table 9 timing limits and the change log. The source interpretation retains 3 us for extended grade and 8 us for standard grade. The change log associates 3 us with 105 C. Units remain exact quantities. This identifies a bounded source interpretation; physical fitment, the operating point and independent applicability review remain unverified. Another part or a changed/unrecognized table cannot inherit this profile.

The preserved memory wrapper already sets TCEM_NS to 3000, and the preserved system testbench already selects the strict limit. The core's default of 8000 is a reusable parameter default, not evidence that the wrapper still has the old fault. The report therefore recognizes the existing strict configuration and proposes no automatic source change.

The experiment freezes three expected outcomes before scoring: loose controller with loose oracle PASS, loose controller with applicable strict oracle FAIL, and strict controller with applicable oracle PASS. All cases compile the unchanged preserved psram_qspi_core against the unchanged behavioral aps6404l_model_r07. The generated bench observes CE# pulse widths and actual written byte count. The behavioral model checks its own protocol rules; an independent exact parser also checks the recorded CE# widths. A success string alone cannot pass the oracle. Compiler results, native exit statuses, logs, original source identities and generated bench hashes are Kernel artifacts.

The loose case is a deliberately configured regression experiment using available source, not a claim to have recovered an unavailable historical revision. Its negative result must fail the native oracle. The strict case must pass that oracle with the complete requested write. The bounded current-controller assessment applies to initialization and writes through the selected core parameters. It does not qualify full wrapper elaboration, read data, fitted silicon or a complete board.

The preserved model is an ARC behavioral model for a 64 Mbit APS6404L, standing in for the nominal 32 Mbit APS3204L. It is not vendor IP or an exact model of the fitted device. Command compatibility, capacity/address behavior, electrical timing, clock/IO constraints and physical measurements remain separate qualification work. The report names these limitations beside the passing host case.

## USB case and historical conclusions

Native graph endpoints retain original pin, pad and net identities. The preserved USBMUX_SEL relationship includes U23.9, J10.2 and R62.1. Direct D213 membership is not supported by that net list. This establishes neither signal direction nor the absence of all possible indirect control paths.

The preserved r10_d213_start coordinator requests and observes mux selection through callbacks. Its header explicitly makes board observations a trust boundary. The bounded R10 C/header search records which source files were inspected and whether a callback initializer is present. Without a reviewed board adapter, GPIO/polarity binding and real observations, the outcome remains UNRESOLVED. Callback success cannot prove mux position or external-host isolation.

Stacy should explain that boundary and propose binding and testing the actual board adapter. She must not invent a GPIO, treat an old chat as source, reapply an old fix or interpret a source-map/host result as physical acceptance. No hardware, firmware, routing, source admission or canonical project source is changed by either investigation.

## Freeze and challenge the method

The method fingerprint covers the portable case contract, investigation service and shared native HDL adapter. Each request pins that method and the exact packet context. A separate qualification receipt freezes the complete runtime source set before selecting a previously unscored variation. The selected question, inputs and independent expected outcome stay outside Stacy's teaching index. The actual case job records its frozen oracle before any simulation begins.

The unseen variation qualifies this deterministic investigation workflow. It does not establish an LLM's engineering reasoning accuracy. Model explanation and authentic provider/reviewer exchanges belong to Pass 13. An implementing author's second check or a separate process is also not the independent case review required by check 12.5.

## Authority recovery and limits

Investigations remain ordinary owned Kernel jobs and registered artifacts; no parallel evidence database or execution authority is introduced. The result reader verifies completed job identity, exact request/method binding, packet freshness, all registered artifact bytes, extra original-page identities and the HDL executable/data fingerprints where applicable. Revoked or changed sources, changed conditions, changed tools and tampered artifacts withhold cached reports and excerpts. Restart reads existing results without replaying jobs.

HDL inputs use a fixed profile with finite permitted system tasks. File IO, source includes, arbitrary macro definitions, foreign hooks and DPI require separate review and are rejected. Variations cannot add a shell command, path, owner or approval. The worker has finite CPU/memory/output limits, the Kernel deadline, process-tree cancellation and source-revision checks. Negative case results remain negative results within a successfully recorded investigation. Independent case review remains OPEN.

The three program ZIPs contain code, public self-knowledge, assets/runtimes and bounded review receipts. Original ROM/PDF/RTL/firmware, private packets, full investigation artifacts, personality, credentials and model weights remain outside the program. Native QA uses a local Linux filesystem and an offscreen Qt display. Owner Debian/Fluxbox ThinkPad, Windows, GPU profiles and cloud/network-mounted SQLite WAL remain separately unqualified. Fourteen devices, seven workspace areas, five pinned slots and explicit saves are retained. iPhone development remains deferred.

Next is Pass 13: explain these checked investigations through actual local inference, permitted provider requests and reviewed procedure candidates. The remaining campaign also includes combined model/memory recovery and actual owner-host release qualification. The independent Pass 12 review is an additional open gate, not silently counted as complete.
