# Stacy born — Pass 2

Delivered: program/project separation, shared controls and durable awareness.
Estimated plan completion: 25% (two of eight passes, not an effort forecast).

## What is in each ZIP

The sealed user-data archive preserves the entire verified Pass 1 source snapshot,
including the original user project and program for recovery. Its inventory marks
892 original paths as quarantined project/history/reference material; the 505
retained original paths are program code, SDK runtime, tools, tests, UI assets and
Ledger help. The manifest and original paths preserve provenance. Nothing is
silently accepted into a clean V1 project. Included planning documents are reference
copies. The archive covers the files supplied with this Ledger snapshot; a larger
external Database ROM or files elsewhere on the owner's computer are not included.

The program ZIP contains the application and a freshly rebuilt Ledger knowledge
seed. No hardware source tree, ARC-OS source tree, user firmware, STRUTHIO game,
Orange Book project chapters, vendor originals, accepted engineering register,
geometry cache, candidate history, journal, credentials or personal profile is
shipped. The navigation definitions retain the 14 device slots and seven areas.
They do not claim an attached project. Original SDK/runtime contracts and small
embedded test fixtures are program resources. The hash-bound UX asset ZIP is a
required application resource and stays with the program.

## Using this build

Extract the program ZIP into its own folder. Use the existing START_LEDGER launcher
or `python -m workbench.launch` with the required PySide6 runtime installed.
It opens PROJECT NOT ATTACHED. The existing Ledger active navigation includes
Stacy awareness, Ledger knowledge, Commands and Settings. Exchange only this program
ZIP during our next coding passes. Keep the sealed archive outside it. Do not unzip
the archive over the program. Pass 4 will review and admit original project material.

Useful local commands: `/awareness`, `/project`, `/find jobs`,
`/describe jobs.submit`, `/open awareness`, `/open knowledge`, and `/tail`.
The existing CLI and MCP schema expose the same registered operations.

## Journal and recovery contract

`activity_journal` in the existing Engineering Kernel database holds every recorded
event without the former 500-event deletion. Increasing SQLite sequences define
commit order; wall-clock timestamps are presentation only. Event IDs deduplicate
replayed deliveries. Correlation, parent and source-generation fields are supported;
job transitions retain process ownership fields and link evidence IDs and bounded
stdout/stderr. No source text or credential values are logged.

Job, candidate and evidence state changes append journal events in their state
transaction. Settings stored in the database share that transaction. Profile settings
and explicit file saves cross a filesystem boundary: private pending receipts are
written first. A crash after replace cannot be described as a rolled-back file.
Stacy shows INCOMPLETE until Recover log reconciles the receipt against
the actual profile or file hash. Conflicts stay pending for human review. Failed
external event delivery is spooled and replayed idempotently. No automatic setting
rewrite or job retry occurs during recovery.

Each awareness consumer persists its cursor and materialized projection in one
transaction, processing at most 200 events per tick. Multiple consumers can catch up
independently. A failed projection cannot advance its cursor. CURRENT means caught
up to a stated journal head; CATCHING_UP exposes backlog; INCOMPLETE exposes missing
segments, failed delivery or unresolved receipts. Process identity is checked
separately from historical job state. A replaced PID is not signalled as our worker.
A lost worker becomes Interrupted only through existing explicit recovery controls.
No LLM calls are made by this monitor. Successful observer reads are excluded from
activity logging to avoid a feedback loop.

## Shared tool contract and truthful coverage

`ledger.capabilities.search` returns compact scope-eligible registry entries;
`ledger.capabilities.describe` returns one argument schema. Human views retain
blocked entries. Registration does not prove a native executable is installed,
qualified, or able to run without an attached project. `ledger.workflow.describe`
points at existing jobs.submit/get/cancel/pause/resume and evidence.read. Pause,
resume, candidate approval and runtime/platform constraints remain enforced by the
existing Kernel. Retry uses a new request key after source review; priority uses
the existing global setting. There is no second scheduler or tool authority.

Kernel request receipts, state transitions, shared settings and navigation, source
opens, explicit saves, focused tabs, the existing desktop/agent job starts and
finishes, and Master Stop are instrumented. Tool stdout/stderr are linked evidence,
not copied into every event. This is not byte-level tracing of every UI event,
third-party program, operating-system call or legacy helper. Runtime health does
not infer native tool or physical hardware qualification. The delivered coverage
and gaps are explicit rather than claiming the program logs literally everything.

The J14 pilot resolves exact CSV lines with path, line number and whole-file SHA256.
It was checked against the preserved source snapshot. The empty program returns
PROJECT_NOT_ATTACHED and no invented source record. This is a source-reference
pilot, not the later general retrieval database or engineering approval.

## Validation and acceptance limits

The package contains PASS_2_VERIFICATION.json with exact test and desktop results,
source-change disclosure, archive verification and fresh-extraction checks.
Existing tests and protected SDK/policy sources are preserved byte for byte in the
archive. New tests exercise long backlog, restart, duplicates, parallel writers,
rollback, missing segments, failed delivery, file/profile receipt recovery,
principal filtering and an actual owned worker cancellation. Offscreen Linux Qt
walkthrough evidence is included separately from native/owner qualification.

The original tools/check_release.py is preserved for its original full-project
contract. It expects hardware/source-identity/Orange Book data that the detached
program deliberately does not ship. Use tools/check_program_release.py for this
profile. Neither the old checker nor its tests were weakened to make an empty
project pass. Previously reported broad-suite issues are not declared resolved.
The ThinkPad, provider service and physical targets still require their own checks.

## Next pass — 3

Add the replaceable local inference adapter through the existing Kernel, beginning
with CPU inference on the owner's AMD ThinkPad. A supported model file will be
inspected for format, memory budget, context and compatibility before activation.
Keep previous-model rollback, cancellation and journal-visible lifecycle. Measure
any Vulkan acceleration rather than requiring CUDA. Start composable local commands
and translate English into validated proposals through the same tool schemas.
Project intake remains Pass 4; model retraining is outside this plan.

records.text:
# Stacy born — Pass 3 implementation candidate

Stacy now has a local Brain panel and a versioned read-only pipeline language.
The original project archive remains separate. This build uses the same PySide6
window, Engineering Kernel, jobs, journal, permissions and proposal review.

## Using Brain

Open Ledger active > Stacy Brain, or `/open brain`. Drop one local GGUF file or a
complete model folder. Add file and Add folder do the same work. Inspection and
hashing run as cancellable jobs without model inference. External files are
registered in place. The explicit copy checkbox copies them into the separate
Stacy model store, outside the program package. Keep weights out of coding ZIPs.

Inspect shows read-only metadata and up to 256 tensor descriptions. The interface
follows the upstream GGUF viewer's metadata/tensor separation, with an independent
bounded reader and no editing. Metadata includes architecture, quantization,
parameter count, template, declared license and exact file-set identity. Model
claims and runtime measurements are labelled separately. Incomplete/mismatched
shards, malformed/truncated files and incompatible projectors are held.

Qualify runs a CPU trial. Use model checkpoints the saved dialogue/journal position,
stops the previous worker, loads and probes the candidate, then atomically changes
the active selection. Qualification also uses sequential handover and restores the
previous running model afterward. Failed activation attempts restore the previous
usable worker. Cancel stops the job/process; a stopped selection stays available
for explicit Use or Restore Previous. Changing weights never changes permissions,
Ledger seed records, saved dialogues or existing engineering job identities.

Chat is local by default. An ordinary English message uses the active worker.
The existing Stacy menu and shared settings allow an explicit Gemini provider
choice; local failure does not fall through to a cloud request. Natural answers
are model-generated and require source verification. Supported selected settings,
commands and HDL views use the existing source-bound ViewContext packet. Saved
user turns commit before inference; all conversation turns remain in private
Ledger state, including turns outside the bounded active context. Full memory
selection/checkpoint restoration belongs to Pass 6.

Enable reviewed Stacy action proposals to request English command plans. The local
model returns a bounded proposal through the existing validation/review controls.
It cannot install/activate models, accept source, change disclosure preferences,
execute a shell or grant its own scopes. Valid JSON alone does not establish truth.

## Commands

`/brain` — local model status.
`/brain stop` — stop local inference through the Kernel.
`/ask Explain what Ledger does` — queue an offline reply.
`/think Show me the failed jobs` — request a reviewed action proposal.
`/plan jobs | where state=Failed | take 5 | select id,tool,state` — inspect a typed plan.
`/pipe jobs | where state=Failed | take 5 | select id,tool,state` — execute that read-only pipeline.

Language version 1 accepts one registered read-only Kernel source and at most
seven where/take/select transforms. It passes JSON rows, not shell strings. Plans
bind to the current Ledger seed and transport principal; optional expected_seed
rejects stale source bindings. No command substitution, redirects, arbitrary
executables, recursive pipelines or unregistered transforms are accepted. Existing
precise commands remain available. This is a small initial language, not a general
C/Unix replacement.

## Runtime and resource contract

Pinned llama.cpp: stable v0.7.0's b11669, commit
620d2225cc436ab0b001e3200e590e3b286ef9ab. Official Linux x64 and Windows x64 CPU
archives ship with their original MIT license and verified upstream archive hashes.
On first use Ledger extracts a private runtime cache and checks its files. No
runtime or model downloads happen during model inspection/loading. Native process
arguments are fixed by Ledger; the worker listens only on authenticated loopback,
with web UI/proxy features disabled. It receives no Ledger execution authority.

CPU is the delivered baseline. Context, trained context limit, weight size,
architecture/KV estimates, available RAM and a memory budget are checked before
loading. Linux uses an address-space cap in an exec trampoline. Windows hard memory
caps and owner-host runtime behavior remain unqualified; the CPU distribution is
included for later testing. Vulkan is deliberately NOT_QUALIFIED until measured
on the owner's Radeon driver. The runtime can contain capabilities that this
Ledger adapter has not qualified; registration does not enable them automatically.

Chat qualification measures actual load time, tokenization/template behavior,
text generation, token usage and available resident-memory metrics. It does not
prove hardware advice or engineering reasoning. Embedding and vision file sets can
be inspected/registered; their native execution profiles are held separately.
Missing original engineering files are not invented or imported from quarantine.

## State, stop and upgrades

Private registry, qualification receipts, dialogue and model selections use the
existing Kernel settings/database. Worker records retain PID/start identity and
are reconciled against live processes. Existing jobs own inspection, qualification,
activation and replies. These profiles implement cancel and a fresh request, not
pause/resume. Master Stop and desktop close stop owned local inference. Failed
loads and cancellations leave the application usable.

The program ZIP excludes private .ledger state, model weights, managed model
copies and user project data. During installed-program updates preserve the local
.ledger directory and the external model locations; they are not files to send
back with the source ZIP. A fresh folder begins with no private model registry.

## Acceptance status and next step

This is an implementation candidate until the owner's ThinkPad demonstrates
CPU inference, a two-model swap, failed activation recovery and a typed workflow.
Linux cloud-host tests and actual native-model captures are development evidence,
not ThinkPad measurements. The progress file distinguishes this open gate from
implemented software. After owner-host qualification, Pass 4 can begin reviewed
archive intake. No further change to the sealed original archive is needed.

## Primary implementation references

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b11669
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b11669/tools/server/README.md
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b11669/gguf-py/gguf/gguf_reader.py
https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/b11669/gguf-py/gguf/scripts/gguf_editor_gui.py
https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml/blob/master/docs/gguf.md
https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M-Instruct

No source code or template is loaded from a model as a Python module. The upstream
Qt editor is a design reference; its write/edit facilities are not exposed here.

## Optional owner qualification report

Use the Brain panel for normal operation. To produce a small repeatable host report after installing this build, run:

```text
python tools/qualify_stacy_host.py --first /path/to/first.gguf --second /path/to/second.gguf
```

Supply two compatible, distinct file sets. The script performs offline loads, replies, a two-model swap, failed-activation recovery and a typed workflow. It exports Stacy_Host_Qualification.zip next to the application. Send back that small report; it excludes weights, user conversation, private profiles, project content and absolute model locations. Any previously running selection is restored when possible. No models are downloaded by the script.

records.text:
# Stacy born — Pass 4 implementation candidate

Pass 4 adds deterministic quarantine review to the existing desktop and shared
Engineering Kernel. It can run before the Pass 3 ThinkPad gate is complete. No
model is needed for intake. The original sealed archive is unchanged and no real
project file is automatically included or admitted in this program ZIP.

## Owner workflow

Open **Ledger active > Stacy intake**, `/open intake`, or **Review intake** on the
empty-workspace screen. Create a private library. Import a ZIP, individual file,
or folder, or drop one onto the intake workspace. Import copies originals into a
private content-addressed vault outside the program; it never moves or executes
the source. The queue is paged at 100 entries. Select a file to see structure,
dependencies, SHA-256, literal preview, qualification and decision receipts.

Automatic admission starts disabled. **Review batch** applies deterministic rules
and records ACCEPTED, HELD or REJECTED decisions. The owner may explicitly allow
automatic text, DOCX, JSON, CSV and source-bound chip-record profiles. Code, CAD,
PDF and images require an individual **Admit as reference** decision. A reason is
required. Missing dependencies, changed bytes, malformed data and conflicting
catalog paths cannot be bypassed with an owner-approved flag inside a file.
Chip records use schema `arc.intake-chip/1` with part, exact variant, source path
and source_sha256. Current variants are F133-B, D213ECV, ECP5-12F and ECP5-45F.
Other chip formats remain generic reference data rather than verified chip facts.

Select mutually dependent unadmitted files with Ctrl/Shift, then **Admit selected
bundle**. This owner decision validates every original, profile and
dependency and commits all receipts together. A complete PCB/schematic pair can
enter as a reference set; malformed or missing members abort the entire decision.
Automatic review never admits dependency cycles. Later reversal of one accepted
member holds its dependents and makes their packets stale.

The V1 catalog contains current admitted references only. Its working version is
1; old working revision history is not imported. Original provenance and separate
admission receipts remain available. Reference admission does not attach a mutable
engineering workspace, promote firmware/application source, prove statements in a
document, or qualify a board. Native ERC/DRC, compilation and physical checks are
explicitly NOT_RUN / NOT_QUALIFIED. Existing protected-source acceptance remains
independent.

## Originals, parsers and dependencies

Each source has a content manifest and each original has a complete SHA-256.
Snapshot mode treats the verified private copy as the original; later changes to
the input folder do not alter it. The API also supports external mode, where the
original source must remain accessible and unchanged. A missing or changed source
never falls back to a cached snippet. Links, path escapes, nonportable/colliding
paths, encrypted ZIP members, oversized entries and extreme compression ratios
are refused. Limits: 10,000 files, 64 MiB per item, 512 MiB per bundle. Runtime
files inside or containing the running program cannot be detached by intake.

The original archive adapter is enabled only by its exact pinned outer SHA-256.
It verifies the seal, selects the quarantined user paths and planning documents,
and retains program/runtime resources separately. Other ZIPs cannot assert this
trusted classification themselves. Archive reads do not alter or admit anything.

Profiles inspect UTF-8 text, strict JSON, CSV shape, OOXML DOCX parts, Python AST,
local quoted includes and KiCad syntax/counterparts. They do not execute imported
code or macros. Dependencies resolve inside the same batch with exact source
hashes where declared; admission is ordered and cycles stay held. Parsing a C or
HDL file only establishes encoding and declared local includes. It is not a
compiler verdict. KiCad syntax is not ERC/DRC. DOCX previews are plain extracted
text. Optional PDF and image readers require separately installed pypdf / Pillow;
their versions appear in receipts. On Linux these optional parsers run in a
12-second, 1-GiB worker; on Windows their hard memory limit is unqualified and
they remain HELD. PDF previews cover at most 16 pages and perform no OCR. Full
multilingual OCR, exact page/section citations and semantic RAG are Pass 5.

## Reversal, retrieval and recovery

The Accepted V1 tab searches admitted text only. Reads recheck original bytes,
current policy/rule fingerprints and dependency decisions. Historical namespaces
are excluded from ordinary retrieval unless explicitly requested. Private library
ACLs are checked before search; global approval scope alone cannot read another
owner's library. Optional read grants do not confer intake decision authority.

Create a local reference packet from an admitted item. Revoke admission to remove
it from current retrieval, hold admitted dependents and invalidate packets using
it. A stale packet returns no content. Save a catalog checkpoint before changing
the accepted set. Restore rechecks bytes, policy and dependencies and creates fresh
receipts atomically; it never silently makes old packets current again. Export
produces a separate V1 ZIP containing accepted originals, current receipts and a
hash manifest. Held/rejected files, private paths and legacy working history are
excluded. Existing destination files and source locations cannot be overwritten.

Imports, reviews and exports use the existing jobs, cancellation, journal and
evidence records. Scans commit READY only after a complete immutable inventory;
interrupted scans never become accepted. Recover records an interruption; start a
new import request to reuse already verified objects. This is cancel/new-request
recovery, not process pause/resume. Decision/catalog/search/packet changes and
their activity event commit in one SQLite transaction. No second scheduler or
independent approval database is introduced.

## API examples

`/intake` reads status. `/call intake.namespaces {}` lists accessible libraries.
The Commands workspace exposes schemas for all intake operations. Source review,
policy edits, admission, reversal, restore and export are owner operations with
explicit Kernel scopes. Import and export are checked again at generic jobs.submit
so an agent cannot bypass the owner boundary. Model responses and imported text
cannot grant permissions. Local packets are not automatically sent to Gemini.

## Progress and gates

Estimated implementation progress after this pass: **47%**, or approximately 50%
after the still-open Pass 3 ThinkPad gate. This is a milestone estimate, not a
time forecast or engineering accuracy score. Pass 4 tooling is implemented as an
isolated candidate; independent protected-source acceptance and actual corpus
admission remain owner review tasks. Next: incorporate the owner's incoming idea,
then Pass 5 verified references, exact locators, language-aware extraction and
bounded retrieval evaluation. Study, long-term memory and frontier exchange remain
later passes.

# Stacy born Pass 5 — exact references and connected evidence

## Delivered candidate

The existing Engineering Kernel remains the only execution and approval authority. Reference admission remains Pass 4 intake's decision. The new reference tables live in the same private engineering.sqlite3 and mutations append the existing activity journal atomically. Background extraction, page rendering and volume verification run as registered jobs. No second scheduler, model trainer or source-promotion authority is introduced.

Use Ledger active > Exact references or `/open references`. Select a library, admit source copies through Review intake, then Index admitted sources. Indexing is an explicit job; it never admits a quarantined file. A failed or cancelled build leaves the previous committed index usable. Real user data and model weights are excluded from the development ZIP.

## Original locations

| Source | Exact address | Limit or unprovided capability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PDF | Zero-based physical page index plus PDF PageLabels or explicitly labelled physical fallback | Page text; no invented table cells, printed numbering, bounding boxes or OCR |
| DOCX | word/document.xml body index, paragraph or table row and XML cell index | XML cell index is not a merged visual grid column; printed pagination is not inferred |
| CSV/TSV | Logical record index, header and column | Header is record zero; quoted multiline records are not physical line numbers |
| JSON | Escaped JSON Pointer | Original scalar values, no schema truth implied |
| Code/text | Inclusive one-based line interval; derivative character offsets if split | Bytes are read, never executed |
| KiCad | Native UUID and parsed S-expression path | Object identity only; not ERC, DRC, routed copper or physical connectivity |

Full source hashes, locator hashes, passage hashes, extraction-rule fingerprints and current admission receipts bind every result. The PDF dependency version and available Poppler text-tool hash are included in the extraction fingerprint. Identical source bytes and the same extraction profile retain passage IDs across rebuilds. Original scripts are preserved; normalization is a separate search derivative. Han glyph detection does not infer a document's language. Translations are NOT_PROVIDED and OCR is NOT_PERFORMED. The reference panel includes an unmodified OFL-licensed Noto Sans CJK SC display font with its complete license and source notice; Chinese glyphs do not depend on a host font install.

A cache row cannot authorize its own quote. Retrieval checks admission, ACL, original bytes and the extraction profile, then independently re-extracts that original in a bounded worker and compares the exact location/text. If an original is missing, altered, revoked, historical without opt-in, or a derivative disagrees, location metadata can remain LOCATED_BUT_UNAVAILABLE, but no cached excerpt is returned.

PDF resources using Identity-H/V fonts without a Unicode map require a measured Poppler pdftotext fallback. It extracts UTF-8 text with explicit page separators, verifies page alignment and records the executable hash/version. If it is missing, fails, exceeds the budget or cannot align pages, affected pages are withheld with a gap rather than a partial Latin-only excerpt. This fixes a measured Chinese-book failure; it is not a universal glyph-accuracy guarantee, OCR or translation.

Open original location renders the selected physical PDF page in Ledger using a measured Poppler pdftoppm executable. Its version and executable hash enter the result. Without that host tool the render is blocked. Rendering is a derivative, not a physical-page measurement or source-fact review. Non-PDF formats show their checked excerpt and native address.

## Retrieval, scope and resources

Private namespace permission is checked before candidate search or packet access. A global approve scope does not confer access to another owner's library. Explicit readers can resolve references but cannot approve source facts, export private originals or mutate decisions. The model has no namespace admission capability.

SQLite FTS5 supplies a lexical baseline; exact passage IDs and a literal normalized Chinese substring fallback cover identifiers and short Chinese queries. Search is capped at 120 candidates and 40 returned hits. It reports lexical ranking, not a semantic recall guarantee. Embeddings are not enabled. The frozen evaluation is deliberately bounded and does not establish performance on an unseen owner's corpus.

Source count is capped at 1,000; extracted text at 8 MiB per source and 32 MiB per library; 16,000 passages per source; 512 physical PDF pages; 4 MiB decoded PDF content stream per page. Index construction uses a 600-second registered job budget and 25-second per-source subprocess timeout. Linux extraction has a 1 GiB address-space limit; reference jobs have a 2 GiB limit. These are resource controls, not a claim of a security sandbox. Active PDF/DOCX content and encrypted PDFs are held. Windows PDF extraction remains blocked until its hard memory-control profile is qualified. No automatic OCR, translation or model call occurs during indexing.

Optional PDF extraction uses the existing requirements-vendor.txt pypdf pin. This candidate's measured dependency versions are recorded in its verification evidence. Optional source fixtures used for testing do not enter the working reference catalog or program seed.

## Evidence Atlas and Impact Radar

Owner-reviewed source records preserve subject, property, exact variant, explicit string-valued operating conditions, original quote, quantity, exact rational unit conversion and support/refutation. The quote and quantity must occur in the checked passage. A manual subject binding is owner-declared, not verification that the part is fitted. REQUIREMENT and SOURCE_CLAIM are source evidence roles; HYPOTHESIS never becomes requirement support.

A question returns Question<SourceFact>, independent support/refutation and applicability, plus missing proof obligations. Different variants or operating conditions do not become a false conflict. Different values in the same source context demand review. A valid source fact never proves firmware compliance or physical performance. No U45 historical example or D213 GPIO is invented to fill an absent original.

Relationships are explicitly OWNER_DECLARED or INFERRED. A JOB_RESULT_FOR edge needs an actual owned completed Kernel job and binds its revision; it is not a physical measurement. Native evidence is obtained by forwarding the caller's principal to the existing links.inspect service. A detached project yields BLOCKED, unknown pins and explicit native-source/board-test obligations. A text relationship never becomes native connectivity.

The impact preview walks only captured admission dependencies and names affected reference packets. It performs no mutation, simulates no hardware result and labels untracked impact UNKNOWN. Genuine J14 pin/net/intent/requirement/result qualification is blocked because this program-only delivery has no reviewed current native project or ROM.

## Local evidence packets and Stacy

Select one to eight passages, supply a question and compile a local engineering knowledge packet. At most 10,000 source characters are included. Canonical context determines a stable program_id; a separate invocation ID identifies each creation. Packets include original locations, source hashes, reviewed fact conditions, read effects, source trust and explicit gaps. No cloud disclosure is granted. These records use the existing ARC canonical JSON profile, not an RFC 8785 claim or the full future staC compiler.

Ask local Stacy with this packet uses the existing local worker and selected model. Source material is marked untrusted reference data. A constrained response schema permits short labels S1–S8 for supplied passages and either ANSWER or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE. At least one supplied label is required for a model reply or evidence-gap explanation. The local adapter maps labels to the original canonical IDs; unknown labels are rejected, and the model-facing packet keeps exact source addresses without requiring the model to copy long hashes. The Kernel checks packet freshness and citation membership again before an assistant response is committed. Reversal during inference prevents that commit. Missing/stale input yields a gap. Citation membership does not establish natural-language entailment, engineering accuracy or effective prompt-injection resistance. The small development model trial is an integration test, not engineering-answer qualification.

## Dated reference editions

Owner-directed export creates a new external ZIP containing content-addressed originals, CATALOG.json with source/rights/extraction metadata, INDEX.sqlite with exact locations and text derivatives, and a byte-hash manifest. It uses SQLite's backup API for the index, hashes readback and publishes without replacing an existing path. Current decisions and index generation are required. It exports neither private conversations nor credentials, grants, private paths or the real quarantined corpus.

Verify reads the archive without importing it, checks safe members, all hashes, content-addressed source bytes, read-only SQLite integrity and locator hashes. With the same extraction fingerprint it also re-extracts originals to reject self-consistent fabricated derivatives. A different fingerprint yields HASH_VERIFIED_DERIVATIVE_REVIEW_REQUIRED, not automatic requalification. This is a portable data edition for a compatible retrieval adapter; arbitrary local LLM applications do not automatically understand a ZIP.

The archive is hash-sealed, not encrypted or inherently immutable. Store a master read-only and use a verified SSD copy. ISO authoring, burning, physical disc readback, archive decryption and historical Chronicle browsing are not implemented by this pass. Source licensing and disclosure permissions remain source-specific. Export does not confer redistribution rights.

The authentic Chinese-book parser probe is deliberately separate from admission. That book remains HELD by the unchanged Pass 4 policy because its passive PDF opening-page destination triggers a conservative OpenAction check. No research probe bypasses that policy. Refining admission for passive PDF navigation requires a separately reviewed policy migration, rather than silently changing the qualification of existing decisions.

## Review and next pass

Existing SDK, policy and tests remain byte-identical to the Pass 4 fairy baseline. Two new SDK modules, reference_extract.py and evidence_contracts.py, and a new test module are protected-source candidate additions. Kernel, CLI, local brain and Qt service changes are disclosed in the delivery diff. Independent protected-source acceptance remains open; development in an isolated candidate is already authorized.

See STACY_PASS_5_VERIFICATION.json and Stacy_Pass_5_Review for actual checks, screenshots, bounded evaluation and the staC compatibility probe. No original user archive was modified. Owner E16 ThinkPad, Windows, native GPU, physical hardware, original ROM and current native-project gates remain open. Approximate implementation progress is 60%, with a 63% planned milestone after those qualification gates.

Pass 6 should add explicit task checkpoints, durable reviewed memory, indexed lessons and resumable context compaction. It must recover source-addressed work after model context is cleared, preserve unknown/conflict markers, and keep source originals, decisions and concise task memory separate. Autonomous idle study and Frontier-model ZIP exchange are subsequent passes.

records.text:
# Stacy born Pass 6 — private learning and evidence-addressed memory

## What is connected

Memory & staC is a native Ledger workspace. Open Ledger active > Memory & staC, `/open memory`, or Memory & staC on the empty-workspace Home. The existing Kernel, SQLite database, jobs, activity journal, local Brain and Master Stop remain authoritative. There is no additional scheduler or background collection. Model weights remain independently replaceable.

The program ZIP contains code, upstream staC source/tests/docs, public self-knowledge and interface assets. It contains no imported personality profile, feedback, conversations, reference originals, private snapshots, recovery keys or model weights. Import the separately supplied personality JSON locally. The original quarantined project archive is unchanged.

## Teach an explicit preference

Import personality JSON in Personality / learning. The original bytes, SHA-256, declared version and selected presentation fields are stored privately. The starting expression is owner-selected; portrait interpretations are not psychometric measurements. Disabling the profile stops its inclusion in local replies. Deleting the profile and feedback leaves task records separate. Original source files and external backups are not erased by that action.

Choose creative_exploration, engineering_execution, review, delivery or general. Enter a preference ID, the direction you want, agreement from zero to one, and a feedback kind. Teach this preference commits an authenticated owner action. Ordinary local chat uses engineering_execution unless a context is supplied; task replies use the selected context. No preference is inferred from silence, cursor motion, CPU load, a build or model output.

The preference engine starts at Beta(1,1), with proposed weights 4 for a correction, 2 for a statement and 0.5 for a confirmed choice. A correction supersedes earlier observations in the same preference/context, even if they were repeated. Supersession links are preserved. Undo removes that observation and lets prior eligible evidence contribute again. Forget removes its direction/source text from active record content and recomputes the projection. This is logical deletion, not a forensic secure-erasure guarantee for SQLite pages, WAL files or external copies.

Only explicitly soft evidence decays. Direct corrections cannot be marked soft. The initial soft half-life is 90 days; weights and half-life are owner-editable through memory.profile.configure. The UI reports a preference posterior, not a calibrated probability of a person's identity or an action's safety. Model-facing soft decay is evaluated at the start of the UTC day for a stable request/validation snapshot. The detailed preference reader can report the current instant. Context projection includes at most six relevant preferences, latest directions first, and reports omitted count. No arbitrary equations from the seed are executed.

The current local Brain receives the selected expression and relevant directions as presentation data. They cannot grant tools or approve engineering facts. Profile or context changes during inference prevent a stale assistant turn from committing. Memory/staC data is excluded from cloud action proposals, including nested typed-pipeline requests. No automatic cloud fallback is added.

## Save, clear and resume

Create a task, fill goal, constraints, summary, findings, contradictions and next useful step. These are owner task notes, not independent evidence. In Exact references, choose a checked source and Keep in task memory to attach its logical locator. Up to eight passages from one library and twenty actual owned jobs can be attached. Job identity, request digest, revision and observed state are recorded; an invented job cannot become evidence.

Save and verify checkpoint requires an owner approve Principal. First the immutable checkpoint draft commits with a journal event. A separate database connection reads it back and checks its digest. A second transaction publishes the receipt and advances the task head with a compare-and-swap check. A failed save, journal append, readback or head comparison cannot dispose of working context. An unpublished draft may remain for diagnosis; it is not a resumable checkpoint.

Start fresh context from checkpoint is a separate owner action. It checks the readback receipt, original availability, exact transcript digest and absence of an active owner reply. It creates an empty successor conversation and retains the old private history, rather than deleting it. Repeating the action returns the same successor. Changed transcripts require a new checkpoint. The model worker's request cache remains disabled. A resumed request receives the checkpoint and re-resolved sources without the old transcript.

Resume with local Stacy rechecks namespace access, admission receipts, source hashes, extraction fingerprints, passage hashes and exact locators. One unavailable source withholds the compact technical findings, summary and all source excerpts, and returns explicit gaps. Saved owner goals and next steps remain task intent. A source-bearing reply is constrained to supplied citation aliases and revalidated before commit. Missing sources require insufficient-evidence output. Citations do not verify natural-language entailment or engineering accuracy.

The checkpoint records pending/completed/cancelled jobs as observations. Resume only reads their current states; it never resubmits a job, restores an execution grant or predicts physical success. A missing restored job is marked NOT_PRESENT_RECONCILE_EXPLICITLY. New work must use existing Kernel operations and approvals. Character counts in the checkpoint preview describe storage/context size; actual model prompt tokens are measured by the existing worker. Compact notes are owner-reviewed and are not claimed to be a lossless summary of every transcript detail.

## Reviewed procedures

Propose procedure stores a draft with source bindings. The draft never enters model resume context. Owner review can approve or reject it. A reviewed procedure remains text, not execution authority or hardware proof. Source loss withholds its body and removes it from active model context. At most three current reviewed procedures enter a resumed request; context-budget checks remain enforced rather than silently dropping decisive evidence.

## Private snapshots and clean recovery

Export private memory writes a new external ZIP and a separate .key recovery file. Keep the key separately. The snapshot is authenticated with HMAC-SHA256 and member hashes; it is not encrypted. It contains this owner's learning records and available owner-owned original copies referenced by checkpoints/procedures. It excludes raw conversation history, model weights, unrelated namespaces, execution grants and live job records. Existing destinations, program directories, private-profile directories and original source folders are refused. Expanded snapshot budget is 128 MiB.

Restore requires an empty owner learning state and the matching recovery key. It verifies safe paths, sizes, member hashes, authentication, profile bytes and checkpoint receipts before publishing records. It does not replay jobs or admit references. Recovered source copies are private unadmitted files. Review them in Intake, index them, and use Relink identical restored sources. Relinking requires identical source bytes, passage identity and locator, and creates a new checkpoint that preserves the old binding in history. Missing dependencies or a changed extraction profile remain a review obligation.

The private key is a local recovery trust mechanism, not an independently certified signature or a substitute for OS-account protection. Losing it prevents authenticated restoration through this interface. External snapshot deletion remains an owner action. A crash can leave unadmitted staged copies; they confer no retrieval or approval authority.

## staC integration

The owner-supplied staC Full Language Project 0.5 contributes 31 unchanged manifest-verified source/test/doc/launcher files. Its installer was not executed. Provenance is recorded in STAC_UPSTREAM_MANIFEST.json. Original upstream modules remain intact; new stac_bridge.py forwards the actual caller through the existing Kernel rather than inheriting the prototype's fixed Tutor identity.

The workbench supports compile, read execution, controlled-English translation, explicit read-observation recording and owner-directed fresh-result export. Compilation grants no runtime authority. Embedded observations live in the shared private memory table and existing activity journal; the prototype's separate CCC database is not used for that path. Standalone human-invoked ./stac remains available with its historical read-only behavior. Its POSIX internal file I/O is not Windows-qualified. The embedded export path uses portable Python file operations with normal Kernel approval; Windows execution still needs owner-host qualification.

The reference adapter supports:

- `library NAMESPACE_ID | search "words" | take 5`
- `library NAMESPACE_ID | reference PASSAGE_ID`
- `library NAMESPACE_ID | question U45 tCEM EXTENDED '{"scope":"controlled fixture"}'`

These call existing references.search, references.resolve and references.question with namespace ACLs. They do not convert a general reference into an independently verified fitted-part manufacturer witness. Historical ARC1@R10 programs still use the native/vendor readers and stay blocked while that project and original ROM are absent. The controlled-English translator recognizes finite templates; it is not general natural-language understanding.

Local planning can propose registered stac.compile/stac.run calls for normal owner review. Embedded read operations refuse internal output redirection; use the explicit owner export button. Host shell redirection and the prototype's POSIX CLI remain human OS operations, not model capabilities.

## Evidence and limits

STACY_PASS_6_VERIFICATION.json and the delivery Review folder record actual focused tests, native desktop steps, context measurements, two-model comparison, cold restoration and source-change checks. Positive reference/source examples are controlled fixtures and do not establish current ARC-1 hardware facts. Original ROM/native J14/U45/D213 evidence, ThinkPad performance, Windows, native GPU and physical board qualification remain separate open gates. Existing SDK/policy/tests are preserved; new protected SDK/test additions and all service edits are disclosed for independent acceptance.

Approximate overall implementation estimate: 72%; planned Pass 6 milestone 75% after open qualification gates. This is an engineering estimate, not a percentage of tests passed or a model-accuracy score. Pass 7 adds reviewed Gemini/Frontier research packets, disclosure receipts and validated return packages. Autonomous idle study and general language expansion remain later work.

# Pass 6 learning design — implementation reference

The owner has selected an arc.stacy.owner_personality_seed/1 JSON as the starting reference. The personal original is preserved separately from this empty program ZIP. It is not installed by Pass 5, and no adaptive updater, hidden collection or model-weight training is enabled. Pass 6 should implement this learning loop together with task checkpoints. Its private data is never part of the public Ledger self-knowledge seed.

## Build sequence

1. Add an explicit owner-controlled profile import through the existing Kernel. Preserve original bytes, schema, version, hash and provenance in private state. Permit inspection, replacement, disable, export and deletion. Treat portrait interpretations and example voices as editable proposals. Selecting a seed establishes a starting reference without converting every interpretation into an owner-confirmed measurement.
2. Project a bounded relevant profile into the existing local Brain context. Select by creative exploration, engineering execution, review or delivery. Keep preferences, technical references and execution authority distinct. Model replacement retains the profile while rerunning context/model compatibility checks. No automatic cloud disclosure.
3. Add authenticated feedback events to the existing Kernel-owned database and journal. Store event ID, preference ID, context, feedback, source reference, timestamp, owner confirmation and supersession. Deduplicate event IDs. A model-produced confirmation field cannot authenticate the owner. Silence, CPU load, cursor motion, a successful build and Stacy-generated text never count as agreement.
4. Compute the supplied neutral Beta(1,1) preference posterior from active events. Use editable proposed weights and an optional 90-day half-life for explicitly soft evidence only. Preserve direct corrections until superseded. Keep partial agreement owner-provided. Recompute after supersession, undo or forgetting. Scores rank suggestions and presentation; they do not authorize tools, measure personality identity or predict operation safety.
5. Add explicit task checkpoints and concise reviewed memory. Persist task intent, relevant exact Pass 5 source addresses, decisions, conflicts, unresolved obligations and the next useful step. Separate working context from originals and durable memory. Clear the model context, restart, and prove that a task resumes from the checkpoint and rechecks original availability.

## Exit evidence

Demonstrate one actual owner correction changing later context in the intended scope. Verify duplicates count once; current corrections override superseded evidence; creative preferences do not silently alter engineering review; partial feedback is explicit; removing feedback recomputes the posterior; a different model receives the same reviewed profile; a stale/missing original contributes no cached technical claim; and unauthorized callers cannot read or edit private memory. Prove recovery after context clearing and process restart, plus disable/export/undo/forget behavior. Measure context budgets on the selected local model.

The resulting capability should be a private, inspectable, correctable personality/reference layer and resumable task memory. Weight fine-tuning, autonomous idle study, semantic embeddings, full staC language consolidation and Frontier research exchange remain separately scoped work. This pass plan preserves existing engineering qualification and approval boundaries.

Implementation update: STACY_PASS_6.md is the current usage and qualification record. The sequence above was the approved design; the implemented candidate now supplies explicit profile/feedback, reviewed procedures and verified checkpoint/context/restore services.

records.text:
# Stacy born · Pass 7 research exchange

Development candidate. Approximate overall implementation estimate: 82%, versus the planned 88% milestone after the genuine external round trip. These are planning estimates, not test-pass or model-accuracy percentages. Owner ThinkPad, live Gemini, genuine-project/ROM, physical qualification and independent protected-source acceptance remain open. Idle study is Pass 8.

## What now exists

The native **Memory & staC → Research exchange** page and the CLI/MCP use twelve permission-checked operations in the existing Engineering Kernel. No new scheduler, tool executor, model service or cloud account is introduced. The staC 0.5 source, engineering tool registrations, physical HOLD and source-acceptance controls remain unchanged.

A request contains one precise question, constraints, attempts, unknowns, escalation reason, selected original excerpts with exact locators and hashes, a source-generation digest of those selected bindings, EKP digest, request ID and request digest. These bind the selected evidence, not the entire mutable library. No private personality, transcript, activity journal, recovery key, weights or unrelated files are added automatically. Owner-entered text itself can contain sensitive information: inspect the complete preview before export or send.

The research-sharing policy starts closed. Select permitted libraries, enable manual and/or Gemini sharing, and explicitly save it. Source ACLs still apply. Each draft records the policy revision. Changing policy requires a fresh request preview. Revoked, changed or unavailable originals block export, applicable import, approval and evaluation. An old retained response remains inspectable with its stale applicability label. Research-sharing rules are distinct from intake admission: permission to read a source does not by itself enable research export.

## Everyday workflow

1. Review and index original references through Intake as before. In References, use **Keep in task memory** to attach exact source addresses.
2. In Research exchange, **1 · Sharing / limits**, select permitted libraries and sharing channels, set usage limits and save. Gemini requires an explicit model and key in existing Stacy settings. Sharing activity stays off on this exchange path regardless of the general chat toggle.
3. On **2 · Request / preview**, use the attached source addresses, enter the question and escalation notes, and create a request. Read its complete saved JSON, source excerpts and locators. Later form edits do not change that saved request: create another request to include them.
4. Export a new external ZIP. Ledger writes a conservative disclosure receipt before publication and a committed receipt after successful publication. The ZIP is not encrypted. Export does not perform an upload. You upload it to the external reviewer yourself.
5. The reviewer follows INSTRUCTIONS.txt and fills response.json from the supplied template. The returned ZIP contains response.json, manifest.json and optional declared text/PDF sources named by their SHA256. It contains no executable material. Member hashes and lengths are exact file-byte hashes, not hashes of parsed JSON.
6. On **3 · Return / compare**, import the returned ZIP. Compare original evidence, newly supplied sources and model interpretations. A reviewer name is a self-description, not authenticated identity. Retain an inconclusive answer when more evidence is needed; use its unknowns to draft a narrower follow-up.
7. Record a disposition and reason. Approval permits evaluation of a proposed read, not engineering acceptance. Select a proposal and evaluate it through Ledger. Resolve current original citations to inspect actual source text. Retained receipts distinguish success from failure.

Imported source documents remain sealed and unadmitted inside the retained original ZIP. To use them as Ledger evidence, explicitly extract the wanted original into a separate folder and use Intake review/indexing. Research import never executes documents, extracts archive paths, applies patches, accepts source candidates, creates live jobs or turns model prose into ROM facts. Proposed code changes belong in the established candidate workflow; this first exchange format deliberately accepts read proposals only.

## Gemini adapter and usage limits

The adapter uses the existing configured Gemini key and explicit model. It sends the same saved request and response template with readable instructions, no tools, no conversation history, no automatic model selection, no redirects and no retries. A 30-second network timeout and bounded response read apply. Truncated, blocked, malformed, tool-calling, source-mismatched or otherwise invalid responses do not become applicable findings. Successful responses use the same importer and still await owner review.

Set a lifetime call ceiling, maximum serialized request bytes and maximum output tokens per call. Calls are reserved before any transmission; uncertain and failed calls count. Editing a policy never resets the recorded count. Output-token settings are provider requests, not proof of billing; provider-side billing controls are required for a monetary cap. The input-byte bound is not a tokenizer measurement. No provider key is copied to request ZIPs, receipts or returned records. No live Gemini call was made in this pass; transport behavior is covered with controlled mocks and remains unqualified on the owner's account.

API reference checked for this candidate: https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content (generateContent, JSON MIME output and maxOutputTokens). No provider prestige changes Ledger permissions or source authority.

## Return trust and failure handling

The portable SDK validates ZIP names, duplicate members, entry types, encryption flags, member count, compressed size, expansion total/ratio, JSON limits, strict keys, finite JSON numbers, manifest membership and file hashes. Imports do not extract ZIP paths. Only response.json and explicitly declared SHA-named .txt/.pdf sources are accepted. New source hashes, request ID, request digest and selected-source generation must match. Original evidence citations must be supplied original IDs; new-source citations must name declared new source members. Interpretation remains an explicit separate class. These checks locate evidence; they do not establish entailment or truth.

Only references.resolve/search/question and staC compile/read are eligible proposal operations. The owner must approve the return and explicitly choose evaluation. The original caller is forwarded to Kernel authorization; a proposal cannot acquire permissions from the reviewer. The evaluated namespace must have been shared in that request, and exact resolve must name a shared passage. Embedded staC proposals must compile into a bound reference query. Search can inspect further current entries within that already shared library; it is a local read and creates no outgoing disclosure. There is no automatic follow-up transmission.

Byte-identical or semantically identical recompressed returns are deduplicated. Review history is bounded, and the first evaluated proposal receipt is reused; an explicit new request is appropriate for a later investigation. Original ZIP bytes are retained per owner with a checksum and verified before review/read evaluation. Inconclusive and rejected returns remain retained data. The journal records state transitions, not private payload contents. A crash after file publication but before metadata commit can leave an unreferenced private sealed return; a retry can reconcile that exact file. Unknown disclosure outcomes stay conservatively recorded, with no automatic resend.

The prior Pass 6 memory backup covers that earlier memory schema; it does **not** back up new research records or retained return archives. Keep outgoing/returned ZIPs and preserve the current local profile when moving an active research investigation. Do not expect an empty new Ledger profile to recognize a return for a request it never created. Portable cross-profile investigation restoration is not claimed by this pass.

## Verification and remaining completion gate

Focused regression tests and actual native Qt walkthrough results are recorded in STACY_PASS_7_VERIFICATION.json and the separate review folder. The walkthrough exports, imports, reviews, resolves an original and evaluates a read through the running desktop using an independently scripted controlled response. This is a local harness round trip, not an external-model demonstration. No model weights or private personality seed are redistributed.

To close the genuine external gate: create an actual unresolved question in your own Ledger profile, export the reviewed packet, upload it to Claude/GPT, return the separately authored ZIP, import it into that same profile, inspect its current sources, record a disposition and evaluate one proposed read. Retain the traceable receipts and originals. Configure Gemini only when you want that optional live qualification. The development package is reviewable before those owner steps.

## Source review disclosure

Protected additions: sdk/cli/arc1cli/research_packets.py and tests/test_stacy_pass7_research.py. Existing SDK, policy and test files remain byte-identical to Pass 6. Native bridges, UI integration, public self-knowledge seed, progress and release metadata are changed and listed in the source comparison. This is an isolated development candidate; independent protected-source acceptance remains open. No hardware sources, budgets, pins, real user corpus or locked user-data archive are changed.

# Stacy born · Study, private editions and smaller releases

Pass 8 is a development candidate. Estimated overall implementation: **90%**. All eight software passes now have implementations; the remaining qualification gates prevent a 100% claim. This percentage is a planning estimate, not a measured feature or accuracy score. The authentic external-model round trip from Pass 7, live Gemini, owner ThinkPad, Windows CPU/model behavior, combined model-swap/cold-restoration demonstration, reviewed native/ROM originals, and independent protected-source acceptance remain open. Physical ARC-1 acceptance remains HOLD.

## Start here

Download all three ZIPs from this release. Each is a normal ZIP. Extract each into the same parent folder, merging their Arc_Ledger folders. All three are required. Do not concatenate the ZIPs. On Linux run `bash START_LEDGER.sh` inside Arc_Ledger; on Windows use START_LEDGER.cmd with the documented Python/PySide6 runtime installed. The launch path verifies all three release receipts and fills only missing byte-identical duplicate assets. It refuses mixed releases, altered files or symlinked targets. No network or model download is involved in assembly. The three parts are balanced by compressed bytes; their numeric order is for download organization, not a strict extraction order.

Use a fresh release folder. Keep your original locked archive, the separately saved personality JSON, external model weights, old application copy and private state. An active investigation uses BOTH the program's private `.ledger` state and its operating-system profile. This release does not delete them. Keep the old release for rollback and seal a private edition before moving private study/memory/research data. Never place private editions or keys inside the distributed program folder. To restore into a new program use the same owner identity, an empty owner profile and the separate recovery key.

## Study is a bounded reader first

Open **Memory & staC → Study / editions**. Attach the source addresses from Tasks / memory, write one study question and list known unknowns. Create study to freeze the admitted originals, namespace admission generation, reference generation, relevant reader code, operation registry, schemas and session limits.

Choose Next stage to run each stage as the registered `study.read` job through the existing Kernel. There is no second executor or job scheduler. The three stages are inventory, questions and procedure. Each commits a checksummed result and verifies it through another database connection. The inventory retains literal excerpts and original locators, extraction gaps and earlier task questions within the same namespace. The question stage records why a question remains open, a weakening observation, one discriminating read, a stopping condition and cost rationale. Contrary technical evidence is explicitly NOT_ASSESSED by this finite reader. Owner-entered contradictions and extraction gaps are retained; the reader does not invent domain conclusions.

The last stage proposes one narrow, versioned procedure: reopen an exact original and check its identity, locator and admission state. It is not an arbitrary Stacy-written script or a generalized scientific learning engine. The local Brain and its replaceable weights remain available in Ledger; this first study pipeline itself uses **zero model tokens and zero cloud calls**. There is no weight training or claim of improved model reasoning.

Pause / cancel retains committed stages and requests cancellation of owned work. Resume requires the owner to reconcile the terminal job; an unknown or failed uncommitted stage cannot silently resume from a timer. A committed read result can survive a later failed terminal receipt without being rerun. A study has three stages, at most nine submitted attempts and a finite data budget. The workflow stops after stage three. Starting a new investigation or changing evidence requires a new frozen session; restoring identical source bytes has a separate, explicit relink operation.

## Procedures need a held-out check and your review

Attach a reference from a **different private library** as a held-out input. Held-out check uses the fixed oracle CURRENT_ORIGINAL_MATCHES_FROZEN_BINDING_V1 through the registered references.resolve operation and the actual caller's permissions. It checks source identity and applicability; it does not judge entailment, engineering accuracy or model learning. Same-library trials cannot earn held-out credit. Revoked or changed inputs cannot supply a fresh passing review.

Approve procedure requires a current passing held-out trial and explicit owner approval. It installs the fixed procedure in the existing reviewed memory catalog with its training and held-out source dependencies. A model review, confidence score, document saying 'approved', or an imported archive never supplies this approval. Rejecting the memory lesson through the older catalog also revokes procedure use. Current-source checks apply again when the procedure is used. There is no arbitrary Python, shell, patch, permission grant or source promotion in a procedure.

## Idle pilot and resource limits

Idle starts disabled and is armed for exactly one existing unfinished session. The pilot is limited to Linux while **Ledger itself remains the active window**. It is not an OS-wide idle detector. Focus loss is a veto because the owner may be working in another app. Recent key, mouse-button, wheel or touch input is a veto; input timestamps stay local and do not become personality feedback.

The trusted desktop bridge supplies input/focus presence and measured aggregate CPU readings. Public commands cannot submit invented idle measurements. Presence must be fresh and belong to the current live desktop process. Unknown CPU, available RAM or required battery/power state prevents idle admission. Other active Kernel work also blocks it. A missing battery inventory is reported as NO_BATTERY_REPORTED rather than measured mains power. On a battery host, charging status alone is not treated as proof of AC; a power-supply online reading is required. Windows idle remains unavailable until separately instrumented and qualified.

Defaults: 90 seconds without local input, host CPU at most 30%, at least 512 MiB available RAM, at least 128 MiB disk free, a 20-second per-stage wall limit, two CPU seconds accounted across the study worker and completed extractor children, 192 MiB RSS, 128 KiB retained session payload and no LLM token allowance. The Linux worker applies inherited address-space and per-process hard CPU limits, background niceness, cooperative worker-RSS, cumulative CPU/time and disk checks, cancellation and idle-veto checks before publication. Available memory respects the host's container ceiling when present. RSS and aggregate CPU are different measurements. Retained-payload limits are logical JSON budgets, not a guarantee on all SQLite/journal/log allocation. The extractor preserves tighter inherited memory ceilings; the RSS check is for the study process rather than a hard aggregate RSS guarantee for all descendants. All work remains read-only apart from bounded private study records and normal Kernel receipts.

Save limits applies to new sessions and disarms idle. An existing session retains its frozen limits. Master Stop pauses unfinished studies, disarms idle and cancels the registered jobs alongside existing work. It cannot be undone by a timer; explicit owner resumption and re-arming are required. Activity and stage records show incomplete, failed and waiting states without promoting them to successful engineering evidence.

## Six grounded feature proposals

Show six feature proposals inspects a frozen operation registry and exact argument schemas. It proposes citation continuity, source-gap research handoffs, source-impact study, reviewed procedures, private editions and portable reference libraries. Every proposal lists operation names, permission scopes, semantic joins, missing glue/review, a deduplication key, cost rationale and a falsifiable test. These are grounded compositions of existing capabilities. They are not claims of six new products and they do not execute themselves. Shared JSON shape or a similar name is not enough to prove semantic compatibility.

## Dated private editions

Seal private edition writes a dated, authenticated ZIP and a **separate recovery key**. Two readbacks verify the seal/index before success; no context is cleared or source removed. The edition includes the owner's memory, research requests, disclosure receipts and original return ZIPs, finite study records and available owned source copies. It excludes model weights, credentials, raw chat transcripts, execution grants, live jobs, other owners' records and desktop idle presence. It is authenticated but **not encrypted**. Keep both artifacts privately and the key separate.

Restore requires an empty owner memory/research/study profile and the matching owner/key. Member bounds, names, hashes, HMAC, record types, checkpoint receipts and study stage digests are checked before records are published. Old jobs are not reinstated; old execution permissions are not restored; idle is off. Source copies are staged unadmitted. Review and index wanted copies through Intake, then use Relink restored for a paused study with identical bytes, passage IDs and locators. Resume preserves the prior committed stage receipts and runs only unfinished work. A changed reader registry requires a new session.

Restored research returns retain their original archive bytes and dispositions but their historical bindings may be unavailable; create a newly reviewed source-bound research request before further applicable exchange. This release does not silently remap an external request's original identity. Reviewed procedure dependencies must be rechecked against current originals before activation/use. A private edition authenticates local recovery data, not an external reviewer or manufacturer claim.

## Clean release and migration

The UI asset pack now stores unique binary payloads in one compressed block with an index. **All 7,943 canonical asset byte streams are unchanged from Pass 7**, including icon exports, original outlines, art, dimensions, sprites and licenses. The portable AssetPack reader supports both the original format and this compact format; authoring retains its prior file-oriented export. Identical large images at multiple installed paths are downloaded once and recreated after all three ZIPs verify. The font, Linux/Windows CPU archives, runtime pins and original user-selected artwork remain unchanged. No model weights or user corpus are in the program release.

Older root verification snapshots and repeated QA galleries are excluded from the new application payload; the saved earlier releases remain intact. Tests, source, public architecture notes, provenance and third-party notices remain available. The reviewed test-fixture change replaces a literal invented home path with a temporary synthetic path and retains its exact assertion. Empty-program Home now uses the existing overlay/resume mechanism and has a regression check for unsaved Preview continuity. The stock release command now selects the detached program contract for PROGRAM_ONLY packages while preserving the native full-project contract for attached projects. It does not treat missing genuine native sources as qualification.

Database additions are confined to the private stacy_study table; existing memory/research schemas are retained. Added Kernel operations and study.read use existing scopes and jobs. Reverting to Pass 7 retains the existing tables and private state but cannot operate new study features. Do not copy a new edition into an old profile without matching-version restore support. Three-part assembly never overwrites an existing changed duplicate asset and never touches `.ledger` or the operating-system profile.

## Verification and remaining issue register

Run `python tools/check_release.py --ui` after assembly. The detached-profile integrity, privacy, seed bindings, menus, Save/Home/resume and changed workspaces are checked. Focused regressions, actual study jobs, interruption/recovery, held-out source checks, two-corpus isolation, private edition cold restore, Master Stop, incomplete/mixed delivery, and asset byte identity are reported in the separate release review.

Open gates: authentic external Claude/GPT return and live Gemini account; owner ThinkPad/Windows/driver/performance profile; genuine ROM/current native and physical evidence; independent protected-source acceptance; a new combined real-model swap plus study-edition cold restore; generalized domain-specific study, semantic contradiction discovery and model-learning benefit. The earlier Pass 6 measured two-model example is historical evidence, not a fresh Pass 8 combined demonstration. This build's narrow reader is qualified only by the recorded source-integrity oracles and measured host/UI checks. No numerical accuracy, physical acceptance or unattended cross-platform qualification is inferred from a completed software pass.

# Stacy born Pass 9 source connections

Development candidate for the knowledge integration campaign. Pass 9 connects original ROM records and a separately identified V1 reference snapshot through the existing Engineering Kernel. It establishes source identities and availability; it does not establish fitted-part applicability, engineering compliance or physical operation.

## Everyday use

Open **Ledger active > Source connections**, or select **Source connections** in Exact references. Summaries are short; **Technical details** expands hashes, reader profiles, qualification and gaps. The ordinary Stacy direction remains selecting her to begin a conversation, concise answers and expandable technical depth. ThinkPad study reporting is the local direction; live iPhone updates and the iPhone development wing are deferred.

1. Mount ROM 001 using the host operating system, or use a privately extracted folder preserving the entire volume. Extracting the outer ZIP alone leaves an ISO; select the mounted volume root containing VOLUME.json. This pass does not mount images or install optical drivers.
2. Select **Connect ROM folder**. The app pins the selected manifest identity and starts a registered verification job. Complete original-object readback, catalog identity, both SQLite databases and every FTS5 index are checked before a connection is published.
3. Search by an exact part identifier, parameter or original Chinese text. Results are archived search derivatives with verified original availability. Missing originals withhold cached excerpts.
4. Select a result and **Reopen and render original page**. A registered job re-extracts the original PDF using the existing bounded reader, preserves its physical page and page-label distinction, and optionally renders it using the measured Poppler tool. No translation or OCR is inferred.
5. Inspect the preserved locked user ZIP with **Inspect locked project archive**. All declared archive members are verified. The native CAD and selected firmware identities are listed without restoring files into the active source tree. **Select as V1 reference baseline** records an explicit owner reference choice. It does not accept engineering claims, promote source or import editable development history.

No source is connected automatically after installation. Original ROM, project archives and private state remain separate from the three program ZIPs.

## Authority and failure behavior

Ten permission-checked operations and two new job tools share the existing Kernel scheduler, cancellation, evidence, argument schemas, CLI and MCP interfaces. Persistent connections are owner-scoped in the existing private Kernel database, with payload checksums and atomic activity events. Other owners cannot enumerate or read the connections. Cloud-proposed actions cannot access these private operations.

Connection and snapshot registration require the approve scope. Original-page jobs additionally require read permission. An execute scope alone cannot open source text. Direct job submission rechecks the same options and authorization. Source jobs cannot use executable candidates or isolated project execution.

Revoke selected connection prevents subsequent reads and invalidates completed page results. Reverification increments the connection generation. Page results must match their completed Kernel job and canonical artifact hash; copying a valid source hash into altered output cannot make that output applicable. Selection epochs prevent a late result from replacing the newly selected context.

The ROM manifest and catalog are checked on use. Original bytes and reader identity are checked before page access and again before publication. Unavailable, changed or revoked originals produce a gap, not a previous cached answer. An archive can remain a historical reference while its contents have no accepted current-design applicability.

## SQLite qualification and mutable copies

The portable reader creates a private exact-byte database copy, checks that copy against its expected digest, and opens it with mode=ro, query_only and trusted_schema disabled. It never asserts immutable media for a writable SSD cache. Live WAL, SHM or journal companions on an allegedly sealed source are rejected. Size, copy time and SQL work have explicit limits.

Qualification uses the Online Backup API from that frozen connection into a disposable database. PRAGMA integrity_check and each FTS5 integrity command run on the disposable backup. rank=1 includes the comparison against external content, which ROM 001's vendor index requires. The original databases are unchanged. This is qualification of a sealed index, not a live-memory archive implementation.

The older SDK RecordStore now uses the same pinned connection rather than immutable=1. Legacy record APIs retain their existing project boundary; the new owner-scoped source service is usable in an empty program without copying the old project catalog back into it.

## Budgets and proof limits

Each sealed SQLite file is at most 160 MiB; copying is bounded to 30 seconds, qualification backup and checks to 60 seconds. ROM verification retains the existing 640,000,000-byte volume allowance. Baseline input is at most 256 MiB compressed, 640 MiB expanded and 5,000 ZIP members; declared members are read and checked, never executed or extracted into the program.

Search is bounded to 40 results and 200 query characters. Han text uses literal substring retrieval; other terms use the existing FTS5 lexical ranking. Original-page extraction retains the existing 512-page document, text, worker-time and memory limits. Long manuals, encrypted or active PDFs and missing native text remain explicit gaps. Model calls and network calls are zero.

Registered source workers use a 2 GiB address-space ceiling and finite CPU time on Linux, plus Kernel timeout, cancellation and owned-process handling. Windows source profiles and PDF hard limits require separate qualification. A native glyph match is not a translation, table-cell reconstruction or semantic engineering judgment.

## Integration campaign

The preceding software implementation estimate remains 90%; this pass does not turn the eight-pass acceptance milestone into production certification. The separate knowledge campaign follows passes 9 through 15, with a 10% target after Pass 9's five source checks. Owner-host, external-model, combined model/edition and independent protected-source acceptance remain open.

Next is Pass 10: exact native part, signal, document and Kernel-evidence relationships with dependency-driven stale states. Current project promotion, fitted-part acceptance and all physical release gates remain separate. Original locked archive bytes are preserved.

Official implementation references: https://sqlite.org/backup.html ; https://sqlite.org/fts5.html#the_integrity_check_command ; https://sqlite.org/uri.html .
