# Stage Six: paired exchange, signed releases and deployment

Candidate 5.0.0a6 completes the six implementation stages of the approved upgrade. Physical and owner acceptance remains pending. Open **View → Exchange & deployment**. The panel has Paired exchange, Offline updates and Computer & appliance pages. Paper/graphite styling, ordinary project files, Project Desk, Changes, Continuing work and the earlier engineering routes remain.

## Begin on one computer

Extract the complete ZIP into a NEW program directory. Keep the previous program. Close Ledger and its coordinator, then make and verify a complete workspace/profile backup before the first open. Use the installed runtime interpreter, normally `.venv/bin/python`; commands below use `python3` as a placeholder for it. Model weights are optional and are not distributed.

Stage Six adds versioned exchange and release tables to the existing Kernel database, plus a versioned SQLite counter/replay database in the existing pill identity folder. Existing sent.json and every retained seen.json exclusion are imported once. Replay history is never pruned. Existing records remain readable. The changed executor binding intentionally makes an old continuing-work grant stale: inspect it and create a new reviewed order rather than expecting automatic resumption. No source file can renew a grant.

The default mode is SINGLE. No new listener, model or service is started by opening the new panel. Existing manual Brain, engineering and locally reviewed developer-candidate update routes retain their previous boundaries; they are not retroactively covered by the new protected-worker or signed publisher-release profiles. External release bundles should use the Offline updates page described below.

## Identities and TLS pairing

The signed `arc.pill/1` archive/contract format is retained. USB transfer remains available. The previous custom encrypted network protocol has been replaced by Python/OpenSSL mutual TLS 1.3, using the existing Ed25519 pill identity. Historical source is inert text in docs/history/pill_link_4_9.py.txt. There is no old-wire fallback. Both network endpoints must upgrade and explicitly pair TLS cards, even if their ordinary pill keys were paired before.

1. On each computer, choose **Show my TLS card**, then **Save my TLS card**. Share only that public JSON file. Never share the private pill identity directory.
2. Enter the other computer's card path. Compare the full 64-character certificate SHA-256 over a separate trusted channel, then enter it and choose **Pair this verified card** on each computer.
3. The TLS certificate public key must match the signed pill card. Each connection requires a paired certificate, TLS 1.3 and the expected exact peer key/certificate pin before application bytes are sent. A name or IP address is not the peer identity. Certificate validity requires a correct host clock.
4. **Revoke selected computer** removes both the pill pairing and TLS pin. New connections, transfers, acceptance and application of a previously staged returned proposal require the sender still to be paired. Existing receipts and replay exclusions are retained. Re-pairing a legacy pill-only card does not reactivate a revoked TLS pin.
5. **Rotate my certificate** retains the signing identity but generates a new one-year leaf certificate. Explicitly exchange and verify the new public TLS card on the other computer. Old pins do not silently roll over. For a compromised signing key, revoke the old identity, create a new identity in a new private state directory, and explicitly re-pair. Keep the old receipts for provenance.

The local OS/account, private state and trusted clock are part of this boundary. This is not protection against an administrator replacing files or restoring stale security history. After deliberately restoring an old backup, reconcile sequence/replay history with the other computer or rotate/re-pair identities before resuming exchange; cloning a live identity and counter into two independent active machines is not supported.

## Request, result and master authority

Choose a profiled working copy and a paired computer. Enter a title and requested result, then **Preview request files**. Inspect the exact admitted files, hashes and exclusions. Existing pill/1 cannot represent hidden names such as .editorconfig or .gitignore; these exclusions are displayed explicitly. Retain configuration through Changes' ordinary working-copy ZIP export where needed. A pill export does not silently claim to contain the whole folder.

**Export reviewed request** rechecks the selected bytes, freezes the signed request and writes `Files/Exports/Pills/ID.pill`. It also queues it for an explicitly started listener when a TLS pin exists. This opens no socket. Exporting, transmitting, accepting and executing are separate actions. Task/operation names in the contract express the request; they grant no native command, work order or network authority.

Transport saves a completed signed pill under `Files/Received/Pills` in quarantine. **Choose & inspect pill** verifies sender, recipient, signature, member hashes and contract. **Accept request as working copy** requires the exact inspected archive SHA-256, reserves the replay claim durably and creates a profiled working copy. The optional Slate checkbox delegates access to that copy; a separate reviewed Continuing work order is still needed for continuing execution. Repeating the same completed acceptance returns its original receipt instead of creating a second copy. A received copy has no local master-publication route.

Edit that copy through Changes, inspect/apply its working proposal, and use **Export signed result** with findings. The result binds the exact request, task, source revision, before hashes and candidate bytes. It does not carry an original-owner grant.

Back on the owner computer, inspect the returned pill, then **Stage returned edits for review**. A mismatched request/sender or changed working base is refused. A valid result becomes a frozen WORKING proposal, with its diffs and paired-pill provenance. Staging applies nothing. Open Changes, review the whole proposal and apply it to the working copy. To change the OS-home master, separately preview the original update and explicitly publish it. Original undo remains a separate Changes history. A transport receipt, model finding or peer signature is never approval to publish originals.

## Explicit network operation and interruption

The appliance can fetch requests from a workstation and send results back without opening an appliance listener. A workstation listener is an explicit process, independent of the appliance coordinator. Stop that process with Ctrl-C or its separately reviewed service control. New exchange client calls observe the workspace's persistent work hold and stop epoch; interrupted client transfer retains resumable bytes. No received message automatically resumes work.

To run the workstation listener, use its existing identity state folder and explicit directories. For a workspace `/home/ledger/Concern/Office`, the normal identity state is `/home/ledger/Concern/Office/.ledger/pills`. Substitute actual paths; the command below does not infer another workspace's keys:

```sh
python3 -m pillkit.tls_link --state /home/ledger/Concern/Office/.ledger/pills serve \
  --listen 192.168.1.20:7717 --any-address \
  --outgoing /home/ledger/Concern/Office/Files/Exports/Pills \
  --into /home/ledger/Concern/Office/Files/Received/Pills
```

Without `--any-address`, only loopback binding is allowed. No OS firewall, router or public exposure is configured. The listener accepts only actively paired TLS identities. It can serve approved exports and receive signed pills for its own identity; receipt remains quarantine only. Opening a listener means allowing the paired computer to write retained incoming data, so keep its storage capacity under observation and remove/archive old receipts deliberately.

CLI `card`, `pair CARD --fingerprint HASH`, `rotate-certificate`, `revoke PEER`, `send PATH --address HOST:PORT --peer KEY`, and `fetch --address HOST:PORT --peer KEY --into DIRECTORY` are available under the same `--state DIRECTORY` prefix. The old `pillkit.link` Python send/fetch/serve entry points now require TLS pairing. Its old custom-wire CLI is intentionally not preserved; use `python3 -m pillkit.tls_link --help`.

Transfers bind peer, pill ID, full SHA-256, declared size and acknowledged offset. One-MiB chunks are fsynced before acknowledgment; interrupted tails beyond the last committed offset are resent. Retries must use the same identity, exact bytes and quarantine directory. Server/keyring restart is supported. A completed archive is admitted only after full digest and signed sender/recipient checks. Messages are limited to 256 MiB, with archive expansion and member limits; these are per-message limits, not a total retained-storage quota. Changed/missing retained files cause an explicit refusal for inspection rather than silently resetting history. A process interruption during final publication is reconciled from verified bytes. Physical power-loss behavior has not been qualified.

## Signed offline update profile

The new release path verifies a deliberately restricted TUF 1 metadata profile: Ed25519/SHA-256, root/timestamp/snapshot/targets roles, consistent snapshot names, threshold root signatures, sequential old-and-new-signed root rotation, expiry, and durable version/hash high-water marks. No delegations, mirrors, automatic online fetch or publisher trust is bundled. This is a limited implementation, not a full TUF client conformance or independent security-audit claim. The security design reference is [TUF specification 1.0.36](https://theupdateframework.github.io/specification/v1.0.36/); the transport uses the installed [Python ssl/OpenSSL interface](https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/ssl.html).

The delivered ZIP is a complete runtime candidate, not a production-publisher-signed update bundle. A real publisher identity, independent root fingerprint distribution, separated root custody, release review and a security review remain operational acceptance work. No placeholder publisher private key is shipped.

The Offline updates page requires the owner to check/confirm the real current UTC on this boot, renewed within 24 hours. A reboot, stale clock confirmation, backwards clock or expired metadata is refused. Offline operation never disables expiration. Offline freshness is only as sound as that checked clock; an offline computer cannot discover a withheld newer release merely from a still-valid older bundle.

Bootstrap a publisher root by file plus independently verified full SHA-256. Its self-threshold must verify. Thereafter root replacement requires a sequential dual-threshold-signed chain. Validated roots and role high-water marks are persisted even if later files are missing or corrupt. A previous metadata version, equal version with different bytes or a release counter at/below the installed counter is refused. Root rotation does not reset version history. Restoring an old backup can restore old high-water marks; this is not hardware-backed anti-rollback.

A release bundle's target is the complete manifested runtime ZIP. Hashes, sizes, product/version, Python range, kernel compatibility, safe member names/types, duplicates, expansion and every inner manifest member are checked as data. No downloaded script or test is executed by preview/install/recovery. A trusted signature authenticates a publisher's bytes; it does not establish software quality. This shared-runtime profile refuses a change to the current requirements pins: a dependency migration needs separate runtime installation and qualification.

After **Verify & preview update**, inspect the verified publisher/version/compatibility. Choose a new or owned release store outside both the program and Office. **Prepare closed-Ledger install command** supplies the exact preview ID/digest, workspace and profile. Close Ledger and stop its coordinator before running it. The command's form is:

```sh
python3 -m workbench.host_cli --root /home/ledger/Concern/Office stop
python3 -m workbench.release_cli --root /home/ledger/Concern/Office \
  --profile /home/ledger/.config/arc1-workbench install PREVIEW_ID \
  --digest PREVIEW_DIGEST --directory /home/ledger/Ledger-releases
```

Use the actual profile shown by your setup, not the example blindly. CLI-created previews should use `workbench.engineering_cli --identity desktop-owner --operator` to match the default local installation identity, or supply the same explicit `release_cli --identity`.

Installation creates and verifies a complete workspace/profile backup, stages the new program beside the old, journals PREPARED and PUBLISHED, and atomically changes the owned relative `current` pointer. `open-current.sh` uses the existing runtime interpreter and retained profile. The old program and data snapshot remain. No process, service or migration starts automatically. If you enabled a systemd user coordinator unit, review/regenerate its program path for the selected release before enabling or starting it again; installation does not rewrite that unit. Clients refuse a live coordinator whose edition digest differs. Open the new program deliberately only after reviewing the receipt. Stop updating if it needs a new runtime rather than reusing the old environment.

If interrupted, inspect `releases.status` and run `workbench.release_cli --root OFFICE --profile PROFILE recover JOURNAL_ID --action FINISH` after closing Ledger. Recovery checks the frozen signed target and retained program before activation. `--action REVERT_POINTER` can return to a known previous program pointer without lowering security high-water marks. It does **not** restore data. Before running an incompatible older program, restore the verified pre-update backup into NEW workspace/profile destinations. External masters and external model weights are outside that snapshot. True power-loss durability and release-store permission review remain real-host acceptance.

## Publisher tooling

Run publisher utilities in a private offline authoring environment. A local trial can create its own root; that does not make it the production publisher. Keep private keys outside all program/workspace/release ZIP inputs:

```sh
python3 -m workbench.release_publisher init /private/publisher-keys
python3 -m workbench.release_publisher build --keys /private/publisher-keys \
  --program Ledger_Slate_5_Stage6.zip --counter 1 --out ledger-release-1.zip
python3 -m workbench.release_publisher rotate-root /private/publisher-keys
```

The initializer creates a 2-of-3 root and one key for each online metadata role; all private keys are together for local setup. Separate custodians and signing procedures are a production responsibility. Build counters must strictly increase and remain monotonic across root rotation. Root rotation produces sequential public metadata signed by old and new thresholds. Public metadata and the exact program target are bundled; private keys are not. Timestamp expires after 30 days, snapshot after 90, targets after 180 and generated roots after 365. Reissue fresh monotonic metadata before expiry, even for a retained target.

## Computer, appliance and phone

**Prepare launch configuration** writes reviewable files into a NEW folder. SINGLE and WORKSTATION use the ordinary Qt launcher. APPLIANCE prepares a `cage -- python -m workbench.launch` route and a systemd user coordinator unit with explicit program, workspace and profile paths. No OS account is created, no unit enabled, no login/linger policy changed and no display/network settings are altered. Activate only after reviewing paths on the actual machine. The Wayland/Cage direction is deliberate; EGLFS qualification is not claimed. Fluxbox remains the ordinary ThinkPad route. Menus, dialogs, games and native tool windows require the actual appliance display walkthrough.

**Share my work summaries with paired view phones** is an explicit opt-in for the current owner's continuing work. The phone's Progress page requires an unexpired, still-present paired `view` session, and sharing can be stopped immediately. It exposes up to 30 task IDs, titles, states, reasons, attempt counts and reserved token counts. It carries no inputs, outputs, grants, approval or execution controls. Existing phone HTTPS/pairing setup is still separate and no phone listener is started by sharing a summary. Re-pair phones after the remote-policy inventory changes.

## Checks and acceptance

```sh
python3 tools/check_release.py --self-test --runtime
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests_stage_six -v
python3 -m workbench.deployment_checks --ui
python3 -m workbench.continuing_checks --workers
```

The first command runs all earlier stage walkthroughs, two independent workspaces using actual mutual TLS on this host, explicit request acceptance/result review/master publication and undo, new-process reopen, full backup/restore, and signed-update recovery after an actual child-process exit. The update fixture is an inert miniature program and is never executed. Stage Six adds sixteen focused boundary tests; the previous fifty-three remain. `STAGE6_RESULT.json` contains measured results; earlier results remain historical receipts.

The physical acceptance sequence is: back up a real workspace; import a small Clock folder without changing its master; complete one bounded assignment; pair the actual workstation/appliance; fetch a request; interrupt/restart transfer; accept and review a result; create a deliberate conflict; revoke/re-pair; separately publish/undo an original; trial a signed release with deliberately expired/tampered metadata; recover its program and restored data; then qualify display behavior and the real protected worker/model profiles. Use the optional phone only after read-only sharing is verified. Implementation is 6/6 stages; physical/owner acceptance, production trust custody, independent security review, actual power loss, protected-worker containment and chosen-GGUF quality remain separate evidence.

# Graphite P05 · the ThinkPad inference path

Graphite 0.2a2 adds a pinned Linux x64 Vulkan worker alongside its CPU worker.
Both are llama.cpp b11669, source commit
`620d2225cc436ab0b001e3200e590e3b286ef9ab`. The GGUF registration, model hashes,
owned jobs, authenticated loopback API, model handover and local records remain
the same. No GGUF weights are included or downloaded by this upgrade.

The intended owner computer has a Ryzen CPU, Radeon integrated GPU and 64 GB
system RAM. The exact product and GPU identifiers remain unverified. Graphite
reads the actual current computer; a cloud inventory is never presented as a
measurement of the owner's ThinkPad. No serial number or UUID is collected.

## What to use

Open Brain from Programs or the existing model controls. The launch preferences
also appear in Settings under Local model:

| Preference | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Auto | Prefer Vulkan when an accessible AMD amdgpu render device and the bundled worker are present. Otherwise select CPU and record why. |
| CPU | Use the existing pinned CPU distribution, with GPU offload explicitly disabled. |
| Vulkan | Discover devices using the pinned worker and request GPU offload. |
| GPU layers: Auto fit (-1) | Let upstream llama.cpp select layers against its reported Vulkan budget. The explicitly selected context stays supplied. |
| GPU layers: 0 | Use CPU. |
| GPU layers: positive | Request at most that many layers. Device limits can still prevent loading. |
| Allow CPU fallback | Make one CPU attempt after Vulkan discovery, load or the initial qualification generation fails. The reason is retained. |

Saved defaults apply to the next explicit Use or Qualify operation. A queued
load keeps its frozen request. Editing a preference never restarts a working
model. Earlier records without these fields retain their CPU meaning.

The running status distinguishes the requested backend from the effective
backend. Vulkan requires a positive `offloaded N/M layers to GPU` readback from
the owned pinned worker's load log. Device discovery alone does not qualify
inference. Qualification receipts name the actual backend and runtime hash.
The normal ready-generation qualification is separate from answer accuracy.

Hardware / Vulkan shows the observed CPU/core features, system RAM, product
name, kernel, DRM render devices and driver/package versions. **Inspect Vulkan
devices** runs only `--list-devices`, in the existing asynchronous UI path.
It loads no model. Software-only Vulkan devices do not qualify as acceleration.
The report labels its device discovery and qualification limits explicitly.

## Debian dependencies

The worker archive is included. The kernel, Mesa and firmware remain maintained
Debian packages, with their package notices and security updates. Graphite does
not copy a cloud machine's drivers onto a laptop or change repository sources,
kernel parameters, user groups or BIOS memory reservations.

From the extracted program folder, the existing Debian installer can add them:

```bash
bash INSTALL_DEBIAN.sh --vulkan --quick --yes
```

That explicit command uses apt and then the normal runtime installer. It needs
the same network/package access and administrator rights as the existing Debian
installer. It is not an offline operating-system image. Offline/check-only
modes still run no apt commands. If `firmware-amd-graphics` has no candidate,
enable Debian's documented `non-free-firmware` component as an owner system
configuration step, then rerun. Graphite does not silently rewrite sources.

The outer release installer accepts the same option: add `--vulkan` to
`python3 INSTALL_LS.py --usb . --target ... --minimal-session --yes`.
Use `--plan` first for a read-only explanation. This checkpoint does not supply
a complete Debian `.deb` or Python wheel cache; full offline delivery is P19.

Runtime packages: `libvulkan1`, `mesa-vulkan-drivers`,
`firmware-amd-graphics`, `vulkan-tools`, `libstdc++6`, `libgomp1`,
`libssl3t64`, `zlib1g`, `libzstd1`, `libgcc-s1`, `libc6`.
The native worker's observed shared-library dependencies include OpenSSL,
zlib and Zstandard as well as the Vulkan loader. These package names target
Debian 13; another distribution may supply the same ABI under different names.
The existing kernel supplies amdgpu. An inaccessible render node is reported;
the upgrade never makes device files world-writable.

## Shared memory, honestly accounted

System RAM is one shared pool. DRM VRAM/GTT figures and Vulkan memory budgets
describe allocation views; Graphite never adds them to system RAM or declares
that 64 GB system RAM means 64 GB dedicated GPU memory. Device allocation limits
can be smaller than the available system memory. A large model fitting in RAM
does not establish interactive generation speed.

The preflight keeps the existing weight/KV estimate and available-host-RAM
budget. It is a conservative planning estimate, not a complete driver allocation
model. Auto layers use upstream device fitting rather than a guessed VRAM size.

CPU retains its address-space resource cap. Vulkan drivers can reserve large
virtual ranges, so a Linux supervisor instead samples the native child's RSS
and host/cgroup memory headroom every quarter second. It ends the worker when
the resident budget or reserved headroom is exhausted. Its receipt says
`RSS_AND_HOST_HEADROOM_GUARD`: **this is not a hard cap on GPU allocations**.
Shared and GPU memory may be accounted differently from process RSS; a kernel
OOM can still happen before a sample. P06 adds coordinated resource admission.
The child dies if its supervisor disappears, and Stop uses the existing owned
PID/start-token process tree. No root is needed for worker supervision.

Cancellation, changed model files and a host-memory guard stop never cause a
CPU retry. A later failed user generation is reported through its original job;
this pass does not replay user work automatically. A failed new load still uses
the existing previous-model recovery path when the owner has not cancelled.

The separately qualified protected MODEL profile stays CPU-only because it has
no GPU device grant. Resident assistant inference uses the new backend route.
Extending a protected profile requires its own deliberate device boundary work.

## Upstream pin, dependencies and reproducible build

Bundled archive:
`runtimes/llama.cpp/b11669/llama-b11669-bin-ubuntu-vulkan-x64.tar.gz`

SHA-256:
`e8709e5ba6c1b093dea7f3de57f4aba842f9a188fba6b465782d65d6fcfa4d9f`

The downloaded bytes were compared to the official release attestation. A
checksum is not itself a signature. The runtime materializer checks that pin
before extraction and verifies its private extracted-file receipt before use.
The distribution retains its upstream licence/notice files. CPU archives and
the Windows CPU add-on metadata are preserved. This pass supplies Linux x64
Vulkan; it does not promise a Windows Vulkan build.

For a local source build of the same revision, upstream documents:

```bash
sudo apt-get install build-essential cmake libvulkan-dev glslc spirv-headers
git clone https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp.git
git -C llama.cpp checkout 620d2225cc436ab0b001e3200e590e3b286ef9ab
cmake -S llama.cpp -B llama.cpp/build -DGGML_VULKAN=1
cmake --build llama.cpp/build --config Release
```

Those commands document reproduction; Graphite uses its bundled verified pin,
not a random executable from PATH. Replacing the shipped worker deliberately
requires updating its runtime manifest and qualification. Local builds need not
be byte-identical to upstream binaries.

Primary references verified for this upgrade:

- [Official b11669 release](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases/tag/b11669)
- [Official Vulkan archive attestation](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/attestations/56338993)
- [Build instructions at the pinned revision](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/620d2225cc436ab0b001e3200e590e3b286ef9ab/docs/build.md)
- [Debian 13 Mesa Vulkan package](https://packages.debian.org/trixie/mesa-vulkan-drivers)
- [Debian AMD firmware package](https://packages.debian.org/trixie/firmware-amd-graphics)
- [Debian 13 OpenSSL shared libraries and compression dependencies](https://packages.debian.org/trixie/libssl3t64)

## Completion boundary and next work

P05 delivers the runtime, selection route, device inventory, launch controls,
fallback and actual offload readback. The cloud has no physical Vulkan device;
owner hardware/model throughput and rendering comfort remain pending. No GPU
speedup or large-model capacity is claimed from this checkpoint.

P06 is the traffic cop: coordinate CPU preparation, inference admission and the
single shared RAM pool. P07 builds intelligent data arrangement; P08 handles
context/cache lifecycle. P05 provides their hardware and worker facts without
claiming those later behaviours already exist.

# Graphite P06 · the shared-memory traffic cop

Graphite 0.2a3 adds resource admission to the existing Kernel worker entry point.
The durable jobs, queue, authority checks, evidence and cancellation remain the
same. There is no separate scheduler daemon, model service or database.

## The useful change

A submitted job first waits in Queued for memory and an available lane. The
existing worker owns that wait with its PID/start token. The tool and its
execution deadline start only after admission. Waiting reasons appear in the
System work list and Work trail. Owner cancellation and Master Stop still stop
queued work, without running it. A live waiting worker is no longer mistaken
for an interrupted request after sixty seconds.

At most four native Kernel jobs run at once. Up to sixteen running/waiting
requests can be retained. Automatic nonforeground submissions stop at fourteen,
keeping two places for foreground requests. The existing same-source and
authority restrictions still apply.

| Lane | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Model turn / handover | One admitted inference job at a time, including activation and qualification. |
| CPU calculation | One by default, configurable to three, alongside inference. |
| I/O | Small indexing, intake and reference jobs share the bounded native capacity. |
| Coordinator | One clip coordinator at a time, leaving native capacity and the calculation lane for its children. |

The owner gets the next available turn; an active tool finishes at its supported
boundary. This is not GPU-kernel preemption or a promise to interrupt a native
edit halfway through. Stop remains the explicit cancellation control.

## Foreground and background

Manual submissions are foreground work. Service-driven agent steps submit
background work. Agenda Now / Normal / Background tiers become the matching
admission priorities. A higher-priority request goes first within its lane,
then creation order breaks ties.

The existing desktop input observer publishes a short, expiring foreground
lease asynchronously. It retains no keys, typed text or pointer positions.
While the owner interacts, new normal/background jobs wait and service-driven
assignments yield before their next step. Their investigation records, cursor,
findings and pending model choice stay in place. When the activity lease expires
or memory becomes available, their normal driver can continue.

The System list offers Foreground / Normal / Background on a queued job's
title by right click. The owner-only `jobs.priority` operation changes its next
admission; the CPU niceness slider remains a separate control. Agenda dragging
continues to change Agenda order. Active jobs are not falsely presented as
reorderable or instantaneously preemptible.

New background job processes default to CPU nice 10 unless an explicit job
request already exists. Cooperative numerical libraries receive a thread hint
of two, clamped to leave a logical CPU where possible. Existing llama.cpp
thread preferences remain explicit launch settings. OS nice changes may be
refused, and restoring a higher OS priority is not promised. These mechanisms
are not CPU-time or memory-bandwidth quotas.

## One memory pool

Admission observes current host available RAM, including other applications and
the existing container ceiling. It preserves a foreground reserve and accounts
for owned jobs and the resident model. It never adds DRM, GTT or Vulkan budgets
to system RAM.

Available RAM already excludes resident memory. For each live commitment the
controller reserves only `max(0, budget - observed process-tree RSS)` as future
growth. A 32 GiB model budget with 8 GiB observed RSS therefore contributes
24 GiB of future commitment. It does not subtract the resident 8 GiB again.
Model weights, KV space and temporary allocations stay inside the existing
model budget; ordinary tools use declared supported budgets where available,
or a conservative labelled estimate.

The resident model is not also counted as a second model reservation while its
own activation job is running. A completed activation leaves the model's
reservation attached to its independently owned live worker. Proven-exited
worker trees no longer occupy admission lanes; unknown ownership stays
conservative. Recovery does not replay a lost operation automatically.

Sequential model replacement can credit only observed private pages of the
owned old model for preflight. Its unused future reservation ends at handover.
The actual launch rechecks measured headroom after the old worker stops. Driver
allocations that cannot be proved reclaimable receive no advance credit.

These are **advisory commitments**, not a new global OS cap. RSS can include
shared pages, some GPU allocations are not visible in process RSS, and library
thread hints do not control all native software. Estimates and observation
limits stay labelled. Other workspaces' future reservations are not globally
brokered; their actual resident use appears in host availability. Existing
protected-worker cgroup caps remain authoritative and their CPU-only device
boundary is unchanged.

## Pressure and continued ownership

New work waits when there is no headroom. A model launch rechecks memory before
starting and before a fallback attempt. A changed headroom condition stops that
load without a CPU allocation retry.

Both Linux CPU and Vulkan model workers now have a supervising parent that
watches resident memory and host/cgroup headroom. CPU also retains its
address-space cap; Vulkan avoids that cap because driver mappings need a large
virtual range. The native child dies when its supervisor disappears. Owned Stop
still revalidates PID/start tokens and terminates the owned tree.

A guard stop is reported as preserving shared host memory. The saved model
selection, dialogue input and investigation remain; the owner explicitly
reloads when there is headroom. Guard failure does not automatically reload the
previous model into the same pressure. No unrelated application is killed.
Sampling is not a hard GPU-allocation guarantee; a kernel OOM can precede a
sample.

## Controls and readback

Settings / Shared resources contains three real owner-controlled values:

- Foreground RAM reserve: 2,048 MiB by default, clamped to a quarter of measured
  host RAM on smaller machines.
- Concurrent CPU calculations: one by default.
- Background library threads: two by default.

The next admission reads the current values. Existing workers keep their
recorded resource limits. Work trail shows current available RAM, reserve,
future commitments, admission headroom, lanes and the caller's waiting jobs.
Technical detail explains the observation and preemption limits.

## Qualification and the next pass

Focused mechanical observations exercise the changed memory arithmetic,
priority, cancellation and ownership boundaries. A real queued worker was held
before tool launch and cancelled. A small real CPU child exercised its resource
trampoline. A short native Qt walkthrough covers the new readback and controls.
No model weights, model generations, benchmark sweep or broad test suite are
needed for this software pass.

ThinkPad memory bandwidth, thermal behaviour, Radeon inference and sustained
responsiveness remain owner-host qualifications. This release makes no tokens
per second or maximum-model-size claim.

P07 builds intelligent data arrangement: useful exact calculations, source
selection and prepared evidence for the model. P08 handles context/cache
lifecycle. P06 provides their admission and foreground handoff boundaries.

## Short-horizon admission forecast

Graphite 0.2a11 applies the forecast to background jobs that pass the current
admission checks. It uses net headroom after the foreground reserve and existing
commitments. At most once a second, an exponentially weighted average updates
the estimated rate of loss with a two-second half-life. The projected headroom
four seconds ahead is current headroom less four seconds of positive estimated
loss. When that projection falls below the requested bytes, the worker waits.
The forecast can hold a job for eight seconds. The current admission checks
still decide whether it can start after that wait. Missing or stale samples let
the current checks decide immediately.

Run `python3 tools/traffic_forecast.py replay` for a synthetic scenario using
the production forecast. Run `python3 tools/traffic_forecast.py capture --help`
to record bounded, read-only samples on a running installation. Replay compares
new arrivals against future sampled headroom. A recording gives observations
from one run. Controlled runs are needed to measure the effect of changing
when work starts.

## Measure the cost of CPU and Radeon overlap

Market execution models charge for the congestion a trade creates. Apply that
idea to one small background CPU batch while the Radeon is idle, processing a
prompt, or generating a reply. Compare repeated runs with and without the batch.
Track time to first content, streaming gaps, input-to-paint delay, and useful
background work completed. The [Almgren–Chriss execution paper](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2001.041)
gives the execution-cost analogy.

Use short-window Linux pressure-stall deltas to flag reclaim or swap trouble.
Measure foreground latency to assess CPU and Radeon overlap. Judge tail latency
and background progress, including the longest queue wait. The
[NIST EWMA handbook](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/mpc/section2/mpc2211.htm)
and [Linux PSI documentation](https://docs.kernel.org/accounting/psi.html)
describe the statistical and stall measurements.

# Ledger & Slate — UI mini pass

This separate UI checkpoint continues the saved I05 implementation. I04 was accepted in the carried checkpoint; I05 actual-model and visible Calc takeover acceptance remain open. I06 has not started. The prior test receipts are historical.

The owner requested this mini pass with **no tests**. No test suite, compilation checks, model runs or acceptance trials were run. The screenshots show the actual Qt application rendered offscreen in a disposable Office workspace. Two explicitly named screenshot-example Agenda items are queued with the runner stopped; neither was executed. Popup screenshots combine the actual window and its actual popup renders, because offscreen Qt exposes them as separate surfaces. They do not demonstrate lifecycle, priority or model behavior.

- Hatch is first in the console row, followed by Line, Half and Tall. It opens exactly New Idea, New Project, On, Off and Reboot, using the existing capture and Project Desk workflows.
- Transparent original SVG assets use the existing Paper/Struthio palette: graphite, pencil yellow and eraser pink. Four interaction states are included at 16, 24, 32 and 48 pixels. The 16-pixel icon omits the mushrooms.
- Hatch lifecycle actions confirm first. Off saves open work, closes a separate persistent admission gate to new Kernel work, pauses the desktop Agenda/idle runners, drains running work and stops the model and phone link. The existing emergency work hold is applied after the drain so it does not kill an in-flight job during graceful shutdown. Long-running work can keep it in a stopping state; Nice → Stop remains available. On explicitly releases the owner work hold and service admission gate. Reboot cycles these services in the current desktop, preserves open tabs and requests restoration of a previously running model when Slate is enabled. It never reboots Linux. Cancelled jobs and phone pairing are not replayed.
- The header has CPU, GPU, RAM and TXT in that order, an independent Slate ON/OFF switch, and Nice. Date and path widgets are hidden. GPU shows unavailable when the Linux driver supplies no utilization. TXT explicitly shows unavailable because the current runtime exposes no trusted live context occupancy; completion tokens are not substituted.
- Slate admission is a persistent owner-controlled setting. New local model activation, qualification and inference jobs are gated at submission and worker admission. Existing requests may finish. Ordinary Ledger tools remain available. The desktop cloud-chat entry and provider proposals also honor the switch.
- Nice keeps Stop fixed above its scrollable work lists. Dragging pending Agenda work commits its actual persistent scheduling order and adopts the neighboring priority tier. Each row also has a niceness slider: Agenda rows use Now / Normal / Background; Kernel jobs use Linux CPU nice values 0–19. Queued CPU requests are persisted and applied before job children start. Running-job changes target the identity-verified owned worker and its verified process descendants; partial changes and OS refusals are reported. Returning to higher CPU priority may be refused by Linux. Shared services outside that process tree retain their own priority. Independently executing Kernel jobs are not a serial queue and are not draggable. The existing overall background CPU policy remains available.
- Visible menus are File, Edit, Tools, Options, Commands, Settings, Properties and Help. Existing actions, shortcuts and contextual chain/Fluxbox pipe menus are retained. Settings uses a Ledger → Settings hierarchy with name, type, value and description, validated editors and the existing stores, defaults and undo.
- Trash is pinned at the bottom-right of the left navigation panel, outside the scrolling tree. Click or keyboard activation opens its contents. Existing recoverable file drops remain available.

The full design brief remains broader than this mini pass: native-host behavioral acceptance, running-process drag reprioritization, and a trusted live model-context occupancy feed remain future work. This checkpoint does not promote I05 acceptance. No files from the I05 archive were removed. Source bindings and the package inventory are refreshed as generated packaging data, without running the validation suite.

INTEGRATION-01 (November 4, 2026): the five choices remain first; a Services row, capability groups and a session footer follow; see docs/HATCH_INTEGRATION_01.md.
